headline: YouTube viewership in Pakistan records surge
description: YouTube viewership in Pakistan records surge
author: Naeem Asghar
article_text:
TikTok has around 100 million users in Pakistan, while nearly 150 million videos are watched and uploaded on the platform daily from the country, the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunications was told on Tuesday.

PTA Chairman Major General (retd) Hafeez ur Rehman shared the figures during a briefing on social media usage, highlighting the growing popularity of digital platforms in the country.

He told the committee that 96 million Pakistanis currently use YouTube and watch around 560 million videos on the platform every day, making Pakistan the world's leading country in terms of YouTube video viewership.

Pakistanis also make millions of calls and send millions of messages daily through WhatsApp, he added.

The meeting, chaired by MNA Syed Aminul Haque at Parliament House, also addressed complaints about poor telecom services, frequent internet disruptions and the slow pace of improvements in network infrastructure.

Committee members questioned why users continued to face connectivity problems despite repeated discussions over the past two and a half years.

Member Ahmad Atiq said mobile networks were barely working in his constituency and along the route to Karachi. He complained that connectivity was deteriorating after every committee meeting, adding that even WhatsApp calls were frequently disconnected in Islamabad.

"If this is the situation in Islamabad, what can one expect in rural areas, where even 3G does not work, while you are talking about 5G?" he asked. He also sought details of the fibre-optic network laid over the past two and a half years.

Another member, Asia Ishaq, said 4G services had also deteriorated since the introduction of 5G, asking whether lawmakers would have to approach the Supreme Court to get the telecom companies to improve their services.

The PTA chairman said he had visited 41 districts along with telecom operators to assess service quality and inspect mobile towers. He said the PTA had directed the operators to improve their services, adding that issuing show-cause notices was the authority's last resort because companies often obtained stay orders from courts against financial penalties.

Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja said data consumption had increased significantly due to the growing use of social media and artificial intelligence.

She said 18 million people were using 5G services in Pakistan and the technology was being rolled out in 24 cities. The government had taken steps to improve telecom services, she added.

Recalling the country's spectrum auctions, the minister said no such auction had been held after Nawaz Sharif left office, adding that his government had introduced 4G services while the present government had conducted the 5G spectrum auction.

Khawaja said disruptions in telecom services had several causes, including theft of infrastructure. In some areas, entire mobile towers were stolen, while diesel and generators installed to keep them operational were also taken away, she told the committee.

headline: Pakistan tests indigenous Fa'az missile
description: Pakistan tests indigenous Fa'az missile
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa'az air-to-air missile, marking a significant milestone in the advancement of the country's aerospace and defence capabilities, the military's media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges.

"Fa'az will significantly enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country's overall defence posture," the statement said.

It added that the successful flight test demonstrated the "technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance" achieved by Pakistan's defence industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with scientists and engineers who played a key role in developing the weapon system.

The president, prime minister, chief of army staff and chief of defence forces, and services chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on the achievement.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful test, describing it as an important development in the defence sector.

"Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat," he said, adding that the nation was proud of its scientists and engineers.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Army successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, which was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

The ISPR had said the missile was capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating enemy missile defence systems because of its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability. Its extended range would further enhance the army's reach and ability to engage deep targets, it added.

A week before that announcement, an extended version of the indigenously developed Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile was successfully test-fired.

headline: Dry weather to prevail in the country
description: Dry weather to prevail in the country
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast dry weather across most parts of the country over the next 24 hours, while northern areas are expected to remain partly cloudy and cold.

However, isolated light rain and snowfall over hills may occur in upper Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan during the period.

According to the Met Office, temperatures recorded in major cities on Tuesday morning were 13°C in Islamabad, 19°C in Lahore, 25°C in Karachi, 15°C in Peshawar, 10°C in Quetta, 6°C in Gilgit, 7°C in Murree and 12°C in Muzaffarabad.

Dry weather to prevail in the country

.

Our Correspondent November 04, 2026 Less than a minute read
facebook twitter whatsup linkded email
ISLAMABAD:

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast dry weather across most parts of the country over the next 24 hours, while northern areas are expected to remain partly cloudy and cold.

However, isolated light rain and snowfall over hills may occur in upper Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan during the period.

According to the Met Office, temperatures recorded in major cities on Tuesday morning were 13°C in Islamabad, 19°C in Lahore, 25°C in Karachi, 15°C in Peshawar, 10°C in Quetta, 6°C in Gilgit, 7°C in Murree and 12°C in Muzaffarabad.

headline: Committee seeks support for dyslexic children
description: Panel calls for providing appropriate academic facilitation to such children in various subjects
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Panel calls for providing appropriate academic facilitation to such children in various subjects

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Federal Education and Professional Training on Tuesday expressed concern over challenges faced by children with dyslexia.

It called for ensuring that their educational future is not compromised due to lack of identification, institutional support and remedial interventions.

The panel stressed that following the enactment of the Dyslexia Act, its effective implementation has become imperative in both public and private educational institutions.

It called for providing appropriate academic facilitation to such children in various subjects.

headline: FIR alone can't bar public employment
description: FIR alone can't bar public employment
author: Hasnaat Malik
article_text:
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that mere registration of a first information report (FIR) cannot constitute a ground for disqualifying a person from public employment, emphasising that an accusation does not amount to proof or presumption of guilt.

A division bench, led by Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan, issued guidelines for federal and provincial governments, administrative authorities and law enforcement agencies to establish uniform, transparent and constitutionally compliant standards for antecedent verification during public-sector recruitment.

In its 10-page judgment, authored by CJ Khan, the court observed that a fundamental distinction must be maintained between the registration of an FIR and judicially established culpability.

"An FIR is merely an accusatory instrument and constitutes neither proof nor presumption of guilt," the judgment stated, adding that once an accused had been acquitted by a competent court, the appointing authority could not disregard the judicial determination or treat the underlying accusation as established misconduct.

The court further held that judicial acquittal must receive due recognition, subject to an objective assessment of a candidate's antecedents and suitability. It directed that adverse character verification must be based on authentic and independently verifiable material rather than conjecture or suspicion.

The judgment also laid down guidelines for the treatment of criminal cases in police character certificates. Where a candidate had been acquitted, the criminal case should not be reflected adversely in the certificate.

If proceedings were still pending, only their pendency could be disclosed, without any presumption of guilt. The court further emphasised that no candidate should ordinarily be excluded from recruitment without being provided a meaningful opportunity of hearing and a reasoned determination.

It said recruitment decisions must conform to prescribed statutory criteria, merit, proportionality and constitutional guarantees of fairness and equality.

The court examined the matter in the context of Articles 4, 10A, 18 and 25 of the Constitution, which collectively safeguard legality, due process, equality before the law, and protection against arbitrary exclusion from lawful employment.

Explaining the constitutional framework, the judgment said Article 4 required executive authorities to act within the law and on relevant considerations, while Article 25 prohibited discriminatory treatment lacking a reasonable basis and connection with a legitimate statutory objective.

It observed that Article 18, although not guaranteeing an absolute right to public appointment, protected eligible citizens against arbitrary impediments to lawful employment.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that mere registration of a first information report (FIR) cannot constitute a ground for disqualifying a person from public employment, emphasising that an accusation does not amount to proof or presumption of guilt.

A division bench, led by Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan, issued guidelines for federal and provincial governments, administrative authorities and law enforcement agencies to establish uniform, transparent and constitutionally compliant standards for antecedent verification during public-sector recruitment.

In its 10-page judgment, authored by CJ Khan, the court observed that a fundamental distinction must be maintained between the registration of an FIR and judicially established culpability.

"An FIR is merely an accusatory instrument and constitutes neither proof nor presumption of guilt," the judgment stated, adding that once an accused had been acquitted by a competent court, the appointing authority could not disregard the judicial determination or treat the underlying accusation as established misconduct.

The court further held that judicial acquittal must receive due recognition, subject to an objective assessment of a candidate's antecedents and suitability. It directed that adverse character verification must be based on authentic and independently verifiable material rather than conjecture or suspicion.

The judgment also laid down guidelines for the treatment of criminal cases in police character certificates. Where a candidate had been acquitted, the criminal case should not be reflected adversely in the certificate.

If proceedings were still pending, only their pendency could be disclosed, without any presumption of guilt. The court further emphasised that no candidate should ordinarily be excluded from recruitment without being provided a meaningful opportunity of hearing and a reasoned determination.

It said recruitment decisions must conform to prescribed statutory criteria, merit, proportionality and constitutional guarantees of fairness and equality.

The court examined the matter in the context of Articles 4, 10A, 18 and 25 of the Constitution, which collectively safeguard legality, due process, equality before the law, and protection against arbitrary exclusion from lawful employment.

Explaining the constitutional framework, the judgment said Article 4 required executive authorities to act within the law and on relevant considerations, while Article 25 prohibited discriminatory treatment lacking a reasonable basis and connection with a legitimate statutory objective.

It observed that Article 18, although not guaranteeing an absolute right to public appointment, protected eligible citizens against arbitrary impediments to lawful employment.

headline: 'Imran knew of governor's rule in K-P'
description: 'Imran knew of governor's rule in K-P'
author: ​ Our Correspondents
article_text:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday said that party founder Imran Khan was fully aware of the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rejecting reports that he had welcomed the provincial government's removal.

Speaking to the media near Adiala Jail, Gohar said Imran had not expressed satisfaction over the fall of the K-P government.

Regarding Salman Safdar's meeting with Imran, Gohar said it was the lawyer's first meeting with the PTI founder since April 8, after a gap of 380 days and called it a positive development.

He lamented that the prolonged suspension of meetings had led to the prevailing political tension.

Had regular meetings been allowed, the situation could have improved, tensions might not have escalated, and the situation in K-P might not have reached the point of governor's rule or emergency, he added.

Gohar rejected reports that his name had been finalised for a meeting with Imran, saying he had consistently tried to facilitate meetings between political leaders and the PTI founder.

'Raja rules out immediate political breakthrough'

Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said Imran's lawyer, Salman Safdar, had said the party founder was in high spirits during their meeting in jail, with his body language and determination reflecting his resolve to stand by his position.

Speaking to the media at Factory Naka in Rawalpindi, Raja said the meeting between Safdar and Imran had been necessary for the functioning of the judicial system because the PTI founder's cases were not progressing.

He said Safdar had told the court that he would not present arguments until he was allowed to meet his client.

Raja said the meeting was a requirement of the legal process rather than a favour extended to the party.

However, he ruled out any immediate breakthrough, saying the meeting with the lawyer could not be equated with the political-level engagement that the party had been seeking. Unless a political meeting took place, he said, the situation would not move forward.

Raja said he did not see the likelihood of a forward bloc emerging within the party, although he would not rule out any possibility altogether. If anyone within the party harboured reservations or ill intentions, these would eventually become apparent, he said.

Raja also clarified that the PTI was not looking towards Maulana Fazlur Rehman as a saviour. He said that, under a political climate of repression, the party saw no reason to turn away those who stood alongside it.

headline: I don't walk away from a dare, says Ali Zafar of 'Gangs of Khorasan' role
description: I don't walk away from a dare, says Ali Zafar of 'Gangs of Khorasan' role
author: Qaisar Kamran
article_text:
"I've waited for a character that would take me far from my comfort zone. Out of all the scripts I read, Bostan Khan was the one that dared me. And I don't walk away from a dare," actor and singer Ali Zafar told The Express Tribune, explaining what drew him to his upcoming project, Gangs of Khorasan.

Known for his romantic screen presence, stylish appearance and soulful music, Zafar is now preparing to step into unfamiliar territory with a character that is a departure from the roles audiences have traditionally associated with him.

In the upcoming web series, Zafar plays Bostan Khan, a mysterious gangster whose rugged appearance, thick moustache and distinctive glasses have already caught the attention of fans after the actor shared a glimpse of his new look on social media.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Zafar described Gangs of Khorasan as a mafia-themed web series, calling it the first of its kind in Pakistan. The project will see him explore a darker and more intense character, moving away from the romantic and light-hearted roles that have been a significant part of his acting career.

The transformation is particularly notable given Zafar's relatively limited acting appearances in recent years. His last major live-action film as a lead actor was Teefa in Trouble (2018), opposite Maya Ali. The film, which also marked his debut as a film producer and writer, became a commercial success. He later lent his voice to the animated film Allahyar and the 100 Flowers of God (2023). His appearance in Gangs of Khorasan therefore marks a significant return to screen acting, particularly in a web-series format, after an extended gap.

The series also features Feroze Khan, Humaima Malick, Sonya Hussyn and Syed Jibran. Feroze has established himself through television dramas including Khaani, Khuda Aur Mohabbat 3 and Akhara, while Humaima gained wider recognition through Shoaib Mansoor's film Bol (2011), followed by appearances in Bollywood and Pakistani cinema, including The Legend of Maula Jatt. Sonya Hussyn, known for her performances in Aisi Hai Tanhai, Ishq Zahe Naseeb and Deemak, has built a reputation for taking on challenging characters. Syed Jibran, meanwhile, has remained a familiar presence on television through dramas such as Chup Raho, Neem and Pagal Khana.

Produced by Anas Ali, with direction associated with Hamza Ansari, Gangs of Khorasan brings together an ensemble cast for a story centred on the world of organised crime. While further details about the storyline and the individual characters remain under wraps, the project's mafia theme and its cast have generated interest.

Ali Zafar started out on Pakistani television as an actor before becoming a popular musician, later also established a career in Bollywood and his success led many Pakistani actors to venture into Hindi films. He has received five Lux Style Awards and a Filmfare Award nomination.

Zafar began his music career as a composer and gained popularity with his single "Channo" from his debut album, Huqa Pani (2003), which sold over five million copies worldwide. "Channo" turned out to be a huge success, topping many music charts and earned him several awards for Best Music Album and Artist. Zafar made his acting debut in cinema with a leading role in the 2010 Bollywood satire film Tere Bin Laden, a moderate box office success. His performance in the film garnered critical appreciation and earned him several nominations in the Best Male Debut category, including Filmfare. He then also worked in several films, including Mere Brother Ki Dulhan, Chashme Baddoor, and Dear Zindagi.

Alongside his acting and singing career, Zafar participates in tours, concerts, and stage shows, is active in humanitarian work, and has a number of endorsement deals.

On 23 March 2021, Ali Zafar was awarded the highest literary award, Pride of Performance, for his contribution in the field of arts and music.

For Zafar, however, the attraction appears to lie in the challenge of playing someone unlike the characters he has portrayed before. His decision to take on Bostan Khan suggests an attempt to expand his acting range and reconnect with audiences through a genre he has not previously explored in this way.

Zafar also introduced the character through a bold social media post, announcing himself as Bostaan Khan in Gangs of Khorasan. Sharing the first-person declaration, "Warned you not to mess with me. My world. My rules. I AM BOSTAAN KHAN!".

article_html:
KARACHI:

"I've waited for a character that would take me far from my comfort zone. Out of all the scripts I read, Bostan Khan was the one that dared me. And I don't walk away from a dare," actor and singer Ali Zafar told The Express Tribune, explaining what drew him to his upcoming project, Gangs of Khorasan.

Known for his romantic screen presence, stylish appearance and soulful music, Zafar is now preparing to step into unfamiliar territory with a character that is a departure from the roles audiences have traditionally associated with him.

In the upcoming web series, Zafar plays Bostan Khan, a mysterious gangster whose rugged appearance, thick moustache and distinctive glasses have already caught the attention of fans after the actor shared a glimpse of his new look on social media.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Zafar described Gangs of Khorasan as a mafia-themed web series, calling it the first of its kind in Pakistan. The project will see him explore a darker and more intense character, moving away from the romantic and light-hearted roles that have been a significant part of his acting career.

The transformation is particularly notable given Zafar's relatively limited acting appearances in recent years. His last major live-action film as a lead actor was Teefa in Trouble (2018), opposite Maya Ali. The film, which also marked his debut as a film producer and writer, became a commercial success. He later lent his voice to the animated film Allahyar and the 100 Flowers of God (2023). His appearance in Gangs of Khorasan therefore marks a significant return to screen acting, particularly in a web-series format, after an extended gap.

The series also features Feroze Khan, Humaima Malick, Sonya Hussyn and Syed Jibran. Feroze has established himself through television dramas including Khaani, Khuda Aur Mohabbat 3 and Akhara, while Humaima gained wider recognition through Shoaib Mansoor's film Bol (2011), followed by appearances in Bollywood and Pakistani cinema, including The Legend of Maula Jatt. Sonya Hussyn, known for her performances in Aisi Hai Tanhai, Ishq Zahe Naseeb and Deemak, has built a reputation for taking on challenging characters. Syed Jibran, meanwhile, has remained a familiar presence on television through dramas such as Chup Raho, Neem and Pagal Khana.

Produced by Anas Ali, with direction associated with Hamza Ansari, Gangs of Khorasan brings together an ensemble cast for a story centred on the world of organised crime. While further details about the storyline and the individual characters remain under wraps, the project's mafia theme and its cast have generated interest.

Ali Zafar started out on Pakistani television as an actor before becoming a popular musician, later also established a career in Bollywood and his success led many Pakistani actors to venture into Hindi films. He has received five Lux Style Awards and a Filmfare Award nomination.

Zafar began his music career as a composer and gained popularity with his single "Channo" from his debut album, Huqa Pani (2003), which sold over five million copies worldwide. "Channo" turned out to be a huge success, topping many music charts and earned him several awards for Best Music Album and Artist. Zafar made his acting debut in cinema with a leading role in the 2010 Bollywood satire film Tere Bin Laden, a moderate box office success. His performance in the film garnered critical appreciation and earned him several nominations in the Best Male Debut category, including Filmfare. He then also worked in several films, including Mere Brother Ki Dulhan, Chashme Baddoor, and Dear Zindagi.

Alongside his acting and singing career, Zafar participates in tours, concerts, and stage shows, is active in humanitarian work, and has a number of endorsement deals.

On 23 March 2021, Ali Zafar was awarded the highest literary award, Pride of Performance, for his contribution in the field of arts and music.

For Zafar, however, the attraction appears to lie in the challenge of playing someone unlike the characters he has portrayed before. His decision to take on Bostan Khan suggests an attempt to expand his acting range and reconnect with audiences through a genre he has not previously explored in this way.

Zafar also introduced the character through a bold social media post, announcing himself as Bostaan Khan in Gangs of Khorasan. Sharing the first-person declaration, "Warned you not to mess with me. My world. My rules. I AM BOSTAAN KHAN!".

headline: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies at 35
description: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies at 35
author: News Desk
article_text:
Country singer Nicole Taylor, one-third of the musical trio Taylor Red, has died aged 35 following a battle with breast cancer.

Her triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie Taylor, confirmed the news in a YouTube video.

Nicole died on September 28. In the emotional video, her sisters said she was "at peace and no longer suffering" as they began sharing details of her illness and final months.

Natalie revealed that Nicole was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2022 after the sisters received the news while they were in a "public place".

Nika later explained that the cancer was Stage 3 and "very aggressive".

Despite undergoing chemotherapy, Nicole continued to encourage those around her to enjoy life.

"She pushed us all to have fun and not live in fear and hopelessness and she even did CrossFit during the time she was getting chemo treatments," Natalie shared.

The sisters also paid tribute to Nicole in a statement on a page created in her memory.

"Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed. She was our leader and our best friend," they wrote.

"We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again," they added. Nika and Natalie also confirmed that a private funeral had already taken place.

The identical triplets began their musical journey playing instruments including guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin.

Originally performing as Red Roots, they later built a substantial online following through comedy videos, musical challenges and social media content.

The sister trio started as a musical entity in 2011, with their first independently released album, Red Roots, that was released on January 24, 2011, with Red Hen Records. Their subsequent studio album, The Middle of Nowhere, was released on March 20, 2012, by Red Hen Records. They released, Triplicity, the third studio album, on January 7, 2014, from Red Hen Records alongside Daywind Music. The group was signed to Inpop Records in 2015.

Taylor Red released track Country Money in March 2021. It was produced by Ilya Toshinsky and written by J.T. Harding, Matt Jenkins, and Andrew DeRoberts. The track was added to Spotify Editorial playlists and went viral on TikTok.

Taylor Red was featured in the national Sonic Drive-In campaign commercials for 2020-2021. The trio performed over 1,000 live shows across America and internationally in countries such as Norway and Canada, opening for acts including Amy Grant, Charlie Daniels, Diamond Rio, Don Williams, High Valley, Josh Turner, and Michael W. Smith.

Taylor Red reportedly amassed more than 13 million TikTok followers and 16 million YouTube subscribers, alongside brand partnerships with major companies.

headline: Children's theatre dominates World Culture Festival 2026
description: Children's theatre dominates World Culture Festival 2026
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The sixth day of the 25-day 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi 2026, organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, featured two children's theatre productions, music, film screenings, dance and the Urdu-English theatre play English Only. A special Spanish dance performance, Flamenco Blanco Flamenco, was also among the highlights of the day.

The programme for children opened with Little Red Riding Hood, presented by Poland's Miniatura City Theatre. Conceptualised, directed and designed by Chile-born artist David Zawalla, the production offered a contemporary interpretation of the well-known fairy tale, set against a futuristic backdrop. Using puppetry, the play portrayed the struggle of the last human girl on a devastated Earth. Norwegian theatre group Erler Teaterkompani presented the adventure-filled production Gangster Hunting with Daisy Detective. The play followed the detective Daisy as she unravelled a mysterious case and pursued a gangster. Children in the audience were also invited to participate in the investigation.

Music enthusiasts attended a special workshop titled Jam and Improvisation, conducted by renowned Serbian guitarist and musician Aleksandar Lipovan.

Under the film screening segment, Polish Featurette presented four short films from Poland: Blue Bird, Momo & Lulu, Dream Up the Title and The Town That Drove Away.

At 7 pm, the Urdu-English theatre production English Only, directed by Awab Bin Farhat, was staged. Set in an English-language classroom in Karachi, the play revolved around four students brought together by their desire to master English.

The day's programme also featured Spain's special dance performance, Flamenco Blanco Flamenco, under the title The Grace of Movement. Through the traditional Spanish art of Flamenco, the performers showcased their artistic skills, combining expressive hand movements, intricate footwork and rhythmic music. The performance highlighted the emotional depth, energy and expressive spirit of Spanish culture, captivating the audience.

Spectators warmly appreciated the artists with enthusiastic applause.

headline: High-level huddle on K-P agrees to scale up IBOs
description: High-level huddle on K-P agrees to scale up IBOs
author: Khalid Mahmood
article_text:
The civil-military leadership on Tuesday agreed to expand intelligence-based operations (IBOs) against terrorists in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and strengthen coordination between federal and provincial institutions during a high-level meeting chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The meeting, attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, federal ministers, governors and senior officials, reviewed the province's security, political and administrative situation.

The participants reviewed the overall national and internal security situation, with particular focus on law and order in K-P, developments following the imposition of governor's rule and emergency, and progress on ongoing counterterrorism operations and IBOs.

Sources said the meeting decided to broaden the scope of IBOs to eliminate terrorism and make coordination between federal and provincial institutions more effective. Participants agreed that a coordinated approach was essential to address the security challenges facing the province.

The prime minister directed the relevant institutions to work under a coordinated strategy to restore law and order, stressing the need for improved cooperation among government departments to ensure effective implementation of decisions.

The meeting was briefed on earlier decisions concerning K-P, progress in their implementation and the results achieved. Governor Kundi informed participants about measures taken across various sectors of the province and the performance of the Area Development Council (ARDC).

The federal government imposed governor's rule and a state of emergency in K-P on October 11 to rein in terrorism and improve governance in the province. On October 22, Prime Minister Shehbaz chaired an Apex Committee meeting and announced Rs160 billion worth of development projects for the province.

The Rs160 billion development package also came under review at Tuesday's meeting. The package focuses on advancing development projects, strengthening security arrangements and undertaking public welfare initiatives in the province.

According to sources, participants also took stock of the country's broader political situation, while matters relating to possible legislation in the coming days were also discussed.

Since the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, the country has witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators, with terrorist attacks declining by 37% compared with September, according to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

However, the institute warned in a report last week that certain incidents remained a cause for concern. In the latest such incident, two policemen were martyred in Mohmand district when gunmen targeted police personnel guarding a polio vaccination team.

A constable and an alleged terrorist were injured in an exchange of fire in the Tamanzai area, within the jurisdiction of Pindiali police station, during an anti-polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Raza Muhammad Khan said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack, expressing "profound grief and sorrow" over the martyrdom of the policemen and paying tribute to their "dedication, bravery and national services".

In a post on X, the president said targeting personnel performing their duties during the anti-polio campaign "to protect children" was "extremely regrettable and condemnable". "Police personnel deployed to protect polio teams are performing a national duty; their sacrifices will not be forgotten," President Zardari said.

In a separate statement, the prime minister paid tribute to the policemen martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and extended condolences to their bereaved families. "Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation," the prime minister said.

Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of Constables Zahoor Khan and Arabi Khan were offered at Police Lines Ghalanai with full official honours. A large number of civil, military and police officials, along with relatives of the deceased, attended the funeral.

On the occasion, DPO Raza Khan, 114 Brigade Commander Brigadier Iftikhar Mehboob, Mohmand Rifles Commandant Colonel Imran Khalid and Deputy Commissioner Mohmand (retd) Captain Bilal Shahid Rao laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred constables to pay tribute to their sacrifice.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a salute to the fallen personnel. Following the funeral prayers, participants prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased, and patience and fortitude for their bereaved families.

(WITH INPUTS FROM OUR PESHAWAR CORRESPONDENT)

RAWALPINDI:

The civil-military leadership on Tuesday agreed to expand intelligence-based operations (IBOs) against terrorists in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and strengthen coordination between federal and provincial institutions during a high-level meeting chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The meeting, attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, federal ministers, governors and senior officials, reviewed the province's security, political and administrative situation.

The participants reviewed the overall national and internal security situation, with particular focus on law and order in K-P, developments following the imposition of governor's rule and emergency, and progress on ongoing counterterrorism operations and IBOs.

Sources said the meeting decided to broaden the scope of IBOs to eliminate terrorism and make coordination between federal and provincial institutions more effective. Participants agreed that a coordinated approach was essential to address the security challenges facing the province.

The prime minister directed the relevant institutions to work under a coordinated strategy to restore law and order, stressing the need for improved cooperation among government departments to ensure effective implementation of decisions.

The meeting was briefed on earlier decisions concerning K-P, progress in their implementation and the results achieved. Governor Kundi informed participants about measures taken across various sectors of the province and the performance of the Area Development Council (ARDC).

The federal government imposed governor's rule and a state of emergency in K-P on October 11 to rein in terrorism and improve governance in the province. On October 22, Prime Minister Shehbaz chaired an Apex Committee meeting and announced Rs160 billion worth of development projects for the province.

The Rs160 billion development package also came under review at Tuesday's meeting. The package focuses on advancing development projects, strengthening security arrangements and undertaking public welfare initiatives in the province.

According to sources, participants also took stock of the country's broader political situation, while matters relating to possible legislation in the coming days were also discussed.

Since the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, the country has witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators, with terrorist attacks declining by 37% compared with September, according to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

However, the institute warned in a report last week that certain incidents remained a cause for concern. In the latest such incident, two policemen were martyred in Mohmand district when gunmen targeted police personnel guarding a polio vaccination team.

A constable and an alleged terrorist were injured in an exchange of fire in the Tamanzai area, within the jurisdiction of Pindiali police station, during an anti-polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Raza Muhammad Khan said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack, expressing "profound grief and sorrow" over the martyrdom of the policemen and paying tribute to their "dedication, bravery and national services".

In a post on X, the president said targeting personnel performing their duties during the anti-polio campaign "to protect children" was "extremely regrettable and condemnable". "Police personnel deployed to protect polio teams are performing a national duty; their sacrifices will not be forgotten," President Zardari said.

In a separate statement, the prime minister paid tribute to the policemen martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and extended condolences to their bereaved families. "Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation," the prime minister said.

Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of Constables Zahoor Khan and Arabi Khan were offered at Police Lines Ghalanai with full official honours. A large number of civil, military and police officials, along with relatives of the deceased, attended the funeral.

On the occasion, DPO Raza Khan, 114 Brigade Commander Brigadier Iftikhar Mehboob, Mohmand Rifles Commandant Colonel Imran Khalid and Deputy Commissioner Mohmand (retd) Captain Bilal Shahid Rao laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred constables to pay tribute to their sacrifice.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a salute to the fallen personnel. Following the funeral prayers, participants prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased, and patience and fortitude for their bereaved families.

In a separate statement, the prime minister paid tribute to the policemen martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and extended condolences to their bereaved families. "Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation," the prime minister said.

Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of Constables Zahoor Khan and Arabi Khan were offered at Police Lines Ghalanai with full official honours. A large number of civil, military and police officials, along with relatives of the deceased, attended the funeral.

On the occasion, DPO Raza Khan, 114 Brigade Commander Brigadier Iftikhar Mehboob, Mohmand Rifles Commandant Colonel Imran Khalid and Deputy Commissioner Mohmand (retd) Captain Bilal Shahid Rao laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred constables to pay tribute to their sacrifice.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a salute to the fallen personnel. Following the funeral prayers, participants prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased, and patience and fortitude for their bereaved families.

headline: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists eliminated in Balochistan
description: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists eliminated in Balochistan
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A soldier was martyred while security forces killed 17 terrorists in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan's Kachhi and Kharan districts, the military's media wing said on Tuesday.

"On November 1, 2026, security forces conducted two intelligence-based operations in Kachhi and Kharan districts of Balochistan on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxies, Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij, neutralising 17 Indian-sponsored terrorists," the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.

The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan, accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through these outfits. Fitna al-Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

The first operation was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district, where security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock, killing 10 of them. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered.

In the second operation in Kharan district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout. Following an intense exchange of fire, seven TTP members were killed, the ISPR said, adding that weapons and ammunition were also recovered.

"Meanwhile, during the intense fire exchange, Sepoy Hikmatullah, having fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom," the statement said.

Sanitisation operations were underway to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area, it added.

The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the security forces for killing the 17 terrorists in the two operations.

In a statement, the president commended security forces for foiling the attempt to block a road in Kachhi district, saying their timely and effective action had thwarted the militants' designs.

He also lauded the successful operation in Kharan district and expressed grief over the martyrdom of Sepoy Hikmatullah.

Zardari said the soldier's sacrifice for the defence, peace and security of the country would always be remembered.

The president said operations under Azm-e-Istehkam would continue until terrorism sponsored and supported by foreign elements was eliminated.

He also praised the continued efforts and sacrifices of security forces and law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism, describing them as a source of pride.

Separately, the premier hailed the security forces for successful IBOs against terrorists.

He paid tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah, prayed for the elevation of his ranks and offered condolences to his family.

The prime minister noted that the security forces were achieving significant successes against terrorism under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam.

He reiterated the government's resolve to eliminate terrorism from the country in all its forms.

Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.

Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.

Over the past few years, Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks, with militants frequently targeting convoys, abducting security personnel and civilians, and attacking security and civilian installations.

However, attacks declined noticeably in October, offering a temporary respite after two consecutive months of rising violence. A sharp increase in kidnappings, particularly in Balochistan, nevertheless continued to pose a serious security challenge.

According to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), Balochistan registered one of the sharpest improvements in its security indicators, with terrorist attacks falling by 46 per cent, from 132 in September to 71 in October.

Overall, 143 terrorist attacks were recorded across the country during October, compared with 226 in September.

The reduction was accompanied by a 57 per cent fall in fatalities and a 71 per cent decline in injuries, while suicide attacks also registered a substantial decrease.

PICSS data showed that the attacks claimed 111 lives in October, compared with 260 in September. The number of people injured dropped from 242 to 69, indicating a 71 per cent reduction.

The number of suicide attacks was jointly the lowest recorded during the same period. However, the 169 terrorists killed also represented the lowest monthly figure in the preceding 12 months, reflecting a decline in terrorist fatalities, the report noted.

headline: Govt cuts fuel prices, unveils LPG reforms
description: Govt cuts fuel prices, unveils LPG reforms
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for Wednesday (today), while announcing sweeping reforms to open the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector to competition, improve supply and curb profiteering.

According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the new price of petrol is Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52 per litre.

Addressing a press conference alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the government to provide maximum relief to low-income groups.

"The government will pass on any reduction in international petroleum prices to consumers," he said. "Pakistan meets around 70% of its fuel requirements through imports and that companies importing petroleum products will be required to publish their prices and cost details online to ensure transparency."

A major focus of the briefing was the LPG sector, where the government plans to abolish the existing quota-based distribution mechanism, introduce competitive auctions and encourage public and private companies to import the commodity at competitive prices.

The minister said domestic LPG production stood at around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes daily, while a substantial portion of demand had traditionally been met through imports from the western border. Supply disruptions had allowed some market players to sell the commodity for Rs700 to Rs800 per kilogramme.

Under the proposed reforms, locally produced LPG will be auctioned in transparent lots of five to 10 tonnes among companies licensed by Ogra. The auction results will be made public, with the process monitored by the petroleum secretary and Ogra chairman.

State-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil, Sui Southern Gas Company and Pakistan LNG Limited, have been directed to arrange bulk supplies through government-to-government and business-to-business agreements. Private companies will also be encouraged to import LPG.

Malik said importers would disclose monthly cost components, including Saudi Aramco's contract price, premiums, freight charges and other expenses, on their websites. The government also plans to establish price stabilisation and vulnerable consumers' protection funds to help deserving households obtain LPG at subsidised rates.

He said the government would ensure that the 10% LPG quota allocated for remote and hard-to-reach areas was properly utilised, with state-owned companies responsible for procuring and distributing the allocated supplies.

The minister added that the Competition Commission had been asked to act against cartelisation and anti-competitive practices, while Ogra would strengthen licensing and audit mechanisms to prevent hoarding and profiteering.

On international pricing, Malik said Saudi Aramco's contract price had risen from $540 per tonne in March to $756 per tonne, prompting a corresponding revision in domestic LPG prices. He said the prevailing spot-market price, after accounting for associated costs, was estimated at Rs450 to Rs500 per kilogramme.

Malik also assured consumers that the government would make every effort to meet winter gas demand, particularly during meal times. He said domestic demand was expected to rise by 400 to 500 million cubic feet per day and that alternative arrangements for imported liquefied natural gas would be made to meet requirements.

Information Minister Tarar said the government had abolished the LPG monopoly and discretionary quota system to introduce transparency and competition. He added that the prime minister had provided Rs130 billion in subsidies to consumers and prioritised public relief during the energy crisis.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for Wednesday (today), while announcing sweeping reforms to open the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector to competition, improve supply and curb profiteering.

According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the new price of petrol is Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52 per litre.

Addressing a press conference alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the government to provide maximum relief to low-income groups.

"The government will pass on any reduction in international petroleum prices to consumers," he said. "Pakistan meets around 70% of its fuel requirements through imports and that companies importing petroleum products will be required to publish their prices and cost details online to ensure transparency."

A major focus of the briefing was the LPG sector, where the government plans to abolish the existing quota-based distribution mechanism, introduce competitive auctions and encourage public and private companies to import the commodity at competitive prices.

The minister said domestic LPG production stood at around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes daily, while a substantial portion of demand had traditionally been met through imports from the western border. Supply disruptions had allowed some market players to sell the commodity for Rs700 to Rs800 per kilogramme.

Under the proposed reforms, locally produced LPG will be auctioned in transparent lots of five to 10 tonnes among companies licensed by Ogra. The auction results will be made public, with the process monitored by the petroleum secretary and Ogra chairman.

State-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil, Sui Southern Gas Company and Pakistan LNG Limited, have been directed to arrange bulk supplies through government-to-government and business-to-business agreements. Private companies will also be encouraged to import LPG.

Malik said importers would disclose monthly cost components, including Saudi Aramco's contract price, premiums, freight charges and other expenses, on their websites. The government also plans to establish price stabilisation and vulnerable consumers' protection funds to help deserving households obtain LPG at subsidised rates.

He said the government would ensure that the 10% LPG quota allocated for remote and hard-to-reach areas was properly utilised, with state-owned companies responsible for procuring and distributing the allocated supplies.

The minister added that the Competition Commission had been asked to act against cartelisation and anti-competitive practices, while Ogra would strengthen licensing and audit mechanisms to prevent hoarding and profiteering.

On international pricing, Malik said Saudi Aramco's contract price had risen from $540 per tonne in March to $756 per tonne, prompting a corresponding revision in domestic LPG prices. He said the prevailing spot-market price, after accounting for associated costs, was estimated at Rs450 to Rs500 per kilogramme.

Malik also assured consumers that the government would make every effort to meet winter gas demand, particularly during meal times. He said domestic demand was expected to rise by 400 to 500 million cubic feet per day and that alternative arrangements for imported liquefied natural gas would be made to meet requirements.

Information Minister Tarar said the government had abolished the LPG monopoly and discretionary quota system to introduce transparency and competition. He added that the prime minister had provided Rs130 billion in subsidies to consumers and prioritised public relief during the energy crisis.

The government has also announced that oil refineries will bear a cumulative burden of Rs15 billion over 30 days under a revised petrol pricing mechanism, allowing a reduction of Rs14.71 per litre at the consumer end.

Malik said the new LPG arrangements were expected to become fully operational before winter, adding that the government aimed to establish a competitive market with transparent pricing and more reliable supplies.

headline: Dems eye gains as US votes in midterms
description: Dems eye gains as US votes in midterms
author: agencies
article_text:
Americans voted on Tuesday in midterm elections widely seen as a referendum on President Donald Trump's second term, with Democrats favoured to regain control of the House of Representatives while the battle for the Senate remained uncertain.

All 435 seats in the House and 35 of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested, with Democrats needing a net gain of three House seats and four Senate seats to take control of both chambers. Opinion polls and nonpartisan analysts have given Democrats an edge in the House.

The Senate contest remains closely fought across several states, including Republican strongholds. The Senate contest has drawn particular attention in Michigan, where progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is challenging Republican Mike Rogers.

The race has also become a test of whether attacks centred on El-Sayed's identity and criticism of Israel will influence voters in the battleground state. Other closely watched Senate contests include Texas, Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Ohio, where Democrats are attempting to make gains in traditionally Republican states.

In Texas, Democrat James Talarico is challenging Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, while former congresswoman Mary Peltola is seeking to unseat Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska.

Voting equipment problems were reported in several parts of the country, including Georgia, Iowa, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma and Wisconsin, potentially causing local delays. In New York's Westchester County, ballot scanners malfunctioned, prompting officials to use emergency procedures and assure voters that all ballots would be counted.

The US Justice Department said it was deploying 1,000 election monitors and observers across all 50 states, describing it as the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history. Democrats criticised the move as potentially intimidating voters.

Republicans currently hold a 53-47 Senate majority, but the battlefield has extended into once reliably conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Democrats must also defend competitive seats. Decision Desk HQ's final forecast projected 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Concerns also emerged over whether Republicans would accept the results if they lost control of Congress. Trump has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims of widespread election fraud, while his administration pursued legal challenges involving ballot certification in Alaska and mail-in ballots in California.

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating high engagement. The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, and mega-rich Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican efforts.

President Donald Trump's name was not on the ballot in Tuesday's US midterm elections, but the results could determine how much political control he retains during the remaining two years of his presidency.

Midterm elections are a routine feature of American democracy, but this particular contest has acquired greater significance because of what is at stake. The war with Iran, its economic consequences, rising concerns over the cost of living and questions about Trump's handling of foreign policy have all become part of the political debate.

For countries outside the United States, including Pakistan, Trump's presidency is often assessed through the prism of foreign policy. American voters, however, have a different set of priorities. Their decisions are more likely to be shaped by the price of petrol, food, housing, employment and the broader state of the economy than by Washington's diplomatic standing abroad.

Yet the domestic and international dimensions of this election are increasingly intertwined. The consequences of the vote could extend well beyond Washington, particularly to a region already unsettled by the confrontation between the United States and Iran.

American political history offers little comfort to a president's party heading into midterm elections. Since 1934, the party controlling the White House has increased its representation in the House of Representatives on only three occasions: 1934, 1998 and 2002.

In 1934, Franklin D Roosevelt's Democrats gained seats amid public support for his New Deal programme. In 1998, Bill Clinton's Democrats made gains despite the impeachment controversy surrounding his presidency, as Republican efforts to remove him proved unpopular with sections of the electorate. In 2002, George W Bush's Republicans gained seats following the September 11 attacks, benefiting from a wave of national unity and support for his leadership.

The pattern is revealing. Midterm elections are generally a referendum on the incumbent president, and the opposition party usually benefits. The president's party often loses seats because voters use the midterms to express dissatisfaction with the administration without having to wait for the next presidential election.

The distinction between the two chambers is important. All 435 House seats are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms and only approximately one-third of the Senate faces voters in each midterm.

Republicans entered this election with narrow majorities in both chambers: 218-214 in the House, with two vacancies, and 53-47 in the Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in the House and four in the Senate to secure control of the latter.

The political indicators heading into election day suggested that Republicans were more vulnerable in the House, while the Senate contest remained considerably more difficult for Democrats.

The emerging results will therefore be watched not simply for which party wins individual constituencies but for what they reveal about the country's political mood and the extent of Trump's remaining political capital.

If Republicans manage to retain both chambers, Trump will claim a political victory and argue that voters have endorsed his domestic and foreign policy agenda.

Such an outcome would give him greater room to pursue his legislative priorities, secure funding for administration programmes and advance presidential appointments. It would also reduce the prospect of sustained congressional investigations into his administration.

More importantly, a Republican-controlled Congress would give Trump greater political flexibility in dealing with Iran. He would face fewer institutional obstacles in seeking additional defence funding and maintaining military pressure on Tehran.

But retaining Congress would not necessarily mean an immediate return to war.

Trump has repeatedly presented himself as a president who can end wars rather than become entangled in prolonged military engagements. A conflict that continues to push up petrol prices, disrupt global trade and undermine consumer confidence would contradict the economic message he has offered American voters.

He could instead use military pressure to extract concessions from Tehran and present a negotiated settlement as a victory for his administration.

A Democratic takeover of the House would fundamentally change the political environment in Washington.

Democrats would gain control of congressional committees, subpoena powers and the ability to launch investigations into the administration's handling of the Iran war. They could demand explanations over military decisions, scrutinise the financial and human costs of the conflict and challenge the intelligence assessments used to justify military action.

If Democrats also capture the Senate, the consequences would be more significant. They could block or delay presidential appointments and make it harder for Trump to advance his broader agenda.

However, there is an important constitutional distinction. Losing Congress does not automatically strip a US president of his authority to order military action. Trump remains commander-in-chief and retains substantial powers over foreign policy and national security.

Congress, meanwhile, controls federal appropriations and has the constitutional authority to declare war. A Democratic-controlled Congress could therefore raise the political and financial cost of a renewed conflict without necessarily being able to prevent an initial military operation.

There is also a potentially dangerous dimension to this scenario. A president facing domestic political setbacks could be tempted to demonstrate strength abroad. It would be premature to assume that an electoral defeat would automatically make Trump more restrained.

Nevertheless, a major military escalation against Iran would carry enormous political and economic risks, potentially giving Democrats further ammunition against the administration.

For Islamabad, the most consequential aspect of the American midterms is not necessarily which party controls Congress. It is whether Trump, after the election, will return to a full-scale military confrontation with Iran or pursue a diplomatic settlement.

The recent military developments have underlined the contradiction at the heart of Washington's Iran policy. Even as diplomatic channels remain open, military pressure continues and the possibility of another round of strikes cannot be ruled out.

The question is whether the election outcome will change Trump's calculation.

If Republicans retain Congress, Trump could interpret the result as an endorsement of his approach and feel more confident about maintaining pressure on Iran. But the economic consequences of another war could still make diplomacy the more attractive option.

If Democrats capture the House, the White House will face greater scrutiny over the objectives, duration and financial costs of military operations. A Democratic majority could make it politically more difficult to sustain a prolonged campaign, although it would not necessarily prevent limited strikes.

The broader calculation will depend on Iran's response, the state of negotiations, the security of American forces and the economic costs of continued confrontation.

For Pakistan, the implications are immediate. Any renewed American military campaign could destabilise an already fragile regional environment, complicate border security and put additional pressure on the country's economic recovery.

The energy dimension is particularly important. Pakistan remains vulnerable to international oil and gas price fluctuations. Any prolonged disruption in the Strait of Hormuz would have serious implications for global energy supplies, shipping costs and the country's import bill.

The recent attack on a Pakistani LNG-bound vessel has already demonstrated how directly the confrontation can affect Pakistan's economic interests. A further escalation could complicate energy procurement and increase the cost of securing supplies.

There is also a diplomatic challenge. Pakistan has sought to maintain working relations with Washington, Tehran and the Gulf countries while avoiding entanglement in the conflict. Another war would make that balancing act considerably more difficult.

Ultimately, the midterm elections will offer an indication of how much political capital Trump retains, but they will not necessarily dictate the direction of American foreign policy.

A Republican victory would strengthen his hand, while a Democratic takeover of one or both chambers would constrain his domestic agenda and subject his administration to greater scrutiny.

But the presidency carries substantial independent powers in national security and foreign affairs. The outcome of the congressional elections will not transfer control of the American military to the opposition.

For Trump, the challenge will be to demonstrate that he can deliver economic relief at home while managing an increasingly complicated international environment. A negotiated settlement with Iran would allow him to claim that his policy of pressure has worked. A return to war, on the other hand, could undermine the very economic message on which Republicans have fought this election.

For Pakistan and the wider region, the most important signal may therefore not come from the final electoral tally but from what Trump does in the days and weeks that follow.

A Republican victory would strengthen his hand, while a Democratic takeover of one or both chambers would constrain his domestic agenda and subject his administration to greater scrutiny.

But the presidency carries substantial independent powers in national security and foreign affairs. The outcome of the congressional elections will not transfer control of the American military to the opposition.

For Trump, the challenge will be to demonstrate that he can deliver economic relief at home while managing an increasingly complicated international environment. A negotiated settlement with Iran would allow him to claim that his policy of pressure has worked. A return to war, on the other hand, could undermine the very economic message on which Republicans have fought this election.

For Pakistan and the wider region, the most important signal may therefore not come from the final electoral tally but from what Trump does in the days and weeks that follow.

headline: Maryam sues Salik over defamation
description: CM Punjab says, 'If you have proof, bring it forward; if not, I will drag you to court'
author: Rameez Khan
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain, an ARY News anchor and the private television channel's chairman, over allegations of widespread corruption in the province, demanding an unconditional apology, retraction of the statements, and damages.

However, Salik Hussain, who belongs to a smaller allied party in the ruling coalition, has stood by his allegations, insisting that corruption was taking place in Punjab.

He has also rejected the suggestion that his remarks were prompted by the appointment of a deputy commissioner on merit, maintaining that the interview had been recorded three weeks earlier.

"If you have proof, bring it forward; if not, I will drag you to court," Maryam said during a laptop distribution ceremony, reiterating the allegation made a day earlier by Information Minister Azma Bukhari that the federal minister had effectively issued a charge sheet against the provincial government out of displeasure over the appointment of a deputy commissioner on merit.

A day earlier, Salik had acknowledged that he had indeed asked the government to appoint a deputy commissioner whose capabilities were better suited to executing mega projects.

The legal notice, issued through Additional Advocate General Punjab Chaudhry Muhammad Nawaz, gives the recipients - Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain, ARY News anchor Naeem Ashraf Butt and ARY Chairman Muhammad Iqbal - seven days to withdraw the allegations, issue an unconditional apology and pay Rs5 billion in damages over what it describes as defamatory statements that have harmed the chief minister's reputation.

The notice concerns an interview with Salik Hussain broadcast on ARY News on November 2 and subsequently uploaded to the channel's official YouTube platform.

During the interview, the federal minister reportedly said: "I have no evidence, but I hear stories about corruption in Punjab every day." He also remarked that "cupboards are filled with files on corruption cases in Punjab".

The notice argues that the minister levelled sweeping allegations despite admitting that he had no evidence to substantiate them. It questions the factual basis of his remarks, asking which departments, officials, projects or transactions he was referring to and whether any official inquiries, investigations or audit reports supported his claims.

It also holds the interviewer responsible, alleging that his introductory and leading remarks facilitated the propagation of unverified allegations without seeking supporting evidence or clarification from the minister.

The notice further names ARY Chairman Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the interview, arguing that those involved in disseminating the statements also bear responsibility for their publication.

According to the notice, the remarks portrayed corruption as widespread across Punjab's administrative machinery and undermined public confidence in the provincial government headed by Maryam Nawaz.

Besides demanding Rs5 billion in damages, the chief minister has sought an unequivocal retraction of the statements, an unconditional apology and a clarification on the same media platforms, with prominence equivalent to that given to the original allegations.

The recipients have also been asked to remove or suitably correct the allegedly defamatory portions of the interview and related clips, while preserving the original recording, unedited footage, editorial notes and other relevant publication records.

The notice warns that failure to comply within seven days would lead to legal proceedings under the Punjab Defamation Act, 2024, before the competent forum.

Earlier, announcing her decision to issue the defamation notice, Maryam said she would not tolerate false allegations. She also challenged the federal minister to leave the government if he believed corruption was so widespread in Punjab.

She maintained that the actual issue was the appointment of a deputy commissioner in Gujrat rather than any development project.

She said she did not entertain requests or recommendations in the appointment of deputy commissioners, commissioners and regional police officers, insisting that all such appointments were made strictly on merit. Those appointed through influence, she added, ended up harming the country.

Rejecting the federal minister's assessment of Chaudhry Pervaiz Elahi as the best chief minister, Maryam said that when she assumed office, Gujrat resembled a village, with rainfall submerging the entire city and forcing people to travel not in cars but on trolleys.

Referring to her own visit to the city, she said she had undertaken development projects worth billions of rupees and could be held accountable for even a penny's worth of corruption.

It is pertinent to mention that Salik Hussain's brother, Chaudhry Shafay Hussain, is also part of the provincial government and serves directly under Maryam Nawaz as Punjab's minister for industries, commerce and investment.

Responding to the allegations against him, Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain said he had merely answered the interviewer's questions honestly, reiterating his position that corruption existed in Punjab.

However, he sidestepped questions about whether he possessed any evidence to support his allegations or whether he should leave the government if corruption was indeed taking place in the province.

Taking an indirect swipe at Maryam Nawaz, he said people holding powerful positions should remain humble.

"May Almighty save people from pride and arrogance," he added.

headline: US will stop $4b in aid to Israel: Trump
description: US will stop $4b in aid to Israel: Trump
author: Reuters
article_text:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after this year, but will still sell weapons to its close Middle East ally.

In a surprise announcement as US voters headed to the polls for midterm elections that will decide who controls Congress, Trump cast the move as partly meant to take away a "bad talking point" he said left-wing Democrats had used against his fellow Republicans over support for military assistance to Israel.

Trump did not provide details or explain how the funding would be stopped at the end of the year, given that the Memorandum of Understanding that provides $3.8 billion in US military aid to Israel each year does not expire until September 2028.

But some analysts suggested Trump's declaration was an Election Day ploy.

Conversations have been under way on how Washington's assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date, and Netanyahu had already said he expects US aid to wind down over time.

Trump, however, appeared to signal that his mind was made up about what would mark a significant shift in US-Israel relations, even as the two countries remain in conflict with Iran more than eight months after jointly attacking the Islamic Republic.

Trump told Fox News' "Fox & Friends" program that Israel no longer needed the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel to criticize Republicans. Opinion polls show that the US public's overall support for Israel has declined mostly due to the Gaza war.

"Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping," Trump said. "We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it," he said.

It was unclear why Trump chose to announce on Tuesday a deal he said he made months ago.

Israel's future leadership is uncertain after an October 27 election in which Netanyahu - who has allied himself tightly to US Republicans - lost his governing majority but denied his opponents a clear path to unseat him. The election results paved the way for what are expected to be protracted negotiations over a new government.

headline: Binance hackers used fake job interview in $6.3b attack
description: Binance hackers used fake job interview in $6.3b attack
author: Reuters
article_text:
Hackers used a bogus job interview and software hidden in an advertisement to compromise the computers of two Binance software engineers before using a third's computer to drain $6.3 billion worth of crypto in last week's record heist, the exchange said on Tuesday.

In its initial report on how hackers pulled off what could be the largest-ever financial theft, Binance detailed a multi-stage hacking endeavour that began in June and set off a series of security breaches culminating in the theft on Thursday.

Even as Binance scrambled to lock down its system and freeze withdrawals after detecting the attack late on Thursday, the hackers were still making off with crypto from the exchange nearly four hours after the first theft, Binance said.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group, a claim North Korea has rejected. Binance has said it is repaying all customers whose funds were stolen.

The attack has raised questions about how hackers breached the world's largest crypto exchange after years of North Korea-linked attacks, which have grown in ambition and frequency, and renewed questions about the vulnerability of digital assets to cybercrime.

Cybersecurity experts and government officials have for years warned about North Korean and other hackers using phony job interviews to target employees at companies of interest, said Michael Barnhart, a researcher with cybersecurity firm DTEX. Fake job interviews are a well-known hacking technique.

Binance said it had detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyberthreats in 2026. That shows Binance is "just getting barraged," Barnhart said.
