Hackers used a bogus job interview and software hidden in an advertisement to compromise the computers of two Binance software engineers before using a third's computer to drain $6.3 billion worth of crypto in last week's record heist, the exchange said on Tuesday.

In its initial report on how hackers pulled off what could be the largest-ever financial theft, Binance detailed a multi-stage hacking endeavour that began in June and set off a series of security breaches culminating in the theft on Thursday.

Even as Binance scrambled to lock down its system and freeze withdrawals after detecting the attack late on Thursday, the hackers were still making off with crypto from the exchange nearly four hours after the first theft, Binance said.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group, a claim North Korea has rejected. Binance has said it is repaying all customers whose funds were stolen.

The attack has raised questions about how hackers breached the world's largest crypto exchange after years of North Korea-linked attacks, which have grown in ambition and frequency, and renewed questions about the vulnerability of digital assets to cybercrime.

Cybersecurity experts and government officials have for years warned about North Korean and other hackers using phony job interviews to target employees at companies of interest, said Michael Barnhart, a researcher with cybersecurity firm DTEX. Fake job interviews are a well-known hacking technique.

Binance said it had detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyberthreats in 2026. That shows Binance is "just getting barraged," Barnhart said.

headline: Eisenkot eyes end to Netanyahu era
description: Eisenkot eyes end to Netanyahu era
author: News Desk
article_text:
After a meeting on Tuesday with the heads of parties in his bloc, Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot said the days of Netanyahu's government were numbered.

He said that starting Tuesday, Netanyahu is "a transitional prime minister, backed only by 46 Knesset members".

This remark implies that the 7-member United Torah Judaism party, which was part of the outgoing government until last year and is normally counted as part of the pro-Netanyahu bloc despite recently voicing public doubt about that, is indeed not a bloc member, potentially hinting at future cooperation with the ultra-Orthodox party. Some members of Eisenkot's bloc staunchly oppose collaborating with the Haredi parties, however.

He also laid out immediate legislative plans and implies that a party often counted as part of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu-led bloc is no longer aligned with him.

Calling the meeting with Naftali Bennett, Avigdor Liberman and Yair Golan as "good and important," Eisenkot says in a video statement that the bloc leaders are "coordinated and prepared for the coming days."

headline: Despite frantic efforts, Iran, US still far apart on deal
description: Despite frantic efforts, Iran, US still far apart on deal
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, while mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to bridge differences and avert a renewed escalation after the US midterm elections.

Overnight, the United States carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday renewed threats of possible military action, telling Fox News Channel: "I'm not looking to ... kill lots of people. If we have to, we'll have to." Qatar has intensified mediation efforts amid fears the conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February could flare up again after Tuesday's midterms.

"Mediators are working

hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, speaking on condition of anonymity. Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran

on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal

discussed over the past eight days.

"Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to Iranian demands including waiving oil sanctions, ending the US naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian funds.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, later said the US response to Iranian demands "was not convincing", adding that Washington "must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them".

"Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he wrote on X.

'WE CANNOT LOSE HOPE'

On Monday, Trump raised doubts about whether he would follow through on a threatened resumption of military strikes against Iran and said a deal with Tehran could happen.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said both the United States and Iran were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had returned to Doha, talks were continuing.

"There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that Qatar remained hopeful a deal could still be reached to pave the way for future negotiations.

"If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations.. and as a mediator, we cannot lose hope," he said. An official briefed on the talks said feedback from Washington and Tehran was expected within the next 36 hours.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters later on Tuesday that there is no deadline for exchanging messages with Washington through mediators or reviewing responses.

The Houthis on Tuesday claimed to have struck an airport and an airbase in Saudi Arabia's Abha and Khamis Mushait areas.

In a post on X, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed that the group had "carried out two military operations", further adding that the "first operation targeted Abha International Airport with a drone, and the strike was precise, leading to the disruption of air traffic at the airport".

headline: 33 killed in Ukraine village
description: 33 killed in Ukraine village
author: Reuters
article_text:
.

At least 33 people were killed when Russian forces bombed a school being used as an aid distribution point in a village near the front line in Ukraine's southeastern region of Zaporizhzhia on Monday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

About 50 people are believed to still be buried under the rubble following the attack in the village of Komyshuvakha, Zelenskiy told a press conference in Berlin with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday.

Zelenskiy had previously said that Russian forces initially dropped aerial bombs on the school, which was being used as a shelter and for distributing humanitarian assistance every Monday.

There were no classes at the school, he said, as the village, lying southeast of the region's main city, also called Zaporizhzhia, was too close to the front line in the 4-1/2-year-old war.

"The Russians struck first just as people were arriving – a few aerial bombs," he said. "Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on the shelter. A vile terrorist strike."

About 50 people are believed to still be buried under the rubble following the attack in the village of Komyshuvakha, Zelenskiy told a press conference in Berlin with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday.

Zelenskiy had previously said that Russian forces initially dropped aerial bombs on the school, which was being used as a shelter and for distributing humanitarian assistance every Monday.

There were no classes at the school, he said, as the village, lying southeast of the region's main city, also called Zaporizhzhia, was too close to the front line in the 4-1/2-year-old war.

"The Russians struck first just as people were arriving – a few aerial bombs," he said. "Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on the shelter. A vile terrorist strike."

headline: IHC to indict CDA official in contempt case
description: IHC to indict CDA official in contempt case
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
Islamabad High Court (IHC) Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar has rejected an unconditional apology offered by Capital Development Authority (CDA) Member Estate Zaman Wattoo over allegedly misleading the court and decided to frame contempt of court charges against him on November 12.

The court directed the prosecutor to appear at the next hearing after preparing the case.

During the proceedings, Chief Justice Dogar remarked that no one should assume that the court was acting as anyone's "B team". He observed that the official's conduct amounted to bulldozing a judicial order and showed a lack of seriousness towards the dignity and respect of the courts.

The chief justice said there appeared to be a perception that ordinary litigants could be made to wait for hours, while people wearing suits and ties could be heard within 10 minutes.

He observed that when a case was fixed before the chief justice's court, it was a senior court and the concerned parties were required to remain present when the matter was called and proceedings commenced.

"I have no personal grudge against anyone," the chief justice remarked, adding that when the order in question was being passed, the official had claimed that he was unwell but appeared before another court on the same day.

The chief justice said the official had been summoned in person that day but had preferred to appear before another court instead of seeking time from the IHC first.

"You have served for 60 years. Do you not know which court is senior?" he asked, observing that the official should have appeared before the IHC and requested an adjournment rather than choosing to attend another court.

At this stage, Zaman Wattoo's counsel, Kashif Ali Malik, offered an unconditional apology. However, the chief justice said the question of an apology would be considered later.

CDA counsel Nazir Jawad requested the court to grant some time, assuring it that he would appear fully prepared at the next hearing. Zaman Wattoo also personally apologised, saying that he respected the court and could never even think of committing contempt.

The chief justice, however, observed that this was not merely a matter of an apology but a clear case of contempt of court.

Prosecutor Adnan Ali informed the court that the official had not tendered an apology in his written response. He said contempt proceedings in such cases were initiated through the framing of charges.

headline: Man goes missing after being barred from flight
description: Man goes missing after being barred from flight
author: Saleh Mughal
article_text:
A passenger has reportedly gone missing from the New Islamabad International Airport. Official sources said the missing passenger had been stopped by airport staff after his name was found on the Passenger Control List (PCL).

The staff had reportedly asked him to wait in the airport's briefing area, from where he appeared to have gone missing. The Airport Police have registered a case of kidnapping and initiated an investigation.

According to the police, the complainant, Muhammad Ikram, who hails from Peshawar, stated that on September 5, 2026, he went to the Islamabad Airport to drop off his elder brother, Muhammad Shah Jahan and his mother, Roshan Bibi, who were travelling to the United States. He said his mother and brother had proceeded inside the airport for boarding, while he waited outside until their flight departed. He added that shortly thereafter, his brother called to inform him that he had been stopped from boarding the plane because his name was on the Passenger Control List (PCL). Ikram stated that his mother returned to him because she could not travel on her own and they both waited for his brother.

He said that they kept waiting for him until 9am and when he still did not return, they visited the FIA Islamabad Zone office in Sector G-6 to inquire about his whereabouts.

headline: Hina Javed's family rejects fresh police probe
description: Hina Javed's family rejects fresh police probe
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
The family of Hina Javed, who was murdered, has rejected the police decision to reopen the investigation into her killing and reiterated its demand for the formation of a judicial commission, saying there was little point in having subordinate officers reinvestigate the case after raising serious concerns over the findings of a high-level inquiry committee.

The victim's family has also formally conveyed its reservations about the fresh investigation to the National Assembly's Standing Committee on Interior.

According to the family, SSP Investigation Saifullah contacted them and asked them to visit his office to sign an application seeking the transfer of the investigation to another district. However, after reading the application, the family refused to endorse the move.

The family said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had advised them to submit an application for transferring the investigation to police in another district. However, it pointed out that a high-level Punjab Police committee had already cleared the nominated suspects.

The family questioned how subordinate police officers could challenge or overturn the findings of a committee headed by an additional inspector general.

In its letter to the parliamentary committee, the family reiterated its demand for a judicial commission to ensure an impartial investigation.

Meanwhile, the victim's brother, Fahad Javed, has submitted an application to the Prosecutor General under the Right to Information law, seeking copies of the forensic reports.

According to the application, police had sent evidence collected from the crime scene, DNA samples, mobile phones, a laptop and other items to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency in Lahore. However, despite receiving the reports, the authorities have not provided copies to the complainant.

The family has demanded copies of all forensic reports and other evidence, along with the formation of a judicial commission to ensure a transparent investigation.

headline: Inquiry report sought into PIMS tragedy
description: Inquiry report sought into PIMS tragedy
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has issued notices to the federal government and others on a petition seeking registration of a case over the deaths of children in the PIMS tragedy and compensation for the affected families.

The notices were issued to the Prime Minister's Office, Ministry of Health, Establishment Division, Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, Auditor General, chief commissioner, deputy commissioner, Capital Development Authority (CDA), Capital Emergency Services, executive director of PIMS, Islamabad Inspector General of Police and Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) director general.

The court also summoned the complete record, including the inquiry report into the incident, and suspended an order passed by a justice of peace dismissing an application for registration of an FIR.

Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro heard the petition filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi.

The petitioner told the court that 14 children had caught fire simultaneously in the PIMS incident, while another child died later. He said no FIR had been registered to date over the deaths.

The court asked whether an inquiry had been conducted into the incident. In response, Rahi said the inquiry report had established negligence.

He requested the court to direct the authorities to register an FIR immediately and submit it before the court by the end of the day's proceedings.

The petitioner further said the justice of peace had dismissed his application for registration of a case on the grounds that petitions concerning the matter were already pending before the high court.

He maintained that, apart from him, no one had approached the police station with an application, and an FIR should have been registered. He questioned the purpose of collecting evidence when no criminal case had been registered to pursue the matter.

headline: Iran war opens door to regional realignment
description: Iran war opens door to regional realignment
author: Pakistan
article_text:
Speakers at a seminar on "impact and significance of Tehran Muslim Unity Conference" agreed that the Iran War has provided an opportunity for regional countries to reshape the region without foreign interference.

The International Parliamentarians Congress (IPC) organised a seminar on the landmark Tehran Muslim Unity Conference in which there was a lively and candid discussion on the impact and consequences of the October 21 meeting in Tehran with the Makkah Defence Alliance on the initiative of Pakistan.

In his opening remarks, Senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed said that "we are living in an era of transformation, turbulence and transition" and he said that the "division and decline of the West together with the rise of China and the emergence of Muslim Middle Powers were new global realities".

Among Muslim Middle Powers, he listed Pakistan, Turkey, Iran, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia and said these countries had a broad consensus that the main threat to the Muslim world came from Israel and hence there was a need for strong Muslim unity.

Referring to Pakistan's pivotal role and the recent developments, Senator Mushahid Hussain quoted the Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who in his press conference in Cairo on 19 December 1946, had said that the "creation of Pakistan would be a source of strength for the Muslims of the Middle East", in other words, the Founder of Pakistan had linked Pakistan's role and destiny even before the creation of Pakistan with the Muslim World, which had now turned into a reality.

headline: Foreign delegates explore Buddhist heritage
description: Foreign delegates explore Buddhist heritage
author: Zulfiqar Baig
article_text:
A 16-member Sri Lankan delegation comprising senior government officials, Buddhist community leaders, archaeologists, academics, business representatives, legal professionals and media personalities has arrived in Pakistan for an eight-day Pakistan Buddhist Heritage Familiarisation Tour aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and advancing cooperation in Gandharan heritage, archaeology, education, cultural preservation and people-to-people connections.

The delegation was formally welcomed at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA). A key highlight of the opening day was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Hazara University, Mansehra, Pakistan and International Buddhist University (NIIBS), Sri Lanka. The agreement provides a framework for student and faculty exchanges, archaeology, Buddhist studies, joint research, academic programmes and heritage preservation.

The MoU was signed by Department of Archaeology Professor and Chairman Hazara University Faculty of Arts and Humanities Dean Dr Shakir Ullah and N. International Buddhist University (NIIBS), Sri Lanka, Founder P D Mandawala in the presence of the Federal Minister, Hazara University Vice Chancellor Dr Ikram Ullah Khan and other distinguished dignitaries.

Following the ceremony, the delegation visited the Islamabad Museum, exploring its archaeological collections and gaining further insight into Pakistan's Gandhara civilization and Buddhist heritage.

German delegation

Earlier on Tuesday, the Deputy Head of Mission of the German Embassy in Islamabad visited historical and archaeological sites in Taxila, including Taxila Museum, the ancient city of Sirkap and Gandhara Art Village.

The visit was organised by the Gandhara Taxila Centre for Development (GTCD) and Gandhara Odyssey (GO), in collaboration with the Archaeology Department of the Punjab government and the Punjab Small Industries Corporation (PSIC).

During the visit, officials of Taxila Museum and the Archaeology Department gave the German delegation a detailed briefing on Taxila's historical significance, archaeological remains of the Gandhara civilisation, important archaeological discoveries and the region's historical and cultural heritage.

The delegation also viewed historical artefacts preserved at Taxila Museum and the ancient city of Sirkap.

headline: Wheat release price cut, flour drops by Rs17 per kg
description: Wheat release price cut, flour drops by Rs17 per kg
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Sindh government has reduced the release price of official wheat by Rs500 to Rs4,500 per 40 kilogrammes, a move that has already triggered a Rs17 per kilogramme decline in flour prices, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said on Tuesday.

Addressing a press conference after a provincial cabinet meeting, Sharjeel said the cabinet had also approved a $1 billion urban development programme, with Asian Development Bank support, for five divisional headquarters across Sindh. The programme will focus on water supply, drainage, sanitation and solid waste management.

The cabinet also approved the registration of Lady Dufferin Hospital Trust under the Sindh Trust Act 2020 and draft rules for registering and regulating charitable organisations under the Sindh Charities Registration and Regulation Act 2019.

The senior minister said Rs502.409 million in additional funds had been approved for five development schemes in Jamshoro district, including the water supply scheme and installation of reverse osmosis plants in Sehwan. Another scheme worth Rs2.993 billion was approved to improve water supply and drainage facilities in Nawabshah town.

A cabinet committee has also been formed to address issues concerning katchi abadis and develop a legal framework for a one-window operation to streamline their administration.

On infrastructure, Sharjeel said 75% of the Ghotki-Kandhkot bridge over the Indus had been completed under the public-private partnership model.

Traffic crackdown

Turning to Karachi's worsening traffic situation, the senior minister announced that a Traffic Management Authority would be established to improve traffic regulation, with legislation to be presented for approval soon. A smart traffic management system would also be introduced to improve traffic flow and monitor violations.

He warned of indiscriminate action against traffic violators, including vehicles carrying fancy or illegal number plates and those displaying firearms. People openly carrying weapons in plain clothes would be arrested, while the vehicle owner accompanying an armed guard would also face detention, he said.

Sharjeel urged citizens to share responsibility for road safety, saying the government alone could not be blamed for violations. Driving by underage children and dangerous stunts such as one-wheeling, even in affluent neighbourhoods, remained serious concerns.

He called on media organisations to support public awareness campaigns, saying the government's priority was to protect lives and prevent road accidents.

The senior minister also vowed to remove encroachments from city roads, while insisting that the government did not intend to deprive people of their livelihoods. However, he said, enforcement of the law and public convenience could not be compromised.

No permission for political rallies on Sharea Faisal

On the MQM-P's proposed rally, Sharjeel said political parties were free to hold public gatherings but must first obtain permission from the relevant authorities and comply with the law.

He categorically ruled out permission for any political gathering on Sharea Faisal, warning the MQM-P against attempting to repeat the events of May 12. Addressing the party, he said the government would not allow a repeat of the violence witnessed that day.

He said political activities were permitted within constitutional and legal limits, but no party could impose its decisions on the government or create an atmosphere of confrontation and unrest.

On the debate over new provinces, Sharjeel reiterated that the PPP and Sindh government had made their position clear, adding that no law or decision could override the Sindh Assembly's authority on the matter.

He also criticised MQM-P leaders Mustafa Kamal, Farooq Sattar and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, questioning their electoral standing and alleging that they had entered parliament through backdoor arrangements rather than direct public votes.

Other developments

Responding to a question about the deadly Tharparkar ambulance incident, Sharjeel said the provincial government had announced financial assistance for the affected families and taken immediate steps following the incident.

He said President Asif Ali Zardari was visiting development projects across the province to review their progress.

On public transport, the senior minister said more than 100 electric buses were expected to arrive in Sindh by the end of November, while double-decker buses would also reach the province soon. Construction of the depot for the Red Line BRT project was progressing rapidly, he added.

article_html:
KARACHI:

The Sindh government has reduced the release price of official wheat by Rs500 to Rs4,500 per 40 kilogrammes, a move that has already triggered a Rs17 per kilogramme decline in flour prices, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said on Tuesday.

Addressing a press conference after a provincial cabinet meeting, Sharjeel said the cabinet had also approved a $1 billion urban development programme, with Asian Development Bank support, for five divisional headquarters across Sindh. The programme will focus on water supply, drainage, sanitation and solid waste management.

The cabinet also approved the registration of Lady Dufferin Hospital Trust under the Sindh Trust Act 2020 and draft rules for registering and regulating charitable organisations under the Sindh Charities Registration and Regulation Act 2019.

The senior minister said Rs502.409 million in additional funds had been approved for five development schemes in Jamshoro district, including the water supply scheme and installation of reverse osmosis plants in Sehwan. Another scheme worth Rs2.993 billion was approved to improve water supply and drainage facilities in Nawabshah town.

A cabinet committee has also been formed to address issues concerning katchi abadis and develop a legal framework for a one-window operation to streamline their administration.

On infrastructure, Sharjeel said 75% of the Ghotki-Kandhkot bridge over the Indus had been completed under the public-private partnership model.

Traffic crackdown

Turning to Karachi's worsening traffic situation, the senior minister announced that a Traffic Management Authority would be established to improve traffic regulation, with legislation to be presented for approval soon. A smart traffic management system would also be introduced to improve traffic flow and monitor violations.

He warned of indiscriminate action against traffic violators, including vehicles carrying fancy or illegal number plates and those displaying firearms. People openly carrying weapons in plain clothes would be arrested, while the vehicle owner accompanying an armed guard would also face detention, he said.

Sharjeel urged citizens to share responsibility for road safety, saying the government alone could not be blamed for violations. Driving by underage children and dangerous stunts such as one-wheeling, even in affluent neighbourhoods, remained serious concerns.

He called on media organisations to support public awareness campaigns, saying the government's priority was to protect lives and prevent road accidents.

The senior minister also vowed to remove encroachments from city roads, while insisting that the government did not intend to deprive people of their livelihoods. However, he said, enforcement of the law and public convenience could not be compromised.

No permission for political rallies on Sharea Faisal

On the MQM-P's proposed rally, Sharjeel said political parties were free to hold public gatherings but must first obtain permission from the relevant authorities and comply with the law.

He categorically ruled out permission for any political gathering on Sharea Faisal, warning the MQM-P against attempting to repeat the events of May 12. Addressing the party, he said the government would not allow a repeat of the violence witnessed that day.

He said political activities were permitted within constitutional and legal limits, but no party could impose its decisions on the government or create an atmosphere of confrontation and unrest.

On the debate over new provinces, Sharjeel reiterated that the PPP and Sindh government had made their position clear, adding that no law or decision could override the Sindh Assembly's authority on the matter.

He also criticised MQM-P leaders Mustafa Kamal, Farooq Sattar and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, questioning their electoral standing and alleging that they had entered parliament through backdoor arrangements rather than direct public votes.

Other developments

Responding to a question about the deadly Tharparkar ambulance incident, Sharjeel said the provincial government had announced financial assistance for the affected families and taken immediate steps following the incident.

He said President Asif Ali Zardari was visiting development projects across the province to review their progress.

On public transport, the senior minister said more than 100 electric buses were expected to arrive in Sindh by the end of November, while double-decker buses would also reach the province soon. Construction of the depot for the Red Line BRT project was progressing rapidly, he added.

headline: Court summons YellowLine project officials over 'irregularities'
description: Court summons Yellow Line project officials over 'irregularities'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A provincial anti-corruption court has summoned former project director Zameer Ahmed Abbasi and other nominated accused in the Yellow Line corruption case after the Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) submitted its charge sheet.

The court took up the case after the ACE filed the charge sheet against former director Zameer Abbasi. According to the charge sheet, alleged financial irregularities exceeding Rs8.56 billion were committed in the Yellow Line projects through illegal payments and misuse of public funds.

The charge sheet nominated Zameer Ahmed Abbasi, Director Technical Tahir Aziz Syed, Deputy Director Procurement Saleem Hussain Bhayo and former Director Procurement Jahan Das as accused.

According to the investigation, the accused allegedly disregarded prescribed procedures in projects financed by the World Bank and made billions of rupees in advance payments to contractors.

The charge sheet stated that advance payments totalling Rs8.56 billion were made to contractors. It further alleged violations of the World Bank's procurement procedures and the terms of construction contracts, with financial disbursements exceeding the actual physical progress of the projects. Former Project Director Zameer Ahmed Abbasi has been accused of allegedly abusing his authority, while former Director Procurement Jahan Das is accused of violating contractual obligations and procurement rules.

headline: MQM-P issued show-cause notice over intra-party polls
description: MQM-P issued show-cause notice over intra-party polls
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has issued a show-cause notice to the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to hold its intra-party elections within the stipulated time, warning that the party could lose its eligibility to obtain or retain an election symbol for future elections.

The ECP has sought an explanation from the party as to why it should not be declared ineligible to obtain or retain an election symbol for upcoming elections.

According to the show-cause notice issued on October 26, 2026, MQM-P failed to fulfil the requirements of Sections 208, 209 and 215 of the Elections Act 2017.

The notice stated that under an order issued on April 16, 2026, the ECP had granted the party an extended deadline of October 15, 2026, to conduct its intra-party elections. However, the party failed to hold the elections within the prescribed period.

Under Section 209 of the Elections Act 2017 and Rule 158 of the Election Rules 2017, a political party is required to submit a certificate confirming the conduct of its intra-party elections to the ECP within seven days of their completion.

The ECP has directed MQM-P to submit its response within 14 days of the issuance of the notice, warning that failure to do so may lead to further legal proceedings.

The commission has made it clear that failure to fulfil the statutory requirements could result in the party being barred from obtaining or retaining an election symbol for future elections.

headline: Power supply to Gharo pumping restored
description: Power supply to Gharo pumping restored
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The power utility K-Electric has restored the electricity to the Gharo Pumping Station after a 15-hour outage, following which water supply to Karachi resumed. According to a Water Corporation spokesperson, the prolonged power suspension resulted in a shortfall of approximately 14 million gallons of water in the city.

The spokesperson said electricity supply to the Gharo Pumping Station was suspended at 1pm on Monday due to a cable fault in K-Electric's power system.

headline: Karachi to experience hot, dry weather for next three days
description: City to experience hot, dry weather for next three days
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Winds are likely to blow from the north and northwest during the first half of the day

Minimum temperature in the metropolis is expected to range between 21 and 23 degrees Celsius, while the maximum may remain between 33 and 35 degrees Celsius over the next three days.

Karachi is likely to experience dry weather over the next three days. Winds are likely to blow from the north and northwest during the first half of the day, shifting to the west and southwest in the afternoon.

A weak westerly weather system has begun affecting the western parts of the country, with light rain expected in a few districts of rural Sindh on Wednesday.

According to the Pakistan Meteorological Department's Early Warning Centre, the system may bring light rain to the western parts of Qambar Shahdadkot and Dadu districts on Wednesday.

headline: Man shot dead while driving to office
description: Man shot dead while driving to office
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Mochko police have registered a murder case after a man was found shot dead inside his car parked along Edhi Graveyard Road.

The FIR was registered on November 3 on the complaint of the deceased's brother, Tayyab Zafar, a resident of North Nazimabad.

In his statement, the complainant said that he received a phone call on November 2 informing him that his elder brother, Saad Zafar, had been shot and killed and that his body was being taken to Civil Hospital Karachi. He went to the hospital mortuary with relatives and friends, where he identified the body of his brother.

According to the FIR, Saad, who was married and had two children, was on his way to his office in Mauripur in his car (BUQ-507) when unidentified assailants shot him near Edhi Graveyard in Mochko at around 8:45pm on November 2.

The complainant nominated unknown persons as the suspects, stating that his brother had been killed over an unidentified dispute or enmity.

Meanwhile, Keamari SSP Singhar Malik has constituted a six-member special investigation team, headed by the SDPO of Mauripur, to investigate the murder of Saad Zafar.

The team, headed by SDPO Mauripur Sub-Division Dr Farooq Ahmed Mushtaq, will investigate the murder case and examine all available evidence to establish the facts.

Other members of the team include Mochko SHO Sub-Inspector Sohail Farooq, Mauripur SHO Sub-Inspector Ansar Iqbal, Mochko SIO Inspector Agha Amir Gopang, Keamari District Call Data Record (CDR) In-charge Zubair Ahmed Magsi, and District CCTV In-charge Shoaib.

The team will collect and preserve all available evidence to identify and arrest the suspects. It will also examine CCTV footage, obtain call data records and analyse the information to trace possible leads.

As per the order, the team must submit a comprehensive report detailing tangible progress in the investigation within five days.

headline: Sindh achieves success in embryo transfer technology
description: Sindh achieves success in embryo transfer technology
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Sindh government has placed an order for 132 embryos of the Red Sindhi and Guzera cattle breeds

The Sindh government has taken a major step towards modernising the livestock sector, improving cattle breeds and increasing milk and meat production, with the successful completion of the province's first embryo transfer experiment.

The experiment was conducted through a collaboration between the Sindh Livestock Department and private organisation FoneGrow at the Sindh Institute of Animal Science, marking the beginning of a new era of scientific cattle breeding in the province.

Livestock Minister Muhammad Ali Malkani briefed Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on the successful experiment and the project. The CM said the advanced technology would help develop superior cattle breeds in a significantly shorter period. He explained that a process which traditionally took around 30 years to improve livestock breeds could now be completed in just five years with the help of this technology.

To expand the initiative, the Sindh government has placed an order for 132 embryos of the Red Sindhi and Guzera cattle breeds.

headline: Probe into 'abduction, forced conversion' of minor girls demanded
description: Probe into 'abduction, forced conversion' of minor girls demanded
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Nearly a decade after Sindh enacted legislation prohibiting child marriages, questions persist over its enforcement, with opposition leader Ali Khursheedi demanding an investigation into the alleged abduction, forced conversion and underage marriage of two girls.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sindh Assembly opposition leader said legislation alone could not protect children unless backed by effective enforcement, urging the provincial government to establish the facts surrounding the cases of Bandia Kumari and Kalpana.

Khursheedi, who belongs to the MQM-Pakistan, pointed out that Bandia belonged to Balochistan but her alleged marriage took place in Sindh, making it incumbent upon the provincial government to investigate the circumstances. He questioned who had solemnised the marriage and verified her age.

Raising concerns over the second case, the MQM-Pakistan said Kalpana's school certificate indicated that she was 13 at the time of her marriage. He called for an investigation into the apparent discrepancy between her educational record and an affidavit declaring her an adult, arguing that an affidavit alone could not establish legal age.

Khursheedi questioned why affected families had to wait for PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to take notice before government machinery swung into action. The chief minister, ministers and police should fulfil their legal responsibilities without waiting for political instructions, he said.

Demanding protection for both girls, the MQM-Pakistan leader called for age verification through authentic records and legal action against those who arranged or facilitated underage marriages. Government officials found guilty of negligence or complicity should also face accountability, he added.

He maintained that religious conversion could not be used to circumvent laws protecting children, stressing that no influential individual should be exempt from investigation and accountability.

headline: Domestic violence case accused flee after pre-arrest bail dismissed
description: Domestic violence case accused flee after pre-arrest bail dismissed
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
An additional district and sessions judge (east) rejected the pre-arrest bail applications of three accused, including two women, in a case registered over a domestic dispute. The accused fled the courtroom after their bail pleas were dismissed.

During the hearing, counsel for the complainant, Zara, Advocate Liaquat Ali Khan Gabol, argued that the accused had assaulted his client after accusing her of visiting a neighbour's house. He said they had injured her and torn her clothes.

The lawyer maintained that all three accused had been nominated in the FIR and that video footage of the incident was available with the police and prosecution. He said the complainant had sustained visible injuries to her face, neck and other parts of her body, as well as internal injuries. He further alleged that the accused had threatened to kill the complainant, her witnesses, her husband and her father, and requested the court to reject their bail applications.

The court subsequently dismissed the bail pleas of Shan, Mehnaz and Shehnaz. The three accused fled after the decision.

headline: KU forms probe committee over law exam results
description: KU forms probe committee over law exam results
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The University of Karachi has constituted a three-member committee comprising representatives of the Supreme Court, Sindh High Court and the Higher Education Commission (HEC) to conduct an impartial and transparent investigation into complaints regarding the second-year examination results and mark sheets of its affiliated law colleges.

The committee will hold detailed discussions with all relevant stakeholders, examine the matter thoroughly and scrutinise the available evidence and records before submitting a fact-based report to the university administration.

The inquiry will include meetings with affected students, teachers who evaluated the answer scripts and officials responsible for reviewing answer scripts following scrutiny applications. The committee members will also visit the examination department and hold discussions with the controller of examinations and other relevant officials.

According to details, some students had pointed out alleged discrepancies and errors in the announced results, claiming that they had passed their examinations but were declared unsuccessful in the issued mark sheets. The affected students subsequently submitted formal applications for scrutiny, maintaining that they were entitled to be declared successful in their BA/LLB examinations.

Under the prevailing rules and regulations, scrutiny is limited to recounting marks and checking the accuracy of their totaling. Re-evaluation of answer scripts does not fall within the scope of the scrutiny process.

headline: Abbasi Shaheed gets new three-storey medical block
description: Abbasi Shaheed gets new three-storey medical block
author: Faran Khan
article_text:
In a major development for healthcare in district central, the construction of a new medical block at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital has been completed after 52 years through a joint initiative of the Sindh government and the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC).

The ground-plus-three-storey building, spread over 200,000 square feet, has a capacity of 150 to 200 beds and will offer modern diagnostic and treatment facilities for various diseases. The block is expected to be formally inaugurated next week.

The new facility is expected to benefit patients from district central as well as other parts of Karachi.

Karachi Metropolitan University Registrar Mahmood Ahmed Khan has said that the new block will operate as a multi-purpose healthcare facility, offering treatment for gastroenterological, cardiac, pulmonary and dermatological conditions. Modern diagnostic services, including X-rays, echocardiography and endoscopy, would also be available. Additional modern medical equipment has been ordered for the hospital.

The block will provide outpatient department (OPD) services across various specialties, along with modern diagnostic and treatment facilities. According to the hospital administration, the facility will be made operational in phases to ensure that patients can access multiple healthcare services under one roof. Plans are also under consideration to provide medical facilities for children with autism and persons with disabilities.

headline: New curriculum to lighten schoolbags
description: New curriculum to lighten schoolbags
author: ADNAN LODHI
article_text:
The Punjab government is planning a revised curriculum for early childhood education to Grade V, promising 25 per cent lighter textbooks, QR code-based video lessons and a shift towards digital and conceptual learning from April next year in a move aimed at reducing academic pressure on young students and modernising the primary education system.

The decision discussed during an education reforms meeting comes amid growing concerns among parents and educationists over the increasing academic burden on primary schoolchildren who are required to carry multiple textbooks, notebooks, workbooks and supplementary course material to schools.

For many children, particularly those in private schools in Lahore and other major cities, the schoolbag has become much more than a collection of prescribed textbooks. Alongside compulsory subjects, the students are frequently expected to carry grammar and mathematics practice books, general knowledge material, computer science books, activity workbooks and additional learning resources.

The situation becomes more challenging when schools introduce supplementary courses and additional academic activities without removing existing material. Children consequently face a combination of heavy bags, lengthy home assignments and pressure to complete several subjects within classroom hours.

The revised curriculum is expected to address part of this problem by reducing textbook volume by 25%. However, educationists believe that the actual benefit will depend on whether schools also review their supplementary reading requirements, homework policies and examination practices.

A reduction in textbook pages alone may not significantly ease students' academic pressure if institutions continue prescribing additional books and practice material.

The government will, therefore, need to ensure that private and public sector schools follow the revised curriculum without unnecessarily expanding the prescribed workload.

According to a senior official of the Punjab Education Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority (PECTAA), the revised curriculum has been prepared for Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) to Grade V and sent to the Cambridge International Education authorities for assessment and comparison with international standards.

The final curriculum content is expected to be ready in December, following which PECTAA will begin printing the revised textbooks in January.

The books are scheduled to be available before the beginning of the new academic session in April.

An important component of the reform is the introduction of QR codes in textbooks. Students will be able to scan these codes through digital devices and access video lessons relating to the relevant topics.

The initiative is intended to make classroom learning more interactive by combining conventional reading material with audiovisual explanations. Difficult mathematical concepts, scientific topics and other lessons could become easier to understand through demonstrations and visual presentations.

The digital component also offers opportunities for students to revise lessons at home and learn at their own pace.

headline: Online shopping disputes fall under consumer courts: LHC
description: Online shopping disputes fall under consumer courts: LHC
author: Rana Yasif
article_text:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that disputes arising from online shopping transactions, including the non-delivery of goods after full payment and subsequent cancellation of orders, fall within the jurisdiction of consumer courts.

The court held that buyers cannot bypass the special legal forum by describing their claims for compensation as general damages, observing that jurisdiction must be determined by the cause of action rather than the terminology or amount of relief sought.

Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan made these observations while dismissing a constitutional petition filed by Dr Muhammad Ahtisham Qamar, who had challenged a civil court's decision to return his damages suit and the subsequent dismissal of his appeal by an additional district judge.

The petitioner had sought recovery of Rs2,116,480 in refund and damages over an online purchase of two clothing articles worth Rs6,480.

According to the petitioner, he had paid the full amount through his credit card, but the articles were not delivered within the stipulated period.

Instead, the sellers cancelled the order after 17 days, citing the Covid-19 pandemic.

Although the amount was subsequently refunded, he sought compensation for alleged mental agony, humiliation and other losses.

The defendants initially denied the online transaction but later admitted that a booking had been made, the stock was unavailable and the amount received had been refunded.

The civil court returned the plaint under Order VII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, directing the petitioner to approach the competent forum under the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005.

The appellate court upheld the decision, prompting him to move the high court.

The petitioner's counsel argued that the claim was primarily for general damages arising from mental distress and humiliation caused by the cancellation of the transaction.

headline: Two women among 8 held from call centre
description: Two women among 8 held from call centre
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Case was registered and the investigation was under way

The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested eight suspects, including two women, during a raid on an allegedly illegal call centre in the Township area and seized 53 digital devices, officials said on Tuesday.

A team conducted the raid at a house after obtaining a search warrant from a court on the basis of a tip.

headline: Fresh housing loan applications to be invited
description: Total of 171,597 beneficiaries have received second installment of their loans, 62,600 houses are nearing completion.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Total of 171,597 beneficiaries have received second installment of their loans, 62,600 houses are nearing completion.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has directed authorities to ensure timely achievement of all targets set for the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme, approving the invitation of fresh applications for loans.

She was informed in a meeting that more than 1.7 million people had registered on the portal, over 225,000 loans had been disbursed and 128,718 houses completed.

A total of 171,597 beneficiaries have received the second installment of their loans and 62,600 houses are nearing completion.

The scheme has achieved a loan recovery rate of 97.6 per cent, with installments amounting to Rs22.29 billion paid.

The application process for the Apni Chhat, Mehfooz Chhat scheme has also been completed.

headline: Man arrested for allegedly killing mother, two sisters
description: Man arrested for allegedly killing mother, two sisters
author: Salman Qureshi
article_text:
Police have arrested a man for allegedly murdering his mother and two sisters and setting their bodies on fire to make the killings appear an accidental blaze at their home in Multan on October 28.

The suspect, identified as Aman Abbas, allegedly killed the three women in the name of honour, according to a police spokesperson.

The incident initially appeared to be an accidental fire at a house in the DHA police station's jurisdiction.

Police said they continued their investigation discreetly after the fire and uncovered evidence suggesting that the deaths were the result of a planned murder.

According to investigators, Aman allegedly struck his mother and two sisters on the head with a wooden object.

He then poured petrol on them and set them on fire in an attempt to conceal the crime.

The police spokesperson said investigators had also obtained CCTV footage from the petrol pump where the suspect had allegedly purchased petrol for the crime.

A case has been registered against Aman on behalf of the DHA police, and he has been arrested.

Police have also launched action against the officials of the petrol pump who allegedly supplied petrol to him in violation of the relevant rules.

Those allegedly involved in the matter have been arrested, the spokesperson said.

Police officials claimed that the suspect confessed to killing the three women during interrogation. The spokesperson said the investigation would be completed on merit and all legal requirements fulfilled to ensure that the suspect was brought to justice.

The incident had occurred on the night of October 28 at a house on the second floor in the Cycle Mor area near Adda Latifabad, Bosan Road.

Initially, a fire at the house was reported to have killed a woman and two children.

headline: Four booked for illegal immigration
description: Four booked for illegal immigration
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Azhar told investigators that he had paid Rs3.4 million to an agent, while Abbas had paid Rs5.1 million

The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has registered a case against four people, including two passengers deported from abroad, for allegedly attempting to reach Europe illegally.

According to the FIA, Azhar Hussain and Ghulam Abbas were deported on October 27 and detained at Islamabad International Airport for questioning. Azhar told investigators that he had paid Rs3.4 million to an agent, while Abbas had paid Rs5.1 million.

Both were allegedly taken through different countries to Libya before being arrested while attempting to enter Italy illegally. The FIA also booked the alleged agents under the Immigration Ordinance 1979 and Prevention of Smuggling of Migrants Act 2018.

headline: Alumni oppose renaming of Punjab Medical College
description: Alumni oppose renaming of Punjab Medical College
author: Khawar Randhawa
article_text:
Professionals and alumni associations have opposed the government's decision to rename the Punjab Medical College as Faisalabad Medical College, urging authorities to retain the institution's historic identity as a constituent college of the Faisalabad Medical University (FMU).

In a joint letter addressed to the Punjab governor, the FMU vice chancellor and the principal of Faisalabad Medical College, the Punjab Medical College Alumni Association in North America (PMCAANA) and Punjab Medical College Alumni UK (PMCAUK) called for the reinstatement of the original name.

The letter, signed by PMCAANA President Dr Saadia Alvi and PMCAUK President Dr Shahnaz Akhtar, refers to the Public Sector Medical Universities (Second Amendment) Ordinance 2026.

It states that Section 5(a) inserts a new sub-section into Section 3 of the Faisalabad Medical University Act 2017, reviving the college as a constituent institution but naming it as Faisalabad Medical College.

The alumni associations argued that the institution, established in 1973, had built a strong reputation in Pakistan and abroad under the name Punjab Medical College.

They said the name represented its history, professional identity and legacy.

Dr Amir Sarfraz, a member of PMCAUK, said thousands of graduates were practising in the UK, United States, Middle East and other countries. Their qualifications were registered with professional and academic bodies, including the General Medical Council (GMC) and the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG), under the name Punjab Medical College.

He warned that changing the name could create confusion and complications in the verification of qualifications, professional registration and credentialing.

He added that retaining the college's original name would not affect the vice chancellor's administrative authority or the university's governance.

FAISALABAD:

Professionals and alumni associations have opposed the government's decision to rename the Punjab Medical College as Faisalabad Medical College, urging authorities to retain the institution's historic identity as a constituent college of the Faisalabad Medical University (FMU).

In a joint letter addressed to the Punjab governor, the FMU vice chancellor and the principal of Faisalabad Medical College, the Punjab Medical College Alumni Association in North America (PMCAANA) and Punjab Medical College Alumni UK (PMCAUK) called for the reinstatement of the original name.

The letter, signed by PMCAANA President Dr Saadia Alvi and PMCAUK President Dr Shahnaz Akhtar, refers to the Public Sector Medical Universities (Second Amendment) Ordinance 2026.

It states that Section 5(a) inserts a new sub-section into Section 3 of the Faisalabad Medical University Act 2017, reviving the college as a constituent institution but naming it as Faisalabad Medical College.

The alumni associations argued that the institution, established in 1973, had built a strong reputation in Pakistan and abroad under the name Punjab Medical College.

They said the name represented its history, professional identity and legacy.

Dr Amir Sarfraz, a member of PMCAUK, said thousands of graduates were practising in the UK, United States, Middle East and other countries. Their qualifications were registered with professional and academic bodies, including the General Medical Council (GMC) and the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG), under the name Punjab Medical College.

He warned that changing the name could create confusion and complications in the verification of qualifications, professional registration and credentialing.

He added that retaining the college's original name would not affect the vice chancellor's administrative authority or the university's governance.

headline: Three drown as car plunges into canal
description: Three drown as car plunges into canal
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Five killed in two road accidents in Hafizabad

Five people were killed and two others injured in two road accidents in Hafizabad district, police and rescue officials said on Tuesday.

In the first incident, a speeding car went out of control near Chak Kharal and plunged into the Qadirabad-Balloki Link Canal, drowning three of its four occupants.

The fourth passenger survived.

Rescue 1122 teams rushed to the scene, retrieved the bodies from the canal and handed them over to the families.

The car was also retrieved from the water.

The deceased were identified as Basharat Ali, 40, Bilal, 17, and Urooj Fatima, 20.

All three belonged to the Chowateyan village in Gujranwala district.

The survivor was identified as Ali, 22, a resident of the same village.

In the second accident near Sukheki, a dumper truck rammed into a motorcycle before overturning, killing the motorcyclist, Nasir Nawaz, and his wife.

The couple belonged to Thatha Khairu Matmal.

The dumper driver, Nasrullah, a resident of Bannu district, suffered severe injuries. Rescue personnel shifted him to a nearby hospital for treatment.

headline: CCD claims killing two in encounter
description: CCD claims killing two in encounter
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
They were shifted to a hospital, where they succumbed to their injuries

Two alleged robbers were killed in an exchange of fire of their accomplices with Crime Control Department (CCD) personnel near Malkhanwala Morr on Satiana Road on Tuesday, while three suspects escaped.

According to police, CCD teams led by Lyallpur Town in-charge Sadiq Cheema and Iqbal Town in-charge Ali Ikram Goraya raided a location near Malkhanwala Morr to arrest wanted suspects. The police claimed that five suspects opened indiscriminate fire on the teams, triggering a shootout that continued for around 30 minutes.

During the encounter, suspects Hasnain and Nokhaiz suffered gunshot wounds allegedly from their accomplices' firing, according to the police.

They were shifted to a hospital, where they succumbed to their injuries.

Their three accomplices escaped because of darkness.

headline: YPP visits Commonwealth Secretariat
description: YPP visits Commonwealth Secretariat
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

A delegation of the Youth Parliament Pakistan (YPP) on Tuesday held a high-level meeting with senior officials of the Commonwealth Secretariat in London to explore avenues for strengthening democratic governance, electoral reforms and youth participation in parliamentary affairs.

Led by YPP President Ubaid Qureshi, the delegation was received by Dr Dinusha Panditaratne, Adviser to the Commonwealth Secretary-General and Head of the Asia Region, along with senior officials of the Secretariat.

The discussions focused on the Commonwealth's work in governance, Good Offices and electoral reforms, highlighting its role in strengthening democratic institutions, promoting peace and fostering cooperation among its 56 member countries.

During the interactive session, Commonwealth officials briefed the delegation on the organisation's governance framework, decision-making mechanisms and programmes aimed at promoting democratic governance, conflict prevention, election management and regional cooperation.

headline: A new desert lizard emerges from Chagai sands
description: A new desert lizard emerges from Chagai sands
author: APP
article_text:
On low sand dunes in western Pakistan, near the borders with Afghanistan and Iran, researchers have identified a desert lizard previously unknown to science.

The species, named Eremias chagaiensis after Chagai District in Balochistan, has a distinctive network of winding brown markings across its back.

An international study reveals a maze-patterned racerunner and resolves a century-old question about another lizard in Balochistan.

The study also provides the first modern specimen- and DNA-based confirmation of Eremias fasciata in Pakistan, more than a century after its first alleged historical report.

The new lizard was documented at four localities during field surveys between 2022 and 2025. Its body reaches 5.7 cm in length, excluding a tail that can be more than twice as long. Unlike the longitudinal stripes typical of many related racerunners, its intricate, maze-like pattern is present in both juveniles and adults.

"Balochistan's deserts are among the least explored places in South Asia. Finding a new lizard here tells us how much is still undocumented," says Rafaqat Masroor of the Pakistan Museum of Natural History, who led the research.

The finding adds to a long but uneven history of herpetological research in Balochistan. Recently, research in northwestern Balochistan has revealed Eremias kakari and two further racerunners, E. rafiqi and E. killasaifullahi by Rafaqat Masroor and Daniel Jablonski, researchers that are collaborating almost a decade.

The new discovery therefore builds on decades of Pakistani and international work, while showing how much remains unresolved.

Appearance, however, did not tell the whole story.

The new species closely resembles Eremias graphica, described from Iran in 2023. Analyses of two mitochondrial and one nuclear gene, together with comparisons of body proportions and scale characters, support its recognition as a distinct evolutionary lineage. In the mitochondrial analyses, E. fasciata, a striped species from the same wider landscape, was recovered as its closest relative. The two species differ by approximately 10.6% in the mitochondrial genes examined.

"At first glance this lizard looked like a species from Iran described in 2023," says Daniel Jablonski of Comenius University in Bratislava and the Natural History Museum Vienna, Austria.

"Appearances can be deceptive. The sand doesn't stop at the border. Surveys in Afghanistan are needed to learn how far this species really lives."

The lizards were observed on loose sand, particularly low dunes and sandy patches near desert shrubs, where they excavate burrows. They were not recorded on the neighbouring gravel plains, which were occupied by E. fasciata. APP

article_html:
PESHAWAR:

On low sand dunes in western Pakistan, near the borders with Afghanistan and Iran, researchers have identified a desert lizard previously unknown to science.

The species, named Eremias chagaiensis after Chagai District in Balochistan, has a distinctive network of winding brown markings across its back.

An international study reveals a maze-patterned racerunner and resolves a century-old question about another lizard in Balochistan.

The study also provides the first modern specimen- and DNA-based confirmation of Eremias fasciata in Pakistan, more than a century after its first alleged historical report.

The new lizard was documented at four localities during field surveys between 2022 and 2025. Its body reaches 5.7 cm in length, excluding a tail that can be more than twice as long. Unlike the longitudinal stripes typical of many related racerunners, its intricate, maze-like pattern is present in both juveniles and adults.

"Balochistan's deserts are among the least explored places in South Asia. Finding a new lizard here tells us how much is still undocumented," says Rafaqat Masroor of the Pakistan Museum of Natural History, who led the research.

The finding adds to a long but uneven history of herpetological research in Balochistan. Recently, research in northwestern Balochistan has revealed Eremias kakari and two further racerunners, E. rafiqi and E. killasaifullahi by Rafaqat Masroor and Daniel Jablonski, researchers that are collaborating almost a decade.

The new discovery therefore builds on decades of Pakistani and international work, while showing how much remains unresolved.

Appearance, however, did not tell the whole story.

The new species closely resembles Eremias graphica, described from Iran in 2023. Analyses of two mitochondrial and one nuclear gene, together with comparisons of body proportions and scale characters, support its recognition as a distinct evolutionary lineage. In the mitochondrial analyses, E. fasciata, a striped species from the same wider landscape, was recovered as its closest relative. The two species differ by approximately 10.6% in the mitochondrial genes examined.

"At first glance this lizard looked like a species from Iran described in 2023," says Daniel Jablonski of Comenius University in Bratislava and the Natural History Museum Vienna, Austria.

"Appearances can be deceptive. The sand doesn't stop at the border. Surveys in Afghanistan are needed to learn how far this species really lives."

The lizards were observed on loose sand, particularly low dunes and sandy patches near desert shrubs, where they excavate burrows. They were not recorded on the neighbouring gravel plains, which were occupied by E. fasciata. APP

headline: Recovery pleas referred to PHC CJ
description: Recovery pleas referred to PHC CJ
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Piqued by officials' failure to submit replies to petitions challenging the detention of PTI leaders, including the chief minister, a Peshawar High Court (PHC) bench on Tuesday referred the matter to the chief justice, requesting the constitution of a larger bench to hear the case.

Sohail Afridi - the non-functional Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister - has not been seen since the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P on Oct 11. His whereabouts remained unknown on the day governor's rule was imposed, and a federal minister confirmed a day later that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody.

Afridi's brother, Mohammad Aamir, filed one of the petitions, alleging that the non-functional chief minister had been "abducted" from the Chief Minister's House on the night the emergency was imposed. He approached the PHC on Oct 13.

On Tuesday, a division bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali referred the petitions to the chief justice after the provincial government and senior police officials failed to submit their replies in compliance with the court's Oct 20 directives.

"These are not ordinary personalities," Justice Ali remarked during the hearing, adding that the chief minister of the province was missing.

The bench observed that the respondents had been given 10 days to submit their replies but had failed to comply.

"We refer this case to the chief justice to constitute a larger bench," Justice Ali said. The K-P advocate general also requested the formation of a larger bench.

The petitions concern the alleged disappearance or detention of several other PTI leaders, including K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, MNAs Junaid Akbar and Dr Amjid Ali, provincial minister Amjid Ali Khan, MPAs Ikramullah and Aurangzeb Khan, former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Mohammad Khalid Khursheed and several other party leaders.

The PTI has alleged that the whereabouts of these leaders have not been disclosed by the government. Multiple petitions have been filed in the high court challenging their alleged detention.

Meanwhile, K-P Advocate General Sanaullah Khan sought three days to submit the replies, saying his office was awaiting responses from the provincial home department, police and other law enforcement agencies.

Bashir Vazir, counsel for the petitioners, alleged that the PTI leaders had been missing for several days. He argued that Article 199 of the Constitution empowered the high court to order the production of Afridi and Swati before it.

He also referred to an immunity law passed by the K-P Assembly, arguing that assembly members could not be arrested in such a manner and that the speaker was also protected under the law.

The law, he said, stipulated that the speaker would remain in office until a successor was elected.

The advocate general said that in more than 200 cases involving detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO), orders had been issued without hearings.

The bench disagreed, observing that reports had been sought from the respondents in those cases but were never submitted. It also noted that the detentions under consideration in the present petitions were not MPO cases.

headline: Dera Murad Jamali Bypass marred by funding issues
description: Dera Murad Jamali Bypass marred by funding issues
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The long-awaited Dera Murad Jamali Bypass, seen as a game-changer for the area, has received no allocation in the current year's Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).

This was disclosed at a meeting of the National Assembly Standing Committee on Communications on Tuesday.

Work on the 11.19-kilometre, two-lane bypass (N-65) began in 2021. The project, estimated to cost Rs1,456.32 million, was approved by the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) on April 22, 2020.

However, the scheme has faced repeated delays. The committee directed the National Highway Authority (NHA) to submit a comprehensive plan at its next meeting, outlining how the project could be completed and identifying potential funding arrangements to prevent further delays.

The committee also expressed concern over staff shortages in the NHA's Balochistan region, given the province's extensive road network and long stretches of highways requiring regular maintenance and supervision.

It directed the NHA to review its staffing requirements and propose measures to strengthen its workforce in Balochistan, bringing staffing levels in line with those in other provinces.

The committee also stressed the need to provide employment opportunities to local residents by making them eligible for recruitment against relevant positions, taking into account regional requirements and the effective management and maintenance of road infrastructure.

It further directed the NHA to prioritise ongoing development schemes, ensure the timely completion of delayed projects and take steps to strengthen its workforce in Balochistan.

QUETTA:

The long-awaited Dera Murad Jamali Bypass, seen as a game-changer for the area, has received no allocation in the current year's Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).

This was disclosed at a meeting of the National Assembly Standing Committee on Communications on Tuesday.

Work on the 11.19-kilometre, two-lane bypass (N-65) began in 2021. The project, estimated to cost Rs1,456.32 million, was approved by the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) on April 22, 2020.

However, the scheme has faced repeated delays. The committee directed the National Highway Authority (NHA) to submit a comprehensive plan at its next meeting, outlining how the project could be completed and identifying potential funding arrangements to prevent further delays.

The committee also expressed concern over staff shortages in the NHA's Balochistan region, given the province's extensive road network and long stretches of highways requiring regular maintenance and supervision.

It directed the NHA to review its staffing requirements and propose measures to strengthen its workforce in Balochistan, bringing staffing levels in line with those in other provinces.

The committee also stressed the need to provide employment opportunities to local residents by making them eligible for recruitment against relevant positions, taking into account regional requirements and the effective management and maintenance of road infrastructure.

It further directed the NHA to prioritise ongoing development schemes, ensure the timely completion of delayed projects and take steps to strengthen its workforce in Balochistan.
