headline: Trump says Iran war worth it despite midterm elections losses
description: Trump suffered military, political defeats: Mohsen Rezaei
author: AFP
article_text:
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the war in Iran was worth the political and economic costs as his Republican Party lost the midterm elections, insisting that the country had "no choice" but to take military action to prevent Tehran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

Asked at the White House whether he believed the conflict was worth it, Trump responded: “I do. Yeah. I mean, well, you have no choice.”

“The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it,” he added.

Asked about Vice President JD Vance's suggestion that the war in Iran contributed to Republican losses, Trump agreed, acknowledging that the conflict had pushed gasoline prices higher in the short term.

“Well, I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up,” he said.

However, he defended the decision to launch and continue the military campaign, arguing that it was necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

“At the same time, if I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again because, long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon,” he said.

Trump suffered military, political defeats: Mohsen Rezaei

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei claimed on Wednesday that Tehran had inflicted military and political defeats on US President Donald Trump.

“The Iranian nation handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz—and a POLITICAL DEFEAT in Washington,” Rezaei wrote on X.

He also said Americans were bearing the financial burden of the war.

“Anyone who takes on Iran will pay the price—from the battlefield to their own doorstep,” he warned.

The remarks came after US Vice President JD Vance blamed the war with Iran for Republicans’ defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote on X on Wednesday, saying voter anger over the conflict had driven former Trump supporters to back Democrats.

Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the elections.

Anyone expecting shift in US policy after midterm election 'seriously mistaken': Iran's supreme leader

Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said that anyone expecting a shift in US policy was “seriously mistaken”, a day after US midterm elections dealt a blow to US President Donald Trump, AFP reported on Wednesday.

“Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the US can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” he said in a written statement published on his website.

Khamenei warned that the Middle East war would become even wider if the United States resumed its attacks on the Islamic republic.

“Should such aggressions be repeated, its (the war) scope will become much wider,” Khamenei said.

Americans said no to war, and we endorse this message: Iran's Ghalibaf

Senior Iranian Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf hailed the US public's rejection of the Iran war by voting against the Republican Party in the Congress midterm election in an X post on Wednesday.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he said.

He added that "If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers," it will suffer "a nightmare."

His comments came as Democrats established a majority in the Senate and House elections in a rebuke against US President Donald Trump's stewardship of the country, which in part has stemmed from the war waged on Iran.

Drones attack Iranian Kurdish opposition in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah and east Erbil, sources say

Two explosive-laden drones attacked the Iranian Kurdish opposition in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah and east Erbil on Wednesday, security sources said.

Iran has repeatedly struck the bases of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan region, accusing the groups of carrying out attacks in Iran.

Four oil tankers destroyed in Hormuz after hitting mines, Tehran says

Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran said on Wednesday, after it warned no one would benefit from a return to war.

It came a day after US President Donald Trump said the United States had launched strikes on the Islamic Republic, following reports of a raid on Qeshm, the largest island in the strait.

"Four non-compliant oil tankers attempting to pass through the prohibited passage south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed after striking naval mines and are still burning," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement quoted by state TV.

"Two other non-compliant ships or vessels have also been halted."

The Guards also said they had shot down a drone over the strait.

Tehran claims control over Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and has targeted vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation since the war erupted.

The conflict, triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, has been at a stalemate for months.

Indirect contact between the United States and Iran via mediators has continued with little sign of any diplomatic breakthrough, and Iran has said it is ready to reopen the strait but only if Washington agrees to a long-standing list of demands.

Tehran's chief negotiator in talks with the United States, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic Republic was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", although President Masoud Pezeshkian insisted his government was trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue".

"No one will benefit from this war" if fighting resumes, Pezeshkian said on Tuesday.

US has no immediate plans to strike Iran: Trump

The US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday.

In an interview with the newspaper hours before polls closed in US midterm elections, Trump described Washington's position toward Iran as a “brilliant situation,” suggesting the administration was satisfied with the current balance of pressure on Tehran.

“We seem to be getting everything we want,” he said.

Asked about indications from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that an attack could take place later this week, Trump said American forces remained prepared to act but suggested that military action might not be necessary.

“I’m ready, we’re ready. We’re locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it,” he said.

Trump argued that the US was not currently engaged in a conventional war with Iran, pointing to previous American military operations against the country's nuclear infrastructure.

“We’re not really in a war, because we hit them with the B-2 bombers and wiped out their nuclear potential incapacity,” he said, referring to the earlier US bombing campaign.

He also referenced Operation Epic Fury and subsequent military actions, arguing that the confrontation did not resemble major conventional conflicts such as World War I, World War II or the ongoing war in Ukraine.

“I don’t consider that we’re in a war like Ukraine, wars like World War I, World War II,” he said.

Despite his assessment, the president acknowledged that Washington remained concerned about Iran's stockpile of approximately 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium.

Trump described the material as “nuclear dust” and said indirect negotiations with Tehran over its future were continuing.

Although much of the material is believed to be buried beneath extensive rubble from previous strikes, Trump said he was not satisfied with the prospect of it remaining there.

“Even though it’s under hundreds of tons of rock, I would say that I’m not happy that it will be there,” he told the FT.

He added that the issue remained among the subjects being discussed in ongoing contacts with Iran.

headline: Robinson wins England cricketer of the year award
description: The 32-year-old claims the honour after taking 28 Test wickets at an average of 9.32 following his international comeback
author: AFP
article_text:
The 32-year-old claims the honour after taking 28 Test wickets at an average of 9.32

Ollie Robinson was named England cricketer of the year on Tuesday to complete his remarkable return to the international arena.

Robinson spent over two years out of favour with the England selectors before making a memorable comeback this year.

The 32-year-old seam bowler took 28 wickets at an average of just 9.32 in Test matches against New Zealand and Pakistan.

Robinson is set for a major role in England's forthcoming red-ball programme, which takes in trips to South Africa, Bangladesh and the 150th anniversary Test against Australia in Melbourne.

The scale of Robinson's impact in his four Tests this year saw him crowned by members at the Vitality Cricket Media Club Awards at Lord's, claiming the trophy named after former England captain Bob Willis.

"It's a huge honour to receive this award. After spending such a long time away from the England side, to come back and have the summer I've had has been incredibly special," Robinson said.

"There were certainly some tough moments along the way, which makes receiving recognition like this mean even more.

"I've absolutely loved being back playing for England and hopefully there's plenty more to come."

Middlesex seam bowler Naavya Sharma, currently in the West Indies with England Lions, took the young cricketer of the year award after a breakout season.

headline: Barcelona cruise past Aston Villa
description: Yamal's opener and Raphinha's double seal a 3-0 win for the Catalan giants
author: AFP
article_text:
Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth.

Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

"Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar.

"This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you...

"From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

"Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports. "Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals."

Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort.

End-to-end

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

article_html:
BARCELONA:

Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth.

Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

"Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar.

"This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you...

"From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

"Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports.
"Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals."

Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort.

End-to-end

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing.
Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo set up Raphinha for Barcelona's third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal across all competitions.

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.

Flick was pleased with Barcelona keeping Villa at bay.

"It was important that we defended together very compactly," said the German coach.
"The back line played on an amazing level, they defended everything."

Aston Villa are well positioned, provisionally third in the league phase table.

Emery said the match was a good lesson for his side against one of the biggest teams in Europe.

"We must be ruthless in the attacking third, we must be more demanding of ourselves, creating those chances to score," Emery told reporters.

"The 3-0 is maybe more (heavy) than we deserved, but we accept this defeat, taking a lot of information for our improvement."

headline: North Korean leader calls for 'rapid' naval build up as Pyongyang warns of stronger response to US 'hostility'
description: Kim says recent geopolitical environment, hostile acts of enemies prove need for 'most developed, powerful warship'
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for a rapid buildup of naval combat power to counter "hostile acts of the enemies," as Pyongyang warned the United States that it will mount a stronger response to Washington's "hostile policy" toward the country, state media reported on Wednesday.

Kim made the remarks during a visit to the Nampho shipyard Monday, where he was briefed on the shipyard's ongoing upgrades and inspected a new warship under construction, state-run Korean Central News Agency reported.

"It is vital and important requirement of the times to rapidly bolster up the surface and underwater combat power for defending the national sovereignty in the sea under various threats," Kim said.

The recent geopolitical environment and hostile acts of the enemies in the region prove the need for "the most developed and powerful warship," he added.

Without providing the ship's specifications, North Korean media said the vessel is "designed to carry out its complex operational mission in consideration of the present-day warfare."

'Dialogue with US remains an 'option'

Kim's powerful sister Kim Yo-jong Wednesday said that dialogue with Washington remains "an option for peace, but that it would not be necessary for its own interest."

She said that the continued "hostile signal" by Washington was compelling the regime to reconsider the "true nature" of the US. "The choice for peace includes dialogue of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us," Kim said in a statement.

Her remarks came a day after she rejected the FBI findings that Pyongyang was behind the theft of more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

"The so-called 'cryptocurrency hacking case by the DPRK' is no more than a tip of iceberg that shows the essence of the US hostile policy toward the DPRK," she maintained.

DPRK refers to North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

"The US abandonment of its hostile policy" toward Pyongyang "is a major premise and key to solving all problems," she said, adding that North Korea has no reason to engage in talks with the US unless that happens. She warned that Pyongyang would respond to what it views as continued US hostility.

headline: Spain's transport minister resigns over deadly train crash
description: Says Spain's transport minister cannot remain in office after two such accidents in less than a year
author: Reuters
article_text:
Spain's transport minister, Oscar Puente, announced his resignation a day earlier over last week's deadly train ‌crash, the country's second this year, hours after laying out the government's emergency aid package for victims and new safety measures.

"A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot continue in office with two accidents of this severity in less than a year," he told lawmakers of the Permanent Deputation, a ​standing committee that sits when parliament is dissolved. He spoke nearly a week after the October 28 crash that killed 69 ​people near the town of Urda in central Spain.

His departure comes less than four weeks before an ⁠early parliamentary election that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called for November 29, and after two deadly crashes on the same line ​this year.

Sanchez praised Puente in a post on X, thanking him for his work and saying the minister had put victims first and ​acted out of a sense of political responsibility.

Puente, who had previously ruled out resigning, said he had decided to step down within minutes of learning of the crash, but chose to remain in office until the immediate emergency response was underway, preliminary investigations had begun, and the first measures to compensate ​victims and improve rail safety had been put in place.

Another train accident in January, involving the same companies on the same line, ​killed 46 people.

October 28 train crash

Several trains were automatically stopped last Wednesday due to the failure of a signalling system on the Madrid-Seville ‌line, after ⁠which central controllers in Madrid took over. The controllers authorised a train operated by state-owned Renfe to proceed, even though there was a stationary privately operated Iryo train ahead, according to Puente.

Investigators estimated an impact speed of 160 to 200 kph (100 to 125 mph).

Emergency aid package for victims

Under measures Puente announced earlier on Tuesday, services on the Madrid-Seville rail line will be reduced until the Railway Safety Agency ​reviews the line's safety system ​and the government completes the ⁠delayed rollout of the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS).

The safety measures include a 40 kph (25 mph) speed limit when relying on a driver to spot obstacles ahead if a signal system fails, hiring ​more staff and improving conditions in rail control centres.

The leftist government also promised to double compulsory ​passenger insurance payouts for ⁠crash victims, speed up compensation payments and improve temporary incapacity cover.

In addition, in what Puente said would be a world first, the railway system will introduce an AI agent to "detect anomalies and monitor conversations" between train drivers and controllers to minimise the likelihood of human error.

"We are ⁠not ​aware of any other railway system that uses this type of mechanism or technology. ​We will be the first to go down this path," Puente said, adding that Spain would also create a real-time digital model of the network.

headline: Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty after Trump's Republicans face election rout
description: Brent futures rise 82 cents, or 0.8%, to $104.42 a barrel
author: Reuters
article_text:
Oil prices ​rose on Wednesday in a volatile session as investors awaited Washington's next move in the war with Iran, after Democrats captured control of the US Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans in the midterm elections.

Brent futures rose 82 cents, or 0.8%, to $104.42 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 50 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.59, reversing earlier ​declines.

In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks as traders weighed ​talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

Vote counting was underway in the ⁠US midterm elections, with Democrats snaring majorities in both houses of Congress for the rest of Trump's second term.

"President ​Trump's conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to ​build strong directional conviction," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.

"I believe some profit-taking and reduction in speculative long positions are justified, particularly after the sharp rally in October," said Sachdeva.

"However, the underlying supply disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz ​have not disappeared. An unexpected drawdown in US crude inventories is also offering some fundamental support," she added.

The ​US had carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said on ‌Tuesday. Another ⁠official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.

Markets remained on watch for any progress in talks to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, as Qatar stepped up mediation efforts to avert an escalation of attacks after the US elections.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran and ​the United States remain far from ​a deal to end ⁠their war.

US President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran.

Meanwhile, crude stocks fell by 5.27 million barrels in ​the week ended October 30, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the ​American Petroleum Institute.

Eight ⁠analysts polled by Reuters had expected, on average, a rise of about 880,000 barrels in crude inventories.

Gasoline stocks rose by 1.43 million barrels, while distillate inventories fell by 1.19 million barrels from a week earlier, the sources said.

"Diesel inventories remain ⁠tight, while ​gasoline stocks rose more than expected. The data are broadly supportive ​of oil prices," Haitong Futures said in a note on Wednesday.

Official data from the US Energy Information Administration is due at 10:30 am EST (1530 ​GMT) on Wednesday.

headline: Democrats sweep Congress in US midterm elections
description: Voters in conservative bastions who propelled the president to his second term swung dramatically ​toward Democrats
author: Reuters
article_text:
Democrats seized control of both the Senate and House on Tuesday, scoring sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Voters in conservative bastions who had propelled the president to his second term in office just two years ago swung dramatically ​toward Democrats, fuelled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high cost of living and anger at Trump's stewardship of the country.

In Texas, the biggest Republican state, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning a Senate seat and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.

Kansas elected its first Democratic senator since the Great Depression nearly a ‌century ago. In South Carolina, a state that Trump carried by nearly 18 points in 2024, Democrats turned aside his hand-picked Senate candidate.

And in Texas, the biggest Republican state, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning a Senate seat and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.

The results will usher in a new era of divided government in Washington, following two years in which the Republican-controlled Congress rarely exercised its power to rein in Trump.

Once seated in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump's administration, family and allies and demand concessions on major legislation. The Democratic Senate can block Trump's nominees, including any US Supreme ​Court justices should a vacancy arise.

"There is now a generational remake of the Senate map that is going to change America," said Chuck Schumer, the party's Senate minority leader. "Americans voted for change, and now Democrats must ​deliver."

Trump, who is barred by the US Constitution from seeking a third term, has exercised an iron grip on his party for most of the last decade. But the new balance of power in Washington may ⁠accelerate his lame-duck status, as attention turns toward the 2028 presidential race and potential successors begin competing for political influence in a post-Trump world.

Despite worries from Democrats that Trump might seek to overturn the election results, as he did in 2020, the president accepted the outcome, congratulating Democrats in ​an interview with Fox News. He also said he would work with Democrats on issues such as immigration, though he threatened to veto any "insane" bills they passed.

Democratic wave

Democrats focused their campaign on corruption and affordability, blaming Trump's tariff policy and the war with Iran for driving up costs while highlighting the ​billions of dollars the Trump family has made since he returned to the White House.

Republicans, led by Trump, attacked Democrats over culture war issues such as transgender rights while portraying their opponents as radical and extreme. But in poll after poll, voters made it clear they were far more concerned with pocketbook issues.

The Democratic wave flooded huge swaths of the country.

Republicans lost ground in all but a handful of the approximately 2,100 counties where most votes had been counted, according to tallies compiled by Reuters and USA Today.

View this post on Instagram

Democrats made gains in the richest counties and the poorest; in counties where more people have college degrees and where fewer do. Democrats' advances were particularly sharp ​in heavily Latino counties, including the border counties of Texas that shifted toward Trump in 2024 and the agricultural towns of the Kansas prairie.

In Seward County, Kansas, home to one of America's biggest beef processing plants and where about half of eligible voters are Hispanic, Democrat Adam Hamilton led ​incumbent Republican Senator Roger Marshall by 13 points, two years after Trump won the county by 39 points.

Democrats flipped more than two dozen House seats currently held by Republicans, locking in a majority. Democrats won all the closely contested House races that have been decided so far, and they won about a dozen races ‌in districts that Trump ⁠won by double digits two years ago.

An unprecedented Republican gambit to redraw several House districts to make them more favourable largely failed, with Democrats hanging on to most of the targeted seats.

Midterm elections are typically seen as a referendum on the sitting president, and Trump did little to disabuse voters of that notion. In the campaign's final weeks, he held dozens of rallies, telling supporters repeatedly to "pretend I'm on the ballot."

He also intervened in several Republican primaries earlier this year to ensure his preferred candidates reached the ballot, despite concerns from some Republicans that his choices carried significant liabilities.

In Texas, Trump backed Ken Paxton, the scandal-ridden state attorney general, over the incumbent, Senator John Cornyn.

"I just wasn't a fan of Cornyn. I just wasn't a fan. I found him to be a disloyal guy... When it wasn't fashionable to be with Trump, he wasn't there. When it was fashionable, he kissed my ass. I remember the other days, and I just felt I couldn't endorse him," Trump told Fox News today.

In South Carolina, the president anointed Darline Graham, a political neophyte, after her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, died suddenly earlier this year. Both candidates lost.

But even candidates who sought to distance themselves from Trump were unable to escape ​voters' wrath. In Maine, Republican incumbent Susan Collins had her 30-year Senate ​career end on Tuesday, despite emphasising her willingness to break with ⁠the president during the campaign.

Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open Senate seat, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber. He defeated Mike Rogers, a former congressman and FBI agent, who entered the race with Trump's backing and sought to falsely portray El-Sayed, an Egyptian American born in Michigan, as a religious extremist.

"You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope," El-Sayed told cheering supporters on Tuesday night, referring to Rogers.

Competitive Senate races in Mississippi and ​Alaska had yet to be called early on Wednesday.

On Tuesday night, as it grew clear Republicans were in danger of losing their congressional majorities, Trump wrote on social media, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if ​I was, we would have won IN ⁠A LANDSLIDE!"

In media interviews, Trump acknowledged the conflict with Iran had played a role in his party's losses but stood by his decision to go to war.

Voters rebuke Trump

According to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets, including major television networks and the Associated Press, half of voters nationwide said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the way the country is headed.

In addition, 70% of voters surveyed said they want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the president.

"In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people ⁠have rebuked the depravity, ​corruption and incompetence of the man named President Donald J Trump," incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia told supporters at a victory party.

Both parties witnessed several historic firsts.

In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of any US state, while Byron Donalds won Florida's gubernatorial race to become the first Black Republican governor in the US. Democrat Gina Hinojosa will become the first Latina governor in Texas, while Democrat Xavier Becerra will be California's first Latino governor.

Democrats seized control of both the Senate and House on Tuesday, scoring sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Voters in conservative bastions who had propelled the president to his second term in office just two years ago swung dramatically toward Democrats, fuelled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high cost of living and anger at Trump's stewardship of the country.

In Texas, the biggest Republican state, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning a Senate seat and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.

Kansas elected its first Democratic senator since the Great Depression nearly a ‌century ago. In South Carolina, a state that Trump carried by nearly 18 points in 2024, Democrats turned aside his hand-picked Senate candidate.

And in Texas, the biggest Republican state, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning a Senate seat and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.

The results will usher in a new era of divided government in Washington, following two years in which the Republican-controlled Congress rarely exercised its power to rein in Trump.

Once seated in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump's administration, family and allies and demand concessions on major legislation. The Democratic Senate can block Trump's nominees, including any US Supreme Court justices should a vacancy arise.

"There is now a generational remake of the Senate map that is going to change America," said Chuck Schumer, the party's Senate minority leader. "Americans voted for change, and now Democrats must deliver."

Trump, who is barred by the US Constitution from seeking a third term, has exercised an iron grip on his party for most of the last decade. But the new balance of power in Washington may ⁠accelerate his lame-duck status, as attention turns toward the 2028 presidential race and potential successors begin competing for political influence in a post-Trump world.

Despite worries from Democrats that Trump might seek to overturn the election results, as he did in 2020, the president accepted the outcome, congratulating Democrats in an interview with Fox News. He also said he would work with Democrats on issues such as immigration, though he threatened to veto any "insane" bills they passed.

Democratic wave

Democrats focused their campaign on corruption and affordability, blaming Trump's tariff policy and the war with Iran for driving up costs while highlighting the billions of dollars the Trump family has made since he returned to the White House.

Republicans, led by Trump, attacked Democrats over culture war issues such as transgender rights while portraying their opponents as radical and extreme. But in poll after poll, voters made it clear they were far more concerned with pocketbook issues.

The Democratic wave flooded huge swaths of the country.

Republicans lost ground in all but a handful of the approximately 2,100 counties where most votes had been counted, according to tallies compiled by Reuters and USA Today.

View this post on Instagram

Democrats made gains in the richest counties and the poorest; in counties where more people have college degrees and where fewer do. Democrats' advances were particularly sharp in heavily Latino counties, including the border counties of Texas that shifted toward Trump in 2024 and the agricultural towns of the Kansas prairie.

In Seward County, Kansas, home to one of America's biggest beef processing plants and where about half of eligible voters are Hispanic, Democrat Adam Hamilton led incumbent Republican Senator Roger Marshall by 13 points, two years after Trump won the county by 39 points.

Democrats flipped more than two dozen House seats currently held by Republicans, locking in a majority. Democrats won all the closely contested House races that have been decided so far, and they won about a dozen races ‌in districts that Trump ⁠won by double digits two years ago.

An unprecedented Republican gambit to redraw several House districts to make them more favourable largely failed, with Democrats hanging on to most of the targeted seats.

Midterm elections are typically seen as a referendum on the sitting president, and Trump did little to disabuse voters of that notion. In the campaign's final weeks, he held dozens of rallies, telling supporters repeatedly to "pretend I'm on the ballot."

He also intervened in several Republican primaries earlier this year to ensure his preferred candidates reached the ballot, despite concerns from some Republicans that his choices carried significant liabilities.

In Texas, Trump backed Ken Paxton, the scandal-ridden state attorney general, over the incumbent, Senator John Cornyn.

"I just wasn't a fan of Cornyn. I just wasn't a fan. I found him to be a disloyal guy... When it wasn't fashionable to be with Trump, he wasn't there. When it was fashionable, he kissed my ass. I remember the other days, and I just felt I couldn't endorse him," Trump told Fox News today.

In South Carolina, the president anointed Darline Graham, a political neophyte, after her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, died suddenly earlier this year. Both candidates lost.

But even candidates who sought to distance themselves from Trump were unable to escape voters' wrath. In Maine, Republican incumbent Susan Collins had her 30-year Senate career end on Tuesday, despite emphasising her willingness to break with ⁠the president during the campaign.

Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open Senate seat, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber. He defeated Mike Rogers, a former congressman and FBI agent, who entered the race with Trump's backing and sought to falsely portray El-Sayed, an Egyptian American born in Michigan, as a religious extremist.

"You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope," El-Sayed told cheering supporters on Tuesday night, referring to Rogers.

Competitive Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska had yet to be called early on Wednesday.

On Tuesday night, as it grew clear Republicans were in danger of losing their congressional majorities, Trump wrote on social media, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN ⁠A LANDSLIDE!"

In media interviews, Trump acknowledged the conflict with Iran had played a role in his party's losses but stood by his decision to go to war.

Voters rebuke Trump

According to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets, including major television networks and the Associated Press, half of voters nationwide said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the way the country is headed.

In addition, 70% of voters surveyed said they want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the president.

"In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people ⁠have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the man named President Donald J Trump," incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia told supporters at a victory party.

Both parties witnessed several historic firsts.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa will become the first Latina governor in Texas, while Democrat Xavier Becerra will be California's first Latino governor.

headline: Israel’s Shin Bet chief seeks to question Arab party leaders over suspected foreign interference in election: report
description: Attorney general calls bid to treat election inquiry as security case unlawful, says Shin Bet yet to share material
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israel’s Shin Bet Director David Zini sought to question three Arab party leaders in an inquiry into possible foreign interference in the Knesset election, even though law enforcement officials found no evidence to justify questioning them, the Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported Tuesday.

KAN identified the three as Mansour Abbas, leader of the United Arab List (Ra’am), Ahmad Tibi, leader of the Arab Movement for Change (Ta’al), and Sami Abu Shehadeh, leader of the Balad party. The broadcaster said investigators had information relevant to the inquiry concerning a fourth politician, a member of the Knesset.

In a separate report, Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth daily said Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara rejected Zini’s request to treat the entire inquiry as a security case at a meeting Sunday with Noam Sohlberg, the judge who chairs Israel’s Central Elections Committee.

The classification would have given the Shin Bet broader powers to deny suspects access to lawyers, tap their phones and collect communications data, the newspaper reported. Baharav-Miara called the request unlawful, while Sohlberg suggested recognising that the case could have a security dimension.

In a statement late Tuesday, Baharav-Miara said investigators needed evidence to justify questioning citizens or elected officials as suspects. She said the Shin Bet or any other agency could submit material that warranted questioning. She also said the Shin Bet had gone two days without turning over the material it had gathered to a special investigative team, delaying the inquiry.

The team was formed on Sohlberg’s recommendation and includes police investigators working under the supervision of state prosecutors.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party accused Baharav-Miara of obstructing the inquiry by blocking the Shin Bet from using powers available in security cases. It called on Sohlberg to explain the matter to the public.

The Joint List issued a statement saying that Zini had “lost his senses” and vowing to oppose any attempt by him or Netanyahu to portray the votes of hundreds of thousands of Arab citizens as a security threat or cast their elected representatives as suspects. “Arab voters do not need permission from Netanyahu or the Shin Bet chief to shape their political future,” the alliance said.

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition Yashar party, warned against using security agencies for political ends. He accused Netanyahu and Likud of trying to undermine public confidence in the election results after their bloc fell short of a parliamentary majority.

Likud has accused Qatar of funding efforts to boost Arab turnout and influence the outcome. The party has presented no public evidence of Qatari interference or widespread fraud. Qatar rejected the accusations last Thursday, describing them as a disinformation campaign aimed at drawing it into Israel’s domestic political disputes.

Sohlberg said late Tuesday that Israeli law required the final results to be published Wednesday and that no one had the authority to withhold them.

The results are due to be presented to President Isaac Herzog, who is expected to begin consultations with party representatives Wednesday on forming a government, according to the Israeli daily Maariv.

The vote count gave Netanyahu’s bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset and Eisenkot’s opposition bloc 48. The Joint List won 11 seats and Ra’am secured eight, giving the two Arab lists a combined 19 seats. Neither bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a majority.

headline: Oklahoma City man charged over threatening letters to election officials
description: Oklahoma City man charged over threatening letters to election officials
author: Reuters
article_text:
An Oklahoma City man was charged with sending hundreds of threatening letters containing white powder to state election officials, lawmakers, pollsters and media organisations ahead of the midterm congressional elections.

Robin Martin, 67, was charged in US District Court in Oklahoma with conveying false or misleading information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications.

Testing of powder found in the letters determined it was either harmless yeast or flour, the FBI said in an affidavit.

Martin, who was arrested Monday, was ordered temporarily detained Tuesday by a federal magistrate pending a November 9 hearing. Lawyers for Martin declined to comment.

Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg said the letters represented a "calculated attempt to terrorise public servants... Intimidation like this has no place in a Nation governed by the rule of law."

The FBI said mailings in early October were addressed to state election officials in all 50 states. It also believes Martin had sent threatening letters in 2024 to election and postal officials.

The threatening letters in October bore an outdated return address of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) in New York, the FBI said.

It added that Martin had also made contact with the DSA in August and obtained the email addresses of DSA members, after which they were added to a mailing list that sent them threatening messages, warning they could be arrested if they voted.

The FBI also linked Martin to a threatening letter in 2024 that "claimed that President Donald Trump won the 2020 election, and voiced concerns regarding some of the same issues recurring in the then-upcoming 2024 election."

The FBI tied the letters to Martin through surveillance video from postal facilities and a Walmart, where a phone believed to have been used in the threats had been purchased.

The government said Martin had also written a letter to FBI Director Kash Patel that was determined to have Martin's fingerprints. The letter had a message written in ultraviolet-reactive ink reading "FBI SAVE THE USA" that was also on other threatening letters.

headline: Cunha inspires Manchester United comeback
description: The Red Devils snatch a 3-2 win over Roma while PSG demolish Villarreal 6-0
author: AFP
article_text:
Manchester United fought back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday to hand beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a reprieve, while holders Paris Saint-Germain continued their perfect start in the competition by hitting Villarreal for six.

Looking set for another abject defeat when two behind within 18 minutes through a smart Mathias Soule finish and Donyell Malen's penalty, United staged a thrilling comeback in the second half to turn a poisonous atmosphere at Old Trafford to one of joy.

Matheus Cunha, who was sent off in stoppage time, saved the day for United with a brace in three minutes with the final whistle nearing, sparking wild celebrations in the stands.

Those scenes at the end of the game couldn't have been more different to the anger which pulsated around the ground in the first half, when United fans threw tennis balls and other objects onto the Old Trafford pitch and directed foul-mouthed chants at the club's majority owners, the Glazer family.

"We knew that the fans would be behind us until the last day, we just had to get a result for them," United captain Bruno Fernandes told TNT.

United head into Sunday's match with Aston Villa, beaten 3-0 at Barcelona, in an entirely different mood after punishing slapdash Roma who vanished in the second half after having shown why they look like league title contenders in Italy.

"I spoke at half-time about being positive. Anything can happen here, I've seen it many times over the years," said Carrick. "You just need something to go our way and the boys were fantastic second half."

Roma, who also threw away a commanding lead against Real Madrid in their only other defeat of the season, failed to deal a knockout blow and crumbled once Bruno Fernandes pulled United back into the game in the 58th minute at the second time of asking from the penalty spot.

The Portuguese thumped home past Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, who saved the first attempt but was let down by his teammates encroaching in the penalty area.

And that set up Cunha to hit Roma with a one-two that decided a thrilling encounter and gave Carrick some breathing room with the international break coming up after the weekend.

Perfect PSG

PSG were in ruthless mood even without star player Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as they beat Villarreal 6-0 on a night in which Europe's elite clubs paid tribute to tragic Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel with a moment's silence before kick-offs.

De Miguel died aged 30 from injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second-division match, leaving football in mourning and condolences pouring in from around the globe.

PSG tore into sorry Villarreal, with Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all striking in eight first-half minutes as the French outfit set a record for the fastest four goals scored in a match in Europe's elite club competition.

It certainly didn't look like PSG were missing Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, captain Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes, and further strikes from Spain World Cup star Ruiz and teenager David Boly rounded off a stellar performance which put Luis Enrique's team top of the table.

"We were impressive throughout and we are really pleased even if it is very difficult for Villarreal," said Luis Enrique. "But it is hard when you play against a team like us that presses constantly."

Another team missing a host of stars in Bayern Munich saw off Atletico Madrid 2-0 to move into the top eight positions.

Teenage Germany forward Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer netted in the second half in Madrid as Bayern triumphed despite the absence of Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari.

Inter Milan recovered from derby defeat at the weekend with a comfortable 3-0 win over Feyenoord which came through goals from Yann Bisseck, Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski.

headline: FM Dar congratulates Oliver Blanco on appointment as Venezuela's foreign minister
description: Asim Iftikhar meets British, Japanese envoys, discusses bilateral ties, regional developments, cooperation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday congratulated Oliver Blanco on his appointment as Venezuela's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade and expressed his desire to further strengthen bilateral relations between Pakistan and Venezuela.

In a post on X, Dar extended “warm felicitations” to Blanco on his appointment as foreign minister of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

“I wish Foreign Minister Blanco every success in his new responsibilities and look forward to working closely with him to further strengthen the friendly ties and mutually beneficial cooperation between Pakistan and Venezuela,” he wrote.

Responding to Dar's post on X, Blanco thanked him for his wishes and expressed his willingness to work together to strengthen bilateral relations.

“Thank you for your kind words and warm wishes. I look forward to working closely together to further strengthen the bonds of friendship between Venezuela and Pakistan and advance our cooperation for the mutual benefit of our peoples,” he wrote.

Earlier, Foreign Secretary Asim Iftikhar Ahmad received British High Commissioner Jane Marriott, with discussions focused on bilateral ties between Pakistan and the United Kingdom, as well as regional and global developments, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said in a post on X.

He also met Japanese Ambassador to Pakistan Akamatsu Shuichi and exchanged views on strengthening multifaceted cooperation between Pakistan and Japan, MoFA said in a separate post on X.

headline: NASA's Swift satellite telescope heads for fiery re-entry 22 years after launch
description: NASA's Swift satellite telescope heads for fiery re-entry 22 years after launch
author: Reuters
article_text:
An ageing NASA satellite telescope that a robotic spacecraft was sent to retrieve on a failed rescue mission this summer was headed for a fiery re-entry into Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday, nearly 22 years after it was launched into orbit.

The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, weighing roughly 3,200 pounds (1,452 kg), was set to tumble out of orbit and burn up in the atmosphere somewhere over the tropics, with fragments surviving re-entry unlikely to threaten populated areas, according to NASA.

The US Space Force has put the odds of harm coming to anyone on Earth at one chance in 2,100, NASA said in an online statement, projecting the time of re-entry at approximately 3:30am EST (0830 GMT). The Aerospace Corporation, a non-profit national security research entity, projected a re-entry window of 5:19am EST, plus or minus two hours.

London-based astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, an honorary professor at the Durham University Space Research Centre, cited revised US Space Force data predicting re-entry most likely to come around 7:45am EST.

"The satellite is in a very circular orbit, skimming the top of the atmosphere," he told Reuters by phone on Tuesday night. "The question is at what point does it heat up enough that it starts breaking up."

NASA's prized $500 million Swift satellite, a first-of-its-kind multi-wavelength space observatory, has been studying gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena since 2004, using its array of three telescopes.

The observatory, which has no onboard propulsion system of its own, has been drifting towards an expected demise for months as it circles the globe at a speed of roughly 17,000 miles per hour (27,359 kph).

Astronomers had hoped to extend Swift's mission for a number of years by giving the satellite telescope a lift.

In July, NASA and Arizona-based start-up Katalyst launched a specially built rescue vehicle called LINK on a mission to rendezvous with Swift, latch onto the satellite and tug the observatory back into a higher, more sustainable orbit.

But the LINK spacecraft itself began spinning uncontrollably soon after reaching space, and by mid-August, mission managers abandoned the effort, resigned to letting Swift continue to meet its fate.

The aborted rescue attempt, the first US mission of its kind, took on heightened significance as a demonstration of a new orbital grappling technology seen as pivotal to the outcome of the US-China space race.

The LINK effort was closely watched as a trial run of a key satellite-maintenance technology with potential dual-use military space applications.

Katalyst touted the mission as a historic endeavour that designed, built and tested the LINK rescue vehicle on an unprecedented nine-month production schedule under a $30 million NASA contract.

Swift was launched more than two decades ago to explore the most powerful known explosions in the universe, bursts of gamma-ray radiation emanating from the cores of distant galaxies.

Originally designed for a two-year prime mission, Swift remained in operation far longer with observations of a wide range of cosmic objects, from galaxies powered by supermassive black holes and stars emitting X-ray flares, to comets and asteroids streaking through our own solar system.

headline: Israel faces uncertainty over arms deals after Trump vows to end US aid
description: KAN estimates Israel’s defence budget would face a shortfall of $3.8 billion a year if US aid ends in January
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli defence and finance officials are assessing how the country would pay for weapons already on order and replenish military stocks depleted by three years of war after US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would end aid to Israel by year’s end, Israeli media reported on Tuesday.

Speaking to Fox News on Tuesday, Trump put annual US aid at $4 billion and said he had reached an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu months earlier to stop it. “We won’t be paying any more to Israel,” he said. He added that Washington would still help Israel if needed and would continue selling it weapons.

A potential gap in the defence budget

Israel’s Finance Ministry first learned of the plan when Trump announced it, Channel 12 reported. The $3.8 billion in annual US military assistance had been expected to help finance Israel’s defence budgets in 2027 and 2028.

A senior defence official told Israeli public broadcaster KAN that the announcement had come as a surprise despite ongoing talks with US counterparts. The official said the relevant agencies had yet to receive the decision and would assess its implications.

Just two weeks earlier, on October 20, an Israeli Defence Ministry delegation had visited Alabama to discuss future purchases with US Army Security Assistance Command officials, KAN reported.

KAN economic commentator Shaul Amsterdamski estimated that if the cutoff began in January, it would leave an immediate gap of 12 billion shekels ($3.8 billion) a year in the defence budget. He said the ministry had already made spending commitments and that the government could cover the shortfall through higher taxes, spending cuts or faster growth that brought in more tax revenue. He considered higher taxes the likeliest outcome.

Who pays for jets already on order?

Officials familiar with Israel’s security talks with Washington told Channel 12 they wanted to know where the money would come from for fighter jets covered by contracts already signed and what currency Israel would use to pay for them.

Officials were also trying to establish whether Trump’s announcement meant funding would stop at the end of the year or whether the two countries would shift gradually to a different model of defence cooperation, the channel reported.

Under a 10-year memorandum signed in 2016, Washington committed $38 billion in military assistance to Israel through 2028. The two countries began formal talks in May on a successor arrangement. The implications of Trump’s announcement for existing commitments and those talks remain unclear.

Years of fighting have depleted military stocks

The Israeli daily Maariv reported that the air force logged as many flight hours over the past three years as it would normally fly in nine years of peacetime, increasing wear on aircraft and adding to maintenance demands.

The newspaper said tanks and armoured personnel carriers went through thousands of engines over the same period. It also reported that the military used as much ammunition in those three years as it had in the three decades before the war.

Maariv said an end to US funding would make it harder for the military to replace that ammunition and equipment, adding to the cost of financing purchases Israel has already agreed to make.

headline: Polio team supervisor abducted during vaccination drive in K-P's Jamrud
description: DPO says Jalil Khan picked up by unidentified armed men as recovery efforts underway
author: Ali Murad
article_text:
A polio campaign team supervisor, identified as Jalil Khan, was abducted by unidentified armed men from the Chapri area of Jamrud in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) during the ongoing seven-day polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Waqar Ahmad said on Wednesday.

According to the DPO, the armed men took Khan to an undisclosed location. A heavy contingent of police was dispatched to the area following the incident, while blockades were set up on key routes in an effort to recover the abducted supervisor, he said.

A day earlier, two policemen were martyred, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a polio vaccination team in K-P's Mohmand district. One terrorist was also injured in the incident.

Earlier in the week, four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being subjected to gunfire in K-P's Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Lower South Waziristan, were subsequently released.

The incident in Tank occurred in the village of Jious, located in the Sheikh Attar union council, where unidentified armed men abducted four polio workers. The gunmen reportedly took all four workers to an undisclosed location.

In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan. Sources said armed men affiliated with the proscribed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were allegedly involved in the kidnapping. However, both polio workers were later released.

The incidents came amid a special anti-polio campaign launched on November 2 in 97 selected districts across the country. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication, the campaign will continue until November 8.

NEOC confirmed Pakistan’s seventh polio case of the year, reported from Khyber district of K-P. The affected child was a 13-month-old girl belonging to Jan Baz Union Council in Bara tehsil, the NEOC said. This was the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year and the sixth from K-P.

The incidents came amid a special anti-polio campaign launched on November 2 in 97 selected districts across the country. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication, the campaign will continue until November 8.

NEOC confirmed Pakistan’s seventh polio case of the year, reported from Khyber district of K-P. The affected child was a 13-month-old girl belonging to Jan Baz Union Council in Bara tehsil, the NEOC said. This was the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year and the sixth from K-P.

headline: Pakistan's Test revival begins against Sri Lanka
description: Hesson orders fast tracks; Azan, Fazal emerge as leading contenders to open the innings against
author: Saleem Khaliq
article_text: Pakistan have decided to put an end to their disappointing performances on lively pitches, with head coach Mike Hesson directing efforts to prepare pace-friendly surfaces for both home Test matches against Sri Lanka. Five players from the playing XI that featured in the final Test against England are now out of contention, meaning Pakistan will have to make several changes to their line-up. The team is also expected to field a new opening combination in its first home Test series of the year. Meanwhile, Babar Azam is featuring in a domestic four-day match on Hesson's advice as he looks to regain his batting form. Pakistan's performance in Test cricket in 2026 has been disappointing, with the team losing six of its seven matches. The Green-shirts suffered whitewash in two series, while another series ended in a 1-1 draw. Pakistan are currently ranked ninth among ten teams in the ICC Test rankings and occupy the bottom, ninth position in the World Test Championship standings. The team management has now begun taking steps to turn things around. Following their triumph in the tri-nation ODI series, Pakistan's next assignment is a two-match Test series against Sri Lanka. The first Test will begin in Rawalpindi on November 9, while the second is scheduled to start in Lahore on November 17. Remarkably, Pakistan will be playing their first home Test of the year in November, despite having already featured in seven Tests across three overseas series. The team managed just one victory during that period, which came in the West Indies, while its overseas campaign had also begun with a defeat. Before that, Pakistan lost both Tests in Bangladesh, while England handed them a humiliating 3-0 series whitewash in the most recent series. Sources revealed that the team management has now agreed to prepare more competitive and lively pitches at home to help the side overcome its struggles on pace-friendly surfaces during overseas tours. Hesson has instructed the ground staff to prepare fast tracks for both Tests against Sri Lanka. Groundsmen are working to produce surfaces that offer greater assistance to fast bowlers. Following the three-day match against Sri Lanka, two fast bowlers from the PCB Patron's XI are expected to be added to the national squad. Mohammad Abbas and Razaullah appear certain to receive call-ups. Five players from the XI that featured in the final Test against England including Saim Ayub, Abdullah Shafique, Shan Masood, Mohammad Imran and Mohammad Ali are no longer part of the team's plans, making a significant overhaul inevitable. Shan Masood scored 95 runs in the first innings of the Birmingham Test. However, the coach reportedly believes it is time to give a younger player an opportunity in place of the 37-year-old batter. The opening combination is also set for a change, with Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal currently emerging as the leading contenders to open the innings. Sources further revealed that Hesson had advised Babar Azam to feature in a domestic four-day match to regain his batting rhythm. As a result, the former Pakistan captain is currently representing his side in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. The PCB's decision to make participation in domestic competitions compulsory has also ensured that star players are representing their respective departments and regions, even if some are reluctant to do so. Pakistan are currently ninth among ten teams in the ICC Test rankings, with only Zimbabwe below them. The Green-shirts also occupy ninth place, the bottom position, in the World Test Championship standings. The Pakistan Cricket Board's think tank has already begun implementing measures to improve the team's performance in the next World Test Championship cycle. Officials are hopeful that the inclusion of young players, combined with a more aggressive approach to Test cricket, will help revive Pakistan's fortunes.

headline: The Elder Scrolls VI reportedly still over two years away despite title reveal
description: Bethesda has revealed The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, but release could still be years away
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Bethesda has officially revealed the title of its long-awaited next instalment in The Elder Scrolls franchise, but fans may still have more than two years to wait before its release.

The game was confirmed as The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel in a video celebrating 40 years of Bethesda Game Studios. However, the announcement offered little beyond the new logo, with no gameplay footage, release window or platform details.

Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier addressed the reveal on Bluesky, pointing out that the game was originally announced alongside Starfield in 2018.

He explained that Bethesda had initially revealed the project partly to reassure fans following the announcement of Fallout 76.

“Sorry to say this game is still more than 2 years away!” Schreier wrote.

The latest announcement comes nearly eight years after the original teaser, which showed a mountainous landscape and confirmed that the project was in pre-production.

Since then, Bethesda has released Fallout 76, Starfield and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, while providing limited updates on its next mainline fantasy RPG.

Schreier previously estimated in a July Bloomberg Q&A that the game was at least two to three years away. His latest comments suggest that a 2028 release may be the earliest possibility, although Bethesda has not announced a launch date.

The studio has confirmed that Sentinel is its primary development focus, with most of its team working on the project. The game is being developed using Creation Engine 3, and internal builds are reportedly playable.

headline: Fact check: Glenn Phillips did not score 16-ball century against India
description: Fact check: Viral claim of Glenn Phillips scoring 16-ball century against India is false
author: Fact Check By iVerify
article_text:
Multiple Pakistani users on social media platform X shared videos since Tuesday claiming that New Zealand batter Glenn Phillips scored a century off just 16 balls, hitting sixes in succession against India. However, Phillips scored 107 runs off 49 deliveries.

India's tour of New Zealand began on October 22, 2026, with a five-match Twenty20 International (T20I) series, followed by five One Day Internationals (ODIs) and two Test matches. The ODI series was scheduled to begin on November 4 in Auckland, with the final match set for November 15.

On Oct 30, New Zealand defeated India by 87 runs in the fourth T20I at Eden Park in Auckland. New Zealand posted 259-7 in their allotted 20 overs, while India managed 172-9 in response.

Phillips played a crucial role in the victory, scoring a century. New Zealand team also won the final T20I on November 1 by seven wickets. However, India clinched the five-match series 3-2.

How it started

A day earlier, an X user who appeared to be a journalist, based on their profile bio and posts, shared a viral video showing Phillips hitting sixes against India, along with a scoreboard showing 100 runs off 16 balls.

The caption said: "New Zealand's batsman Phillips smashed India with a barrage of boundaries, hitting 6 sixes in 1 over, and smashed a century off 16 balls."

The post gained 552,200 views.

Today, another X user, who also appeared to be a journalist based on their bio and posts, shared the same clip with the following caption: “Two new world records. A century in 16 balls, six after six. New Zealand has set a new trend and completely thrashed India.”

The post garnered 45,300 views.

Subsequently, the video was shared by other users, as can be seen here, here, here, here, here, here, and here, collectively gaining 178,962 views.

Methodology

A fact-check was initiated to verify the claim due to its widespread circulation on social media and significant public interest in the purported record-breaking feat, particularly whether scoring a century in just 16 balls was possible.

A keyword search was conducted to determine whether any credible sports news outlets had reported the record-breaking century. However, no such reports were found.

Multiple Pakistani users on social media platform X shared videos since Tuesday claiming that New Zealand batter Glenn Phillips scored a century off just 16 balls, hitting sixes in succession against India. However, Phillips scored 107 runs off 49 deliveries.

India's tour of New Zealand began on October 22, 2026, with a five-match Twenty20 International (T20I) series, followed by five One Day Internationals (ODIs) and two Test matches. The ODI series was scheduled to begin on November 4 in Auckland, with the final match set for November 15.

On Oct 30, New Zealand defeated India by 87 runs in the fourth T20I at Eden Park in Auckland. New Zealand posted 259-7 in their allotted 20 overs, while India managed 172-9 in response.

Phillips played a crucial role in the victory, scoring a century. New Zealand team also won the final T20I on November 1 by seven wickets. However, India clinched the five-match series 3-2.

How it started

A day earlier, an X user who appeared to be a journalist, based on their profile bio and posts, shared a viral video showing Phillips hitting sixes against India, along with a scoreboard showing 100 runs off 16 balls.

The caption said: "New Zealand's batsman Phillips smashed India with a barrage of boundaries, hitting 6 sixes in 1 over, and smashed a century off 16 balls."

The post gained 552,200 views.

Today, another X user, who also appeared to be a journalist based on their bio and posts, shared the same clip with the following caption: “Two new world records. A century in 16 balls, six after six. New Zealand has set a new trend and completely thrashed India.”

The post garnered 45,300 views.

Subsequently, the video was shared by other users, as can be seen here, here, here, here, here, here, and here, collectively gaining 178,962 views.

Methodology

A fact-check was initiated to verify the claim due to its widespread circulation on social media and significant public interest in the purported record-breaking feat, particularly whether scoring a century in just 16 balls was possible.

A keyword search was conducted to determine whether any credible sports news outlets had reported the record-breaking century. However, no such reports were found.

A further keyword search for the fastest century in T20 international cricket revealed that Estonia's Sahil Chauhan holds the record, reaching 100 runs in just 27 balls against Cyprus on June 17, 2024, as reported by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

Meanwhile, South African cricketer AB de Villiers holds the record for the fastest century in ODI cricket, scoring 100 runs off 31 deliveries against the West Indies on January 18, 2015.

Furthermore, even if a batter hit six sixes in succession and scored a six off each of 16 deliveries, the total would amount to just 96 runs, falling four runs short of a century.

Further examination of the match scorecard on Cricbuzz revealed that Phillips scored 107 runs off 49 deliveries, hitting 10 sixes and six fours against India on October 30, 2026. The figures were also corroborated by a report published by the ICC, confirming that the viral claim of a century in just 16 balls was false.

headline: Abdul El-Sayed becomes 1st Muslim elected to US Senate in Michigan win
description: El-Sayed defeats Republican Mike Rogers, retaining crucial Democratic-held seat in closely contested race
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate after defeating former Republican Representative Mike Rogers in Michigan's closely watched race Tuesday, holding onto a crucial Democratic-held seat, according to projections by US media.

El-Sayed, a medical doctor and former public health official, won a competitive Democratic primary to run for the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters.

His historic victory came after a contentious campaign in which his Muslim faith became a central issue, with President Donald Trump and other Republicans repeatedly attacking him over his religious background.

El-Sayed rejected allegations linking him to extremism.

The victory also comes in a state narrowly won by Trump in the 2024 presidential election.

El-Sayed will become the first Muslim to serve in the Senate when the new Congress convenes in January.

'Bad guys lost ... We won!'

He celebrated his projected victory in Michigan early Wednesday, delivering an emotional message to supporters while taking direct aim at Trump and Vice President JD Vance.

Speaking at his election-night watch party, El-Sayed thanked Michigan voters and pledged to bring the same determination, openness, and compassion to the US Senate that he said voters had demonstrated throughout his campaign.

“Michigan, I cannot wait to serve you with the same big-heartedness, open-mindedness, grit, and earnestness that you've shown me,” El-Sayed told supporters.

He urged supporters to celebrate the result as a collective victory, framing the outcome as a rejection of his political opponents and a triumph for those who had campaigned for a broader political cause.

“Let them know tomorrow that the bad guys lost,” he said. “Let them know that we together, fighting for something bigger, we won. We won! So Mike, enjoy your retirement."

The Democratic candidate also directed pointed remarks toward Vance, referencing the constitutional process through which newly elected senators are sworn into office.

“There is this delicious irony in the fact that you're constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January,” said El-Sayed.

He then addressed Trump, citing the president's campaign rallies where he made a show of having trouble pronouncing El-Sayed’s name.

“Donald, look, I know you struggled with my name,” El-Sayed said. “So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator."

El-Sayed's early life

Born in Rochester Hills, Michigan, to Egyptian immigrant parents, El-Sayed pursued a career in medicine and public health before entering politics.

He graduated from the University of Michigan in 2007, earned a doctorate in public health from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar in 2011, and received his medical degree from Columbia University in 2014.

In 2015, he became health director for Detroit, Michigan’s largest city, overseeing efforts to rebuild the city's public health services following its financial crisis.

He held the position until 2017 before making an unsuccessful bid for Michigan governor in 2018, losing the Democratic primary to Gretchen Whitmer.

El-Sayed later served as director of the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services from 2023 to 2025, which includes Detroit.

Political rise and historic Senate bid

El-Sayed returned to electoral politics in 2026, defeating Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary in August.

His campaign attracted support from prominent progressive figures, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib.

He campaigned on expanding healthcare access through Medicare for All, lowering housing costs, reducing the influence of wealthy donors in politics, and strengthening economic opportunities for working families.

On foreign policy, El-Sayed emerged as an outspoken critic of US military support for Israel, describing Israel's military campaign in Gaza as genocide and calling for an end to unconditional American military assistance.

His positions on Israel became a central source of controversy during the campaign.

Stevens, whom he defeated in the Democratic primary, broke with her party just two days before the general election and endorsed Rogers, citing her concerns over El-Sayed's campaign rhetoric and political associations.

Her move drew a strong backlash among fellow Democrats while failing to derail El-Sayed’s path to victory.

Faith and political identity

El-Sayed's Muslim identity also became a prominent issue during the Senate race, with President Donald Trump and other Republican figures repeatedly criticising him over his faith and political positions.

El-Sayed rejected the attacks, arguing that the president was using his name and religion to divert attention from rising living costs and economic challenges facing Americans.

His election marks a historic first for the Senate, although Muslim Americans have previously served in the House of Representatives.

Keith Ellison became the first Muslim elected to Congress in 2006, while Rashida Tlaib and Ilhan Omar became the first Muslim women elected to Congress in 2018.
