Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate after defeating former Republican Representative Mike Rogers in Michigan's closely watched race Tuesday, holding onto a crucial Democratic-held seat, according to projections by US media.

El-Sayed, a medical doctor and former public health official, won a competitive Democratic primary to run for the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters.

His historic victory came after a contentious campaign in which his Muslim faith became a central issue, with President Donald Trump and other Republicans repeatedly attacking him over his religious background.

BREAKING: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan’s U.S. Senate race, becoming the first Muslim senator in American history. pic.twitter.com/Vr6jdDIxa5

— Washington Report (@Washington_Rep) November 4, 2026

El-Sayed rejected allegations linking him to extremism.

The victory also comes in a state narrowly won by Trump in the 2024 presidential election.

El-Sayed will become the first Muslim to serve in the Senate when the new Congress convenes in January.

'Bad guys lost ... We won!'

He celebrated his projected victory in Michigan early Wednesday, delivering an emotional message to supporters while taking direct aim at Trump and Vice President JD Vance.

Speaking at his election-night watch party, El-Sayed thanked Michigan voters and pledged to bring the same determination, openness, and compassion to the US Senate that he said voters had demonstrated throughout his campaign.

“Michigan, I cannot wait to serve you with the same big-heartedness, open-mindedness, grit, and earnestness that you've shown me,” El-Sayed told supporters.

Read: Democrats capture Congress in sweeping setback for Trump

He urged supporters to celebrate the result as a collective victory, framing the outcome as a rejection of his political opponents and a triumph for those who had campaigned for a broader political cause.

“Let them know tomorrow that the bad guys lost,” he said. “Let them know that we together, fighting for something bigger, we won. We won! So Mike, enjoy your retirement."

The Democratic candidate also directed pointed remarks toward Vance, referencing the constitutional process through which newly elected senators are sworn into office.

“There is this delicious irony in the fact that you're constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January,” said El-Sayed.

He then addressed Trump, citing the president's campaign rallies where he made a show of having trouble pronouncing El-Sayed’s name.

“Donald, look, I know you struggled with my name,” El-Sayed said. “So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator."

El-Sayed's early life

Born in Rochester Hills, Michigan, to Egyptian immigrant parents, El-Sayed pursued a career in medicine and public health before entering politics.

He graduated from the University of Michigan in 2007, earned a doctorate in public health from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar in 2011, and received his medical degree from Columbia University in 2014.

In 2015, he became health director for Detroit, Michigan’s largest city, overseeing efforts to rebuild the city's public health services following its financial crisis.

He held the position until 2017 before making an unsuccessful bid for Michigan governor in 2018, losing the Democratic primary to Gretchen Whitmer.

El-Sayed later served as director of the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services from 2023 to 2025, which includes Detroit.

Political rise and historic Senate bid

El-Sayed returned to electoral politics in 2026, defeating Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary in August.

His campaign attracted support from prominent progressive figures, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib.

He campaigned on expanding healthcare access through Medicare for All, lowering housing costs, reducing the influence of wealthy donors in politics, and strengthening economic opportunities for working families.

On foreign policy, El-Sayed emerged as an outspoken critic of US military support for Israel, describing Israel's military campaign in Gaza as genocide and calling for an end to unconditional American military assistance.

His positions on Israel became a central source of controversy during the campaign.

Stevens, whom he defeated in the Democratic primary, broke with her party just two days before the general election and endorsed Rogers, citing her concerns over El-Sayed's campaign rhetoric and political associations.

Her move drew a strong backlash among fellow Democrats while failing to derail El-Sayed’s path to victory.

Faith and political identity

El-Sayed's Muslim identity also became a prominent issue during the Senate race, with President Donald Trump and other Republican figures repeatedly criticising him over his faith and political positions.

El-Sayed rejected the attacks, arguing that the president was using his name and religion to divert attention from rising living costs and economic challenges facing Americans.

His election marks a historic first for the Senate, although Muslim Americans have previously served in the House of Representatives.

Keith Ellison became the first Muslim elected to Congress in 2006, while Rashida Tlaib and Ilhan Omar became the first Muslim women elected to Congress in 2018.

headline: Trump acknowledges role of Iran war in Democratic sweep in midterm elections
description: Says ​war ⁠in Iran had weighed on Republican candidates, even as voters ​backed his handling of it
author: AFP
article_text:
US President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the US-Israeli war on Iran played a role in his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections, as ​Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the ​Senate.

"I think a part of it was Iran," ⁠Trump told Fox News in an interview; "Iran was a ​piece of it," he separately told The Wall Street ​Journal.

But despite the Republican losses on Tuesday -- and his campaign promise of "no new wars" -- Trump stood by his decision to attack Iran.

"I ​did the right thing," he said in his ​interview with the Wall Street Journal. "I would have done it again."

The ‌war, ⁠now in its ninth month, has been unpopular among Americans since it began. On the campaign trail, Democratic candidates across the country blamed the conflict for driving up the ​cost of ​gas and other ⁠goods.

Trump has offered shifting goals and timelines for the war, alternately threatening to ramp ​up US military strikes and saying he could ​end ⁠the conflict at any time.

"Buckle up"

Trump posted later that he was going to "become a political pundit" and give the reasons why Republicans lost.

First in his crosshairs was Greg Abbott, the loyal Texas governor unseated by Democrat Gina Hinojosa. Trump said that if Abbott hadn't become a "RINO" (Republican In Name Only) "he wouldn't have lost".

Many of them Trump had hand-picked and traveled across the country to rally support for – even lavishing praise, in one case, on the "ass" of Republican Ohio Senate candidate Jon Husted.

But the White House also called the quality of the Republicans into question.

"Candidate quality matters, and President Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves," a White House official said.

Earlier, there was a bunker mentality in the White House as Trump and his top cabinet members watched the bruising results come in at a reception in the lavish East Room.

Some White House staffers dined on take-out from US chain restaurant The Cheesecake Factory – a dig at Democratic former president Barack Obama, who had said Trump's White House renovations were "looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory".

The question now is how Trump will react to being a lame duck president for the last two years of his second term, with Democrats in control of both the House and Senate.

The White House indicated that Trump is unlikely to go quietly.

Iran is on his mind and there is widespread speculation that the president will resume large-scale military action against Tehran – doubling down on a war that it is now clear voters loathed.

"Anyone who voted Democrat today is going to have a serious case of buyer's remorse when gas prices come down quickly when the Iran conflict is solved but they're still stuck with a list of liberal extremist Democrats," the White House official said.

The White House also gave a dark hint of retribution against his political enemies.

"A final note here: regardless of how today plays out, President Trump's resolve to stop the Radical Left is only going to become stronger. Buckle up."

article_text:
Novak Djokovic battled from behind to beat Valentin Vacherot 6-7 (5/7), 7-5, 6-1 in the first round of the Paris Masters on Tuesday, while Ben Shelton opened his campaign with a comfortable win.

For the Serbian 24-time Grand Slam champion, it marked a return to winning ways at ATP 1000-level tournaments for the first time since his run to the fourth round at Indian Wells back in March.

Djokovic also exacted his own bit of revenge on Vacherot in just the second meeting between the pair -- the Monegasque downed the 39-year-old on his way to a sensational Shanghai Masters title last season.

"I knew that coming into the court it was going to be a very tight match as it was," Djokovic told reporters.

"He's very confident and he's one of the best servers we have in the game," he added of Vacherot, who lifted the second title of his career last week in Basel.

Victory also kept alive Djokovic's chances of landing a spot in the season-ending ATP Finals later in November.

Djokovic is currently 11th in the race to the eight-man tournament in Turin.

However, he insisted his main focus was not the ATP Finals but "to win every match" on his return to the Paris Masters. In his last appearance at the tournament in 2023, he lifted the trophy for the seventh time.

In an even opening frame, Vacherot got his nose in front at the end of an error-strewn first-set tie-break as he put together a run of four points to take the lead.

After going down a break early in the second set, Djokovic called for a medical timeout for a massage on his right shoulder.

The short stoppage seemed to break Vacherot's concentration as he dropped his serve straight away.

On Djokovic's second break point, the 27-year-old completely misjudged a routine return from his opponent and could only watch in disbelief as the ball bounced on the line right in front of him.

Vacherot then received treatment for a foot issue and soon found himself level at one set each as Djokovic displayed his trademark killer instinct to seize his first break opportunity in the 12th game of the set and send the match to a decider.

The 10th seed ground down Vacherot in his first service game to get his nose in front before then running away with the match.

He will next meet Rinky Hijikata in the second round on Wednesday.

Monfils goodbye

US Open finalist Shelton, who as third seed enjoyed a bye through the first round, put on a commanding display in the night session with a 6-3, 6-4 win over Cameron Norrie.

The world number four needed just 71 minutes to see off the former eighth-ranked Briton, with the only hiccup being a break of his own serve near the end of the second set which the 24-year-old instantly righted to close in on victory.

The American then ceded centre stage to Gael Monfils for a ceremony to honour the career of the hugely popular French player, who retired last month at the age of 40.

Rising star Rafael Jodar was last on centre court but fell in straight sets to former world number two Casper Ruud.

The 20-year-old Spaniard currently sits ninth in the race to Turin, and his defeat meant Italy's Flavio Cobolli secured his spot in the season-ender despite having to withdraw from the Paris Masters with a leg injury. Elsewhere, Holger Rune, who beat Djokovic in the 2022 final, exited at the first hurdle this time as he continues his return from a lengthy lay-off. The Dane lost 7-5, 6-4 to Tommy Paul.

Matteo Berrettini edged out 14th seed Brandon Nakashima 6-4, 3-6, 7-6 (10/8) and Taylor Fritz showed grit to see off Benjamin Bonzi in three sets.

New home favourite Moise Kouame was unable to recreate his Roland Garros heroics as the French 17-year-old went down 6-3, 6-1 to lucky loser Nuno Borges.

Play continues on Wednesday when world number one Alexander Zverev and seven-time major winner Carlos Alcaraz will both get their tournaments underway at the round-of-32 stage.

headline: Carney rules out Russia at World Hockey Juniors
description: The government vows to keep Russian and Belarusian competitors out of the tournament
author: AFP
article_text:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed Tuesday that Russians would not compete at next month's World Junior Hockey Championships despite being reinstated by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, are set to host the tournament of future NHL stars from December 26, 2026, to January 5, 2027.

Speaking to reporters at a Commonwealth summit in Antigua, Carney made his position clear that Russia's war in Ukraine and support from Belarus will keep those nations on the sidelines.

"Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific war in Ukraine. As long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Carney said.

"So if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there."

Russian talent has been banned from global competition by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022, after being a major world power in the sport for decades. But Russia was reinstated by CAS to ice hockey world championships on Friday.

Since that decision, rivals Finland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark and the Czechs have said they will not play against Russia at the next world championships.

A field of 10 nations is already set to compete in Canada including the Canadians, United States, defending champion Sweden, Latvia, Finland, Germany, Slovakia, Norway, Czechia and Switzerland.

Immigration Minister Lena Metlege Diab also said in a government statement that Canada's opposition to Russia participating in global sporting events would continue.

"Canada's position has not changed because Russia's actions have not changed," the statement said.

"Canada remains committed to ensuring that sport is not used to confer legitimacy, prestige or international standing on such states."

Diab will "exercise her authorities (to) prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering Canada.

"Canada will also continue to require that events receiving Government of Canada funding prohibit the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes under their national symbols."

headline: Inter cruise past Feyenoord
description: Bisseck, Esposito and Zielinski score in a 3-0 victory
author: AFP
article_text:
Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck.

The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter's pace and attacking ability.

"We knew that quality was already there. It was about determination, pride, and character -- values that this group has always demonstrated," Inter boss Cristian Chivu told reporters.

On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute.

Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal.

Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter.

The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked.

And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards.

England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range.

'Not good enough'

The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst's team, as Feyenoord's defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot.

The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes. With the game effectively over as a contest, Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram.

Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption. And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences.

The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord's solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase.

Feyenoord's next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart.

"The reality is that we currently have three points from four matches, which, frankly, isn't good enough," van Bronckhorst told reporters.

"Moving forward, we'll need to win matches if we want to progress in the Champions League."

headline: Bayern skeleton crew sink Atletico in Champions League
description: Teenage forward Karl opens the scoring before Laimer seals 2-0 win in Madrid
author: AFP
article_text:
Bayern Munich overcame a horror list of absences to cruise to a 2-0 win away at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Teenage Germany forward Lennart Karl opened the scoring and Konrad Laimer added another as Bayern triumphed despite a bulging casualty ward.

Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari were on Bayern's injury list but it meant little as freshly-minted Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane and captain Joshua Kimmich marshalled his troops to a memorable victory.

The German champions also arrived in Madrid without coach Vincent Kompany, sick with a meningitis-related condition.

"There was a lot of noise around us heading in but we're very convinced of the squad we have, of the players we've got at our disposal and I think we showed over 90 minutes the type of football we can play," Laimer, who was named man of the match by UEFA, told Amazon Prime.

"We could've scored another goal or two. It was a very deserved win against a good team and an important three points."

Despite laying on an assist for Laimer, Kane failed to score meaning he missed out on equalling Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in 11 straight Champions League games.

"We are standing together despite the difficult times at Bayern in the last weeks and are delighted we could experience this team victory together," Bayern captain Manuel Neuer said.

"We heard that people were doubting how well we could perform today against a top team, just two points behind Barcelona in La Liga, but to give an answer in the way we did is sensational."

Atletico's 'cold shower'

Atletico's Marcos Llorente told Movistar+ the hosts were stunned by Bayern's opener.

"They're a strong side but we were holding our own. It's the little details that decide a game, and we weren't expecting that first goal.

"We were covering well, so it hit us like a bucket of cold water."

With two wins and two draws, Bayern climbed to eighth spot on the table while Atletico finish Tuesday night in 22nd spot on the 36-team table.

Undermanned Bayern were handed a boost pre-match when Michael Olise was given the all clear to start after being subbed out late with a knee injury against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

Olise joined Bayern's two remaining senior forwards Kane and Karl in the starting line-up, with wingback Alphonso Davies pushed up onto the left wing.

Atletico were received their own late injury withdrawal when Christian Romero was ruled out on matchday. Julian Alvarez came close to giving the hosts an early lead, flashing inches wide of the post three minutes in.

Kane had his own chance to break the deadlock midway through the opening half but blasted wide of Jan Oblak's goal on the turn.

Atletico had repelled the visitors despite ceding possession and field position but it was a simple mistake from the hosts which allowed Bayern to take the lead.

Robin Le Normand took too long on the ball allowing the energetic Karl to pick his pocket and loft a shot over the advancing Oblak. Chasing the game, Diego Simeone made three changes but Bayern scored next when Kane drifted a clever pass into Laimer's path, allowing the Austrian to blast in off the crossbar.

Bayern could have had a third with 10 minutes remaining when Dayot Upamecano outmuscled his marker and headed in, but the big Frenchman was penalised for an offensive foul.

Despite having few remaining bench options, Bayern looked the team most likely to score in the dying moments as they easily kept Atletico at bay in a comfortable victory.

"They're a strong side but we were holding our own. It's the little details that decide a game, and we weren't expecting that first goal.

Bayern could have had a third with 10 minutes remaining when Dayot Upamecano outmuscled his marker and headed in, but the big Frenchman was penalised for an offensive foul.

headline: Groom goes viral for having to beat bride at Valorant before he can marry her
description: Chinese groom had to defeat his bride in Valorant before he could take her to their wedding ceremony
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Chinese groom had to defeat his bride in Valorant before he could take her to their wedding ceremony

A groom in China has gone viral after being challenged to defeat his bride in Riot Games’ tactical shooter Valorant before he could take her to their wedding ceremony.

A video shared on Instagram shows the groom sitting down to play against his bride as part of the couple’s wedding celebrations.

The unusual challenge reportedly forms part of a Chinese wedding tradition in which the groom and his friends must complete a series of tasks prepared by the bride and her bridesmaids before they can proceed with the ceremony.

Rather than opting for more conventional wedding games, the couple incorporated Valorant into the celebrations, reportedly drawing on their shared interest in playing the game together.

The groom ultimately emerged victorious, completing the challenge and earning the right to collect his bride for the ceremony. The video has since circulated on social media, with the gaming competition attracting attention from viewers.

This is not the first time a couple in China has incorporated video games into their wedding celebrations. In 2023, another couple made headlines after organising a League of Legends competition for their wedding. The bride reportedly defeated her husband and his wedding party during the event.

headline: Squash stars head to Pakistan
description: Four international events offer $439,000 prize money
author: ZUBAIR NAZEER KHAN
article_text:
Pakistan will host four consecutive international squash tournaments following the ongoing Asian Team Squash Championships in Islamabad, with total prize money of $439,000 on offer across the events.

The tournaments, featuring leading men's and women's players from around the world, are expected to provide a boost to squash in Pakistan, offering local players opportunities to compete against international opposition while strengthening the country's profile as a sporting destination.

Three of the four Professional Squash Association (PSA) events will be held in Karachi, while Islamabad will host the opening tournament. The schedule begins with the Chief of Air Staff International Squash Championship, a $40,000 men's silver-level event, which will take place in Islamabad from November 24 to 28.

Pakistan's Noor Zaman, who has climbed three places to 25th in the latest world rankings after winning the World Under-23 Championship, will be the top seed. Fellow Pakistani Ashab Irfan, who has improved seven places in the rankings, is seeded fourth. Mohammad Asim Khan, ranked 68th in the world, has been seeded seventh, while Pakistan's Nasir Iqbal will also feature in the competition. Karachi will then host three international tournaments offering a combined $399,000 in prize money.

The Chief of Naval Staff Squash Championship, an $18,000 event, will be held from December 1 to 5 at the PN Roshan Khan-Jahangir Khan Squash Complex. The tournament will also include a women's PSA event carrying $1,000 in prize money.

The action will move to the Creek Club for the Sindh Open International Squash Championship, scheduled for December 6 to 10.

Pakistan's Noor Zaman will be the country's sole representative in the men's draw, where world number 17 Youssef Soliman of Egypt is the top seed.

In the women's competition, Egypt's world number 14 Salma Hany will lead the field, with compatriot and world number 19 Nada Abbas seeded second.

The $130,000 tournament will offer equal prize money in the men's and women's competitions.

The series of events will conclude with the Karachi Open, a Gold-level championship scheduled for January 5 to 10, 2027, featuring a total prize purse of $250,000.

The men's competition will offer $125,000, with an equal amount distributed among the 32 players in the women's draw.

headline: SSGC announces winter gas supply timings for consumers
description: Company prioritises domestic consumers, schedules gas availability during breakfast, lunch, dinner hours
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) on Wednesday announced designated gas supply timings for domestic consumers during the winter season, prioritising availability during cooking hours in accordance with the directives of the Government of Pakistan.

In a post on X, SSGC said it was committed to prioritising domestic customers and ensuring gas availability during designated cooking hours.

According to the schedule shared by the company, gas would be available for breakfast from 6:30am to 9am, lunch from 12pm to 2:30pm and dinner from 6pm to 9pm.

The company said the arrangements were aimed at “managing gas load effectively this winter” while ensuring a steady gas supply in line with government directives.

Govt unveils LPG reforms

A day earlier, the government announced sweeping reforms to open the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector to competition, improve supply and curb profiteering.

Addressing a press conference alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the government to provide maximum relief to low-income groups.

A major focus of the briefing was the LPG sector, where the government plans to abolish the existing quota-based distribution mechanism, introduce competitive auctions and encourage public and private companies to import the commodity at competitive prices.

The minister said domestic LPG production stood at around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes daily, while a substantial portion of demand had traditionally been met through imports from the western border. Supply disruptions had allowed some market players to sell the commodity for Rs700 to Rs800 per kilogramme.

Under the proposed reforms, locally produced LPG will be auctioned in transparent lots of five to 10 tonnes among companies licensed by Ogra. The auction results will be made public, with the process monitored by the petroleum secretary and Ogra chairman.

State-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil, Sui Southern Gas Company and Pakistan LNG Limited, have been directed to arrange bulk supplies through government-to-government and business-to-business agreements. Private companies will also be encouraged to import LPG.

Malik said importers would disclose monthly cost components, including Saudi Aramco's contract price, premiums, freight charges and other expenses, on their websites. The government also plans to establish price stabilisation and vulnerable consumers' protection funds to help deserving households obtain LPG at subsidised rates.

He said the government would ensure that the 10% LPG quota allocated for remote and hard-to-reach areas was properly utilised, with state-owned companies responsible for procuring and distributing the allocated supplies.

The minister added that the Competition Commission had been asked to act against cartelisation and anti-competitive practices, while Ogra would strengthen licensing and audit mechanisms to prevent hoarding and profiteering.

On international pricing, Malik said Saudi Aramco's contract price had risen from $540 per tonne in March to $756 per tonne, prompting a corresponding revision in domestic LPG prices. He said the prevailing spot-market price, after accounting for associated costs, was estimated at Rs450 to Rs500 per kilogramme.

Malik also assured consumers that the government would make every effort to meet winter gas demand, particularly during meal times. He said domestic demand was expected to rise by 400 to 500 million cubic feet per day and that alternative arrangements for imported liquefied natural gas would be made to meet requirements.

Information Minister Tarar said the government had abolished the LPG monopoly and discretionary quota system to introduce transparency and competition. He added that the prime minister had provided Rs130 billion in subsidies to consumers and prioritised public relief during the energy crisis.

The government has also announced that oil refineries will bear a cumulative burden of Rs15 billion over 30 days under a revised petrol pricing mechanism, allowing a reduction of Rs14.71 per litre at the consumer end.

Malik said the new LPG arrangements were expected to become fully operational before winter, adding that the government aimed to establish a competitive market with transparent pricing and more reliable supplies.

headline: Mendis leads Sri Lanka recovery against Patron’s XI
description: Visitors reach 162-5 in Islamabad as Saqib Khan strikes twice in warm-up contest
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Kusal Mendis leads Sri Lanka XI's recovery with an unbeaten 45 as the visitors reached 162 for five against Patron’s XI in their warm-up match at Islamabad Cricket Club on Wednesday.

Sri Lanka, who elected to bat after winning the toss, recovered from a difficult start after losing three wickets for just 40. Till filing of the story they had progressed to 162 in 38.4 overs, with Mendis providing the backbone of the innings.

Mendis struck eight boundaries in his 48-ball knock, maintaining an aggressive approach despite the early setbacks. Anjala Bandara was unbeaten on seven.

Earlier, Lahiru Udara anchored the innings with 65 from 105 deliveries, including seven fours and three sixes. His contribution proved crucial after Pasindu Sooriyabandara fell for eight and Dinesh Chandimal departed without scoring, both to Saqib Khan.

Dhananjaya De Silva added 14 before becoming Mohammad Salman's only victim, leaving Sri Lanka struggling at 40-3. Udara subsequently combined with Mendis to rebuild the innings before Ali Shabbir dismissed him for 65. Shabbir later removed Sonal Dinusha for ten to finish with two wickets.

Saqib was the standout bowler, returning figures of 2-25 from 11 overs, while Shoaib Akher Juniorr. impressed with an economical spell, conceding just 12 runs in seven overs.

The match provides Sri Lanka with valuable preparation ahead of their upcoming two-Test series against Pakistan, scheduled to begin in Rawalpindi on November 9, with the second Test in Lahore from November 17.

headline: PSX soars nearly 4,000 points in euphoric rally
description: Buying frenzy sweeps bourse as US midterm outcome lifts hopes of Iran peace
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A wave of cheer swept through the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Wednesday as renewed hopes of easing geopolitical tensions and a shift in Washington's political dynamics following the United States midterm elections lifted investor confidence.

Reflecting the upbeat mood, the benchmark KSE-100 Index surged 3,994.62 points, or 2.38% to settle at 172,013.48 points, crossing another major milestone and posting one of its strongest single-session gains in recent trading history. The market had opened on a positive note, with the index gaining 1,707.48 points, or 1.02%, to reach 169,726.34 at 10:04am.

A further boost to market sentiment came from the decline in international oil prices, which eased as investors weighed the implications of the US midterm election results against uncertainty over Washington's next move in the US-Israeli war on Iran. The combination of softer oil prices and hopes of a possible easing of geopolitical tensions provided an encouraging backdrop for equities, supporting the upbeat mood at the local bourse.

Internationally, Brent crude futures fell $1.75, or 0.7%, to $101.85 a barrel at 10:34am GMT, after dropping as much as $2 earlier in the session. Similarly, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined $1.18, or 1.2%, to $94.91 a barrel, reversing an earlier gain of $1.

headline: Jennifer Connelly makes surprise Marvel return in ‘VisionQuest’
description: The actress has previously voiced two artificial intelligence systems created by Tony Stark
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jennifer Connelly has made a surprise appearance in Marvel’s VisionQuest, with the actress reportedly voicing a mysterious artificial intelligence character in the Disney+ series.

Connelly is credited as the voice of D.E.E.D.E.E. in the fifth episode, titled “Firewall”. The appearance has caught the attention of Marvel fans, particularly because the actress is married to series star Paul Bettany, who plays Vision.

D.E.E.D.E.E. is an artificial intelligence associated with Tony Stark in Marvel lore. Stark created several AI systems to manage his laboratories and technology, making the character’s introduction a potential connection to the wider Marvel universe. However, Connelly’s role in the episode appears limited to a brief vocal appearance, with no confirmation yet of whether she will return.

The casting also marks another connection between Connelly and Marvel adaptations. She previously played Betty Ross, Bruce Banner’s love interest, in 2003’s Hulk. When Marvel rebooted the character in The Incredible Hulk in 2008, Liv Tyler took over the role.

Connelly later joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe through voice work in Spider-Man: Homecoming. She voiced Karen, the artificial intelligence integrated into Peter Parker’s Spider-Man suit, which was also created using Stark technology.

Outside Marvel, Connelly has appeared in several projects adapted from comic books and graphic novels, including The Rocketeer, Snowpiercer and Alita: Battle Angel.

Her appearance in VisionQuest adds another unexpected layer to the series, which has already attracted attention for its connections to previous Marvel stories. Whether D.E.E.D.E.E. becomes more significant in later episodes remains unclear.

For now, the cameo offers a playful connection between Connelly and Bettany’s Marvel careers, while giving longtime fans another detail to discuss as the series unfolds.

headline: Two bodies recovered in Indian Himalayas as search continues for six missing trekkers
description: Search operation suspended as rescuers face heavy snowfall, poor visibility, challenging high-altitude terrain
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Indian rescue teams recovered two bodies from a trekking route in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, while six people remained missing amid heavy snowfall and difficult terrain, local media reported Wednesday.

The bodies of a man and a woman were recovered Tuesday near Kedar Kharak, at an altitude of approximately 4,000 metres (13,123 feet), according to the Hindustan Times.

Uttarkashi District Disaster Management Officer Shardul Gusain confirmed the recovery, saying the identities of the deceased had yet to be established.

A joint team from the State Disaster Response Force and Nehru Institute of Mountaineering located the bodies during a search operation along the Kedartal trekking route.

The operation was suspended at around 3pm (0930GMT) Tuesday because of difficult conditions, with rescuers returning to their base camp.

Search operations were scheduled to resume Wednesday, with additional personnel, supplies, and life-support equipment being dispatched to the area. Authorities also prepared an alternative helipad near the site to facilitate rescue operations and the evacuation of the bodies to Harsil.

Read Also: At least 40 missing after avalanche in India’s Himalayan state of Uttarkhand

The group had set out on October 27 and was expected to return by October 29, but failed to do so, prompting a search. Rescuers have faced heavy snowfall, poor visibility, and challenging high-altitude terrain.

Authorities have not confirmed the fate of the remaining six missing people.

headline: Israeli opposition leaders say Netanyahu cannot remain in power after US midterm elections
description: Golan warns Netanyahu’s continued tenure could lead to international sanctions, clash with Washington
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli opposition leaders said Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could not remain in power following Democratic gains in the United States midterm elections, warning that his continued rule threatens Israel’s international standing and relations with its closest ally.

Yair Golan, leader of the opposition Democrats party, said the election results had revealed “just how toxic Netanyahu is among both Democrats and Republicans.”

In a post on US social media company X, Golan warned that Netanyahu’s continued tenure alongside National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir could lead Israel toward “international sanctions, international isolation, and a clash with the US, our friend and most important ally.”

Meanwhile, Israeli lawmaker Gilad Kariv also called for Netanyahu to leave office. In a statement, Kariv said Netanyahu “destroyed the relations with the Democratic Party and with half of the Republican Party.”

“He must not continue to lead the State of Israel,” Kariv added, rejecting calls for a unity government led by Netanyahu.

The remarks came as Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, dealing a setback to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. Trump has backed Netanyahu, whose political future has been the subject of debate amid efforts to form Israel’s next government.

Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Jewish opposition parties and 19 for Arab parties.

headline: Rybakina, Gauff drawn together at WTA Finals
description: Sabalenka and Andreeva headline a competitive Group Two lineup
author: REUTERS
article_text: World ​number one Elena Rybakina and American Coco Gauff were drawn in Group One for the WTA Finals, while second-ranked Aryna ‌Sabalenka will face third-ranked Mirra Andreeva in Group Two at the season-ending championship. Defending ‌champion Rybakina will begin ⁠her ​title defense against Gauff, four-time ​WTA Finals participant Jessica ‌Pegula and reigning Wimbledon champion ​Linda Noskova, who is making her tournament debut. Sabalenka's group also includes 19-year-old Andreeva, 2018 WTA ⁠Finals champion Elina Svitolina and Czech Karolina Muchova. The event, ‌which brings together the season's top eight qualifiers, will be held at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden from November ⁠8 to 15. The top ⁠two players from each ​round-robin group ‌will advance to the semifinals. Rybakina, who claimed the world number one ranking after September's US Open, said the position brought both added scrutiny and motivation. "It has been an unbelievable couple of months," Rybakina said during ⁠Tuesday's draw ceremony. "It is of course pressure because of all of ⁠the attention, but at the same time it's motivation because you don't want to lose. In this sport, you still need to work a lot." Sabalenka will be looking for vengeance after losing her top ranking to Rybakina at the US ⁠Open. The Belarusian won both Indian ​Wells and Miami earlier this year to complete the "Sunshine Double." In July, organizers announced the tournament would move from Riyadh to Indian Wells following the early ​end of the WTA's hosting ‌agreement with Saudi Arabia.

headline: Foden eyes return to top form
description: The City midfielder credits regular playing time and recent goals for rebuilding his confidence after a difficult spell
author: REUTERS
article_text: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is beginning to rediscover the form that made him one of the Premier League's standout players, after a recent scoring streak boosted his confidence ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash at RB Leipzig. Foden, who won the ⁠Premier League Player of the Season and Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year awards in 2024 after scoring a career-best 27 goals in all competitions, endured a dip in form that ultimately ⁠cost him a place in England's 2026 World Cup squad. "Hopefully I can get back to that level," Foden told reporters on Tuesday. "I think I'm slightly starting to get back there now with ⁠my recent performances." The 26-year-old scored his ⁠first Premier League goal of the season against Ipswich Town last month after serving a suspension following a red card in the Manchester derby. He followed it up with a hat-trick and an assist in City's 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens. "I had the unfortunate red ⁠card against United. But the break did me good. I think ⁠I came back really fresh-minded and sharp," he said. "Being involved in goals gives you a lot of confidence and when you're playing regularly as well you kind of just get into a rhythm and a groove." Asked about his international future, Foden said he had not spoken ⁠to England manager Thomas Tuchel since being left out of the World Cup squad and was concentrating on performing for City. "All I try and do really is focus on my own game and hopefully one day the call-up might come back," he said.

Asked about his international future, Foden said he had not spoken ⁠to England manager Thomas Tuchel since being left out of the World Cup squad and was concentrating on performing for City.

"All I try and do really is focus on my own game and hopefully one day the call-up might come back," he said.

headline: Hannah Einbinder debuts Haley Stevens impression after Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan senate victory
description: Einbinder imitates Stevens, including her distinctive way of speaking and encouraging supporters
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hannah Einbinder has followed through on a promise to showcase her impression of Michigan Representative Haley Stevens after Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won the state's US Senate race.

The Hacks actress shared a video of herself performing the impression on Wednesday, November 4, after teasing the idea on Instagram Stories the night before.

Einbinder had promised to reveal what she called her “perfect” Stevens impression if “our guys (gender neutral) win tonight”. Following El-Sayed's victory, she posted a video from a bar with the caption “As promised”.

In the clip, Einbinder imitates Stevens, including her distinctive way of speaking and encouraging supporters to give their opponents “a little bit of stick it to ’em”. She also shared a separate post celebrating El-Sayed's win, writing “Mazel tov, Abdul”.

The joke comes after Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed earlier this year, endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers shortly before Election Day. Her decision drew criticism from Democrats, particularly because she had previously pledged to support the party's nominee.

Stevens said her endorsement followed tensions with El-Sayed's campaign and concerns about his conduct and political associations. The disagreement also involved criticism surrounding the campaign's messaging on Israel and its connections to political commentator Hasan Piker.

El-Sayed's victory marks a significant milestone, with him set to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. His campaign focused on issues including healthcare, economic affordability and campaign finance.

Einbinder has previously spoken publicly in support of Palestinian rights. During her acceptance speech at the 2025 Emmy Awards, the actress said “Free Palestine”, drawing attention to her political advocacy.

The comedian's impression adds a pop-culture moment to a closely watched Michigan election, following a campaign marked by tensions within the Democratic Party.

headline: Federal govt signs off on Pak-Kuwait defence agreement
description: Announces fuel subsidy to continue until end of December; approves Rs160b development package for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal cabinet on Wednesday ratified the Pakistan-Kuwait Defence Cooperation Agreement.

The agreement was finalised on June 11, 2023, to promote cooperation between the two countries in the defence sector.

A statement from the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said the Kuwaiti government had ratified the agreement on July 19.

The agreement establishes a framework for military cooperation between the Kuwaiti and Pakistani armed forces, covering military training, education, intelligence sharing, logistics, defence technology, research and exchanges of expertise, to strengthen institutional military ties between the two countries.

It also provides for cooperation in military manufacturing, electronic communications systems, scientific research, military media and cultural and sports activities.

Under the agreement, a joint military committee will oversee implementation, including the organisation of joint military exercises, official visits and other cooperative programs.

The pact will remain in force for five years and will be automatically renewed unless either side decides to terminate it. It also commits both countries to protecting confidential military information and resolving any disputes arising from the agreement through diplomatic channels.

The ratification follows a series of high-level contacts between Kuwaiti and Pakistani military officials in recent months aimed at expanding bilateral defence coordination.

The agreement comes as Kuwait continues to deepen security cooperation with international partners amid heightened regional security challenges in the Gulf.

Kuwait has been among several Gulf countries targeted by Iranian missile and drone attacks during the recent regional escalation. Tehran has said the strikes were aimed at US military facilities hosted by Gulf states, while Kuwaiti authorities said their air defences intercepted projectiles that entered the country's airspace.

Transfer of powers to K-P governor

The federal cabinet also approved the transfer of powers delegated to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to the provincial governor for the conduct of day-to-day affairs during the period of emergency.

According to the PMO statement, the move was intended to facilitate administrative matters and improve governance in the province. The governor would submit a monthly report to the federal government reviewing the exercise of these powers.

The cabinet expressed hope that the K-P Advisory Council, under the governor’s leadership, would work for the welfare and prosperity of the province’s people and help restore peace and security.

The prime minister also said a Rs160 billion development package had been finalised for K-P, with security given priority.

He said a large number of terrorists had been eliminated in the province and expressed confidence that terrorism would be eradicated through the sacrifices of security personnel and the coordinated efforts of law enforcement agencies, the provincial government and the federal government.

Describing K-P as Pakistan’s most beautiful province, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised its people for resisting terrorism for decades and paying a heavy price in sacrifices.

He said Balochistan had also faced terrorism for a long time, adding that the menace had been eliminated in 2018 but had unfortunately resurfaced. He expressed hope that it would once again be comprehensively suppressed. He added that the federal and provincial governments would work with security institutions to eliminate terrorism.

New currency note designs approved

On the recommendation of the Ministry of Finance, the cabinet approved the designs of new currency notes after receiving a detailed briefing on the process.

The briefing informed the meeting that proposals had been invited from artists and designers across the country. A cabinet committee established by the prime minister had also held consultations with relevant stakeholders on the proposed designs.

The new notes would feature enhanced security measures to prevent counterfeiting and use modern materials intended to extend their lifespan, the statement said.

The cabinet also approved the introduction of a Rs10 coin to replace the existing Rs10 banknote.

The Federal Cabinet further ratified decisions taken at the October 26 meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Government-Owned Institutions.

It also ratified decisions taken at meetings of the Cabinet Committee on Legislative Cases held on January 22, February 26, August 5, 18 and 27, and September 11 and 22.

Pakistan continuing efforts to promote regional peace and stability

PM Shehbaz also said Pakistan was continuing diplomatic efforts to promote regional peace and stability, while the government was taking measures to shield the public from rising international petroleum prices.

He also announced that the fuel subsidy programme would continue until the end of December and said a Rs160 billion development package had been approved for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Addressing a cabinet meeting in Islamabad, he said international oil prices had risen sharply amid unrest in the region and that Pakistan was continuing to play its role in efforts to establish peace.

He said a Pakistani delegation had visited Tehran twice during the previous week, while Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir had also travelled to Iran, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Iran and Turkiye had held discussions there, which, according to the prime minister, took place in a positive atmosphere.

The discussions also covered ways to promote regional understanding in connection with an agreement involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, he said.

Fuel subsidy to continue until December

The prime minister said the government’s fuel subsidy programme would continue until the end of December, adding that 15 million people had used tokens under the scheme. Assuming an average family size of five, he said, the programme had benefited at least 75 million people.

He said the government had provided approximately Rs28 billion in subsidies and was closely monitoring the programme to ensure transparency.

However, reports of irregularities at some petrol pumps had emerged, prompting him to direct Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik to shut down outlets found involved in malpractice and take strict action against those responsible.

PM Shehbaz said the government had also prevented an increase of Rs15 per litre in petrol prices from being passed on to consumers following a rise in international petroleum prices the previous Friday.

He said the petroleum minister and his team had held discussions with refineries and persuaded them to absorb the additional cost instead of transferring the burden to the public. The prime minister congratulated the minister and his team for their efforts.

PM says LNG mafia era has ended

The prime minister said the government had ended what he described as the LNG import mafia, which he said had earned billions of rupees over several decades.

He praised the deputy prime minister, the energy and finance ministers and their teams for their efforts, saying LPG imports and management were now being handled through government institutions, including Pakistan State Oil and Pakistan Petroleum Limited, under a competitive and transparent mechanism.

PM Shehbaz said LPG imports would be opened to competition, while the locally produced LPG quota would be auctioned. The government would use the resulting profits to provide subsidies to consumers, he added.

PM Shehbaz said the government was holding meetings every two to three days to review preparations for the winter season, particularly in view of challenges affecting maritime routes and the availability and supply of fuel, LPG and other resources.

He said the government would make every possible effort to ensure that the required quantities of LPG and petroleum products reached consumers and that power generation plants continued operating.

It would also seek to contain the impact of rising prices and prevent supply-related difficulties, he added.

Defence developments and G24 appointment

PM Shehbaz congratulated the nation on Pakistan’s successful test of an air-to-air missile, which he said had taken place the previous day.

He credited Field Marshal Munir, his team and the institutions and individuals involved in the test for the achievement.

The prime minister also congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on his election as chairman of the Group of 24. He said Pakistan would fulfil the responsibility with diligence and effectively present its position at international forums.

The federal cabinet on Wednesday ratified the Pakistan-Kuwait Defence Cooperation Agreement.

The agreement was finalised on June 11, 2023, to promote cooperation between the two countries in the defence sector.

A statement from the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said the Kuwaiti government had ratified the agreement on July 19.

وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیرِ صدارت وفاقی کابینہ کا اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا.

وفاقی کابینہ نے خیبرپختونخوا میں انتظامی امور کی سہل انجام دہی اور گورننس کی مزید بہتری کیلئے وزیر اعلی کو تفویض شدہ اختیارات کی صوبے میں ایمرجنسی کی مدت کے دوران روزمرہ کے امور کی انجام… pic.twitter.com/cMBpEs9Bc8

— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) November 4, 2026

The agreement establishes a framework for military cooperation between the Kuwaiti and Pakistani armed forces, covering military training, education, intelligence sharing, logistics, defence technology, research and exchanges of expertise, to strengthen institutional military ties between the two countries.

It also provides for cooperation in military manufacturing, electronic communications systems, scientific research, military media and cultural and sports activities.

Under the agreement, a joint military committee will oversee implementation, including the organisation of joint military exercises, official visits and other cooperative programs.

Read More: Pakistan, Kuwait call for de-escalation amid widening US-Iran conflict

The pact will remain in force for five years and will be automatically renewed unless either side decides to terminate it. It also commits both countries to protecting confidential military information and resolving any disputes arising from the agreement through diplomatic channels.

The ratification follows a series of high-level contacts between Kuwaiti and Pakistani military officials in recent months aimed at expanding bilateral defence coordination.

The agreement comes as Kuwait continues to deepen security cooperation with international partners amid heightened regional security challenges in the Gulf.

Kuwait has been among several Gulf countries targeted by Iranian missile and drone attacks during the recent regional escalation. Tehran has said the strikes were aimed at US military facilities hosted by Gulf states, while Kuwaiti authorities said their air defences intercepted projectiles that entered the country's airspace.

Transfer of powers to K-P governor

The federal cabinet also approved the transfer of powers delegated to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to the provincial governor for the conduct of day-to-day affairs during the period of emergency.

According to the PMO statement, the move was intended to facilitate administrative matters and improve governance in the province. The governor would submit a monthly report to the federal government reviewing the exercise of these powers.

The cabinet expressed hope that the K-P Advisory Council, under the governor’s leadership, would work for the welfare and prosperity of the province’s people and help restore peace and security.

The prime minister also said a Rs160 billion development package had been finalised for K-P, with security given priority.

He said a large number of terrorists had been eliminated in the province and expressed confidence that terrorism would be eradicated through the sacrifices of security personnel and the coordinated efforts of law enforcement agencies, the provincial government and the federal government.

Describing K-P as Pakistan’s most beautiful province, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised its people for resisting terrorism for decades and paying a heavy price in sacrifices.

He said Balochistan had also faced terrorism for a long time, adding that the menace had been eliminated in 2018 but had unfortunately resurfaced. He expressed hope that it would once again be comprehensively suppressed. He added that the federal and provincial governments would work with security institutions to eliminate terrorism.

New currency note designs approved

On the recommendation of the Ministry of Finance, the cabinet approved the designs of new currency notes after receiving a detailed briefing on the process.

The briefing informed the meeting that proposals had been invited from artists and designers across the country. A cabinet committee established by the prime minister had also held consultations with relevant stakeholders on the proposed designs.

The new notes would feature enhanced security measures to prevent counterfeiting and use modern materials intended to extend their lifespan, the statement said.

The cabinet also approved the introduction of a Rs10 coin to replace the existing Rs10 banknote.

The Federal Cabinet further ratified decisions taken at the October 26 meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Government-Owned Institutions.

It also ratified decisions taken at meetings of the Cabinet Committee on Legislative Cases held on January 22, February 26, August 5, 18 and 27, and September 11 and 22.

Pakistan continuing efforts to promote regional peace and stability

PM Shehbaz also said Pakistan was continuing diplomatic efforts to promote regional peace and stability, while the government was taking measures to shield the public from rising international petroleum prices.

He also announced that the fuel subsidy programme would continue until the end of December and said a Rs160 billion development package had been approved for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Addressing a cabinet meeting in Islamabad, he said international oil prices had risen sharply amid unrest in the region and that Pakistan was continuing to play its role in efforts to establish peace.

He said a Pakistani delegation had visited Tehran twice during the previous week, while Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir had also travelled to Iran, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Iran and Turkiye had held discussions there, which, according to the prime minister, took place in a positive atmosphere.

The discussions also covered ways to promote regional understanding in connection with an agreement involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, he said.

— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) November 4, 2026

Fuel subsidy to continue until December

The prime minister said the government’s fuel subsidy programme would continue until the end of December, adding that 15 million people had used tokens under the scheme. Assuming an average family size of five, he said, the programme had benefited at least 75 million people.

He said the government had provided approximately Rs28 billion in subsidies and was closely monitoring the programme to ensure transparency.

However, reports of irregularities at some petrol pumps had emerged, prompting him to direct Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik to shut down outlets found involved in malpractice and take strict action against those responsible.

PM Shehbaz said the government had also prevented an increase of Rs15 per litre in petrol prices from being passed on to consumers following a rise in international petroleum prices the previous Friday.

He said the petroleum minister and his team had held discussions with refineries and persuaded them to absorb the additional cost instead of transferring the burden to the public. The prime minister congratulated the minister and his team for their efforts.

PM says LNG mafia era has ended

The prime minister said the government had ended what he described as the LNG import mafia, which he said had earned billions of rupees over several decades.

He praised the deputy prime minister, the energy and finance ministers and their teams for their efforts, saying LPG imports and management were now being handled through government institutions, including Pakistan State Oil and Pakistan Petroleum Limited, under a competitive and transparent mechanism.

PM Shehbaz said LPG imports would be opened to competition, while the locally produced LPG quota would be auctioned. The government would use the resulting profits to provide subsidies to consumers, he added.

Read More: LPG price hike crushes rickshaw drivers

PM Shehbaz said the government was holding meetings every two to three days to review preparations for the winter season, particularly in view of challenges affecting maritime routes and the availability and supply of fuel, LPG and other resources.

He said the government would make every possible effort to ensure that the required quantities of LPG and petroleum products reached consumers and that power generation plants continued operating.

It would also seek to contain the impact of rising prices and prevent supply-related difficulties, he added.

Defence developments and G24 appointment

PM Shehbaz congratulated the nation on Pakistan’s successful test of an air-to-air missile, which he said had taken place the previous day.

He credited Field Marshal Munir, his team and the institutions and individuals involved in the test for the achievement.

The prime minister also congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on his election as chairman of the Group of 24. He said Pakistan would fulfil the responsibility with diligence and effectively present its position at international forums.

headline: World leaders react to Democrats winning US midterms
description: The result could have major implications for global trade, security and energy prices
author: Reuters
article_text:
Governments and politicians around the world reacted to the Democrats winning the US midterm elections, a result that could have major implications for global trade, security and energy prices.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on X, "Yesterday, the American people voted against policies that only serve to impoverish people. Against hatred. Against sexism. Against climate denial and against the privileges of the elites."

"It happened in Brazil. It has just happened in the US. And it will happen soon in Spain," he said.

Speaking to Reuters, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere said the Democrat win was "a powerful political signal about a change of course among American voters."

"Voices are now emerging in American politics that are closer to us than the president and the administration have stood for, for example on climate and environment, and in foreign policy and development aid policy," he said.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said to reporters that the results will "introduce a new era in world relations."

"We have seen that the Democrats have taken control of the Senate and of the House, and the people of America have spoken."

The European Parliament's Vice President Christel Schaldemose said on X: "Not because everything now changes for the better, but because it could benefit the support for Ukraine, the green transition, and relations with the rest of the world."

"But the EU must continue the course of standing stronger and standing on its own two feet. That's not up for debate."

Greek Government Spokesperson Pavlos Marniakis on local SKAI TV said "Greek-American relations will remain strong. The United States is our strategic ally, and this will continue for major projects and all major agreements. Nothing will be affected by this outcome. It is obvious that we respect every outcome; the conclusions are clear."

"Beyond that, what I can tell you is that it appears that on the key committees there will be individuals with whom the Greek government has very good relations, and that is important for the country."

Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov was quoted by Russian state news agency RIA as saying, "Let's wait for the final results. The Democratic Party leadership's approach to relations with Russia is sharply negative. There is nothing new about that."

"Our principled and consistent line regarding Ukraine — as well as our foreign policy in general — is not based on short-term considerations and, naturally, does not depend on the fluctuations of the political barometer in other countries. We will continue our work in accordance with the directives of the President of the Russian Federation," he said.

The Japanese Chief Cabinet Minoru Kihara at a press briefing commented on the outcome, saying, "Regardless of the outcome of this election, the Japan-US alliance is the cornerstone of Japan's foreign and security policy."

"As the international situation becomes turbulent and increasingly uncertain, a strong Japan-US alliance is essential for maximising Japan's national interests and for peace and stability in the international community," she said.

headline: ‘A father is always gonna be sexually attracted to his daughter’: Steven Tyler’s controversial comments about daughter Liv resurface amid abuse lawsuit
description: Aerosmith returned to the stage at the Hollywood Bowl for its first full live performance since 2023
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Steven Tyler is facing renewed scrutiny after controversial comments he made about his daughter, actress Liv Tyler, resurfaced online amid an ongoing civil lawsuit alleging sexual abuse.

The remarks appeared in music writer Gavin Edwards’ 2006 book Is Tiny Dancer Really Elton’s Little John?, in which Tyler discussed whether he had ever experienced inappropriate attraction towards Liv. The Aerosmith frontman made a disturbing generalisation about fathers and daughters, “A father is always gonna be sexually attracted to his daughter...” while also stating that acting on such feelings was something a man should never do.

The comments have circulated again as Tyler, 78, continues to defend himself against allegations brought by Julia Misley, formerly known as Julia Holcomb. Misley alleges that Tyler sexually abused her after they met in 1973, when she was 16 and he was 25. Tyler has denied wrongdoing and has disputed her claims.

In April 2026, a California judge rejected Tyler’s attempt to dismiss the entire lawsuit but allowed certain allegations connected to California to proceed. The decision was procedural and did not establish the allegations as fact. The case remains unresolved.

Meanwhile, Tyler has returned to performing with Aerosmith. The band appeared at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles on October 29, marking its first full live performance since 2023. Liv Tyler and actress Alicia Silverstone introduced the musicians before the show.

The concert followed Aerosmith’s retirement from touring after Tyler sustained a vocal injury. The performance featured several of the group’s best-known songs, including “Dream On”, “Sweet Emotion” and “Walk This Way”.

Liv Tyler, whose mother is singer and model Bebe Buell, has not been accused of being involved in the allegations against her father. The resurfaced comments concern Tyler’s past statements, while Misley’s lawsuit addresses alleged conduct involving her during her teenage years.

With the legal proceedings continuing, Tyler’s public appearances and past remarks remain subjects of renewed attention.

headline: Kohli leads India to crushing win
description: Veteran batter smashes a brilliant 74 at Eden Park
author: AFP
article_text: Virat Kohli hit a brilliant 74 to lead India to a five-wicket win over New Zealand in their first one-day international at Auckland's Eden Park on Wednesday. The veteran right-hander hit his 80th ODI fifty off just 35 balls, showing his enduring class on a night when no other batsman was able to flourish. In a rain-affected match, India chased down a reduced 143 for victory with 56 balls remaining after New Zealand stuttered to 185 all out in the first innings, taking a 1-0 lead in the five-game series. Kohli, who turns 38 on Thursday, strode to the middle at the end of the first over, after former captain Rohit Sharma departed for a duck. He immediately found his timing on a quick and bouncy wicket, playing a stunning array of pulls and hooks which left New Zealand's pace attack flummoxed. Kohli hit 13 fours and a six in his 51-ball stay, frequently attacking the short ball. Indian captain Shubman Gill and Kohli combined for a 113-run partnership, Gill adding 37 from 56 deliveries. Rain interrupted the chase in the 11th over, when India were at 54-1, and then again an over later at the end of the 12th, with the tourists having added a further 10 runs. When they returned a third time, India were targeting a total of 143 runs in 32 overs under Duckworth Lewis -- that is, a further 79 runs in 20 overs. Kohli hit double digits from the next three overs to effectively kill the chase. Jacob Duffy took three wickets for New Zealand. India won the toss and chose to field, after brief showers caused a 10-minute delay to the start. New Zealand steadily reached 73-2 in the 14th over despite Will Young and Henry Nicholls both falling cheaply. Tim Seifert, playing in place of Devon Conway after he was concussed in a freak collision with Matt Henry in training on Tuesday, departed for 38, mistiming a pull shot to mid-on. His would be the highest score for New Zealand, with Daryl Mitchell's 28 and Glenn Phillips's 30 the next-best scores until a blistering 34 from 23 balls by last man Blair Tickner. Arshdeep Singh took 4-70 from his 10 overs, while Gurnoor Brar had 3-44 in 9.2 overs, as New Zealand were bowled out for 185 in the 41st over. The second game of the five-match series is in Wellington on Saturday.

headline: US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress
description: Democrats regain control of both chambers of Congress as Texas, Florida, Wisconsin, Ohio mark historic firsts
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
The 2026 US midterm elections produced a series of historic firsts across the country, with women and candidates from minority communities breaking longstanding barriers in races for governor and Congress.

The results included the election of the first Black woman governor in US history, the first Native American woman to win a Senate seat, and the first Muslim member of Congress from New Jersey, among other milestones.

The election also reshaped the balance of power in Washington. Democrats secured a majority in the US Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, dealing a significant blow to the second half of US President Donald Trump's presidency. US media projected a 53-42 Democratic advantage as of 1200 PKT, driven by at least seven seat pickups across the nation.

Democrats also won control of the US House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterms after Johnny Garcia defeated Carlos De La Cruz in Texas’s 35th District, according to The Associated Press.

The victory gave Democrats the 218 seats needed for a majority in the 435-member chamber, ending Republican control and dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump. As of 1139 PKT, 87 seats had yet to be called.

The victories also extended beyond Washington, with Democrats winning key gubernatorial races in traditionally Republican states, including Georgia and Texas.

First Muslim elected to US Senate

Abdul El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Democrat and former public health official, made history Tuesday by becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate after defeating Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's closely watched midterm election.

El-Sayed, 42, is a medical doctor and former public health official who previously served as Detroit’s health director and headed the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services, including Detroit, Michigan’s largest city.

Born and raised in Michigan to an Egyptian immigrant father, he graduated from the University of Michigan, earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar, and received his medical degree from Columbia University.

He won the Democratic nomination in August, defeating US Rep. Haley Stevens in a closely watched primary. His campaign focused on healthcare, economic inequality, and curbing corporate influence in politics.

First Black woman elected governor

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms made history by defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Georgia, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state.

The former Atlanta mayor is also Georgia’s first woman and first Black governor. Her victory returned the governor’s office to Democrats for the first time since 1998, ending more than two decades of Republican control.

Bottoms previously served as Atlanta’s mayor from 2018 to 2022 and worked in local government before entering statewide politics.

First Native American woman to lead a state

Former US Interior Secretary Deb Haaland became the first Native American woman elected governor of a US state after defeating Republican Gregg Hull in New Mexico.

A citizen of the Laguna Pueblo, Haaland previously made history in 2021 as the first Native American to serve as a US Cabinet secretary when then-President Joe Biden appointed her to lead the Interior Department.

Her election marks another milestone in Native American political representation, bringing a member of an Indigenous community to the leadership of a state.

First Native American woman elected to Senate

Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the US Senate after defeating Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.

Flanagan, an enrolled member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, will succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Tina Smith.

Before becoming lieutenant governor in 2019, she served on the Minneapolis Board of Education and represented St. Louis Park in the Minnesota House of Representatives.

She has also worked on Indigenous rights and relations between the state government and tribal nations.

First Muslim member of Congress from New Jersey

Democrat Adam Hamawy won New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, becoming the state’s first Muslim member of Congress.

A plastic surgeon and former US Army combat surgeon, Hamawy defeated Republican Gregg Mele.

His election adds another milestone to the growing representation of Muslim Americans in the US Congress.

First Latina governor of Texas

Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican incumbent Greg Abbott to become Texas’ first Latina governor.

Her victory also marks a return of Democrats to the governor’s office after more than three decades. The last Democrat to hold the post was the late Ann Richards, who left office in 1995.

Hinojosa’s win gives Democrats control of the state’s top office after years of Republican leadership and marks a significant change in Texas’ political landscape.

First Black governors in Florida and Wisconsin

Republican Byron Donalds became Florida’s first Black governor and the first Black Republican elected governor in US history after narrowly defeating Democrat David Jolly.

Donalds, a member of the US House of Representatives, will succeed Ron DeSantis. His victory also makes him the first Black candidate elected to statewide office in Florida.

In Wisconsin, Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Tom Tiffany to become the state’s first Black governor.

Crowley previously served as Milwaukee County executive and will succeed Democrat Tony Evers.

First woman elected governor of Ohio

Democrat Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to become Ohio’s first woman elected governor and its first Jewish governor.

A physician and former director of the Ohio Department of Health, Acton became widely known during the COVID-19 pandemic for her role in the state’s public health response.

Although Nancy Hollister briefly served as governor for 11 days in 1998-99, Acton is the first woman elected to the office.

3 Black women to serve simultaneously in Senate

Democrat Juliana Stratton’s victory in Illinois’ Senate race will bring the number of Black women serving simultaneously in the chamber to three for the first time when she takes office in January 2027.

She will join Democratic Sens. Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland and Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.

Stratton, who served as Illinois lieutenant governor under Gov. JB Pritzker, will also become the second Black woman elected to represent Illinois in the Senate, following Carol Moseley Braun, who won her seat in 1992.

Her election means Illinois will have two women of color in the Senate, alongside Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth.
