He won the Democratic nomination in August, defeating US Rep. Haley Stevens in a closely watched primary. His campaign focused on healthcare, economic inequality, and curbing corporate influence in politics.

First Black woman elected governor

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms made history by defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Georgia, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state.

The former Atlanta mayor is also Georgia’s first woman and first Black governor. Her victory returned the governor’s office to Democrats for the first time since 1998, ending more than two decades of Republican control.

Bottoms previously served as Atlanta’s mayor from 2018 to 2022 and worked in local government before entering statewide politics.

First Native American woman to lead a state

Former US Interior Secretary Deb Haaland became the first Native American woman elected governor of a US state after defeating Republican Gregg Hull in New Mexico.

A citizen of the Laguna Pueblo, Haaland previously made history in 2021 as the first Native American to serve as a US Cabinet secretary when then-President Joe Biden appointed her to lead the Interior Department.

Her election marks another milestone in Native American political representation, bringing a member of an Indigenous community to the leadership of a state.

First Native American woman elected to Senate

Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the US Senate after defeating Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.

Flanagan, an enrolled member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, will succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Tina Smith.

Before becoming lieutenant governor in 2019, she served on the Minneapolis Board of Education and represented St. Louis Park in the Minnesota House of Representatives.

She has also worked on Indigenous rights and relations between the state government and tribal nations.

First Muslim member of Congress from New Jersey

Democrat Adam Hamawy won New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, becoming the state’s first Muslim member of Congress.

A plastic surgeon and former US Army combat surgeon, Hamawy defeated Republican Gregg Mele.

His election adds another milestone to the growing representation of Muslim Americans in the US Congress.

First Latina governor of Texas

Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican incumbent Greg Abbott to become Texas’ first Latina governor.

Her victory also marks a return of Democrats to the governor’s office after more than three decades. The last Democrat to hold the post was the late Ann Richards, who left office in 1995.

Hinojosa’s win gives Democrats control of the state’s top office after years of Republican leadership and marks a significant change in Texas’ political landscape.

First Black governors in Florida and Wisconsin

Republican Byron Donalds became Florida’s first Black governor and the first Black Republican elected governor in US history after narrowly defeating Democrat David Jolly.

Donalds, a member of the US House of Representatives, will succeed Ron DeSantis. His victory also makes him the first Black candidate elected to statewide office in Florida.

In Wisconsin, Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Tom Tiffany to become the state’s first Black governor.

Crowley previously served as Milwaukee County executive and will succeed Democrat Tony Evers.

First woman elected governor of Ohio

Democrat Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to become Ohio’s first woman elected governor and its first Jewish governor.

A physician and former director of the Ohio Department of Health, Acton became widely known during the COVID-19 pandemic for her role in the state’s public health response.

Although Nancy Hollister briefly served as governor for 11 days in 1998-99, Acton is the first woman elected to the office.

3 Black women to serve simultaneously in Senate

Democrat Juliana Stratton’s victory in Illinois’ Senate race will bring the number of Black women serving simultaneously in the chamber to three for the first time when she takes office in January 2027.

She will join Democratic Sens. Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland and Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.

Stratton, who served as Illinois lieutenant governor under Gov. JB Pritzker, will also become the second Black woman elected to represent Illinois in the Senate, following Carol Moseley Braun, who won her seat in 1992.

Her election means Illinois will have two women of color in the Senate, alongside Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth.

headline: Kim Kardashian reveals when she plans to retake bar exam after previous failure
description: Sarah Paulson backs her All’s Fair co-star, predicting she will become a great lawyer
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kim Kardashian is still determined to become a lawyer, but she is not rushing into another attempt at the California bar exam.

The reality star and All’s Fair actress, who has pursued a legal career since 2019, says she plans to retake the examination when she has enough time to prepare. Speaking to PEOPLE at the New York City premiere of All’s Fair season 2 on November 2, Kardashian admitted that the test remains on her mind.

“I am always thinking about the bar,” she said, adding that she intends to wait until the right moment before trying again.

View this post on Instagram

Kardashian, who completed a four year Law Office Study Program in 2025, took the California bar exam in July that year. She later revealed that she had not passed, but insisted the result had strengthened her determination to continue.

“I was so close to passing the exam and that only motivated me even more,” she wrote in a message to fans at the time.

Her decision to postpone another attempt comes as she balances several professional commitments, including the new season of All’s Fair, an upcoming film project and her reality series The Kardashians, alongside raising her four children.

Her co-star Sarah Paulson is confident Kardashian will eventually achieve her goal. Asked about her prospects as a lawyer, Paulson said, “She’s going to be a great lawyer. She will.”

Kardashian began pursuing law after becoming involved in criminal justice reform. Her work included advocating for people serving prison sentences, including Alice Johnson, whose sentence was commuted in 2018.

She also passed California’s baby bar exam in 2021 on her fourth attempt, describing the achievement as a difficult milestone.

Kardashian has previously suggested she could eventually leave reality television to focus on courtroom work. For now, however, she says she will return to studying when her schedule allows.

headline: Sindh declares Nov 9 holiday for public, private schools
description: Schools across the province to remain closed on account of birth anniversary of Allama Muhammad Iqbal
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Schools across the province to remain closed on account of birth anniversary of Allama Muhammad Iqbal

The Sindh government on Wednesday announced a public holiday for all public and private schools across the province on November 9 to mark the birth anniversary of poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal.

According to a notification issued by the School Education and Literacy Department, all educational institutions functioning under its administrative control will remain closed on the day.

The department said the decision had been taken in pursuance of a resolution adopted at a meeting of the Steering Committee on Education held on February 12.

The notification was circulated to the relevant education authorities and institutions for implementation.

It also directed all regional directors of school education (elementary, secondary and higher secondary/primary) across Sindh to ensure that the notification was circulated among educational institutions.

The Directorate General of Inspection and Registration of Private Institutions was also asked to take the necessary action in this regard.

headline: Pakistan’s Maliha stuns European champion at MMA worlds
description: Hunza fighter advances to quarter-finals after split-decision victory over Russia’s Veronika Drozdova
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan’s Maliha Ali produced an impressive performance to defeat two-time European champion Veronika Drozdova at the IMMAF World Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia, on Tuesday.

The 24-year-old from Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan, edged the 19-year-old Russian by split decision in their featherweight (65.8kg) bout to advance to the quarter-finals.

Maliha, a wushu champion and national kickboxing gold medallist, entered the tournament after winning silver at the IMMAF World Cup in Angola earlier this year.

Fighting from a southpaw stance, she started cautiously before taking the fight to Drozdova against the cage and landing clean strikes to finish the opening round strongly.

She stepped up her performance in the second, securing a takedown and moving into full mount, where she landed several heavy blows from the top.

However, Maliha appeared to tire in the final round, allowing Drozdova to secure a takedown and control much of the action on the ground.

The Russian took the third round, but Maliha’s dominance in the opening two proved decisive as the judges awarded her the victory.

She celebrated the announcement with a roar before embracing her opponent and dropping to the mat in prostration, with the Pakistan flag draped over her shoulders.

Pakistan MMA Federation president Omar Ahmed also celebrated jubilantly from her corner.

Maliha will face Mexico’s Andrea Gabriela Guzman Salazar in Wednesday’s quarter-finals as she targets a place in the last four.

Her twin sister Manesha, who won gold at the World Cup in Luanda earlier this year, will also compete on Wednesday, taking on Poland’s Martyna Caruk.

headline: Saudi Arabia says danger has passed in Najran after earlier alert
description: Four airstrikes target Houthi weapons depots, military vehicles at Central Security Camp in Al-Bayda province
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence said Wednesday that the danger had passed in southwestern Najran province following an earlier warning of a “potential danger.”

In a statement on US social media platform X, the Civil Defence urged residents to continue following its instructions and to “avoid gathering and filming.”

This marked the second such alert issued for Najran province on Wednesday. Earlier in the day, Saudi authorities also issued a warning for Riyadh province before announcing that “the danger has passed.”

Earlier, four airstrikes targeted weapons depots and military vehicles belonging to Yemen’s Houthi group at the Central Security Camp in Al-Bayda province, Al-Jumhuriya TV reported on Wednesday, citing field sources. The broadcaster provided no details on casualties or the extent of the damage, and the party responsible for the attack remained unidentified.

The Houthis control most of Al-Bayda, a strategically important province in central Yemen that borders eight others.

Al-Jumhuriya TV also reported that Houthi missile shelling targeted the vicinity of Al-Allala military camp in Qatabah district, in northern Al-Dhalea governorate, with reports of deaths and injuries among recruits.

Separately, Aden TV reported that an ambush killed or wounded Houthi fighters during an attempted infiltration in the Al-Aqroud area, south of Taiz. The broadcaster also said artillery belonging to the armed forces targeted Houthi positions on the fronts in Marib.

In another development, Aden TV reported that the Houthis targeted a prison at the Iron Factory in Lahj province with a ballistic missile. It said there were reports of deaths and injuries among detainees inside the prison.

Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have been conducting an operation dubbed “Dawn of Yemen,” aimed at regaining control of state institutions and retaking the capital, Sanaa, from the group.

Fighting between the two sides resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than 250,000 people, according to United Nations reports. The renewed fighting ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed since April 2022, while worsening Yemen’s humanitarian crisis amid continued conflict and displacement.

Yemen has been mired in civil war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

headline: At least 7 Muslims elected to US Congress in midterm elections
description: Candidates campaigned on civil rights, healthcare and opposition to unconditional US military support for Israel
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
At least seven Muslim lawmakers won seats in the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, marking historic gains in both chambers as candidates campaigned on civil rights, healthcare and foreign policy.

The elections shifted the balance of power in Washington, with Democrats winning control of both the Senate and House of Representatives from Republicans.

Several newly elected and returning lawmakers campaigned on international legal standards, humanitarian assistance and opposition to unconditional US military support for Israel amid the ongoing genocide in Gaza.

Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan

The 42-year-old Democratic candidate defeated former Republican Representative Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

A physician and former public health official, El-Sayed won the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters following a contentious campaign in which his religion became a target of attacks by Republicans and President Donald Trump.

El-Sayed, who won the Democratic primary in August, criticised unconditional US arms transfers to Israel and described its military operations in Gaza as genocide.

His former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, endorsed Rogers two days before the general election over El-Sayed's rhetoric.

Adam Hamawy, New Jersey

The 56-year-old Democrat defeated Republican Gregg Mele in the state's 12th Congressional District, becoming the first Muslim elected to represent New Jersey in Congress.

A plastic surgeon, retired US Army combat physician, and Iraq War veteran, Hamawy volunteered at the European Hospital in Gaza in 2024.

He campaigned for universal Medicare, cancellation of medical and student debt, abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and an end to US military assistance to Israel.

Darializa Avila Chevalier, New York

The Democrat secured a House seat after previously defeating longtime incumbent Representative Adriano Espaillat in the June primary.

Chevalier, a civil rights investigator, doctoral student and convert to Islam, won more than 85% of the vote.

Her campaign focused on community organising and advocacy for Palestinian rights.

Incumbent Muslim lawmakers retain seats

Four Muslim members of the House of Representatives won reelection to two-year terms, maintaining their roles in congressional debates over foreign policy and Palestinian rights.

Rashida Tlaib, Michigan

The Palestinian-American Democrat secured a fifth term representing the state's 12th Congressional District, defeating Republican James Hooper.

The only Palestinian-American member of Congress, Tlaib has advocated enforcement of domestic and international arms regulations, civilian protection and Palestinian self-determination.

Ilhan Omar, Minnesota

The Democrat won a fifth term representing the state's 5th Congressional District, defeating Republican John Nagel and independent candidate DeVelle Jackson.

Omar, who arrived in the US at age 12, became the country's first Somali-American federal lawmaker when she took office in 2019.

She has advocated humanitarian assistance and oversight of US arms transfers while facing repeated political attacks over her background.

Andre Carson, Indiana

The Democrat retained his Indianapolis-based 7th Congressional District seat against Republican Patrick McAuley and Libertarian James Sceniak.

Serving since 2008, Carson is the longest-serving Muslim lawmaker in the House.

His policy positions have emphasised international legal institutions, equal human dignity and humanitarian assistance.

Lateefah Simon, California

The Democrat retained her seat representing the state's 12th Congressional District in the East Bay, defeating fellow Democrat Jamie Joyce.

Simon has advocated against offensive US arms deliveries.

Meanwhile, Muslim candidate Aisha Wahab maintained an early lead in a separate congressional race in California as vote counting continued.

article_html:
At least seven Muslim lawmakers won seats in the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, marking historic gains in both chambers as candidates campaigned on civil rights, healthcare and foreign policy.

The elections shifted the balance of power in Washington, with Democrats winning control of both the Senate and House of Representatives from Republicans.

Several newly elected and returning lawmakers campaigned on international legal standards, humanitarian assistance and opposition to unconditional US military support for Israel amid the ongoing genocide in Gaza.

Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan

The 42-year-old Democratic candidate defeated former Republican Representative Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

A physician and former public health official, El-Sayed won the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters following a contentious campaign in which his religion became a target of attacks by Republicans and President Donald Trump.

El-Sayed, who won the Democratic primary in August, criticised unconditional US arms transfers to Israel and described its military operations in Gaza as genocide.

His former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, endorsed Rogers two days before the general election over El-Sayed's rhetoric.

Adam Hamawy, New Jersey

The 56-year-old Democrat defeated Republican Gregg Mele in the state's 12th Congressional District, becoming the first Muslim elected to represent New Jersey in Congress.

A plastic surgeon, retired US Army combat physician, and Iraq War veteran, Hamawy volunteered at the European Hospital in Gaza in 2024.

He campaigned for universal Medicare, cancellation of medical and student debt, abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and an end to US military assistance to Israel.

Darializa Avila Chevalier, New York

The Democrat secured a House seat after previously defeating longtime incumbent Representative Adriano Espaillat in the June primary.

Chevalier, a civil rights investigator, doctoral student and convert to Islam, won more than 85% of the vote.

Her campaign focused on community organising and advocacy for Palestinian rights.

Incumbent Muslim lawmakers retain seats

Four Muslim members of the House of Representatives won reelection to two-year terms, maintaining their roles in congressional debates over foreign policy and Palestinian rights.

Rashida Tlaib, Michigan

The Palestinian-American Democrat secured a fifth term representing the state's 12th Congressional District, defeating Republican James Hooper.

The only Palestinian-American member of Congress, Tlaib has advocated enforcement of domestic and international arms regulations, civilian protection and Palestinian self-determination.

Ilhan Omar, Minnesota

The Democrat won a fifth term representing the state's 5th Congressional District, defeating Republican John Nagel and independent candidate DeVelle Jackson.

Omar, who arrived in the US at age 12, became the country's first Somali-American federal lawmaker when she took office in 2019.

She has advocated humanitarian assistance and oversight of US arms transfers while facing repeated political attacks over her background.

Andre Carson, Indiana

The Democrat retained his Indianapolis-based 7th Congressional District seat against Republican Patrick McAuley and Libertarian James Sceniak.

Serving since 2008, Carson is the longest-serving Muslim lawmaker in the House.

His policy positions have emphasised international legal institutions, equal human dignity and humanitarian assistance.

Lateefah Simon, California

The Democrat retained her seat representing the state's 12th Congressional District in the East Bay, defeating fellow Democrat Jamie Joyce.

Simon has advocated against offensive US arms deliveries.

Meanwhile, Muslim candidate Aisha Wahab maintained an early lead in a separate congressional race in California as vote counting continued.

headline: Starc topples Jansen to reclaim No1 spot in Test rankings
description: The 36-year-old overtakes South Africa's Marco Jansen following his impressive wicket-taking run
author: REUTERS
article_text:
The 36-year-old overtakes South Africa's Marco Jansen following his impressive wicket-taking run

Australia ​fast bowler Mitchell Starc has moved to the top of the ICC test bowling rankings, reclaiming the top spot from South African all-rounder Marco ​Jansen.

Starc ​was the leading wicket-taker in the ​recently concluded series in South Africa, picking up 15 ⁠wickets in three tests, Although Australia ‌lost the final test to lose a thrilling series 2-1, Starc ⁠finished with nine ⁠wickets in the ​match ‌which included a first-innings haul of 6-72 Jansen had claimed the top position in the bowlers' and all-rounders' rankings only last ⁠week after a superb performance with ⁠the bat and ball in the second test, before being displaced by the 36-year-old Australian.

South Africa's Simon Harmer, who was named Player of ⁠the Match after the ​spinner claimed his maiden 10-wicket match haul in the third test, climbed nine places to ​seventh

headline: Dylan Sprouse exposes shockingly low residual payment for ‘The Suite Life of Zack and Cody’
description: The actor and Phill Lewis also reflected on their close bond years after working together on Disney Channel
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Dylan Sprouse has revealed that he received just five cents in residuals for his time on Disney Channel’s hit sitcom The Suite Life of Zack and Cody, despite the show’s popularity and extensive international reach.

The actor made the surprising revelation during the November 3 episode of his Wildmen podcast, where he reunited with former co-star Phill Lewis to discuss their experiences working on the beloved series.

Sprouse explained that the only residual payment he could recall receiving was connected to a crossover episode featuring Hannah Montana.

“The only residual check I have ever received for The Suite Life at all was a crossover episode with Hannah Montana for five cents,” he said, emphasising that he was serious about the amount.

The original series aired from 2005 to 2008, followed by its spin-off, The Suite Life on Deck, which ran from 2008 to 2011. Together, the shows produced around 190 episodes during Sprouse’s time with Disney Channel.

Lewis also discussed the contracts actors had during the production, claiming that episodes could be filmed in large numbers within a calendar year while being counted as a single television season. He suggested this arrangement helped the network avoid paying additional salary increases.

Sprouse described the show as popular but underfunded, while both actors reflected on how television worked before streaming services became widespread. Lewis recalled the programmes airing repeatedly throughout the day and reaching audiences in approximately 90 countries.

Despite the financial discussion, Sprouse spoke warmly about Lewis, who played hotel manager Marion Moseby on the series. He described the actor as a second father figure and revealed that they continue to spend time together and speak regularly.

Sprouse also credited Lewis with helping shape his love of acting, praising his talent and personality.

Both The Suite Life of Zack and Cody and The Suite Life on Deck are currently available to stream on Disney+.

headline: Google unveils $15 billion data centre investment in Malaysia
description: US tech giant says investment will be made over next two years, expanding on $2 billion investment announced in 2024
author: AFP
article_text:
Google announced plans on Wednesday to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure as demand booms for artificial intelligence services.

The country is Southeast Asia's fastest growing hub for new data centres — warehouse-like buildings crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators.

"Malaysia is one of Southeast Asia's most dynamic digital economies, driven by 99% internet penetration and rapid AI adoption across government agencies, businesses, and consumers," the United States tech giant said in a statement. It said the $15 billion investment will be made "over the next two years (2027 to 2028)", expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024.

AI data centres require large amounts of electricity — placing increased pressure on grids often still reliant on fossil fuels — and, in many cases, water to cool down hot computing equipment. Backlash is growing worldwide against their environmental impact, and there are also concerns over noise, pollution, their appearance and how many jobs the facilities actually create.

Google pledged Wednesday that its data centre campuses in Malaysian industrial zones would be "energy-efficient". The company said it would work to "bolster local water security, and add more than one gigawatt of clean energy capacity" to the national grid.

"Once operational, the facilities are projected to sustain more than 9,000 local jobs per year, with wages averaging 45% above the national median," it added.

Malaysia accounts for more than half of under-construction data centre capacity among Southeast Asian countries, including Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Vietnam, according to market intelligence firm DC Byte.

The International Monetary Fund forecasts that Malaysia's economy will grow by 5.2% in 2026, partly encouraged by data centre activity. But by 2035, data centres are forecast to swallow up one-third of Malaysia's total energy consumption, the deputy prime minister told parliament in July.

The government said at that time it would only approve data centre projects after ensuring sufficient energy and water supply capacity.

In October, a Finnish authority ordered work on two of Google's data centre sites in the country halted until mandatory environmental impact assessments have been completed.

headline: Josh O’Connor breaks silence on James Bond casting rumours
description: Pierce Brosnan has praised Callum Turner, describing his former co-star as a particularly strong candidate
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Josh O’Connor has described the speculation linking him to the role of James Bond as an extraordinary experience, but has offered no confirmation about whether he is being considered for the part.

The Challengers and The Crown actor addressed the reports while attending the opening of the Everyman Theatre in his hometown of Cheltenham, England, on November 3. Speaking about being mentioned among potential successors to Daniel Craig, O’Connor called it an “incredibly bizarre pinch me moment”.

“To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary,” he said, adding that there was nothing further he could share about the possibility.

O’Connor, 36, has reportedly been among a small group of actors linked to screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ next Bond film. The Hollywood Reporter previously reported that Callum Turner and Jack Lowden were also among those being considered.

However, no successor to Craig has been officially announced, and the reports do not confirm that any of the actors has secured the role.

The upcoming film is set to be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for Dune, with Steven Knight, creator of Peaky Blinders, writing the screenplay.

Lowden recently responded to the speculation in an interview with British GQ, describing the attention as flattering but declining to add to the discussion.

Former Bond actor Pierce Brosnan has also shared his thoughts on the possible contenders. Speaking to Vanity Fair, he praised the actors reportedly in the running and singled out Turner, his co-star in The Only Living Boy in New York.

“Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” Brosnan said.

The casting search is being led by Nina Gold, who previously cast O’Connor as Prince Charles in The Crown and Lowden as River Cartwright in Slow Horses. The identity of the next 007 remains unconfirmed.

headline: Pakistan, UK voice concern over terrorism threat from Afghanistan: FO
description: Both sides agree to address emerging threats, including disinformation and the misuse of social media
author: web.desk
article_text:
Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Wednesday reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening counterterrorism cooperation, expressing concern over the continued threat posed by terrorist groups including the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) operating in and from Afghanistan, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said.

In a statement issued after the annual Pakistan-UK Counterterrorism Dialogue held in Islamabad, the Foreign Office said the two sides had discussed the evolving global and regional security environment, including threats posed by terrorist organisations and transnational networks.

The UK also expressed condolences over the loss of innocent lives in terrorist attacks in Pakistan and reiterated its support for Islamabad in the fight against terrorism.

Both sides underscored the need for a stable and secure Afghanistan as a cornerstone of lasting peace and prosperity across the region.

The dialogue also reviewed ongoing bilateral and multilateral cooperation in counterterrorism, with both countries reaffirming their shared commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

The discussions further focused on exchanging best practices and exploring new avenues of partnership to address emerging trends in terrorism, including misinformation and disinformation campaigns, the exploitation of social media platforms and the misuse of emerging technologies.

Both sides also acknowledged Pakistan's contributions to regional stability and security and agreed to strengthen institutional linkages and maintain regular engagement to advance their shared counterterrorism objectives.

The two countries agreed to hold the next round of the Pakistan-UK Counterterrorism Dialogue in London in 2027, on mutually agreed dates.

headline: Apple AI tools come to China after two-year delay
description: Trial rollout restricted to developers but public access to Apple Intelligence services will come in December
author: AFP
article_text:
Apple began on Wednesday a long-delayed trial rollout of in-house artificial intelligence tools for Chinese users, playing catch-up to homegrown smartphone makers in a major market for the United States giant.

The on-device features dubbed "Apple Intelligence" were first released in the US and other countries in autumn 2024, marking the firm's first major push into generative AI. But strict Chinese regulatory requirements for the fast-evolving technology have held back its launch there — as well as the fact that models from Google and OpenAI, which Apple has used elsewhere to boost its own AI capabilities, are not available in the country.

Apple, which has largely stayed out of the global AI investment frenzy, announced it will work with a Chinese partner — Alibaba's Qwen — to integrate more powerful AI features into devices alongside its own basic AI offerings.

Wednesday's trial rollout is restricted to developers, but public access to Apple Intelligence services in China will come in December, the company said in a statement at the weekend.

The long-anticipated Chinese rollout of Apple Intelligence "fills a long-standing gap in Apple's AI offering", said Ivan Lam, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research. However, it does not necessarily give the Californian company "a significant advantage" in a crowded market, Lam said.

The initial release includes 18 AI features, from live translation of phone calls to tools for summarising and proofreading messages, but not the latest upgrade of iPhone assistant Siri.

'Concession'

Chinese regulations require AI service providers to register with the country's internet watchdog, and there are requirements to use local data centres and process data domestically.

Apple only secured regulatory approval in July, after reportedly holding talks with Chinese tech firms including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance and Tencent about partnerships on Apple Intelligence. Major US AI firms, including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, have either banned Chinese users or restricted access to their services, and are unlikely to secure regulatory clearance.

Working with local partners on Apple Intelligence "signifies a structural concession by Apple regarding its pricing and defining power over the AI experience in the Chinese market", Zhang Yi, founder of research firm iiMedia, told AFP. Apple's delay in introducing AI tools in China was not due to lags in research and development, but rather "compliance costs", he said.

Despite reporting a 21% increase in revenue in the Greater China region, which includes Hong Kong and Taiwan, for the past quarter, Apple's new CEO John Ternus still faces significant challenges in an evolving market.

According to research firm Omdia, more than 110 million iPhones in China can support Apple Intelligence, providing a foundation for quick adoption — but competition is fierce. article_html:
Apple began on Wednesday a long-delayed trial rollout of in-house artificial intelligence tools for Chinese users, playing catch-up to homegrown smartphone makers in a major market for the United States giant.

The on-device features dubbed "Apple Intelligence" were first released in the US and other countries in autumn 2024, marking the firm's first major push into generative AI. But strict Chinese regulatory requirements for the fast-evolving technology have held back its launch there — as well as the fact that models from Google and OpenAI, which Apple has used elsewhere to boost its own AI capabilities, are not available in the country.

Apple, which has largely stayed out of the global AI investment frenzy, announced it will work with a Chinese partner — Alibaba's Qwen — to integrate more powerful AI features into devices alongside its own basic AI offerings.

Read: In China, the AI bubble has already burst

Wednesday's trial rollout is restricted to developers, but public access to Apple Intelligence services in China will come in December, the company said in a statement at the weekend.

The long-anticipated Chinese rollout of Apple Intelligence "fills a long-standing gap in Apple's AI offering", said Ivan Lam, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research. However, it does not necessarily give the Californian company "a significant advantage" in a crowded market, Lam said.

The initial release includes 18 AI features, from live translation of phone calls to tools for summarising and proofreading messages, but not the latest upgrade of iPhone assistant Siri.

'Concession'

Chinese regulations require AI service providers to register with the country's internet watchdog, and there are requirements to use local data centres and process data domestically.

Apple only secured regulatory approval in July, after reportedly holding talks with Chinese tech firms including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance and Tencent about partnerships on Apple Intelligence. Major US AI firms, including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, have either banned Chinese users or restricted access to their services, and are unlikely to secure regulatory clearance.

Working with local partners on Apple Intelligence "signifies a structural concession by Apple regarding its pricing and defining power over the AI experience in the Chinese market", Zhang Yi, founder of research firm iiMedia, told AFP. Apple's delay in introducing AI tools in China was not due to lags in research and development, but rather "compliance costs", he said.

headline: Asim Azhar invites Lahore's Surtaal Kids Band to open his tour
description: The singer invited the young performers of Lahore’s Surtaal Music Academy to open his upcoming November tour
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Singer Asim Azhar announced a special opening act for his upcoming Asim Ali Tour, inviting young performers from Lahore’s Surtaal Music Academy to join him at concerts across Pakistan.

The Surtaal Kids Band will accompany Azhar at three stops on the Pakistan leg of his tour: Faisalabad on November 6, Lahore on November 7 and Islamabad on November 8. The concerts will mark the children's first public performances on such a major platform.

The announcement came through a collaborative Instagram post featuring Azhar and the academy, in which the young musicians expressed their excitement about performing alongside the singer.

“Surtaal Kids Band is coming to the Asim Ali Tour! 6th Nov | FAISALABAD | 7th | LAHORE | 8th Nov ko | ISLAMABAD with @asimazhar Bhai. See You There!” the academy wrote in its announcement.

In the accompanying video, Azhar is seen sitting among the children as he explains what prompted him to invite them to perform at his concerts. “The kids invited me here with so much love that I thought I should return the gesture by giving them an opportunity to perform as the opening act of my Asim Ali Tour,” he said.

The interaction then turns into a musical moment, with the children performing a rendition of Azhar’s hit song Jo Tu Na Mila to showcase their vocal abilities. The singer also joins them, making the visit even more memorable for the young performers.

View this post on Instagram

Based in Lahore, Surtaal Music Academy has been attracting attention on social media for its young musicians' impressive renditions of traditional and contemporary music.

Established in 2016 by music educator Zia-ul-Haq, the academy aims to make structured music education accessible to children, particularly those from underprivileged backgrounds. It provides free music lessons and trains more than 100 students in vocals and various musical instruments, helping them develop their abilities and gain opportunities to perform.

The students recently went viral for their soulful rendition of the popular song Alfaaz, which they performed alongside Norwegian singer and dancer William Gamborg during his visit to the academy. The performance received widespread appreciation on social media, with viewers praising the children's command of Qawwali and affectionately referring to them as the “little Nusrats”.

The performance brought wider attention to the academy and its young musicians, highlighting the talent emerging from its classrooms and the opportunities that can help young artists reach wider audiences.

Now, with their upcoming appearances alongside Azhar, the children are set to take another significant step in their musical journey. Their inclusion in the tour offers them an opportunity to perform before larger audiences while highlighting how established artists can help create space for the next generation of Pakistani musical talent.

headline: Police use tear gas on protesting teachers, detain 42 marching towards CM House in Karachi
description: Teachers demand restoration of service structure, promotions and employment rights, attempt to march towards CM House
author: Ayesha Khan Ansari
article_text:
Police used water cannons, tear gas and batons to disperse protesting primary school teachers from various districts of Sindh near the Chief Minister's House on Wednesday, detaining 42 demonstrators demanding the restoration of their service structure, promotions and other employment-related rights.

The protesters, representing the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (ASPTA), staged a sit-in outside the press club before attempting to march towards the CM House, which was immediately blocked by a heavy police contingent.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) South Mahzor Ali said the police had detained 42 men for protesting in the red zone.

He said the protestors are in the process of being released after Karachi Bar Association General Secretary Arshad Shar guaranteed on behalf of the demonstrators that the detained persons will not engage in protests inside the red zone.

“The protestors will be handed over to the Karachi Bar Association after they file the undertaking,” SSP Shar added.

View this post on Instagram

Teachers from Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Jacobabad, Mirpur Mathelo, Sukkur, Shaheed Benazirabad and other districts participated in the demonstration.

The Express Tribune witnessed police personnel preventing the demonstrators from reaching their destination by charging with batons, firing tear gas shells and using a water cannon, triggering chaos at the scene.

Several teachers were injured, one of whom was taken to the hospital, while a number of protesters, including the association’s central president, were reportedly taken into custody as they pressed the authorities to accept their 14 work-related demands.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, a protesting teacher, Kausar, said that police had subjected demonstrators to severe tear gas shelling as they attempted to move towards the CM House. She also claimed that the association's central president, Ijaz Ali Chandio, had been taken into custody.

Kausar said teachers would not call off their protest or reopen schools until their leadership was released and progress was made towards meeting their demands.

Shabina Khan, another teacher associated with the Primary Teachers Association Hyderabad, said teachers had been campaigning for their demands since August and that the protest had not been organised without prior notice.

She said the association had already submitted a list of 14 demands to the government, with the restoration of a formal service structure for primary school teachers among its foremost demands.

According to Shabina, many primary teachers worked on the same grade for years, with limited opportunities for career progression.

She said teachers were currently serving in grades 9, 14 and 16, while high school teachers had better promotion opportunities and their Departmental Promotion Committees (DPCs) were held regularly.

She added that the government had also discontinued the progression of primary teachers to high school teacher posts.

Shabina highlighted that Sindh Education and Literacy Minister Syed Sardar Ali Shah had expressed his desire on October 5 to see primary teachers promoted up to grade 20. However, she maintained that a formal service structure was necessary to make such promotions possible and provide teachers with a clear career progression pathway.

Another key demand, she said, was that teachers' service should be counted from their initial date of appointment. Under the existing arrangement, the initial three-year contractual period is not included in the service record, adversely affecting their chances at promotions and grade upgrades.

“Some senior primary teachers in Sindh have been serving for 18 years but are still working in grade 9, whereas teachers recruited between 2022 and 2025 have been appointed in grade 14,” she revealed.

To end absenteeism, Shabina said the association has demanded that the district-level biometric attendance and transfer systems be restored, while asserting that the Sindh Secretariat centralised both systems, creating difficulties for teachers.

“Transfers are sometimes made to distant areas without taking their preferences or convenience into account,” she lamented.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Saima Khan, the association's district vice president, said smaller government schools should not be merged with larger institutions.

“The government should explore alternative solutions to address administrative issues,” she added.

She said the cluster hub policy, under which primary schools were being merged into larger schools, was undermining the identity and status of primary schools and their teachers.

“Teachers are being assigned administrative responsibilities beyond their core duties,” she protested.

The protesters also expressed concern over the declining number of standalone primary schools across Sindh, saying several institutions were being merged with higher secondary or larger schools.

They specifically cited the proposed merger of Hyderabad's historic Firdous Primary School with a higher secondary school, saying such decisions threatened the separate identity of primary education institutions.

In a unified call, the teachers demanded the restoration of a formal service structure, upgradation of grades, counting of service from the initial date of appointment, decentralisation of the biometric attendance and transfer systems, withdrawal of the cluster hub policy and preservation of the independent status of primary schools.

They vowed to protest until their rights were granted.

Following the protest, roads surrounding the Karachi Press Club were closed to traffic, while Sir Syed Road was also shut. Traffic was diverted towards Aiwan-e-Sadr Road and Zainab Market, according to traffic police.

KARACHI:

Police used water cannons, tear gas and batons to disperse protesting primary school teachers from various districts of Sindh near the Chief Minister's House on Wednesday, detaining 42 demonstrators demanding the restoration of their service structure, promotions and other employment-related rights.

The protesters, representing the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (ASPTA), staged a sit-in outside the press club before attempting to march towards the CM House, which was immediately blocked by a heavy police contingent.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) South Mahzor Ali said the police had detained 42 men for protesting in the red zone.

He said the protestors are in the process of being released after Karachi Bar Association General Secretary Arshad Shar guaranteed on behalf of the demonstrators that the detained persons will not engage in protests inside the red zone.

“The protestors will be handed over to the Karachi Bar Association after they file the undertaking,” SSP Shar added.

 
 
 
 
View this post on Instagram
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Teachers from Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Jacobabad, Mirpur Mathelo, Sukkur, Shaheed Benazirabad and other districts participated in the demonstration.

The Express Tribune witnessed police personnel preventing the demonstrators from reaching their destination by charging with batons, firing tear gas shells and using a water cannon, triggering chaos at the scene.

Several teachers were injured, one of whom was taken to the hospital, while a number of protesters, including the association’s central president, were reportedly taken into custody as they pressed the authorities to accept their 14 work-related demands.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, a protesting teacher, Kausar, said that police had subjected demonstrators to severe tear gas shelling as they attempted to move towards the CM House. She also claimed that the association's central president, Ijaz Ali Chandio, had been taken into custody.

Kausar said teachers would not call off their protest or reopen schools until their leadership was released and progress was made towards meeting their demands.

Shabina Khan, another teacher associated with the Primary Teachers Association Hyderabad, said teachers had been campaigning for their demands since August and that the protest had not been organised without prior notice.

She said the association had already submitted a list of 14 demands to the government, with the restoration of a formal service structure for primary school teachers among its foremost demands.

According to Shabina, many primary teachers worked on the same grade for years, with limited opportunities for career progression.

She said teachers were currently serving in grades 9, 14 and 16, while high school teachers had better promotion opportunities and their Departmental Promotion Committees (DPCs) were held regularly.

She added that the government had also discontinued the progression of primary teachers to high school teacher posts.

Shabina highlighted that Sindh Education and Literacy Minister Syed Sardar Ali Shah had expressed his desire on October 5 to see primary teachers promoted up to grade 20. However, she maintained that a formal service structure was necessary to make such promotions possible and provide teachers with a clear career progression pathway.

Another key demand, she said, was that teachers' service should be counted from their initial date of appointment. Under the existing arrangement, the initial three-year contractual period is not included in the service record, adversely affecting their chances at promotions and grade upgrades.

“Some senior primary teachers in Sindh have been serving for 18 years but are still working in grade 9, whereas teachers recruited between 2022 and 2025 have been appointed in grade 14,” she revealed.

To end absenteeism, Shabina said the association has demanded that the district-level biometric attendance and transfer systems be restored, while asserting that the Sindh Secretariat centralised both systems, creating difficulties for teachers.

“Transfers are sometimes made to distant areas without taking their preferences or convenience into account,” she lamented.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Saima Khan, the association's district vice president, said smaller government schools should not be merged with larger institutions.

“The government should explore alternative solutions to address administrative issues,” she added.

She said the cluster hub policy, under which primary schools were being merged into larger schools, was undermining the identity and status of primary schools and their teachers.

“Teachers are being assigned administrative responsibilities beyond their core duties,” she protested.

The protesters also expressed concern over the declining number of standalone primary schools across Sindh, saying several institutions were being merged with higher secondary or larger schools.

They specifically cited the proposed merger of Hyderabad's historic Firdous Primary School with a higher secondary school, saying such decisions threatened the separate identity of primary education institutions.

In a unified call, the teachers demanded the restoration of a formal service structure, upgradation of grades, counting of service from the initial date of appointment, decentralisation of the biometric attendance and transfer systems, withdrawal of the cluster hub policy and preservation of the independent status of primary schools.

They vowed to protest until their rights were granted.

Following the protest, roads surrounding the Karachi Press Club were closed to traffic, while Sir Syed Road was also shut. Traffic was diverted towards Aiwan-e-Sadr Road and Zainab Market, according to traffic police.

headline: Australia social media teen ban a 'modest' step, says govt in top court challenge
description: Reddit, advocacy group say law violates constitutionally protected speech as govt calls it harm minimisation measure
author: Reuters
article_text:
Australia's world-first teen social media ban was a modest, non-partisan and justified curb on political expression, a lawyer for the government told the top court on Wednesday, rejecting a legal challenge by Reddit.

Nearly a year since Australia banned large social media platforms from allowing under-16s to hold accounts, messaging platform Reddit and a libertarian advocacy group have sought to invalidate the law on grounds that it violates constitutionally protected speech.

The government is defending the law, calling it a necessary harm minimisation measure.

A win for the plaintiffs would be a major setback not just for Australia but for lawmakers around the world who followed with similar measures in what has become a global movement to protect child physical and mental health in the digital age.

After a lawyer for Reddit told the court the law's imposition on free speech for minors was disproportionate to the benefits of keeping them off social media, Stephen Lloyd, for the government, said the ban was a relatively minor measure with proven positive effects. "The burden is indirect and modest in extent," Lloyd told the court's seven-judge panel on the second day of hearings.

The law "incrementally" reduced children's ability to send and receive content online, while they could still view some content without an account, he added, noting it was "viewpoint neutral" so did not target any particular type of political expression.

Under the law, children and caregivers face no punishment but platforms can be fined up to A$99 million ($68.97 million) for systemic noncompliance.

So far, multiple studies including by Australian regulator the eSafety Commissioner have found that most of the country's under-16s still use social media, and the government has said it is preparing an enforcement lawsuit.

On Wednesday, Lloyd said it was unclear if noncompliance was the result of weaknesses in age assurance technology or platforms' failure to implement it, but added that the law would contribute to the government's child protection aims regardless.

The hearing has been adjourned to a date to be decided, when the judges are expected to give a ruling.

headline: Hailey Bieber reveals PMDD diagnosis after giving birth to son Jack Blues
description: Hailey Bieber says she was diagnosed with PMDD six months after welcoming her son, Jack Blues
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hailey Bieber has revealed that she struggled with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) after giving birth to her son, Jack Blues, describing the emotional symptoms she experienced in the months following childbirth.

The Rhode founder, 29, discussed her experience in an interview with Women's Wear Daily. She explained that becoming a mother increased her interest in women's health and the physical and emotional changes associated with pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.

"After I had my son, I struggled with that a bit, and there's just not a lot of conversation or research around it," Bieber said, referring to her experience with PMDD.

She previously discussed her diagnosis during a March appearance on the SHE MD podcast, revealing that she was diagnosed approximately six months after giving birth.

Although Bieber had experienced premenstrual syndrome (PMS) before pregnancy, she said the emotional symptoms became considerably more intense after welcoming Jack. She particularly struggled in the days leading up to her period.

"I was like, 'This just feels way more intense than before,' like the lead-up to getting your period," she explained.

"You're like, 'Why does it feel like my whole entire life is gonna end? Like, I don't understand.' You just have all these swirling thoughts and feelings, and just everything feels like the biggest deal in the world."

Bieber said the feelings would ease once her period began and that her symptoms gradually improved over time.

PMDD is similar to PMS but can involve more severe symptoms, including intense mood changes, irritability, depression and anxiety in the weeks before menstruation.

The model also spoke about how motherhood has affected her life, describing it as an experience she had always wanted. Bieber and her husband, Justin Bieber, welcomed Jack on August 22 2024.

She has also expressed interest in having another child, although she is not rushing to expand their family.

"I definitely do want one more," she said. "I'm not in a rush, but I definitely want one more."

headline: ‘Obsession’ director Curry Barker releases disturbing new short film ‘Mama Bear’
description: The filmmaker’s latest project delivers a sinister twist in under five minutes
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Curry Barker, the filmmaker behind horror hit Obsession, has returned to YouTube with a disturbing new short film titled Mama Bear, bringing viewers a chilling doppelganger story in under five minutes.

Barker previously gained attention online through independent projects including The Chair and Milk & Serial, which attracted millions of views before his latest feature made waves in cinemas. With Mama Bear, he revisits the platform that helped establish his reputation as a horror filmmaker.

The short centres on Floyd, played by Jon Lee Richardson, who receives a frantic phone call from a friend claiming that someone who looks exactly like him has been spotted. Floyd initially dismisses the warning as a joke.

Things take a sinister turn when he receives a voicemail from his girlfriend, Lacey, portrayed by Katie Sarfie. Her furious message suggests that Floyd, or someone resembling him, has done something deeply upsetting. The film never fully explains what happened, leaving viewers to piece together the disturbing mystery.

The story builds towards a shocking conclusion, with Barker using the familiar concept of a doppelganger to create suspense and unease. The short demonstrates his ability to take established horror ideas and give them an unpredictable edge.

That approach also featured in Obsession, which follows Bear, played by Michael Johnston, as he makes a wish for his crush Nikki, portrayed by Inde Navarrette, to love him unconditionally. The wish leads to increasingly disturbing consequences.

Barker has several projects in development. His horror comedy Anything But Ghosts, starring Aaron Paul alongside Barker and longtime collaborator Cooper Tomlinson, is expected to arrive in May 2027.

He has also been tapped to direct a new The Texas Chainsaw Massacre film following A24’s acquisition of the franchise rights. The project remains in its early stages, with plot details yet to be announced.

headline: Ariana Grande fans criticise Ricky Alvarez after NYC marathon appearance
description: Ariana Grande fans criticised Ricky Alvarez after video showed their interaction at New York City Marathon
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ariana Grande fans criticised Ricky Alvarez after video showed their interaction at New York City Marathon

Ariana Grande and Ricky Alvarez have faced online scrutiny after appearing together at the New York City Marathon, where some fans criticised the photographer for not helping the singer during a brief interaction.

The couple attended the event in Manhattan, where a digital content creator behind the project Ella's Envelope approached them and asked whether they would leave an encouraging message for runners.

Grande agreed and wrote "You did it!" alongside several small heart doodles on a clipboard. She also signed the message "Ari + Ricky", before it was passed to a runner who was reportedly surprised to discover who had written it.

However, footage of the encounter shared on Instagram prompted criticism from some viewers, who focused on Alvarez's behaviour while Grande wrote the message.

In the video, the singer appeared to manage her drink while using the clipboard, leading some fans to question why Alvarez did not offer to hold it for her.

"Eww, he gave me the ick in this whole interaction. I hope I'm wrong," one user commented.

Another wrote sarcastically, "And way to go, Ricky, for not grabbing the drink and holding it for Ariana Grande while she was writing."

Other viewers also questioned Alvarez's facial expressions and perceived lack of involvement. The reactions reflect some fans' interpretations of the brief interaction rather than any confirmed issue between the couple.

headline: Curry Barker reveals hidden detail in ‘Obsession’ that fans may have missed
description: Inde Navarrette also reveals a deleted scene showing Bear searching for Nikki
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Curry Barker and Inde Navarrette have revealed eerie details hidden in Obsession, giving fans fresh reasons to revisit the 2026 horror film.

During an interview with Entertainment Weekly, the director and actress discussed details viewers might have overlooked, including an unsettling photograph connected to Bear, played by Michael Johnston, and Nikki, portrayed by Navarrette.

Navarrette first pointed to the altar featured towards the end of the film. She explained that Bear’s hair appears there because Nikki repeatedly cuts it. The collection of objects also includes his lunchbox and photographs, adding further significance to the scene.

Barker then drew attention to a detail involving two photographs inside Bear’s lunchbox. In an earlier scene, Bear discovers pictures labelled “you” and “not me”. The labels refer to images of Bear alone and Bear with Nikki.

According to Barker, the photograph marked “you” contains a particularly unsettling clue. He explained that the image was taken from a high angle, with Navarrette describing its perspective as looking downwards.

The interviewer suggested that the photograph might have been taken from the bed, but Barker questioned that explanation, pointing out that Nikki would have been positioned too high for that viewpoint.

The discussion also revealed that a scene involving Bear searching for Nikki was removed from the finished film. Navarrette described the sequence as a “sick scene”, explaining that Bear walks around calling out for Nikki and asking where she is.

In the deleted moment, Nikki responds that she is “just in the room”.

Although the scene did not make the final cut, the revelation has given viewers another detail to consider when revisiting the film. The filmmakers’ comments also highlight how seemingly ordinary objects and images contribute to the unsettling atmosphere of Obsession.

headline: Usman Mukhtar celebrates wife's birthday with playful banter
description: Actor shares montage of their memories, praising his wife as a loving mother, caring sister and his best friend
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Actor Usman Mukhtar celebrated his wife Zunaira Inam Khan's birthday with a heartfelt Instagram tribute, sharing a montage of their memories together and a loving message that mixed admiration with his trademark humour.

Taking to Instagram, the actor shared a video featuring glimpses of Zunaira at different moments in their life together.

The montage brought together sweet memories, celebrations, candid interactions and funny moments, offering fans a glimpse into the couple's relationship away from the spotlight.

Alongside the video, Usman penned a birthday message celebrating his wife's many qualities and the different roles she plays in the lives of those around her.

"To the woman who is the most loving mother, the most caring sister, a wonderful daughter, an incredible wife, and, above all, possibly the most intelligent human being I have ever known," he began.

The actor went on to appreciate how effortlessly Zunaira manages her many responsibilities, adding a playful touch to his otherwise emotional message.

"You wear so many hats and somehow manage to make it all look effortless (which is frankly getting a little annoying for the rest of us)," he joked.

Concluding his message, Usman wrote, "Happy Birthday, Zunaira! I hope life gives you as much happiness as you bring to everyone around you. I love you more than words can say."

View this post on Instagram

The affectionate message, coupled with the collection of personal memories, offered a glimpse into the warmth and humour that characterise their relationship.

Usman and Zunaira tied the knot in an intimate Nikah ceremony on March 31, 2021. Their wedding took place amid COVID-19 restrictions, with the actor announcing their marriage on social media and expressing gratitude for having Zunaira by his side.

The couple later celebrated their wedding festivities with family and friends, sharing glimpses of the occasions with their followers.

Their family grew in February 2025 when they welcomed their first child, a daughter named Siera Inam Mukhtar. Announcing the arrival of their baby girl, Usman expressed gratitude for the new addition to their family, describing her as a beautiful blessing who had brought immense joy into their lives.

The actor has also marked previous wedding anniversaries with affectionate messages for Zunaira. In 2024, he described her as his best friend and full-time reality check, joking that their relationship felt like a romantic comedy mixed with a roast session.

On their fourth anniversary in 2025, he wrote about how life would not feel complete without Zunaira and their daughter, describing his wife as his best friend and the person who keeps him grounded.

His latest birthday tribute continued that tradition, celebrating not only Zunaira as his wife and the mother of their daughter but also the friendship and humour that underpin their relationship.

headline: Ellen DeGeneres called ‘cheapskate’ for GoFundMe donation to late producer
description: Ellen DeGeneres faces criticism over her $5,000 donation to fundraiser for late producer Matthew Wright's family
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ellen DeGeneres has faced criticism over her $5,000 donation to a GoFundMe campaign supporting the family of Matthew Wright, her former show's longtime producer, following his death at 52.

The comedian shared an emotional video paying tribute to Wright on Monday, remembering him as a funny, intelligent and kind colleague who played an important role in the programme.

"He was an amazing guy, he was funny, god he made me laugh, he would surprise me with things that he did all the time," she said.

DeGeneres also described Wright as "the glue to our entire family at the Ellen Show", revealing that they had been preparing to work on another project before his unexpected death.

She additionally reflected on his friendship with former show DJ Stephen "tWitch" Boss, who died in 2022, saying she believed the two were now "together, dancing and laughing."

However, attention soon turned to DeGeneres' contribution to a fundraiser launched by Wright's relatives to help cover expenses following his death.

Although her $5,000 donation made her one of the campaign's leading contributors, some social media users questioned whether the amount was sufficient given her estimated $500 million fortune.

Podcaster and author Dana Parish highlighted the contribution in a post on X, prompting criticism from users.

One commenter wrote, "Big spender. She was crying her eyes out so much, why didn't she just pay the entire 50k?" Another called the donation "heartless", while a third described DeGeneres as a "cheapskate".

Others defended the comedian, arguing that her personal relationship with Wright and the circumstances surrounding the donation were not fully known. One user wrote, "I can't stand Ellen, but this post is stupid. We don't know if they were still friends or even liked each other."

Ellen DeGeneres has faced criticism over her $5,000 donation to a GoFundMe campaign supporting the family of Matthew Wright, her former show's longtime producer, following his death at 52.

The comedian shared an emotional video paying tribute to Wright on Monday, remembering him as a funny, intelligent and kind colleague who played an important role in the programme.

"He was an amazing guy, he was funny, god he made me laugh, he would surprise me with things that he did all the time," she said.

DeGeneres also described Wright as "the glue to our entire family at the Ellen Show", revealing that they had been preparing to work on another project before his unexpected death.

She additionally reflected on his friendship with former show DJ Stephen "tWitch" Boss, who died in 2022, saying she believed the two were now "together, dancing and laughing."

However, attention soon turned to DeGeneres' contribution to a fundraiser launched by Wright's relatives to help cover expenses following his death.

Although her $5,000 donation made her one of the campaign's leading contributors, some social media users questioned whether the amount was sufficient given her estimated $500 million fortune.

Podcaster and author Dana Parish highlighted the contribution in a post on X, prompting criticism from users.

One commenter wrote, "Big spender. She was crying her eyes out so much, why didn't she just pay the entire 50k?" Another called the donation "heartless", while a third described DeGeneres as a "cheapskate".

Others defended the comedian, arguing that her personal relationship with Wright and the circumstances surrounding the donation were not fully known. One user wrote, "I can't stand Ellen, but this post is stupid. We don't know if they were still friends or even liked each other."

headline: Two terrorists, including suicide bomber, killed in K-P
description: K-P IG says security forces foiled a large-scale terrorist attempt by neutralising terrorists
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Two terrorists were killed and another was injured in a police operation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), police said on Wednesday.

The incident occurred in the Lakki Marwat district, where police launched an operation following a tip-off.

The terrorists, belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij, opened fire on police, who returned fire, killing two of them. A third terrorist managed to escape after being injured.

Fitna al-Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfikar Hameed told reporters that security forces had foiled a “large-scale terrorist attempt” by neutralising the terrorists.

Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.

Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.

On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.

In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.

On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.

In July, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.

In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation, which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

With additional input from Web Desk

headline: Organisational lapses hit SAFF Cup ahead of kick-off
description: India face accommodation delays in Dhaka, Pakistan’s hotel is changed before team’s departure
author: Alam Zeb Safi
article_text:
The SAFF Cup 2026 kicks off in Dhaka on Thursday but organisers have already faced embarrassing moments over accommodation arrangements for participating teams. A well-placed source has informed this correspondent that the Pakistan team’s hotel was changed before the squad departed for Dhaka on Tuesday. Pakistan, coached by Nolberto Solano, arrived in the Bangladesh capital in the early hours of Wednesday. “Yes, our hotel was changed, but it happened before the team’s departure,” a well-connected source told this correspondent. The main concern is that Pakistan will begin their campaign on Thursday with a crucial encounter against India. It remains to be seen how quickly the players can settle in after a long journey from Islamabad to Dhaka via Qatar. Meanwhile, media reports suggest that the Indian team also had to wait several hours for accommodation following its arrival in Dhaka. “The team landed in the Bangladesh capital around 2:15 pm after a slight delay and was given the address of a private hotel on Gulshan Avenue. However, upon reaching the property, the team discovered that rooms had not been allocated for them,” a web portal reported. According to the report, Indian players were still waiting for accommodation until 5pm IST.

However, a subsequent report confirmed that the Indian team had eventually secured accommodation in Dhaka. Social media was also abuzz with reports about the alleged poor treatment of the Indian team, which will enter the tournament as defending champions. This correspondent also approached a senior SAFF official for comment, but received no response. The high-profile Pakistan-India encounter will be played at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday. Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano is targeting a strong performance in the six-team tournament, which Nepal will miss due to a suspension. “We go step by step. We have a big game against India on Thursday, followed by Maldives. Our focus is on these two matches and qualifying for the semi-finals. We have to think of every game as a final. The first final is against India, and the second final is against Maldives,” Solano said. Comparing the intensity of Pakistan-India encounters to the rivalry between Peru and Chile, Solano said: “Peru-Chile is just like Pakistan-India. It has the same intensity. I understand what these games mean to the fans. We want to please the people because we know what it means to them. These games are special, and that itself is motivation.” Pakistan, India and Maldives are placed in Group B, while hosts Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Bhutan make up Group A. Pakistan have never won the SAFF Cup, finishing third in the 1997 edition hosted by Nepal. India are the most successful team in the tournament's history, having won the title a record nine times. Maldives have lifted the trophy twice, while Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Sri Lanka have won it once each. Bhutan will face hosts Bangladesh in the tournament's second match on Thursday under floodlights. The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for November 14, while the final will take place on November 17. India are fielding second string, rather, under-23 team, in the tournament which will provide a very good opportunity for Pakistan’s home-grown players to put up a strong fight against them

headline: Pierce Brosnan praises Callum Turner as potential next James Bond
description: Pierce Brosnan has praised Callum Turner as speculation continues over who will become next James Bond
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Pierce Brosnan has praised actor Callum Turner amid speculation that he could be selected to play the next James Bond in the upcoming 007 film directed by Denis Villeneuve.

The former Bond actor shared his thoughts on the casting process in an interview with Vanity Fair published on Tuesday, revealing that he has a particular appreciation for Turner, with whom he has previously worked.

"All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire," Brosnan said. "Callum Turner is someone I've worked with, and he's so strong."

Turner is reportedly among the final candidates being considered for the role, alongside Slow Horses actor Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor. According to reports, the three actors participated in the final round of screen tests alongside an unidentified fourth candidate.

Despite expressing support for Turner, Brosnan said he believed any of the shortlisted actors could take on the iconic role successfully.

"They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film," he said. "They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men."

He added that he wished whoever secured the part "the very best of life and strength and courage", while admitting that he was eagerly waiting for the casting announcement.

Brosnan is not the only former Bond-related figure to express support for a potential successor. Gary Oldman, who stars alongside Lowden in Slow Horses, previously told Global News that he hoped his co-star would be chosen.

The next James Bond film will be the franchise's first since Amazon MGM Studios took full creative control following discussions with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

Villeneuve is set to direct the 26th instalment, with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman have also been selected to oversee the project.

The film will follow Daniel Craig's final appearance as Bond in 2021's No Time to Die.

headline: Machine Gun Kelly accused of using Dakota Johnson romance to make Megan Fox jealous
description: Source claims MGK is trying to provoke ex-fiancée Megan Fox through his relationship with Dakota Johnson
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Machine Gun Kelly has reportedly been trying to make his ex-fiancée, Megan Fox, jealous by highlighting how happy he is with his new girlfriend, Dakota Johnson.

According to a source quoted by Star, the singer's behaviour stems from repeated attempts to reconcile with Fox before beginning his relationship with Johnson.

"Almost right up until he met Dakota, he was trying to get Megan back," the source claimed. "She turned him down over and over and that definitely hurt his ego, which is why he's trying so hard now to rub it in her face that he's moved on."

MGK, whose real name is Colson Baker, and Fox, 40, ended their on-off relationship in December 2024, shortly before welcoming their daughter, Saga, now 19 months old.

However, the source claimed that Fox has no interest in rekindling their relationship and is reportedly comfortable with Baker moving on.

"The ridiculous part is that Megan is glad that he's moved on," the source said. "She does not want to get back together with him, not now, and not ever."

The insider also described Fox's frustration with what they characterised as Baker's immature behaviour, suggesting that his alleged attempts to provoke a reaction are only reinforcing her existing concerns.

According to the source, Baker has continued trying to get Fox's attention, even when discussing his relationship with Johnson.

The insider claimed that although he might believe comparisons between the two women are compliments to Johnson, they are not being received that way.

"Dakota likes him, but this petty drama is a turn-off, so if he wants to hang on to her, he needs to get it together and let this bad blood with Megan go," the source added.
