headline: Pakistan Under-19 begin title defence on Friday
description: The defending champions are drawn alongside UAE, India and Nepal in Group A
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
The ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026 will begin in Oman on Thursday, 5 November with defending champions Pakistan U19 taking on the UAE on Friday, 6 November at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat.

The eight-team 50-over tournament consist of two groups. Pakistan, UAE, India and Nepal are in Group A, while Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Malaysia are in Group B.

The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for Thursday, 12 November. The final will take place on Saturday, 14 November.

Pakistan will be led by Farhan Yousaf, who also captained the side in the previous edition when Pakistan defeated India by 191 runs at the ICC Cricket Academy Ground in Dubai.

Following their opening match, Pakistan will face India on Sunday, 8 November before taking on Nepal in their final group match on Tuesday, 10 November.

Talking exclusively to PCB Digital, Pakistan U19 captain Farhan Yousaf said:

“Our preparations have been progressing really well. The PCB’s initiative to send us to Oman ahead of the tournament has been extremely beneficial, allowing us to assess the weather, pitches and playing conditions.

“As defending champions, we understand the responsibility that comes with the title. We are not taking anything for granted and are determined to carry forward the positives from last year with the same hunger, commitment and winning mindset.

“The morale within the squad is very high and the players are confident heading into the tournament. We had a strong squad last year and the addition of new players has further strengthened the team.

“The confidence and support shown by the team management have been instrumental in our preparations. We are focused on building on last year’s success, maintaining our positive approach and performing consistently throughout the tournament.”

15-member squad

Farhan Yousuf (captain), Abdul Qadir (wk), Abdul Subhan, Ahmed Hussain, Ali Raza, Hamza Zahoor (wk), Hasnain Abbas Dar, Hayam Khan, Huzaifa Ahsan, Jahangir Bilal, Mohammad Huzaifa, Mohammad Seyam, Niqab Shafiq, Rizwanullah and Usman Khan

Player support personnel

Shahid Anwar (head coach & team manager), Rao Iftikhar Anjum (fast bowling coach), Zohaib Khan (spin bowling coach), Humayun Farhat (fielding coach), Ubaid Ullah (Physiotherapist), Ibrar Ahmed (trainer) and Ali Hamza (performance analyst)

Pakistan’s fixtures at the ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026 - OMAN

6 November – Pakistan v UAE – OCA Ground 2

8 November – Pakistan v India – OCA Ground 1

10 November – Pakistan v Nepal – OCA Ground 1

12 November – Semi finals

14 November – Final

article_html:
The ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026 will begin in Oman on Thursday, 5 November with defending champions Pakistan U19 taking on the UAE on Friday, 6 November at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat.

The eight-team 50-over tournament consist of two groups. Pakistan, UAE, India and Nepal are in Group A, while Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Malaysia are in Group B.

The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for Thursday, 12 November. The final will take place on Saturday, 14 November.

Pakistan will be led by Farhan Yousaf, who also captained the side in the previous edition when Pakistan defeated India by 191 runs at the ICC Cricket Academy Ground in Dubai.

Following their opening match, Pakistan will face India on Sunday, 8 November before taking on Nepal in their final group match on Tuesday, 10 November.

Talking exclusively to PCB Digital, Pakistan U19 captain Farhan Yousaf said:

“Our preparations have been progressing really well. The PCB’s initiative to send us to Oman ahead of the tournament has been extremely beneficial, allowing us to assess the weather, pitches and playing conditions.

“As defending champions, we understand the responsibility that comes with the title. We are not taking anything for granted and are determined to carry forward the positives from last year with the same hunger, commitment and winning mindset.

“The morale within the squad is very high and the players are confident heading into the tournament. We had a strong squad last year and the addition of new players has further strengthened the team.

“The confidence and support shown by the team management have been instrumental in our preparations. We are focused on building on last year’s success, maintaining our positive approach and performing consistently throughout the tournament.”

headline: Katseye postpones Detroit concert 30 minutes before showtime due to illness
description: Katseye postponed its Detroit concert after Megan Skiendiel fell ill, leaving fans waiting at arena
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Katseye postponed its Detroit concert just 30 minutes before it was due to begin on Tuesday November 3, after member Megan Skiendiel became unwell. The announcement came while fans had already gathered inside Little Caesars Arena for the group's Wildworld Tour.

The global girl group, currently performing as a quartet while two members are on hiatus, shared the news through a statement on Instagram Stories. The group confirmed that Skiendiel was unable to perform and needed time to recover.

"Megan is unwell and unable to perform tonight, and we want to make sure she has the time she needs to rest and recover," the statement read.

Katseye also apologised to fans who had travelled or made arrangements to attend the concert. "We know so many of you have traveled, made plans, and been looking forward to tonight. We are incredibly disappointed that we won't get to see you, and we're truly sorry for the inconvenience."

The group clarified that the show had been postponed rather than cancelled, but did not announce a replacement date. It thanked fans for their patience and support, adding: "We love you and can't wait to see you soon."

The short notice left many attendees disappointed. Photos shared on social media showed the arena already filled with concertgoers, while a message announcing the postponement appeared on the venue's stage screen. One mother described the atmosphere in a TikTok video, saying, "We're in an arena full of crying little girls."

The postponement comes during Katseye's first arena tour, which began in Dublin on September 1 and has travelled through Europe, Canada and the eastern United States.

The North American leg is scheduled to conclude in Mexico City on 28 November before the tour resumes in Asia on January 28 2027.

The group is also currently without members Sophia Laforteza and Manon Bannerman, both of whom are taking breaks to prioritise their health and well-being. Management has said Laforteza is expected to return in 2027.

headline: Eric Dane’s memoir reveals heated on-set clash with Josh Duhamel during ‘Las Vegas’
description: Dane was filming with a herniated disc in his neck when the incident unfolded in 2004
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Eric Dane has revealed a tense confrontation with Josh Duhamel on the set of NBC drama Las Vegas in his posthumously released memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments.

The actor, who guest starred on the series in 2004, recalled how a fight scene became increasingly painful while he was dealing with a herniated disc in his neck. Dane said he had asked Duhamel, who played the show’s lead character, to avoid pulling on his tie during filming.

According to Dane’s account, Duhamel initially agreed but repeatedly grabbed the tie during takes, aggravating his injury. After the second attempt, Dane warned a producer that the situation needed to be addressed.

Dane described losing his temper when the same action happened again. He removed his suit jacket, confronted Duhamel and challenged him to fight. The cameras continued rolling, leaving Dane concerned that viewers would see him as the aggressor.

Reflecting on the incident in his memoir, Dane acknowledged that his reaction was wrong and expressed regret over how he handled the situation.

“Josh and I have seen each other since and we’re cool,” he wrote. “But I want to say it again. Josh, I was wrong. I should’ve walked away. I’m sorry, dude.”

Dane appeared in two episodes of Las Vegas in 2004, before landing his breakout role as Dr Mark Sloan on Grey’s Anatomy in 2006.

Duhamel has also spoken about how immersing himself in emotionally intense roles sometimes affected his behaviour on set. In an earlier interview with In Depth with Graham Bensinger, he recalled becoming withdrawn while portraying Danny McCoy, a former Marine dealing with trauma in Las Vegas.

Dane’s memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments, is now available. The book offers reflections on his life and career, including experiences from his years working in television.

Dane described losing his temper when the same action happened again. He removed his suit jacket, confronted Duhamel and challenged him to fight. The cameras continued rolling, leaving Dane concerned that viewers would see him as the aggressor.
Reflecting on the incident in his memoir, Dane acknowledged that his reaction was wrong and expressed regret over how he handled the situation.
“Josh and I have seen each other since and we’re cool,” he wrote. “But I want to say it again. Josh, I was wrong. I should’ve walked away. I’m sorry, dude.”
Dane appeared in two episodes of Las Vegas in 2004, before landing his breakout role as Dr Mark Sloan on Grey’s Anatomy in 2006.

Duhamel has also spoken about how immersing himself in emotionally intense roles sometimes affected his behaviour on set. In an earlier interview with In Depth with Graham Bensinger, he recalled becoming withdrawn while portraying Danny McCoy, a former Marine dealing with trauma in Las Vegas.
Dane’s memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments, is now available. The book offers reflections on his life and career, including experiences from his years working in television.

headline: Mariyam Nafees hits back at intrusive questions about having another child
description: Actor sarcastically tells followers to find a job as a nanny if they are so concerned about her family plans
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Actor Mariyam Nafees has hit back at people who repeatedly question her about having another child, expressing frustration over the intrusion into her personal life during a recent Instagram Q&A session.

The actor addressed the matter after a follower asked her, “Next baby when?”, prompting a sarcastic response about people's tendency to interfere in celebrities' family planning. “Life would be going so well and then people would pop up with their questions,” she said.

Questioning why anyone would be concerned about her decision to expand her family, Nafees asked, “What difference will me having another kid make in your life?”

Taking a further dig at the person asking, she suggested that the question might make sense if they were a nanny looking for a job. Otherwise, she could not understand why anyone would be so interested in her family plans.

“If you are a nanny and need a job, that is another thing. Otherwise, how does it make any difference to you?” she remarked.

Her response highlighted a recurring issue faced by married female celebrities, who are often questioned about pregnancy, motherhood and plans to have more children. She made it clear that decisions about expanding a family are personal and should not become subjects of public interrogation.

View this post on Instagram

Nafees made her acting debut with the popular drama Diyar-e-Dil in 2015 and gradually gained recognition through her performances in several television projects.

She has since appeared in dramas including Yaqeen Ka Safar, Munkir, Jhooti, Fitrat, Ishq Jalebi, Neem and Jaan-e-Jahan. Her portrayal of Khajista in Yaqeen Ka Safar remains among her notable television roles.

Beyond acting, Mariyam is also known for her outspoken personality and candid views on social issues, including joint-family pressures and women's space within marriage.

The actor married filmmaker Amaan Ahmed on March 25, 2022. The couple welcomed their first child, a baby boy named Syed Eesa Amaan Ahmed, in March 2025.

Mariyam has openly shared moments from her pregnancy and motherhood journey on social media. She has also spoken about her husband's involvement in parenting and the importance of sharing responsibilities.

While the actor has remained candid about different aspects of motherhood, her latest response makes one thing clear: being a public figure does not mean celebrities are obliged to answer every personal question about their marriages, children or plans to expand their families.

headline: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ gets 3D release on Meta VR glasses
description: DNEG collaborated on the film’s 3D conversion, marking Meta’s first such partnership with a Hollywood studio
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set to reach audiences beyond cinemas, with Lionsgate partnering with Meta to bring the upcoming film to the technology company’s virtual reality glasses.

The collaboration will see the Francis Lawrence directed prequel converted into 3D for its theatrical release before becoming available on Meta VR glasses in spring 2027. The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

According to Deadline, the project marks the first time Meta has partnered with a Hollywood studio to convert a feature film into 3D. The conversion was completed in collaboration with DNEG, the Oscar winning visual effects and animation company.

The partnership also signals a new distribution opportunity for Lionsgate, which plans to announce additional feature titles for Meta VR glasses and their availability at a later date.

Meta unveiled the glasses at its Connect 2026 event. The device features a 5K Infinite Display, Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos spatial audio and IMAX Enhanced technology. The glasses reportedly weigh approximately 100 grams.

The move gives audiences another way to experience the latest instalment in the hugely successful Hunger Games franchise. The five films released so far have earned more than $3.3bn worldwide, according to the report.

Sunrise on the Reaping is based on Suzanne Collins’ novel of the same name and takes place decades before the events of the original story, following a young Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games.

The film is directed by Lawrence, who previously helmed several entries in the franchise. Its theatrical release is expected to be one of Lionsgate’s major releases for the Thanksgiving period.

Although the partnership focuses on 3D film viewing rather than artificial intelligence, it brings together a major Hollywood studio and a technology company investing heavily in immersive entertainment.

headline: Naqvi says One Constitution Avenue to be converted into five-star hotel in 'coming months'
description: Iqbal says CDA involved in irregularities, fraud, Tarar says matter will be referred to NAB for further investigation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced on Wednesday that One Constitution Avenue would be converted into a five-star hotel, assuring that all those entitled to compensation would be paid their dues.

In a press conference in Islamabad, Naqvi said that a joint investigation team (JIT) report on the project was presented before the federal cabinet and action had been taken on its recommendations, further adding that the government had now legally taken possession of the property.

Naqvi added: "We will convert this building to a five-star hotel in the coming months, which was its basic purpose in the first place. There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad, and soon we will try to sign an agreement with a big chain for this purpose."

“As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi stated, adding that this was binding on the government after the report.

In an earlier press conference, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, speaking alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, said that a JIT report submitted to the cabinet had found "irregularities and rigging" in the One Constitution Avenue project.

He said: "The prime minister had ordered an inquiry committee into the fraud that took place in the name of One Constitution Avenue, and today the JIT report was placed before the cabinet, which consisted of members from NAB, FIA, FBR, SECP, IB and ISI. They investigated the entire project and submitted a report that the cabinet considered today."

The planning minister underscored that the bidding process for the project was manipulated, further noting that the Capital Development Authority (CDA) was found not only to be "negligent" but also culpable and "involved" in the irregularities and fraud that took place.

The minister added: "The rules were relaxed to favour certain individuals, and the company that was given the lease was not the rightful claimant of the lease".

He further stated that the precondition of a bank guarantee was removed to favour the developer, adding that the paperwork submitted for the project was also found to be dubious.

Iqbal underlined that the apartments that were sold were done so "illegally", further noting that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel but was later converted into selling apartments.

"The JIT identified the individuals involved in the manipulation, including Abdul Hafeez Shaikh, who is the mastermind and has connived with officers from CDA," he said.

The minister also stated that other CDA officers, including former chairman Kamran Lashari, Dr Faisal Awan, and Azhar Ali Chaudhry, were also involved in this fraud.

He said that these "individuals defrauded many Pakistanis of their savings and secured personal financial benefit from this project".

Iqbal stated that the recommendations of the JIT report maintain that Shaikh and his company were "prosecuted" and also "blacklisted" for any future public sector projects.

The minister added: "The project should be redirected towards its original purpose, and a transparent bidding process should be carried out, and security clearance from institutions should be obtained. Fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured."

Iqbal said that the project should also be renamed because the name of One Constitution Avenue was taken through deceit, as the first building on Constitution Avenue was the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. "They only took the name of One Constitution for marketing purposes."

For those people who invested in this project and were deceived, it is the government's responsibility to compensate, and the principal amount plus interest would be returned, so that they do not suffer any loss.

The minister added that JIT also recommended that CDA and its ordinance should be overhauled and an independent master plan commission should be established.

"All records will be digitised so that nobody can manipulate the records, and officers will be rotated every two years," he said.

Tarar says no one above the law in One Constitution Avenue case

Tarar, also speaking at the press conference, said the government would ensure equal application of law in the One Constitution Avenue project, making it clear that neither influential individuals nor wealthy people would be allowed to escape accountability.

The minister said the JIT, constituted to examine irregularities in the One Constitution Avenue project, had identified shortcomings in the process dating back to the mid-2000s and also pointed out the officials involved at the time of the award of the contract.

He said the JIT had conducted a fair investigation, identified the offences and those responsible, and recommended that the matter be referred to the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) for further investigation.

Tarar said the government was equally committed to protecting bona fide investors who had purchased apartments in the project with their hard-earned money without knowledge of the alleged irregularities.

He added the JIT had also recommended safeguarding the interests of genuine investors, including those residing in Pakistan and abroad, and ensuring appropriate compensation for their investments in view of the proposed re-tendering and redesigning of the project.

He said the NAB investigation would be conducted strictly on merit and expedited, with a target of completion within three months, followed by the initiation of the trial process.

Background of One Constitution Avenue case

On May 19, a division bench of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) comprising Justice Azam Khan and Justice Raja Inam Amin Minhas issued a notice to the CDA on the intra-court appeal submitted by the sub-lease holders of 20 more apartments of One Constitution Avenue and sought its response.

On May 4, the IHC issued a detailed verdict on the One Constitution Avenue project, upholding the Capital Development Authority's (CDA) decision and ruling that the buyers lack ownership rights.

The court stated that the buyers lacked ownership rights, as the project’s lease had been terminated and the proper legal processes had not been followed regarding the transfer of ownership.

On May 1, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a high-level committee to review the matter of One Constitution Avenue after authorities took control of a multi-storey residential building following a ruling by the IHC in a long-running dispute over the cancellation of its lease.

The project originally stems from a 13.5-acre plot awarded to BNP Group following an auction on March 9, 2005, for Rs4.88 billion. Although possession was handed over the same year after an initial payment of Rs800 million, BNP has so far paid Rs1.02b, while the remaining Rs3.85b is recoverable in instalments until 2026.

In July 2016, the CDA cancelled the lease, citing multiple violations. The decision was upheld by the IHC in 2017, which also declared the conversion of a planned five-star hotel into luxury apartments illegal. However, the Supreme Court set aside that judgment in early 2019, directing the developer to pay Rs17.5b in instalments over eight years.

The CDA argued that BNP failed to meet its financial obligations after 21 years, maintaining that full ownership was conditional upon 100% payment of the land cost. Of the total Rs17.5b liability, only Rs2.9b — around 16.6% — has reportedly been paid.

The complex is reported to include apartments owned by several prominent figures, including Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan, Chaudhry Aitzaz Ahsan, Shandana Gulzar Aurangzeb, former minister Burjees Tahir, former caretaker prime minister Nasirul Mulk and Kashmala Tariq.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced on Wednesday that One Constitution Avenue would be converted into a five-star hotel, assuring that all those entitled to compensation would be paid their dues.

In a press conference in Islamabad, Naqvi said that a joint investigation team (JIT) report on the project was presented before the federal cabinet and action had been taken on its recommendations, further adding that the government had now legally taken possession of the property.

Naqvi added: "We will convert this building to a five-star hotel in the coming months, which was its basic purpose in the first place. There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad, and soon we will try to sign an agreement with a big chain for this purpose."

“As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi stated, adding that this was binding on the government after the report.

In an earlier press conference, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, speaking alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, said that a JIT report submitted to the cabinet had found "irregularities and rigging" in the One Constitution Avenue project.

He said: "The prime minister had ordered an inquiry committee into the fraud that took place in the name of One Constitution Avenue, and today the JIT report was placed before the cabinet, which consisted of members from NAB, FIA, FBR, SECP, IB and ISI. They investigated the entire project and submitted a report that the cabinet considered today."

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has said that the Joint Investigation Team's report has uncovered serious irregularities, manipulation, and fraud in the One Constitution Avenue project in Islamabad.@PlanComPakistan @betterpakistan @MoIB_Official @CDAIslamabad #RadioPakistan… pic.twitter.com/WiDPOGye3r

— Radio Pakistan (@RadioPakistan) November 4, 2026

The planning minister underscored that the bidding process for the project was manipulated, further noting that the Capital Development Authority (CDA) was found not only to be "negligent" but also culpable and "involved" in the irregularities and fraud that took place.

Read More: CDA put on notice in One Constitution Avenue case

The minister added: "The rules were relaxed to favour certain individuals, and the company that was given the lease was not the rightful claimant of the lease".

He further stated that the precondition of a bank guarantee was removed to favour the developer, adding that the paperwork submitted for the project was also found to be dubious.

Iqbal underlined that the apartments that were sold were done so "illegally", further noting that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel but was later converted into selling apartments.

"The JIT identified the individuals involved in the manipulation, including Abdul Hafeez Shaikh, who is the mastermind and has connived with officers from CDA," he said.

The minister also stated that other CDA officers, including former chairman Kamran Lashari, Dr Faisal Awan, and Azhar Ali Chaudhry, were also involved in this fraud.

He said that these "individuals defrauded many Pakistanis of their savings and secured personal financial benefit from this project".

Iqbal stated that the recommendations of the JIT report maintain that Shaikh and his company were "prosecuted" and also "blacklisted" for any future public sector projects.

The minister added: "The project should be redirected towards its original purpose, and a transparent bidding process should be carried out, and security clearance from institutions should be obtained. Fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured."

Iqbal said that the project should also be renamed because the name of One Constitution Avenue was taken through deceit, as the first building on Constitution Avenue was the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. "They only took the name of One Constitution for marketing purposes."

For those people who invested in this project and were deceived, it is the government's responsibility to compensate, and the principal amount plus interest would be returned, so that they do not suffer any loss.

The minister added that JIT also recommended that CDA and its ordinance should be overhauled and an independent master plan commission should be established.

"All records will be digitised so that nobody can manipulate the records, and officers will be rotated every two years," he said.

Tarar says no one above the law in One Constitution Avenue case

Tarar, also speaking at the press conference, said the government would ensure equal application of law in the One Constitution Avenue project, making it clear that neither influential individuals nor wealthy people would be allowed to escape accountability.

Federal Minister Attaullah Tarar said the government would ensure equal application of law in the One Constitution Avenue project, making it clear that neither influential individuals nor wealthy people would be allowed to escape accountability.#AttaTarrar #OneConstitutionAvenue pic.twitter.com/ybz6WnaE6c

— APP (@appcsocialmedia) November 4, 2026

The minister said the JIT, constituted to examine irregularities in the One Constitution Avenue project, had identified shortcomings in the process dating back to the mid-2000s and also pointed out the officials involved at the time of the award of the contract.

He said the JIT had conducted a fair investigation, identified the offences and those responsible, and recommended that the matter be referred to the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) for further investigation.

Tarar said the government was equally committed to protecting bona fide investors who had purchased apartments in the project with their hard-earned money without knowledge of the alleged irregularities.

He added the JIT had also recommended safeguarding the interests of genuine investors, including those residing in Pakistan and abroad, and ensuring appropriate compensation for their investments in view of the proposed re-tendering and redesigning of the project.

He said the NAB investigation would be conducted strictly on merit and expedited, with a target of completion within three months, followed by the initiation of the trial process.

Background of One Constitution Avenue case

On May 19, a division bench of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) comprising Justice Azam Khan and Justice Raja Inam Amin Minhas issued a notice to the CDA on the intra-court appeal submitted by the sub-lease holders of 20 more apartments of One Constitution Avenue and sought its response.

On May 4, the IHC issued a detailed verdict on the One Constitution Avenue project, upholding the Capital Development Authority's (CDA) decision and ruling that the buyers lack ownership rights.

The court stated that the buyers lacked ownership rights, as the project’s lease had been terminated and the proper legal processes had not been followed regarding the transfer of ownership.

On May 1, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a high-level committee to review the matter of One Constitution Avenue after authorities took control of a multi-storey residential building following a ruling by the IHC in a long-running dispute over the cancellation of its lease.

Also Read: PM constitutes high-level committee over One Constitution Avenue dispute, stays official action

The project originally stems from a 13.5-acre plot awarded to BNP Group following an auction on March 9, 2005, for Rs4.88 billion. Although possession was handed over the same year after an initial payment of Rs800 million, BNP has so far paid Rs1.02b, while the remaining Rs3.85b is recoverable in instalments until 2026.

In July 2016, the CDA cancelled the lease, citing multiple violations. The decision was upheld by the IHC in 2017, which also declared the conversion of a planned five-star hotel into luxury apartments illegal. However, the Supreme Court set aside that judgment in early 2019, directing the developer to pay Rs17.5b in instalments over eight years.

The CDA argued that BNP failed to meet its financial obligations after 21 years, maintaining that full ownership was conditional upon 100% payment of the land cost. Of the total Rs17.5b liability, only Rs2.9b — around 16.6% — has reportedly been paid.

The complex is reported to include apartments owned by several prominent figures, including Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan, Chaudhry Aitzaz Ahsan, Shandana Gulzar Aurangzeb, former minister Burjees Tahir, former caretaker prime minister Nasirul Mulk and Kashmala Tariq.

The planning minister underscored that the bidding process for the project was manipulated, further noting that the Capital Development Authority (CDA) was found not only to be "negligent" but also culpable and "involved" in the irregularities and fraud that took place.
The minister added: "The rules were relaxed to favour certain individuals, and the company that was given the lease was not the rightful claimant of the lease".
He further stated that the precondition of a bank guarantee was removed to favour the developer, adding that the paperwork submitted for the project was also found to be dubious.

Iqbal underlined that the apartments that were sold were done so "illegally", further noting that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel but was later converted into selling apartments.
"The JIT identified the individuals involved in the manipulation, including Abdul Hafeez Shaikh, who is the mastermind and has connived with officers from CDA," he said.
The minister also stated that other CDA officers, including former chairman Kamran Lashari, Dr Faisal Awan, and Azhar Ali Chaudhry, were also involved in this fraud.
He said that these "individuals defrauded many Pakistanis of their savings and secured personal financial benefit from this project".
Iqbal stated that the recommendations of the JIT report maintain that Shaikh and his company were "prosecuted" and also "blacklisted" for any future public sector projects.

The minister added: "The project should be redirected towards its original purpose, and a transparent bidding process should be carried out, and security clearance from institutions should be obtained. Fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured."

Iqbal said that the project should also be renamed because the name of One Constitution Avenue was taken through deceit, as the first building on Constitution Avenue was the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. "They only took the name of One Constitution for marketing purposes."

For those people who invested in this project and were deceived, it is the government's responsibility to compensate, and the principal amount plus interest would be returned, so that they do not suffer any loss.
The minister added that JIT also recommended that CDA and its ordinance should be overhauled and an independent master plan commission should be established.
"All records will be digitised so that nobody can manipulate the records, and officers will be rotated every two years," he said.
Tarar says no one above the law in One Constitution Avenue case

Tarar, also speaking at the press conference, said the government would ensure equal application of law in the One Constitution Avenue project, making it clear that neither influential individuals nor wealthy people would be allowed to escape accountability.

The minister said the JIT, constituted to examine irregularities in the One Constitution Avenue project, had identified shortcomings in the process dating back to the mid-2000s and also pointed out the officials involved at the time of the award of the contract.

He said the JIT had conducted a fair investigation, identified the offences and those responsible, and recommended that the matter be referred to the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) for further investigation.

Tarar said the government was equally committed to protecting bona fide investors who had purchased apartments in the project with their hard-earned money without knowledge of the alleged irregularities.

He added the JIT had also recommended safeguarding the interests of genuine investors, including those residing in Pakistan and abroad, and ensuring appropriate compensation for their investments in view of the proposed re-tendering and redesigning of the project.
He said the NAB investigation would be conducted strictly on merit and expedited, with a target of completion within three months, followed by the initiation of the trial process.
Background of One Constitution Avenue case

On May 19, a division bench of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) comprising Justice Azam Khan and Justice Raja Inam Amin Minhas issued a notice to the CDA on the intra-court appeal submitted by the sub-lease holders of 20 more apartments of One Constitution Avenue and sought its response.
On May 4, the IHC issued a detailed verdict on the One Constitution Avenue project, upholding the Capital Development Authority's (CDA) decision and ruling that the buyers lack ownership rights.
The court stated that the buyers lacked ownership rights, as the project’s lease had been terminated and the proper legal processes had not been followed regarding the transfer of ownership.

On May 1, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a high-level committee to review the matter of One Constitution Avenue after authorities took control of a multi-storey residential building following a ruling by the IHC in a long-running dispute over the cancellation of its lease.

The project originally stems from a 13.5-acre plot awarded to BNP Group following an auction on March 9, 2005, for Rs4.88 billion. Although possession was handed over the same year after an initial payment of Rs800 million, BNP has so far paid Rs1.02b, while the remaining Rs3.85b is recoverable in instalments until 2026.

In July 2016, the CDA cancelled the lease, citing multiple violations. The decision was upheld by the IHC in 2017, which also declared the conversion of a planned five-star hotel into luxury apartments illegal. However, the Supreme Court set aside that judgment in early 2019, directing the developer to pay Rs17.5b in instalments over eight years.

The CDA argued that BNP failed to meet its financial obligations after 21 years, maintaining that full ownership was conditional upon 100% payment of the land cost. Of the total Rs17.5b liability, only Rs2.9b — around 16.6% — has reportedly been paid.

The complex is reported to include apartments owned by several prominent figures, including Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan, Chaudhry Aitzaz Ahsan, Shandana Gulzar Aurangzeb, former minister Burjees Tahir, former caretaker prime minister Nasirul Mulk and Kashmala Tariq.

headline: 'It is a cappuccino. It can't be $10,' says Harry Styles about NYC coffee prices
description: Singer jokes coffee and tipping costs spookiest part this Halloween
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Singer Harry Styles, who recently completed a 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York, ​thought prices for coffee in the city were some ‌of the spookiest things he saw around Halloween.

"It is a cappuccino. It can't be $10, it can't be," he said during one of his last concerts, ​according to videos posted by fans on social media.

"The ​scariest thing about this Halloween is the price of ⁠caffeinated beverages in this city. Astronomical. It's out of control," he ​added, before also complaining about expensive tipping.

Some fans, in comments after ​the video, thought it was amusing that such a wealthy and successful personality would complain about such an ordinary thing as the price for a ​cup of coffee.

"Harry is right... $10 for a cappuccino plus at ​least a 20% tip?," said one fan. "Are you for real?"

Others, meanwhile, criticized ticket ‌prices ⁠for his concerts.

Coffee has suffered a series of cost shocks in recent years including climate-related production shortfalls in major producers and the imposition of US tariffs, which were later removed.

The price of a ​pound of ground ​roast coffee ⁠in US cities averaged $9.33 in September, according to the latest inflation reading from the Bureau of Labor ​Statistics.

That is the highest ever for the month ​and ⁠91% higher than in 2020, adding another item to the cost of living discussion as the US votes in the midterm elections.

Coffee companies say ⁠they ​had to cut profit margins during the ​cost shock to prevent prices rising even more, and are now in a period ​of recovering their margins.

headline: Sonam Kapoor revisits Elizabeth Taylor’s iconic Bulgari emerald necklace after Kim Kardashian moment
description: From Taylor’s romance with Richard Burton to its $6.1 million auction, the necklace has a remarkable celebrity legacy
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Sonam Kapoor is taking a trip down memory lane, and the jewellery in question has quite the history. After Kim Kardashian recently brought Elizabeth Taylor's iconic emerald-and-diamond Bulgari necklace back into the spotlight, the Bollywood actor shared throwback photographs of herself wearing the legendary piece.

Taking to Instagram, Sonam posted pictures of herself in a striking red ensemble, accessorised with the spectacular emerald necklace. Her caption was as witty as ever:

"Since everyone’s talking about Elizabeth Taylor’s iconic Bulgari necklace, I thought I’d throw it back to when I had my little moment with her. My big fashion revelation at the time? Red and green look rather fabulous together. Groundbreaking, I know." "Clearly, this necklace has a better social life than most of us," she added.

View this post on Instagram

And she isn't wrong. Few pieces of jewellery have enjoyed a social calendar quite as extraordinary as this one.

Long before it became a coveted piece of jewellery history, the emerald-and-diamond necklace was part of one of Hollywood's most famous love stories.

The necklace was created by Italian luxury jewellery house Bulgari around 1962, when Taylor was in Rome filming Cleopatra. It was during this period that Taylor's romance with her co-star Richard Burton blossomed, with the couple becoming regular visitors to Bulgari's famous boutique on Via Condotti.

Burton, who famously indulged Taylor's love of extravagant jewellery, gifted her an extraordinary collection of Bulgari emerald pieces over the course of their relationship. The necklace was presented to Taylor as a wedding gift in 1964, according to Christie's auction catalogue.

The necklace also featured a distinctive design element: a hoop at the front that allowed Taylor to suspend a magnificent detachable emerald-and-diamond pendant from it. The pendant was a separate jewel, originally gifted to her by Burton around the time of their engagement in 1962.

Together, the pieces formed part of Taylor's celebrated Bulgari emerald suite, a collection that reflected both her extraordinary personal style and her enduring romance with Burton.

The necklace was also an exquisite example of Bulgari's distinctive approach to coloured gemstones.

According to Christie's auction catalogue, the platinum creation featured 16 graduated rectangular and square-cut emeralds, each surrounded by circular-cut diamonds. These were separated by delicate diamond motifs incorporating circular, marquise and pear-shaped stones.

While Elizabeth Taylor made the necklace famous, she was not the last celebrated woman to wear the historic creation.

PHOTO: Harper's Bazaar Australia

In February 2013, actress Julianne Moore wore the very same necklace at a Bulgari celebration at the brand's Rodeo Drive boutique in Beverly Hills.

The event showcased pieces from Taylor's jewellery collection, which Bulgari had acquired following the 2011 auction.

Moore's appearance marked one of the necklace's first major public outings after its return to the jewellery house.

PHOTO: Getty Images

Most recently, Kardashian brought the necklace back into the conversation during a visit to Bulgari's Rome boutique.

The reality star and entrepreneur was given the opportunity to try on the historic piece, sharing her experience and admiration for Taylor on social media.

PHOTO: People

Following Taylor's death in 2011, her extraordinary jewellery collection went under the hammer at Christie's in New York.

The Bulgari emerald-and-diamond necklace was sold on December 13, 2011, for an impressive $6,130,500, substantially exceeding its pre-sale estimate of $1 million to $1.5 million.

What makes Taylor's Bulgari necklace so fascinating is that its appeal goes far beyond its monetary value.

It represents an era when jewellery was deeply personal, when extraordinary gemstones were exchanged as declarations of love and when Hollywood glamour was defined by unapologetic extravagance.

Perhaps that is why it continues to captivate a new generation of celebrities and fashion enthusiasts, decades after it first became part of Hollywood history.

The necklace was created by Italian luxury jewellery house Bulgari around 1962, when Taylor was in Rome filming Cleopatra. It was during this period that Taylor's romance with her co-star Richard Burton blossomed, with the couple becoming regular visitors to Bulgari's famous boutique on Via Condotti.

Burton, who famously indulged Taylor's love of extravagant jewellery, gifted her an extraordinary collection of Bulgari emerald pieces over the course of their relationship. The necklace was presented to Taylor as a wedding gift in 1964, according to Christie's auction catalogue.

The necklace also featured a distinctive design element: a hoop at the front that allowed Taylor to suspend a magnificent detachable emerald-and-diamond pendant from it. The pendant was a separate jewel, originally gifted to her by Burton around the time of their engagement in 1962.

Together, the pieces formed part of Taylor's celebrated Bulgari emerald suite, a collection that reflected both her extraordinary personal style and her enduring romance with Burton.

The necklace was also an exquisite example of Bulgari's distinctive approach to coloured gemstones.

According to Christie's auction catalogue, the platinum creation featured 16 graduated rectangular and square-cut emeralds, each surrounded by circular-cut diamonds. These were separated by delicate diamond motifs incorporating circular, marquise and pear-shaped stones.

While Elizabeth Taylor made the necklace famous, she was not the last celebrated woman to wear the historic creation.

In February 2013, actress Julianne Moore wore the very same necklace at a Bulgari celebration at the brand's Rodeo Drive boutique in Beverly Hills.

The event showcased pieces from Taylor's jewellery collection, which Bulgari had acquired following the 2011 auction.

Moore's appearance marked one of the necklace's first major public outings after its return to the jewellery house.

PHOTO: Getty Images

Most recently, Kardashian brought the necklace back into the conversation during a visit to Bulgari's Rome boutique.

The reality star and entrepreneur was given the opportunity to try on the historic piece, sharing her experience and admiration for Taylor on social media.

PHOTO: People

Following Taylor's death in 2011, her extraordinary jewellery collection went under the hammer at Christie's in New York.

The Bulgari emerald-and-diamond necklace was sold on December 13, 2011, for an impressive $6,130,500, substantially exceeding its pre-sale estimate of $1 million to $1.5 million.

What makes Taylor's Bulgari necklace so fascinating is that its appeal goes far beyond its monetary value.

It represents an era when jewellery was deeply personal, when extraordinary gemstones were exchanged as declarations of love and when Hollywood glamour was defined by unapologetic extravagance.

Perhaps that is why it continues to captivate a new generation of celebrities and fashion enthusiasts, decades after it first became part of Hollywood history.

headline: UK ban on Palestine Action is challenged at top court, some protesters arrested
description: Palestine Action co-founder says group’s ban is unlawful as over 4,000 people are arrested for showing support
author: Reuters
article_text:
A co-founder of Palestine Action challenged Britain's decision to ban ​the campaign group as a terrorist organisation at the UK Supreme Court on Wednesday, arguing that ‌the move was disproportionate and undermined counter-terrorism laws.

The British government proscribed Palestine Action last year after a series of high-profile incidents mostly targeting defence firms, culminating in a break-in at the Royal Air Force's Brize Norton air base in which two planes were damaged.

Britain's Home Office (interior ministry) argues ​that the group's escalating actions, causing serious property damage, particularly a 2024 raid targeting Israeli defence firm Elbit Systems (ESLT.TA), ​amounted to terrorism and justified the ban.

But the move has drawn criticism from civil liberties ⁠groups and prominent supporters including Irish novelist Sally Rooney, whose books can no longer be sold in Britain over her plans ​to provide royalties to the group.

There have been more than 3,600 arrests linked to support for Palestine Action between proscription ​in July 2025 and this June, representing more than one-third of all terrorism arrests in Britain since 9/11, according to Home Office statistics.

With the arrest of over 300 people last weekend outside the US embassy in London, plus two dozen or so outside the Supreme Court ​on Wednesday, the figure is now more than 4,000 – though any resulting charges could be dropped if the ban ​is overturned.

Lawyer compares group to suffragettes

Founded in 2020, Palestine Action carried out hundreds of "actions", many involving obstructing or occupying premises, or spraying ‌graffiti and ⁠breaking windows of businesses they said were linked to providing arms to Israel.

After Israel began bombarding Gaza in response to a deadly attack by Hamas-led fighters in October 2023, Palestine Action's campaign escalated, the Home Office says, with the Elbit raid causing an estimated £1 million ($1.35 million) of damage.

Lawyers representing Huda Ammori, who co-founded Palestine Action, said that, at the time ​the group was proscribed, government ​officials had assessed that ⁠just three of 385 actions carried out over five years had met the definition of terrorism.

London's High Court initially ruled that the ban was unlawful, but the Court of Appeal overturned that decision ​in June, rejecting comparisons with historical groups such as the suffragettes who campaigned for ​women's right to ⁠vote.

Ammori's lawyer Raza Husain, however, said on Wednesday that the suffragettes and other groups "used tactics similar or more extreme than Palestine Action", citing the suffragettes' early 20th-century bombing campaign.

The Home Office, though, says the 2024 Elbit attack did involve the use of violence ⁠and ​weapons against security staff and police officers, one of whom suffered a ​spinal injury when she was hit with a sledgehammer.

The United States in August also designated Palestine Action as a terrorist group. President Donald Trump has described ​activists who targeted his Turnberry golf resort in Scotland last year as "terrorists".

headline: Rizwan's double ton puts Peshawar Blues in command
description: Star player hits 200 not out against Faisalabad in QT
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Peshawar Blues captain Mohammad Rizwan struck a brilliant unbeaten double century to put his side in a commanding position on the second day of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold tournament on Wednesday.

Rizwan finished on 200 not out off 391 balls, hitting 35 fours and a six, as Peshawar declared their first innings at 503-4 against Faisalabad at Abbottabad Cricket Stadium.

Resuming at 306-3, Rizwan and Najab Khan continued their substantial partnership. Najab eventually departed for 133, having struck 25 boundaries and a six, while Mohammad Haris provided late support with an unbeaten 70.

Faisalabad’s Asad Raza and Mudasar Zunair claimed two wickets apiece.

In reply, Faisalabad reached 118-2 at stumps, with Mohammad Adnan dismissing Faham-ul-Haq for 31 and Sameer Saqif for 25.

At Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, Lahore Whites were dismissed for 234 in reply to FATA’s 362. Aamir Jamal top-scored with 71, while Ali Zaryab made 51. Shaheen Shah Afridi and Afaq Afridi took three wickets each for FATA, who closed on 22-1.

Hamza Aziz claimed six wickets for Lahore after FATA resumed on 311-6, finishing with 6-97. Earlier, Fawad Arshad had led FATA’s innings with 91.

At the National Ground Islamabad, Karachi Blues were bowled out for 280 after resuming on 9-1. Muhammad Gazi Ghori scored 88, while captain Rameez made 49. Athar Mehmood took 3-72 for Sialkot Blues, with Hasan Ali and Hamza Nazar claimed two wickets each.

Multan reached 249-7 against Islamabad, taking a 34-run lead after the visitors were dismissed for 215.

Iram Rafiq was unbeaten on 93 and Sharoon Siraj made 82. Musa Khan took three wickets for Islamabad.

On the opening day, Peshawar had been lifted by centuries from Rizwan and Najab, while Sialkot Blues’ Mohammad Huraira also scored a hundred against defending champions Karachi Blues.

Resuming at 306-3, Rizwan and Najab Khan continued their substantial partnership. Najab eventually departed for 133, having struck 25 boundaries and a six, while Mohammad Haris provided late support with an unbeaten 70.

Faisalabad’s Asad Raza and Mudasar Zunair claimed two wickets apiece.

In reply, Faisalabad reached 118-2 at stumps, with Mohammad Adnan dismissing Faham-ul-Haq for 31 and Sameer Saqif for 25.

At Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, Lahore Whites were dismissed for 234 in reply to FATA’s 362. Aamir Jamal top-scored with 71, while Ali Zaryab made 51. Shaheen Shah Afridi and Afaq Afridi took three wickets each for FATA, who closed on 22-1.

Hamza Aziz claimed six wickets for Lahore after FATA resumed on 311-6, finishing with 6-97. Earlier, Fawad Arshad had led FATA’s innings with 91.

At the National Ground Islamabad, Karachi Blues were bowled out for 280 after resuming on 9-1. Muhammad Gazi Ghori scored 88, while captain Rameez made 49. Athar Mehmood took 3-72 for Sialkot Blues, with Hasan Ali and Hamza Nazar claimed two wickets each.

Multan reached 249-7 against Islamabad, taking a 34-run lead after the visitors were dismissed for 215.

Iram Rafiq was unbeaten on 93 and Sharoon Siraj made 82. Musa Khan took three wickets for Islamabad.

On the opening day, Peshawar had been lifted by centuries from Rizwan and Najab, while Sialkot Blues’ Mohammad Huraira also scored a hundred against defending champions Karachi Blues.

headline: Mendis, Udara rescue Sri Lanka in three-day game
description: Solid fifties lift visitors to 223-7 declared against PCB Patron’s XI
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Skipper Kusal Mendis and Lahiru Udara struck solid fifties as Sri Lanka declared their first innings at 223-7 against PCB Patron’s XI at the Oval Ground in Islamabad on Wednesday.

In the three-day show, which serves as a warm-up ahead of the Test series, Sri Lanka, who opted to bat first, had to face great trouble in the start.

Patron’s XI’s pacers exploited early moisture to put pressure on the visitors. At one stage Sri Lanka were 40-3.

However at this stage Kusal Mendis and Lahiru Udara, who opened the innings, took time at the crease and revived the innings with a solid 90-run partnership for the fourth wicket.

Ali Shabir broke the stand when he held Udara off his own bowling, to give the hosts a sort of relief.

Udara smashed seven fours and three sixes in his 65 for which he faced 105 balls and stayed at the wicket for 105 minutes.

Ali then immediately had the wicket of Sunal Dinusha (10), held by Azan Awais, to leave Sri Lanka at 153-5.

However, Kusal found an able partner in Anjala Bandara who put on 45 runs for the sixth wicket association with his skipper to boost Sri Lanka’s total.

Fast bowler Ubaid Shah broke the partnership when he got rid of Kusal who hammered a solid 66.

Kusal, who also played a few good strokes, smashed 11 fours in his 72-ball knock. The skipper took 157 minutes at the crease.

Bandara batted until Mendis declared the innings at 223-7 to test his bowlers also in good bowling conditions before the stumps.

Bandara struck five fours in his unbeaten 33 for which he faced 61 balls and stayed for 112 minutes at the crease.

Earlier, Sri Lanka had a poor start when Saqib Khan got two back-to-back wickets of Pasindu Sooriyabandara (8) and Dinesh Chandimal (0) to leave Sri Lanka reeling at 21-2.

Mohammad Salman then had Dhananjaya De Silva to reduce the visitors to 40-3.

De Silva struck two fours in his 14 which came off 20 balls.

Saqib (2-28), Salman (2-52) and Ali Shabir (2-28) were the successful bowlers for the Patron’s XI.

In response, Patron’s XI reached 43-2 in 15 overs.

Test batsman Azan Awais was batting on 19 and with him at the other end was Mohammad Taha on 16.

Azan had struck three fours in his 46-ball knock while Taha smashed two fours from 18 balls.

Earlier fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka got rid of Abdullah Fazal (2) before Rathnayake had Sameer Minhas (3) to leave Patron’s XI struggling at 23-2.

Ahsan Raza and Tariq Rasheed are supervising the match while Zulfiqa Jan, former first-class cricketer, is acting as reserve umpire.

Kamran Chaudhry is the match commissioner.

The side show will serve Sri Lanka to do some warm-up ahead of the first Test of the two-match Test series which will begin at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium with the first Test from November 9.

Some of the key players of Pakistan squad are currently playing in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy first round to do some practice ahead of the first Test.

Skipper Babar Azam is playing for Lahore Whites.

headline: Jennifer Lawrence quotes ‘The Hunger Games’ while urging fans to vote in US midterms
description: “Midterms bb. Don’t forget who burns with us. Go vote,” Lawrence wrote, adding a link to Vote.org
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jennifer Lawrence has turned to her iconic The Hunger Games character Katniss Everdeen to encourage Americans to vote in the 2026 US midterm elections.

The Oscar-winning actress shared a photo of herself making the franchise’s famous three-finger salute on Instagram Stories on Tuesday, November 3, alongside a message urging her 8.7 million followers to head to the polls.

“Midterms bb. Don’t forget who burns with us. Go vote,” Lawrence wrote, adding a link to Vote.org to help people find their nearest polling locations.

Her caption references one of Katniss’ most memorable lines from The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1, released in 2014. In the film, the character delivers a speech challenging President Snow after a hospital in her home district is bombed.

“You can torture us and bomb us and burn our districts to the ground. But do you see that? Fire is catching. And if we burn, you burn with us!” Katniss declares in the scene.

The three-finger salute has also become a recognisable symbol of resistance, extending beyond the fictional world of Panem and appearing in real-world protests and pro-democracy movements.

Although Lawrence did not endorse a particular candidate or political party in her post, the wording of her message prompted fans to interpret the reference in a political context.

Her decision to speak out comes after she previously expressed uncertainty about using her celebrity platform to discuss politics. In a 2025 interview with The New York Times, Lawrence said she was reconsidering how publicly sharing her political opinions could affect audiences' willingness to engage with her work.

She explained that she did not want to contribute to further division and wanted to protect the ability of audiences to connect with films and art regardless of her personal views.

Lawrence is also preparing to reprise her role as Katniss in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. She recently confirmed her return alongside Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson, more than a decade after the original franchise concluded.

Speaking on the Call Her Daddy podcast in October, Lawrence described reuniting with her former co-stars and the original crew as an “unbelievable” and emotional experience.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, directed by Francis Lawrence, is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

The Oscar-winning actress shared a photo of herself making the franchise’s famous three-finger salute on Instagram Stories on Tuesday, November 3, alongside a message urging her 8.7 million followers to head to the polls.

“Midterms bb. Don’t forget who burns with us. Go vote,” Lawrence wrote, adding a link to Vote.org to help people find their nearest polling locations.

Her caption references one of Katniss’ most memorable lines from The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1, released in 2014. In the film, the character delivers a speech challenging President Snow after a hospital in her home district is bombed.

“You can torture us and bomb us and burn our districts to the ground. But do you see that? Fire is catching. And if we burn, you burn with us!” Katniss declares in the scene.

The three-finger salute has also become a recognisable symbol of resistance, extending beyond the fictional world of Panem and appearing in real-world protests and pro-democracy movements.

Although Lawrence did not endorse a particular candidate or political party in her post, the wording of her message prompted fans to interpret the reference in a political context.

Her decision to speak out comes after she previously expressed uncertainty about using her celebrity platform to discuss politics. In a 2025 interview with The New York Times, Lawrence said she was reconsidering how publicly sharing her political opinions could affect audiences' willingness to engage with her work.

She explained that she did not want to contribute to further division and wanted to protect the ability of audiences to connect with films and art regardless of her personal views.

Lawrence is also preparing to reprise her role as Katniss in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. She recently confirmed her return alongside Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson, more than a decade after the original franchise concluded.

Speaking on the Call Her Daddy podcast in October, Lawrence described reuniting with her former co-stars and the original crew as an “unbelievable” and emotional experience.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, directed by Francis Lawrence, is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

headline: PIA to launch three direct weekly Islamabad-Birmingham flights from Dec 1
description: Spokesperson says airline aims to increase the total number of weekly flights between Pakistan, UK to 23
author: Talib Fareedi
article_text:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Wednesday said it would launch three weekly direct flights between Islamabad and Birmingham from December 1, expanding its UK network to facilitate Pakistani residents in northern and central parts of Britain.

According to a PIA spokesperson, the flights would initially operate on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays.

The spokesperson added that the UK was an important destination for PIA, adding that the airline aimed to increase the total number of weekly flights between Pakistan and the UK to 23.

On September 3, PIA decided to expand its air operations to London, increasing the number of weekly flights to seven from October 27.

A PIA spokesperson stated the national flag carrier would operate daily flights between Pakistan and London, including five weekly flights between Islamabad and London and two between Lahore and London, adding that the increase in flight frequency reflected growing passenger demand and confidence in the national airline.

PIA resumed direct flights to Britain in October last year, months after UK authorities ended a five-year suspension imposed over aviation safety concerns.

The flag carrier was earlier barred from flying to Britain, the European Union and the United States in June 2020, a month after one of its Airbus A320 aircraft plunged into a Karachi neighbourhood, killing nearly 100 people.

The deadly crash was blamed on human error.

Britain lifted restrictions on Pakistani carriers in July 2025 after concluding that aviation safety standards were "satisfactory and in line with international norms".

headline: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
description: Trump-backed Republican Senate candidates lose in South Carolina, North Carolina and Texas
author: Reuters
article_text:
President Donald Trump asked voters to pretend he was on ​the ballot in the midterm elections and handpicked Republican candidates in some of the country's most consequential Senate races. By Tuesday night, voters had rejected them.

Trump-backed ‌candidates in South Carolina, North Carolina, Texas and Michigan all lost, handing Democrats control of the chamber and exposing the limits of Trump's political power.

Trump has spent more than a decade reshaping the Republican Party around his MAGA movement, dictating primary matchups and pushing aside conservative figures he felt were insufficiently loyal or not aligned with his vision. Trump repeatedly favored loyalists and ideological allies over more established Republicans with stronger statewide networks and ​proven electoral track records, betting that his endorsement could overcome their political liabilities.

Tuesday's results revealed he was unable to persuade the broader electorate to back his choices.

One of the ​most stunning repudiations came in South Carolina, which had not elected a Democratic senator since 1998 and which Trump won by 18 percentage points ⁠in 2024. Trump backed Darline Graham, the sister of late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham. But Democrat Annie Andrews won the seat in a stunning upset.

In North Carolina, Trump endorsed former national ​Republican campaign official Michael Whatley, who lost in a rout to former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper.

In Texas, Trump intervened in a messy Republican primary election to promote scandal-plagued Attorney General Ken Paxton over ​Senator John Cornyn, a Trump ally who some in the party considered a safer pick in the general election. Democrat James Talarico glided to a victory on Tuesday night, delivering Democrats a seat the party had not won since 1988.

Former US Representative Mike Rogers, Trump’s choice in Michigan, was defeated by Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who will be the first Muslim to serve in the Senate.

The losses came as Trump's popularity was lower heading into ​Tuesday’s vote than in the aftermath of the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol, according to Reuters/Ipsos polls. That helped fuel concerns among Republicans that the president had become a ​drag on the party he remade around himself.

“This is a Trump Quake,” said Doug Heye, a veteran Republican strategist, pointing to voter frustration over high prices caused by tariffs and the war in Iran. "Trump spent the ‌year telling ⁠voters what was important to him, not to them."

Trump struck a defiant tone as election returns arrived.

"I wasn’t on the ballot, and if I were, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote in a Tuesday night social media post.

One White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Trump “did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves.”

A senior White House official, also speaking anonymously, told Reuters the administration had polling data as far back as six weeks ago showing Republicans would lose both the House of Representatives and ​Senate, and Trump embarked on a month-long nationwide ​campaign to try to salvage Republicans' prospects.

'Gave that seat away'

Some independent analysts said the Senate losses bore Trump's fingerprints specifically. Thomas Kahn, a professor at American University, said the president's intervention in the Texas Republican primary had cost his party a safe seat, arguing that a nomination for Senator John Cornyn "would have been a slam ​dunk for Republicans to win."

North Carolina, Kahn said, was another clear case. The Republican incumbent senator, Thom Tillis, said last year that he would not seek re-election after a public split with Trump, who threatened to back a primary challenger against him after Tillis balked at Medicaid cuts in the president's tax-and-spending bill.

"He essentially gave that seat away to Democrats," Kahn said. "Roy Cooper would not have run if Thom Tillis had run for re-election."

Former North Carolina Governor Pat McCrory, a Republican, said Trump's interventions in his party's primaries had divided Republicans in state after state.

In South Carolina, ⁠McCrory said, the ​president went against two local congressmen, a fight that "really divided the party" — an example, in his telling, of a ​president spending his political capital against his own side.

McCrory's sharpest criticism was aimed at Trump's connection with the voters who built his coalition.

"I think President Trump's greatest strength was he had a common touch with the working-class people," ​McCrory said. "He lost that skill. He better regain that skill for the good of the country."

headline: IHC fixes Imran and Bushra's appeals against sentences in £190m case for Nov 10
description: Division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar, Justice Muhammad Asif will hear appeal
author: APP
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday fixed the hearing of the appeals of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi against their convictions in the £190 million case for November 10.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif would hear the appeals, according to the cause list issued by the IHC Registrar’s Office.

The court had sought arguments from counsel for the convicts on their appeals challenging the sentences.

At the previous hearing, the court had adjourned the proceedings without taking up the matter following a request by Imran’s counsel, Barrister Salman Safdar.

In January 2025, an Islamabad accountability court sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison in the reference filed by the National Accountability Bureau.

The £190m case pertains to allegations linked to the Al-Qadir Trust, a welfare organisation established in 2018. The trust, which runs a university outside Islamabad, is accused of being used as a front to receive land worth millions of dollars from a real estate tycoon.

According to the government, the donations were made in exchange for the former premier’s administration using repatriated funds from the United Kingdom to pay fines on behalf of the businessman instead of depositing the amount into the national exchequer. Imran has denied the allegations, maintaining that neither he nor his wife derived any financial benefit from the trust or related transactions.

headline: ICJ to rule on Myanmar genocide case over Rohingya on Nov 19
description: Case filed by Gambia concerns military crackdown that forced over 700,000 Rohingya Muslims to flee to Bangladesh
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Case filed by Gambia concerns military crackdown that forced over 700,000 Rohingya Muslims to flee to Bangladesh

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) would deliver its judgment on November 19 on whether Myanmar violated the UN Genocide Convention in its treatment of the Rohingya Muslim minority, the court announced on Tuesday.

The ruling is scheduled for 10am local time in The Hague, Netherlands, in a case brought by Gambia in 2019, with 11 states intervening in the proceedings.

The lawsuit accuses Myanmar of violating its obligations under the 1948 Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide during military operations against the Rohingya.

Gambia's decision to bring the case before the UN's highest court was hailed as a "historic achievement" by members of the Rohingya community.

The Rohingya are a stateless Muslim minority who have faced decades of discrimination and displacement in Myanmar.

More than 700,000 fled the country's Rakhine State following a military crackdown in August 2017, with most seeking refuge in neighbouring Bangladesh.

The UN has described the Rohingya as the world's most persecuted minority, while a report by the Ontario International Development Agency estimated that thousands were killed by Myanmar's security forces.

headline: Iranian officials gloat as US voters deal blow to Trump
description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf says Americans reject war over conscience and the cost of living
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iran's government savoured the stinging rebuke delivered to Donald Trump in the midterm elections, declaring voters had rejected the war launched by ​the US president even as Tehran remained on high alert for the possibility of renewed strikes.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and ‌we endorse this message," Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, posted on X, adding that Washington should not ignore public opinion by attacking his country again.

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party was in power, warning against "even the slightest inclination towards submission" to the US.

"The US sees the end of its hegemony as distant; we see it as near," he added.

Old foes

Democrats ​captured majorities in both the Senate and House in Tuesday's election, with victories in Republican strongholds underscoring deep frustration with Trump's stewardship of the economy and his decision to ​launch a war that drove up gas prices.

In Iran, a news outlet run by the judiciary shared a joke circulating on X that "Trump failed at ⁠regime change in Iran, but he succeeded in Texas", a reference to the southern state where a Democrat won a Senate race for the first time in decades.

But two senior Iranian sources ​told Reuters that while Iranian leaders welcomed the Democrats’ victory, Tehran was concerned that Trump could seek to compensate for it with a military strike, and remained on high alert.

Iran's leaders have long ​regarded the United States as their main enemy, referring to it as "the Great Satan".

At a state-organised rally on Wednesday commemorating the student takeover of the US embassy in Tehran during the 1979 Islamic revolution, demonstrators voiced triumph at an election they linked to Iran's success in surviving months of US attacks.

"The fact that the might of these warmongering Republicans has been broken, something unprecedented in human history, means that from now on we will ​see the real war unfolding inside the US Senate and among American officials," said one, giving only his family name of Nazari.

Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war amid fears it ​could reignite after the election, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.

The US and Israel attacked Iran on February ‌28, and Iran ⁠responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. Conflict also erupted in Lebanon between Iran-backed Hezbollah and Israel, and more recently spread to Yemen, from where the Iran-aligned Houthis have struck energy facilities, airports and other targets in Saudi Arabia.

Global oil and gas prices have shot up, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz severely disrupted after Tehran declared it closed, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran, hitting Iran's economy hard.

'Iran’s shadow over US elections'

Ahead of the US election, senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks with ​the US to weaken Trump politically ahead of the ​vote.

Some news outlets played on the timing ⁠of the election on the anniversary of the embassy seizure, when radical students cemented Iran's toppling of the US-backed Shah by storming the embassy and holding 52 Americans hostage there for 444 days.

Major Iranian newspaper Hamshahri linked the events with a front-page image showing Trump blindfolded with his head ​bowed.

With a headline declaring "Iran's shadow over US elections", it said Washington had been "47 years Iran's captive: from the capture of the spies' ​nest (US embassy) to the November ⁠2026 US Congress elections".

The Iran war has been unpopular among Americans since it began, and blaming the war for driving up costs was a focus of the Democrats' election campaign.

Khamenei's message signalled that Tehran had no intention of showing flexibility on its demands for lasting control over the Strait of Hormuz or conditions to end the conflict.

"The consequences of (US) miscalculations and arrogant delusions have manifested as a heavy burden ⁠of costs, ​borne by the American people and the puppet regimes subservient to the US government," he said.

Trump has offered shifting goals ​and timelines for the war that is now in its ninth month.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," Trump told Fox News, referring to the ​election result.

The conservative Iranian newspaper Jam-e Jam declared the election result "The twilight of Trumpism".
