article_html:
Iran's government savoured the stinging rebuke delivered to Donald Trump in the midterm elections, declaring voters had rejected the war launched by ​the US president even as Tehran remained on high alert for the possibility of renewed strikes.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and ‌we endorse this message," Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, posted on X, adding that Washington should not ignore public opinion by attacking his country again.

Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message.

If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare.

— محمدباقر قالیباف | MB Ghalibaf (@mb_ghalibaf) November 4, 2026

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party was in power, warning against "even the slightest inclination towards submission" to the US.

The full text of the message issued by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Imam Sayyid Mojtaba Khamenei, on the occasion of the National Day of Fighting Global Arrogance, Nov. 4, 2026 pic.twitter.com/bjCedjH29h

— Khamenei Media (@Khamenei_m) November 4, 2026

"The US sees the end of its hegemony as distant; we see it as near," he added.

Old foes

Democrats ​captured majorities in both the Senate and House in Tuesday's election, with victories in Republican strongholds underscoring deep frustration with Trump's stewardship of the economy and his decision to ​launch a war that drove up gas prices.

In Iran, a news outlet run by the judiciary shared a joke circulating on X that "Trump failed at ⁠regime change in Iran, but he succeeded in Texas", a reference to the southern state where a Democrat won a Senate race for the first time in decades.

But two senior Iranian sources ​told Reuters that while Iranian leaders welcomed the Democrats’ victory, Tehran was concerned that Trump could seek to compensate for it with a military strike, and remained on high alert.

Read: Anyone expecting shift in US policy after midterm election 'seriously mistaken': Iranian supreme leader

Iran's leaders have long ​regarded the United States as their main enemy, referring to it as "the Great Satan".

At a state-organised rally on Wednesday commemorating the student takeover of the US embassy in Tehran during the 1979 Islamic revolution, demonstrators voiced triumph at an election they linked to Iran's success in surviving months of US attacks.

"The fact that the might of these warmongering Republicans has been broken, something unprecedented in human history, means that from now on we will ​see the real war unfolding inside the US Senate and among American officials," said one, giving only his family name of Nazari.

Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war amid fears it ​could reignite after the election, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.

The US and Israel attacked Iran on February ‌28, and Iran ⁠responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. Conflict also erupted in Lebanon between Iran-backed Hezbollah and Israel, and more recently spread to Yemen, from where the Iran-aligned Houthis have struck energy facilities, airports and other targets in Saudi Arabia.

Global oil and gas prices have shot up, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz severely disrupted after Tehran declared it closed, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran, hitting Iran's economy hard.

'Iran’s shadow over US elections'

Ahead of the US election, senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks with ​the US to weaken Trump politically ahead of the ​vote.

Some news outlets played on the timing ⁠of the election on the anniversary of the embassy seizure, when radical students cemented Iran's toppling of the US-backed Shah by storming the embassy and holding 52 Americans hostage there for 444 days.

Major Iranian newspaper Hamshahri linked the events with a front-page image showing Trump blindfolded with his head ​bowed.

With a headline declaring "Iran's shadow over US elections", it said Washington had been "47 years Iran's captive: from the capture of the spies' ​nest (US embassy) to the November ⁠2026 US Congress elections".

The Iran war has been unpopular among Americans since it began, and blaming the war for driving up costs was a focus of the Democrats' election campaign.

Also Read: Democrats sweep Congress in US midterm elections

Khamenei's message signalled that Tehran had no intention of showing flexibility on its demands for lasting control over the Strait of Hormuz or conditions to end the conflict.

"The consequences of (US) miscalculations and arrogant delusions have manifested as a heavy burden ⁠of costs, ​borne by the American people and the puppet regimes subservient to the US government," he said.

Trump has offered shifting goals ​and timelines for the war that is now in its ninth month.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," Trump told Fox News, referring to the ​election result.

The conservative Iranian newspaper Jam-e Jam declared the election result "The twilight of Trumpism".

headline: Troops deployed in Indonesia as president sacks aide accused of wiretapping
description: Presidential official says wiretaps may amount to treason amid growing rift between president and predecessor
author: Reuters
article_text:
Indonesia's president sacked his chief of staff on Wednesday after his arrest in a wiretapping scandal ‌that the government said pointed to treason, as the military said thousands of troops were being mobilised in the capital to boost security.

Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who was appointed chief of staff just a few weeks ago, was among three senior police officers detained on Tuesday, accused of illegally tapping the phones of President Prabowo Subianto and unnamed journalists, politicians, government ​officials and business people since early 2025.

The illegal wiretaps were carried out by "rogue individuals" whose actions indicated treason, presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi ​said.

"It also tends toward acts that endanger state interests and the safety of the nation's leadership, including the safety of ⁠the head of state," Hadi told reporters.

Reuters could not immediately contact the three suspects or their lawyers.

The scandal comes as the president, a retired army ​general, faces pressure on multiple fronts, with widening public discontent about his big-spending populist policies and a slump in investor confidence over his administration's handling ​of the $1.5 trillion G20 economy.

Political intrigue has been growing in Indonesia in recent weeks amid a rift between Prabowo and his two-term predecessor and former backer Widodo, who remains highly influential, despite stepping back from politics.

Listyo, the former national police chief, was known as a loyalist of Widodo.

Military mobilized to ‘safeguard and protect stability'

Troops were deployed to Jakarta to "safeguard and ​protect the stability of Indonesia's security," navy spokesperson Tunggul said late on Wednesday.

The deployment was also related to upcoming training in areas near Jakarta, Tunggul, ​who goes by one name, added.

Soldiers on the capital's streets are not uncommon in Indonesia, where the military has been regularly deployed ahead of anti-government protests.

Elected president in ‌2024 by ⁠a big majority, former special forces commander Prabowo has seen his approval rating slide in his second year in office, with unease over food prices and his troubled free meals and village cooperatives programmes.

His administration has also been under intense investor scrutiny this year, with ratings outlook cuts, concerns about policy unpredictability, and record stock market routs after warnings by global index provider MSCI of an equities market downgrade.

Prabowo's party Gerindra said it would hold talks with other political parties to discuss the ​wiretapping, with its secretary-general Sugiono on Wednesday ​calling the scandal "insubordination" within the government.

In ⁠a post on X on Wednesday, former President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono appealed to Prabowo to "restore civility to our politics".

Motive for wiretaps unclear

The government has yet to determine the motive for the wiretapping, said Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Indonesia's senior ​minister for legal affairs.

Police late on Tuesday said the suspects were being investigated for unauthorised wiretaps. The targets ​of the wiretaps were ⁠not disclosed.

Amnesty International in Indonesia urged authorities on Wednesday to reveal who the subjects of the wiretaps were and said the public had a right to know.

"If this scandal is allowed to continue unchecked, it could pave the way for a secret police apparatus used to tame the opposition," it said.

Sana Jaffrey, a state-building ⁠researcher at ​the Australian National University, said the troop deployment in Jakarta could signal concerns about tension ​between the military and police loyal to former chief Listyo.

"If Prabowo increasingly sees threats to his personal security, then this could strengthen the case for relying more heavily on the military," she ​said, adding that the immediate concern was the risk of unintended escalation.

article_html:
Indonesia's president sacked his chief of staff on Wednesday after his arrest in a wiretapping scandal ‌that the government said pointed to treason, as the military said thousands of troops were being mobilised in the capital to boost security.

Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who was appointed chief of staff just a few weeks ago, was among three senior police officers detained on Tuesday, accused of illegally tapping the phones of President Prabowo Subianto and unnamed journalists, politicians, government ​officials and business people since early 2025.

The illegal wiretaps were carried out by "rogue individuals" whose actions indicated treason, presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi ​said.

Read: IOC regrets Indonesian decision to block entry for Israeli gymnasts

"It also tends toward acts that endanger state interests and the safety of the nation's leadership, including the safety of ⁠the head of state," Hadi told reporters.

Reuters could not immediately contact the three suspects or their lawyers.

The scandal comes as the president, a retired army ​general, faces pressure on multiple fronts, with widening public discontent about his big-spending populist policies and a slump in investor confidence over his administration's handling ​of the $1.5 trillion G20 economy.

Political intrigue has been growing in Indonesia in recent weeks amid a rift between Prabowo and his two-term predecessor and former backer Widodo, who remains highly influential, despite stepping back from politics.

Listyo, the former national police chief, was known as a loyalist of Widodo.

Military mobilized to ‘safeguard and protect stability'

Troops were deployed to Jakarta to "safeguard and ​protect the stability of Indonesia's security," navy spokesperson Tunggul said late on Wednesday.

The deployment was also related to upcoming training in areas near Jakarta, Tunggul, ​who goes by one name, added.

Soldiers on the capital's streets are not uncommon in Indonesia, where the military has been regularly deployed ahead of anti-government protests.

Elected president in ‌2024 by ⁠a big majority, former special forces commander Prabowo has seen his approval rating slide in his second year in office, with unease over food prices and his troubled free meals and village cooperatives programmes.

His administration has also been under intense investor scrutiny this year, with ratings outlook cuts, concerns about policy unpredictability, and record stock market routs after warnings by global index provider MSCI of an equities market downgrade.

Prabowo's party Gerindra said it would hold talks with other political parties to discuss the ​wiretapping, with its secretary-general Sugiono on Wednesday ​calling the scandal "insubordination" within the government.

In ⁠a post on X on Wednesday, former President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono appealed to Prabowo to "restore civility to our politics".

Motive for wiretaps unclear

The government has yet to determine the motive for the wiretapping, said Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Indonesia's senior ​minister for legal affairs.

Police late on Tuesday said the suspects were being investigated for unauthorised wiretaps. The targets ​of the wiretaps were ⁠not disclosed.

Amnesty International in Indonesia urged authorities on Wednesday to reveal who the subjects of the wiretaps were and said the public had a right to know.

Also Read: Indonesia says no to $1 billion fee for Trump's 'Board of Peace' seat

"If this scandal is allowed to continue unchecked, it could pave the way for a secret police apparatus used to tame the opposition," it said.

Sana Jaffrey, a state-building ⁠researcher at ​the Australian National University, said the troop deployment in Jakarta could signal concerns about tension ​between the military and police loyal to former chief Listyo.

"If Prabowo increasingly sees threats to his personal security, then this could strengthen the case for relying more heavily on the military," she ​said, adding that the immediate concern was the risk of unintended escalation.

headline: Pakistan name squad for AFC Under-17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers
description: Young Shaheens to face Iran, Jordan, Laos and Sri Lanka in Group D in the continental event
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Young Shaheens to face Iran, Jordan, Laos and Sri Lanka in Group D in the continental event

Pakistan on Wednesday unveiled a 23-member squad for the AFC Under-17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers, which will be held in Laos from November 8 to 20, the Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) said.

The squad was selected following the conclusion of the PFF National Under-17 Football Championship 2026, which provided a platform for emerging players from across the country to compete for national team places.

Head coach Mohammad Habib will lead Pakistan in Group D, where they will face Iran, Jordan, hosts Laos and Sri Lanka.

Pakistan will aim to secure qualification for the continental tournament as the young players look to build on their performances in the domestic championship.

Squad:

Goal-keepers: Samar Razzaq, Wali Ullah, Ahsan Ullah; Defenders: Nadeem Hussain, Hamza Khan, Muhammad Hammad, Syed Manzar Shah, Mubashir Shah, Muhammad Awais, Hasnain Ali, Mohsin Amin; Midfielders: Abdul Sammad, Arsalan Fareedi, Muhammad Khalil Ullah, Muhammad Irmad Sarwar, Muhammad Anees, Bari Dad, Essa Khan; Forwards: Muhammad Raffy, Muhammad Moosa, Muhammad Shahzad, Hazrat Abbas, Haris Khan

headline: Israeli president receives official election results as committee rejects fraud allegations
description: Election chief warns against undermining vote integrity, says final results are 'binding on all of us'
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday received the official results of last week's parliamentary elections as the Central Elections Committee rejected fraud allegations raised by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and right-wing parties.

"Voices are seeking to undermine the election results. This is a real danger," Committee Chairman Judge Noam Sohlberg said during a ceremony attended by Herzog, according to Israeli news website Ynet.

Sohlberg said allegations concerning aspects of the electoral process remained under investigation but warned against questioning the legitimacy of votes cast by Arab citizens.

"We must not cast doubt on voting in Arab society, just as we must not cast doubt on any other group in Israeli society," he said.

The election results are "binding on all of us," Sohlberg stressed.

Earlier Wednesday, the committee approved the final results, with 15 members voting in favor, two against and 14 abstaining, according to Ynet.

The approval followed the committee's announcement that it had found no evidence that the integrity of last week's parliamentary elections had been compromised.

Netanyahu and right-wing parties in his bloc had alleged fraud and voting manipulation within Israel's Arab community.

Herzog to begin government formation consultations

Herzog is scheduled to begin consultations with representatives of elected parties Wednesday afternoon to determine which lawmaker should be tasked with forming the next government, Ynet reported.

During the consultations, parliamentary parties are expected to recommend candidates for prime minister.

Herzog will then decide which candidate has the best chance of assembling a governing coalition and grant that lawmaker the mandate to form a government.

Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot is expected to receive 48 recommendations from Yashar, Yachad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu.

Netanyahu is expected to secure 46 recommendations from Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Shas and Religious Zionism.

The predominantly Arab parties, including the Joint List and Ra'am, and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party have yet to announce whom they will recommend, according to Ynet.

Sohlberg said allegations concerning aspects of the electoral process remained under investigation but warned against questioning the legitimacy of votes cast by Arab citizens.
"We must not cast doubt on voting in Arab society, just as we must not cast doubt on any other group in Israeli society," he said.
The election results are "binding on all of us," Sohlberg stressed.
Earlier Wednesday, the committee approved the final results, with 15 members voting in favor, two against and 14 abstaining, according to Ynet.
The approval followed the committee's announcement that it had found no evidence that the integrity of last week's parliamentary elections had been compromised.
Netanyahu and right-wing parties in his bloc had alleged fraud and voting manipulation within Israel's Arab community.
Herzog to begin government formation consultations
Herzog is scheduled to begin consultations with representatives of elected parties Wednesday afternoon to determine which lawmaker should be tasked with forming the next government, Ynet reported.
During the consultations, parliamentary parties are expected to recommend candidates for prime minister.
Herzog will then decide which candidate has the best chance of assembling a governing coalition and grant that lawmaker the mandate to form a government.
Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot is expected to receive 48 recommendations from Yashar, Yachad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu.
Netanyahu is expected to secure 46 recommendations from Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Shas and Religious Zionism.
The predominantly Arab parties, including the Joint List and Ra'am, and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party have yet to announce whom they will recommend, according to Ynet.

headline: Explainer: What does Democratic control of Congress mean for Trump?
description: Democrats' House and Senate takeover gives them power to probe the administration, challenge policies and scrutinise spending
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections has handed them control of both chambers of Congress, setting up a period of divided government that could complicate President Donald Trump’s agenda during the final two years of his term.

Democrats on Tuesday secured a majority in both chambers of Congress, winning a projected 54 seats in the Senate and 224 seats in the House of Representatives.

When the new Congress convenes in January 2027, Trump will face a Democratic-controlled House of Representatives and Senate, limiting his ability to advance legislation and potentially complicating his administration’s spending priorities.

Here is what the shift in power means for the president:

Stronger congressional oversight

One of the biggest changes will be Democrats’ control of congressional committees in both chambers.

Committees can hold hearings, request government documents, and summon officials to testify. They can also issue subpoenas, although disputes over their authority and executive privilege can lead to legal challenges.

Scott Lucas, a professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, said that Democrats are more likely to focus on investigations and accountability.

A demonstrator wearing a frog costume and holding a "CLEAN HOUSE" banner near the White House in Washington, DC, during the US midterm elections on November 4, 2026. Photo: Reuters

These could include inquiries into Trump's stockholdings, potential insider trading involving his family, and the wealth he has accumulated while in office.

“What Democrats can also do because they now control the committees in both houses is have hearings for accountability,” he said.

Lucas also expects renewed scrutiny of the files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, with victims’ families and many Democrats saying the Justice Department has yet to release all the files required under a law passed last year.

“I think you'll see hearings reopen on the Epstein files,” he said.

Other possible inquiries could focus on federal agencies and whether they have been weakened or pressured by the administration, "like the Justice Department to restore the independence of those agencies,” Lucas said.

More legislative obstacles

Democrats will be able to introduce legislation reflecting their own priorities, including proposals on health care, education, and immigration. Lawmakers could also seek legislation to address potential conflicts of interest involving elected officials.

“For example, trying to seek accountability on stockholdings might be a bill that you see very clearly so that representatives don't have conflicts of interest,” he said.

“They could proceed with proposed legislation on health, on education, to push back on the immigration crackdown.”

Supporters react after media outlets projected Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico's victory in Austin, Texas. Photo: Reuters

However, passing such measures will be difficult if Trump opposes them.

“Donald Trump has already been ruling through executive orders, and there is only one major bill that he has passed ... but Democrats can propose their own legislation. They can put forth their own priorities.”

“Now all of that legislation could get vetoed by Trump, of course, and you need a two-thirds majority to override that,” Lucas explained.

A presidential veto can be overturned only if two-thirds of members voting in both the House of Representatives and the Senate support the measure.

This means Democrats would need Republican support to enact major legislation over Trump's objections.

Lucas said some Republicans may become more willing to cooperate with them, as the election result could weaken Trump's influence over his own party and encourage some Republican lawmakers to distance themselves from the president.

Greater leverage over government spending

Democrats will have greater influence over federal spending, including the defense budget, military operations, and foreign military assistance, as Congress controls government appropriations.

They could use budget negotiations to scrutinize Pentagon spending, demand greater transparency over military operations, including the ongoing Iran war, and seek changes to defend funding priorities.

However, the president retains authority as commander-in-chief, and funding already appropriated under existing laws can generally continue to be spent.

Lucas, however, said he would be surprised if Democrats deliberately pursued a government shutdown, describing such a move as irresponsible.

"I'd be very surprised if Democrats go for shutting down the government. That won't be responsible.”

Instead, he expects Democrats to wait and see how Trump responds to the new balance of power.

“I think they will wait to see if Trump wants to shut down the government, which is very possible if he feels he's not getting his way,” Lucas said.

Last year, the country witnessed the longest government-wide shutdown in history of 43 days, from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025, ending after Congress passed a funding measure that Trump signed into law.

Appointment and administration battles

A Democratic-controlled Senate will have the power to scrutinise and reject Trump’s nominees for federal judgeships, Cabinet positions, ambassadorships, and potential Supreme Court vacancies.

Democrats could also use oversight hearings to scrutinise senior administration officials.

Lucas suggested that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth could face particular scrutiny if the months-long Iran war continues.

“They may open up hearings on certain officials like the Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, especially if the Iran war continues to go so badly and he keeps urging the military,” Lucas said.

He also pointed to the possibility of congressional scrutiny of senior Justice Department officials.

“I think they will push back on other officials, maybe short of impeachment, like the head of the Justice Department, Todd Blanche, because he's effectively Trump's lawyer,” he said.

Democrats charge that Trump has weaponised and politicised the Justice Department, using it as a tool to target his political enemies.

Impeachment issue

Democrats could technically launch another impeachment process against Trump, as the House has the power to impeach a president with a simple majority.

But removing him from office would be much harder. Conviction in the Senate requires a two-thirds majority of senators present.

Trump was impeached twice during his first term, in 2019 over his dealings with Ukraine and in 2021 over his role in the events surrounding the Jan. 6 attack on the US Capitol. The Senate acquitted him in both cases.

Lucas does not expect Democrats to make impeachment their priority.

Senator-elect from Kansas Hamilton in Overland Park, November 3, 2026. Photo: Reuters

“Remember, you need a two-thirds majority to convict in the Senate, so you would need 67 seats. At most they're going to have 56 and more likely it's going to be around 54, maybe 55.”

Current projections put Senate Democrats at 54 seats.

Lucas said the emphasis would be on holding officials accountable rather than trying to remove Trump from office.

“I look for them more to go for those hearings for accountability rather than impeachment when it comes to Trump.”

What happens next?

The new Congress is scheduled to begin its term on Jan 3, 2027. Republicans retain control of both chambers until the current congressional term ends.

Democratic control will not automatically reverse Trump’s executive actions or remove his constitutional powers. However, it will give the opposition party greater authority to investigate his administration, challenge his legislative priorities, and influence federal spending.

The next two years could thus see increased congressional scrutiny, prolonged negotiations over government funding, and a more contested relationship between the White House and Capitol Hill.

However, passing such measures will be difficult if Trump opposes them.

“Donald Trump has already been ruling through executive orders, and there is only one major bill that he has passed ... but Democrats can propose their own legislation. They can put forth their own priorities.”

“Now all of that legislation could get vetoed by Trump, of course, and you need a two-thirds majority to override that,” Lucas explained.

A presidential veto can be overturned only if two-thirds of members voting in both the House of Representatives and the Senate support the measure.

This means Democrats would need Republican support to enact major legislation over Trump's objections.

Lucas said some Republicans may become more willing to cooperate with them, as the election result could weaken Trump's influence over his own party and encourage some Republican lawmakers to distance themselves from the president.

Greater leverage over government spending

Democrats will have greater influence over federal spending, including the defense budget, military operations, and foreign military assistance, as Congress controls government appropriations.

They could use budget negotiations to scrutinize Pentagon spending, demand greater transparency over military operations, including the ongoing Iran war, and seek changes to defend funding priorities.

However, the president retains authority as commander-in-chief, and funding already appropriated under existing laws can generally continue to be spent.

Lucas, however, said he would be surprised if Democrats deliberately pursued a government shutdown, describing such a move as irresponsible.

"I'd be very surprised if Democrats go for shutting down the government. That won't be responsible.”

Instead, he expects Democrats to wait and see how Trump responds to the new balance of power.

“I think they will wait to see if Trump wants to shut down the government, which is very possible if he feels he's not getting his way,” Lucas said.

Last year, the country witnessed the longest government-wide shutdown in history of 43 days, from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025, ending after Congress passed a funding measure that Trump signed into law.

Appointment and administration battles

A Democratic-controlled Senate will have the power to scrutinise and reject Trump’s nominees for federal judgeships, Cabinet positions, ambassadorships, and potential Supreme Court vacancies.

Democrats could also use oversight hearings to scrutinise senior administration officials.

Lucas suggested that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth could face particular scrutiny if the months-long Iran war continues.

“They may open up hearings on certain officials like the Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, especially if the Iran war continues to go so badly and he keeps urging the military,” Lucas said.

He also pointed to the possibility of congressional scrutiny of senior Justice Department officials.

“I think they will push back on other officials, maybe short of impeachment, like the head of the Justice Department, Todd Blanche, because he's effectively Trump's lawyer,” he said.

Democrats charge that Trump has weaponised and politicised the Justice Department, using it as a tool to target his political enemies.

Impeachment issue

Democrats could technically launch another impeachment process against Trump, as the House has the power to impeach a president with a simple majority.

But removing him from office would be much harder. Conviction in the Senate requires a two-thirds majority of senators present.

Trump was impeached twice during his first term, in 2019 over his dealings with Ukraine and in 2021 over his role in the events surrounding the Jan. 6 attack on the US Capitol. The Senate acquitted him in both cases.

Lucas does not expect Democrats to make impeachment their priority.

Senator-elect from Kansas Hamilton in Overland Park, November 3, 2026. Photo: Reuters

“Remember, you need a two-thirds majority to convict in the Senate, so you would need 67 seats. At most they're going to have 56 and more likely it's going to be around 54, maybe 55.”

Current projections put Senate Democrats at 54 seats.

Lucas said the emphasis would be on holding officials accountable rather than trying to remove Trump from office.

“I look for them more to go for those hearings for accountability rather than impeachment when it comes to Trump.”

What happens next?

The new Congress is scheduled to begin its term on Jan 3, 2027. Republicans retain control of both chambers until the current congressional term ends.

Democratic control will not automatically reverse Trump’s executive actions or remove his constitutional powers. However, it will give the opposition party greater authority to investigate his administration, challenge his legislative priorities, and influence federal spending.

The next two years could thus see increased congressional scrutiny, prolonged negotiations over government funding, and a more contested relationship between the White House and Capitol Hill.

headline: ‘La Bola Negra’ wins audience award at 2026 London Film Festival
description: The film was selected by festivalgoers through a public vote, with the British Film Institute announcing the winners
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
La Bola Negra, the Spanish queer drama directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, has won the Audience Award for Best Feature Film at the 70th BFI London Film Festival.

The film was selected by festivalgoers through a public vote, with the British Film Institute announcing the winners on November 4. Its recognition follows a successful festival run and growing international attention ahead of the upcoming awards season.

Rooted in the legacy of Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca, La Bola Negra explores queer identity, desire, love and suffering through interconnected stories spanning different periods.

The film received its gala screening at the Southbank Centre's Royal Festival Hall on October 8, attended by directors Ambrossi and Calvo alongside cast members Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau and Penélope Cruz.

Meanwhile, Grace Harper Brighouse's Dependence won the Audience Award for Best British Discovery. The documentary follows the filmmaker as she revisits decades of home videos following her father's death, exploring the experience of loving someone struggling with addiction.

The 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival ran for 12 days, featuring 258 titles from 87 countries across its programme. The festival also recorded its highest-ever audience attendance in London.

The Audience Awards were separate from the festival's juried competitions, which recognised films including Sergei Loznitsa's Imperium, winner of the Best Film Award in the Official Competition.

The win adds to the growing recognition of La Bola Negra, which has also been selected to represent Spain in the Best International Feature Film category at the 2027 Academy Awards.

The film stars Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Glenn Close and Penélope Cruz. It marks another major achievement for the directing duo, widely known as Los Javis, as the film continues its international awards campaign.

headline: Mir Raza murder case: Third IO gets 10 days to crack case
description: Karachi court orders IO to submit the challan and investigation report within the stipulated time
author: Abbas Naqvi
article_text:
A Karachi court has granted the third newly appointed investigation officer (IO) an additional 10 days to complete the probe into the Mir Raza murder case.

Raza, a waffle-making business owner, went missing from his PECHS residence in the early hours of July 28. Later, his body was found within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station. His murder was confirmed in the second post-mortem exam after the first exam failed to answer key questions.

Later, a judicial commission was formed to probe into the police misprobe, which suggested the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) in the case. The Sindh government issued an order on October 24 for its formation, with Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Ali Baloch as its lead. Senior officers of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers Sindh and National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) were to be included in the team.

The new IO, Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Fareed Ahmed Khan, appointed by the JIT in the case, was allowed additional days by the magisterial court on Tuesday to submit the challan and investigation report.

Appearing before the Judicial Magistrate Karachi East, DSP Khan said more than 1,100 pages of case records have been obtained and are currently being reviewed and requested a fortnight to complete the investigation; however, the court granted him only 10 days to submit the complete case report.

Inspector Shabbir Laghari was initially appointed as the IO, after which the investigation was handed over to DSP Siraj Lashari. The case failed to reach a conclusive stage under either officer.

View this post on Instagram

A one-member judicial commission, constituted on the directives of the Sindh government, raised several questions about the performance of the first IO, Inspector Laghari. Aligned with the victim’s family's request, the commission recommended that the investigation be handed over to a JIT.

Although a JIT was formed, it failed to submit the challan or a progress report before the court within the stipulated time. Consequently, the court issued a show-cause notice to the JIT head, DIG Baloch, seeking an explanation for the delay on November 2.

Events surrounding the case

Raza went missing from his residence in PECHS, Karachi, in the early hours of July 28. His body was subsequently recovered within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station and buried after a post-mortem examination at Jinnah Hospital.

The police initially treated the incident as a suicide; however, Raza’s family disputed this conclusion, alleging that his body bore visible signs of torture.

Following concerns raised by the family and anomalies identified in the initial post-mortem report, the body was exhumed on August 8 for a fresh examination. The subsequent medical findings, formally issued around August 31, established that Raza had died from a firearm injury entering from the back, ruling out suicide and raising serious questions about the circumstances surrounding his death.

A judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial was subsequently constituted to examine the circumstances of Raza’s death and the handling of the investigation.

In its report, submitted to the Sindh Chief Minister on October 15, the commission concluded that Raza had been murdered and severely criticised the police investigation, describing it as an "epic failure".

The commission identified serious shortcomings, including reliance on unverified text messages and selectively obtained CCTV footage, inconsistencies in medical reports, alleged mishandling and destruction of evidence, and irregularities in the constitution and replacement of the medical board.

Justice Sial also raised concerns about the possible involvement or negligence of police and health department officials, observing that the possibility of an initial cover-up could not be conclusively ruled out. It recommended further criminal and departmental proceedings against the officials concerned, alongside a fresh investigation through a JIT, citing the serious loss of public confidence in the police investigation.

Following the commission’s findings, the Sindh government initiated steps to implement its recommendations.

On October 24, a JIT headed by DIG West Zone Karachi Irfan Ali Baloch was constituted.

Separately, the provincial government established an inquiry committee, headed by Additional IG counter terrorism department (CTD) Zulfiqar Ali Larik, to examine the conduct and performance of 13 police officers and personnel identified in the commission’s report.

Disciplinary and administrative action was also initiated against several police officials, while inquiries were ordered into the role of health department officials and irregularities in medico-legal procedures.

The government thus moved towards implementing the commission’s recommendations, with the JIT tasked with establishing the circumstances of Raza’s murder and identifying those responsible.

article_html:
KARACHI:

A Karachi court has granted the third newly appointed investigation officer (IO) an additional 10 days to complete the probe into the Mir Raza murder case.

Raza, a waffle-making business owner, went missing from his PECHS residence in the early hours of July 28. Later, his body was found within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station. His murder was confirmed in the second post-mortem exam after the first exam failed to answer key questions.

Later, a judicial commission was formed to probe into the police misprobe, which suggested the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) in the case. The Sindh government issued an order on October 24 for its formation, with Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Ali Baloch as its lead. Senior officers of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers Sindh and National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) were to be included in the team.

The new IO, Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Fareed Ahmed Khan, appointed by the JIT in the case, was allowed additional days by the magisterial court on Tuesday to submit the challan and investigation report.

Read: Sindh home minister apologises 'unconditionally' to Mir Raza's judicial commission

Appearing before the Judicial Magistrate Karachi East, DSP Khan said more than 1,100 pages of case records have been obtained and are currently being reviewed and requested a fortnight to complete the investigation; however, the court granted him only 10 days to submit the complete case report.

Inspector Shabbir Laghari was initially appointed as the IO, after which the investigation was handed over to DSP Siraj Lashari. The case failed to reach a conclusive stage under either officer.

 
 
 
 
View this post on Instagram
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

A one-member judicial commission, constituted on the directives of the Sindh government, raised several questions about the performance of the first IO, Inspector Laghari. Aligned with the victim’s family's request, the commission recommended that the investigation be handed over to a JIT.

Although a JIT was formed, it failed to submit the challan or a progress report before the court within the stipulated time. Consequently, the court issued a show-cause notice to the JIT head, DIG Baloch, seeking an explanation for the delay on November 2.

Events surrounding the case

Raza went missing from his residence in PECHS, Karachi, in the early hours of July 28. His body was subsequently recovered within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station and buried after a post-mortem examination at Jinnah Hospital.

The police initially treated the incident as a suicide; however, Raza’s family disputed this conclusion, alleging that his body bore visible signs of torture.

Following concerns raised by the family and anomalies identified in the initial post-mortem report, the body was exhumed on August 8 for a fresh examination. The subsequent medical findings, formally issued around August 31, established that Raza had died from a firearm injury entering from the back, ruling out suicide and raising serious questions about the circumstances surrounding his death.

Read more: Judicial commission grills doctor over errors in Mir Raza's first post-mortem report, calls it 'criminal negligence'

A judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial was subsequently constituted to examine the circumstances of Raza’s death and the handling of the investigation.

In its report, submitted to the Sindh Chief Minister on October 15, the commission concluded that Raza had been murdered and severely criticised the police investigation, describing it as an "epic failure".

The commission identified serious shortcomings, including reliance on unverified text messages and selectively obtained CCTV footage, inconsistencies in medical reports, alleged mishandling and destruction of evidence, and irregularities in the constitution and replacement of the medical board.

Justice Sial also raised concerns about the possible involvement or negligence of police and health department officials, observing that the possibility of an initial cover-up could not be conclusively ruled out. It recommended further criminal and departmental proceedings against the officials concerned, alongside a fresh investigation through a JIT, citing the serious loss of public confidence in the police investigation.

Following the commission’s findings, the Sindh government initiated steps to implement its recommendations.

On October 24, a JIT headed by DIG West Zone Karachi Irfan Ali Baloch was constituted.

Also Read: Sindh govt forms JIT to investigate Mir Raza case, orders action against police officials

Separately, the provincial government established an inquiry committee, headed by Additional IG counter terrorism department (CTD) Zulfiqar Ali Larik, to examine the conduct and performance of 13 police officers and personnel identified in the commission’s report.

Disciplinary and administrative action was also initiated against several police officials, while inquiries were ordered into the role of health department officials and irregularities in medico-legal procedures.

The government thus moved towards implementing the commission’s recommendations, with the JIT tasked with establishing the circumstances of Raza’s murder and identifying those responsible.

headline: Govt slashes petrol by Rs7.06, diesel by Rs3.71 for Nov 5
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs362 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs387.81 under daily price mechanism
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government on Wednesday slashed the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.71 per litre for November 5.

According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs362 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs387.81 per litre for Thursday.

The latest revision comes a day after the government reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of HSD by Rs3.68 for November 4.

On Monday, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.

Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.

Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.

Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

headline: US Vice President Vance says Iran war is ‘the reason we lost’ midterms
description: Democratic wave raises doubts over his status as frontrunner for Republican nomination in 2028 presidential election
author: AFP
article_text:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance said in a lengthy post on X — apparently referring to President Donald Trump’s remarks that the Iran war was “part of it” but that it was still justified.

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest,” added Vance.

“But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

The Democratic wave in Tuesday’s midterms has raised major questions over Vance’s previous status as the frontrunner for the Republican nomination in the 2028 presidential election.

He has not yet formally declared that he will run.

Vance, a longtime vocal critic of US foreign interventionism, had reportedly been sceptical behind the scenes about the war on Iran that Trump and Israel launched in late February.

Vance also acknowledged that Republican voters who backed Trump and himself two years ago had switched sides due to the war and its effects on the US economy.

“The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026,” Vance said.

He said a pollster that he respected showed the Iran war and the economy were key factors in voters abandoning Republicans, along with a desire to “change our relationship to Israel”.

Meanwhile, top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said the Iran war “must end” and suggested his party’s incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.

“This war must end. It must end,” Schumer told journalists, later noting that the “power of the purse” is “one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people”.

White House insists Trump is ‘still your president’ after midterm rout

Donald Trump is “still your president”, the White House said on Wednesday, a day after his Republican Party suffered sweeping losses in midterm elections seen as a referendum on his second term.

The White House delivered the message in a post on X featuring a picture of a glaring Trump looming over the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.

“PSA: TRUMP IS STILL YOUR PRESIDENT,” text superimposed on the image said, using the abbreviation for public service announcement.

“Thank you for your attention to this matter,” the post added, using a phrase Trump frequently employs in his social media messages.

Opposition Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday, dealing a major blow to Trump and the Republican Party.

headline: Harry Potter store opening in London draws trans rights protesters amid JK Rowling controversy
description: Protesters assembled outside the store holding placards reading “Protect trans lives” and “stop funding trans erasure”
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The opening of London's new Harry Potter flagship store on Oxford Street was met with a protest by transgender rights supporters on Wednesday, November 4, as demonstrators gathered outside to challenge the franchise's association with author JK Rowling.

Around 16 protesters assembled outside the store, holding placards reading “Protect trans lives” and “Stop funding trans erasure”. They also used megaphones to chant “Trans rights are human rights” and called on fans waiting to enter the shop to reconsider supporting the franchise.

The demonstration was linked to the ongoing controversy surrounding Rowling's views on transgender rights and her financial support for organisations campaigning against aspects of trans-inclusive policies.

One protester, speaking to Variety, said they wanted to ensure transgender people had their voices heard during the store's opening. They argued that Rowling's influence on public discussions about transgender rights made it important for demonstrators to be present.

Despite the protest, the queue of Harry Potter fans continued entering the store, with the line reportedly stretching around the block. The demonstration was largely peaceful, while security personnel helped manage the crowds.

A spokesperson for the Harry Potter Shop said the business was pleased to welcome hundreds of fans and supported people's right to express their personal viewpoints peacefully.

The new flagship is located at The Ribbon, 134-140 Oxford Street, and spans more than 21,000 square feet across two floors. Inspired by Diagon Alley, it features a full-sized Knight Bus, a Ukrainian Ironbelly dragon installation, a recreation of the Leaky Cauldron and a themed food and beverage experience offering Butterbeer.

Actor Tom Felton, who portrayed Draco Malfoy in the film franchise, was among the first visitors to explore the store ahead of its public opening. He praised the attention to detail and said the setting reminded him of the original film sets.

The protest adds to the continuing debate around the Harry Potter franchise's relationship with its creator. Rowling has faced criticism from transgender rights advocates over her public comments on gender identity and her support for campaigns opposing certain transgender-inclusive policies. She has denied being transphobic.

The controversy has also extended to other Harry Potter events and productions, including the upcoming HBO television adaptation, on which Rowling serves as an executive producer.

The Oxford Street demonstration highlights how disagreements over Rowling's views continue to follow the franchise, even as its commercial attractions draw fans.

headline: Opp forms APC committees, vows countrywide movement against govt after huddle
description: Achakzai, Abbas and PTI leaders with JUI-F chief discuss constitutional supremacy, democratic rights amid K-P crisis
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Opposition parties on Wednesday announced the formation of committees to organise an All Parties Conference (APC) and resolve differences among political groups, while vowing to launch a countrywide movement against what they described as an undemocratic government.

The announcement was made after an opposition meeting at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, where leaders also condemned what they called a campaign of character assassination against the JUI-F chief and criticised the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

“The committee comprises Salman Akram Raja, Kamran Murtaza, Mustafa Khokhar, Aamir Dogar, Nasir Shirazi and Mohammad Aslam Ghauri,” Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) Vice Chairman Allama Raja Nasir Abbas announced at a press conference at Fazl's residence.

He said a separate subcommittee would work to resolve differences among the parties and explore ways for them to work together in the future. He announced that Sallahuddin Ayubi, Akhunzada Hussain and Khalid Yousaf would serve as its coordinators.

Abbas said the APC would be held within a week to 10 days, with a committee tasked with consulting political parties, finalising the agenda and announcing the date.

Speaking at the presser, TTAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai said the gathering had been convened to condemn the government's attacks on Maulana Fazl and express solidarity with him.

“The way the government is targeting Maulana Fazlur Rehman is condemnable. We have come here to express our solidarity with him,” he said.

“We clearly declare that this approach will not work. If someone speaks the truth and points out your wrongdoings, such behaviour will not only pollute the political arena but could also lead to extremely dangerous consequences,” he warned.

Achakzai said a committee had been formed to arrange the APC, which was expected to be held this month, adding that another committee would work to address differences and reservations between the PTI and the JUI-F and improve relations between the two parties.

He said the opposition would launch a movement across the country against what he termed as an “undemocratic government”.

Criticising the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P, Achakzai said the measures amounted to an insult to the mandate of the province's 40 million people.

“Do not provoke us or launch unjustified attacks against us. God forbid, if an incident takes place as a result, it may become difficult for everyone to handle the consequences,” he warned.

Fazl, addressing the press conference, thanked the opposition leaders for attending the meeting and said the participants had held serious consultations on the country's political situation.

“It has been agreed that this consultation process will continue. A committee has been formed for the All Parties Conference, while a subcommittee has also been established to address any mutual reservations,” he said.

He said the opposition had consistently raised concerns over governor's rule, the imposition of emergency and what he described as attempts to take control of mineral resources.

“We have represented the nation on these issues. We have spoken for the people's trust, and we will play our role in protecting it,” he said.

Fazl alleged that provincial rights and resources were being taken away under various pretexts. Referring to Balochistan, he said attempts were being made to bring profitable coastal areas, including Gwadar, under federal control.

He also referred to discussions about placing islands in Sindh under federal control.

He said the rights granted to provinces and their people under the 18th Amendment were now under threat.

Referring to the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with K-P, he said his party had expressed reservations at the time, arguing that the province was not prepared to absorb the region.

He said the factors behind the earlier move had been political, while the current developments appeared to be driven by control over resources.

“We have reservations about these contradictory policies and strategies. We have presented our concerns with full arguments,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said the opposition was raising national issues through political discourse, but the government was targeting individuals instead of addressing the concerns.

He referred to what he described as attempts to divert public attention towards matters such as the installation of a generator, construction of a cabin and the location of a kitchen at his residence.

“These things are laughable. Through such absurdities, they are diverting the public's attention elsewhere,” he said.

Fazl said his party would not be distracted by such matters and would continue to protect national resources and provincial rights.

“We will neither allow any international institution to plunder our country's assets nor permit Pakistan's own institutions to deprive the people of their rights,” he said.

He alleged that votes were stolen during elections and resources were plundered after governments were formed, saying such practices were contrary to democracy, the Constitution and Shariah.

Responding to a question about the federal government's position on provincial autonomy and the creation of new provinces, Fazl said the centre was particularly concerned about two issues: the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award and mineral resources.

“This has always been our clear stance. You have heard us say that the federal government is currently troubled by two things: the NFC Award and mineral resources,” he said.

He added that his party had raised the issues at public gatherings even before the recent measures, saying the developments had now made its concerns evident.

Questioning the purpose behind calls for creating new provinces, JUI-F chief said granting financial powers to district governments could turn them into rivals of provincial administrations.

“Establishing district governments and granting them financial powers means setting provincial institutions against the provincial government,” he said.

Drawing a comparison with the establishment, he said that an institution which was supposed to be subordinate to the government had become more powerful than it.

“All these measures amount to destroying the country's system. We, however, want a balance within the system in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he said.

Opposition leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also criticised the government's actions, alleging that the country was being run in an unconstitutional manner and that the rule of law had disappeared.

“Lawlessness, oppression and unconstitutional measures are increasing by the day, while the sanctity of homes is being violated,” he said.

He alleged that the government had undermined the electoral process, damaged the Constitution and attacked the independence of the judiciary before moving against people's homes and, subsequently, the mandate of K-P.

“By imposing emergency and governor's rule in the province, the government has sent a message to the people that their mandate has no value,” he said.

Abbas said a country could not function when institutions ceased to exist, and individuals took control of the system. He warned that public confidence in the system was essential for the country's stability.

He also condemned what he described as a campaign of character assassination against Maulana Fazl after the JUI-F chief criticised the government's policies, governor's rule and emergency in K-P.

“Whether this happens to Nawaz Sharif, Shehbaz Sharif or even our enemy, it is wrong and condemnable. This is a bad tradition,” he said.

“Today you are entering our homes; tomorrow people may enter yours. Remember, you reap what you sow,” he added.

Opposition huddle at Fazl's residence

Earlier, opposition parties gathered at Fazl's residence to discuss the prevailing political situation, including the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).

The JUI-F media cell confirmed that it was a meeting of the "united opposition". The Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) also confirmed the development.

Those attending the meeting included Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and National Assembly Chief Whip Aamir Dogar.

Other participants included Senator Noor-ul-Haq Qadri, Senator Kamran Murtaza, former K-P chief minister Akram Khan Durrani, JUI-F leaders Hafiz Hamdullah, Maulana Attaur Rehman and Maulana Attaul Haq Darvesh, and Senator Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi.

The meeting discussed unity among opposition parties, supremacy of the Constitution and the law, protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the prevailing political situation and the opposition's future course of action.

Other participants included Pashtun Tahaffuz Movement (PTM) spokesperson Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai, PTI core committee member and legal counsel to Imran Khan Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, Agha Nasir Shirazi, Akhunzada Hussain, Zahir Durrani and Aslam Ghauri.

On October 11, governor's rule and an emergency were imposed in K-P, transferring executive authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government to the governor. An 11-member advisory council was formed to assist him in overseeing provincial administrative affairs.

The federal government also established a separate administrative structure for 12 districts, including an area representative and a development council to facilitate local representation and development planning.

The latest gathering is the first joint meeting of opposition parties to formulate a response to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, with both Fazl and Achakzai in attendance.

Following the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule, Fazl accused the government of backing out of negotiations with the PTI and the opposition despite initially agreeing to their demands.

He categorically rejected the imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in K-P, saying that if an emergency had to be imposed, it should be imposed on the federal government, which he described as illegitimate.

The criticism subsequently spilled over into the assembly, escalating the war of words between the government and the JUI-F chief. Fazl had accused the government of misusing the Constitution.

Federal ministers hit back, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi criticised Fazl over his opposition to governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

Later, a delegation of the PTI and TTAP expressed full support for the JUI-F chief's speech in the National Assembly and condemned what it described as his character assassination by government ministers following his strong criticism of the government's actions.

“The committee comprises Salman Akram Raja, Kamran Murtaza, Mustafa Khokhar, Aamir Dogar, Nasir Shirazi and Mohammad Aslam Ghauri,” Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) Vice Chairman Allama Raja Nasir Abbas announced at a press conference at Fazl's residence.

He said a separate subcommittee would work to resolve differences among the parties and explore ways for them to work together in the future. He announced that Sallahuddin Ayubi, Akhunzada Hussain and Khalid Yousaf would serve as its coordinators.

 Abbas said the APC would be held within a week to 10 days, with a committee tasked with consulting political parties, finalising the agenda and announcing the date.

Speaking at the presser, TTAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai said the gathering had been convened to condemn the government's attacks on Maulana Fazl and express solidarity with him.

“The way the government is targeting Maulana Fazlur Rehman is condemnable. We have come here to express our solidarity with him,” he said.

“We clearly declare that this approach will not work. If someone speaks the truth and points out your wrongdoings, such behaviour will not only pollute the political arena but could also lead to extremely dangerous consequences,” he warned.

Achakzai said a committee had been formed to arrange the APC, which was expected to be held this month, adding that another committee would work to address differences and reservations between the PTI and the JUI-F and improve relations between the two parties.

He said the opposition would launch a movement across the country against what he termed as an “undemocratic government”.

Criticising the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P, Achakzai said the measures amounted to an insult to the mandate of the province's 40 million people.

“Do not provoke us or launch unjustified attacks against us. God forbid, if an incident takes place as a result, it may become difficult for everyone to handle the consequences,” he warned.

Fazl, addressing the press conference, thanked the opposition leaders for attending the meeting and said the participants had held serious consultations on the country's political situation.

“It has been agreed that this consultation process will continue. A committee has been formed for the All Parties Conference, while a subcommittee has also been established to address any mutual reservations,” he said.

He said the opposition had consistently raised concerns over governor's rule, the imposition of emergency and what he described as attempts to take control of mineral resources.

“We have represented the nation on these issues. We have spoken for the people's trust, and we will play our role in protecting it,” he said.

Fazl alleged that provincial rights and resources were being taken away under various pretexts. Referring to Balochistan, he said attempts were being made to bring profitable coastal areas, including Gwadar, under federal control.

He also referred to discussions about placing islands in Sindh under federal control.

He said the rights granted to provinces and their people under the 18th Amendment were now under threat.

Referring to the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with K-P, he said his party had expressed reservations at the time, arguing that the province was not prepared to absorb the region.

The JUI-F chief said the opposition was raising national issues through political discourse, but the government was targeting individuals instead of addressing the concerns.

He referred to what he described as attempts to divert public attention towards matters such as the installation of a generator, construction of a cabin and the location of a kitchen at his residence.

“These things are laughable. Through such absurdities, they are diverting the public's attention elsewhere,” he said.

Fazl said his party would not be distracted by such matters and would continue to protect national resources and provincial rights.

“We will neither allow any international institution to plunder our country's assets nor permit Pakistan's own institutions to deprive the people of their rights,” he said.

He alleged that votes were stolen during elections and resources were plundered after governments were formed, saying such practices were contrary to democracy, the Constitution and Shariah.

Responding to a question about the federal government's position on provincial autonomy and the creation of new provinces, Fazl said the centre was particularly concerned about two issues: the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award and mineral resources.

“This has always been our clear stance. You have heard us say that the federal government is currently troubled by two things: the NFC Award and mineral resources,” he said.

He added that his party had raised the issues at public gatherings even before the recent measures, saying the developments had now made its concerns evident.

Questioning the purpose behind calls for creating new provinces, JUI-F chief said granting financial powers to district governments could turn them into rivals of provincial administrations.

“Establishing district governments and granting them financial powers means setting provincial institutions against the provincial government,” he said.

Drawing a comparison with the establishment, he said that an institution which was supposed to be subordinate to the government had become more powerful than it.

“All these measures amount to destroying the country's system. We, however, want a balance within the system in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he said.

Opposition leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also criticised the government's actions, alleging that the country was being run in an unconstitutional manner and that the rule of law had disappeared.

“Lawlessness, oppression and unconstitutional measures are increasing by the day, while the sanctity of homes is being violated,” he said.

He alleged that the government had undermined the electoral process, damaged the Constitution and attacked the independence of the judiciary before moving against people's homes and, subsequently, the mandate of K-P.

“By imposing emergency and governor's rule in the province, the government has sent a message to the people that their mandate has no value,” he said.

 Abbas said a country could not function when institutions ceased to exist, and individuals took control of the system. He warned that public confidence in the system was essential for the country's stability.

He also condemned what he described as a campaign of character assassination against Maulana Fazl after the JUI-F chief criticised the government's policies, governor's rule and emergency in K-P.

“Whether this happens to Nawaz Sharif, Shehbaz Sharif or even our enemy, it is wrong and condemnable. This is a bad tradition,” he said.

“Today you are entering our homes; tomorrow people may enter yours. Remember, you reap what you sow,” he added.

Opposition huddle at Fazl's residence

Earlier, opposition parties gathered at Fazl's residence to discuss the prevailing political situation, including the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).

The JUI-F media cell confirmed that it was a meeting of the "united opposition". The Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) also confirmed the development.

Those attending the meeting included Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and National Assembly Chief Whip Aamir Dogar.

Read: PTI, TTAP affirm 'full support' for Fazl after govt hammering in Parliament

Other participants included Senator Noor-ul-Haq Qadri, Senator Kamran Murtaza, former K-P chief minister Akram Khan Durrani, JUI-F leaders Hafiz Hamdullah, Maulana Attaur Rehman and Maulana Attaul Haq Darvesh, and Senator Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi.

The meeting discussed unity among opposition parties, supremacy of the Constitution and the law, protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the prevailing political situation and the opposition's future course of action.

Other participants included Pashtun Tahaffuz Movement (PTM) spokesperson Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai, PTI core committee member and legal counsel to Imran Khan Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, Agha Nasir Shirazi, Akhunzada Hussain, Zahir Durrani and Aslam Ghauri.

On October 11, governor's rule and an emergency were imposed in K-P, transferring executive authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government to the governor. An 11-member advisory council was formed to assist him in overseeing provincial administrative affairs.

The federal government also established a separate administrative structure for 12 districts, including an area representative and a development council to facilitate local representation and development planning.

Also Read: Opposition unites against governor's rule in K-P

The latest gathering is the first joint meeting of opposition parties to formulate a response to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, with both Fazl and Achakzai in attendance.

Following the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule, Fazl accused the government of backing out of negotiations with the PTI and the opposition despite initially agreeing to their demands.

He categorically rejected the imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in K-P, saying that if an emergency had to be imposed, it should be imposed on the federal government, which he described as illegitimate.

The criticism subsequently spilled over into the assembly, escalating the war of words between the government and the JUI-F chief. Fazl had accused the government of misusing the Constitution.

Federal ministers hit back, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi criticised Fazl over his opposition to governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

Later, a delegation of the PTI and TTAP expressed full support for the JUI-F chief's speech in the National Assembly and condemned what it described as his character assassination by government ministers following his strong criticism of the government's actions.
