Opposition parties on Wednesday announced the formation of committees to organise an All Parties Conference (APC) and resolve differences among political groups, while vowing to launch a countrywide movement against what they described as an undemocratic government.

The announcement was made after an opposition meeting at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, where leaders also condemned what they called a campaign of character assassination against the JUI-F chief and criticised the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

“The committee comprises Salman Akram Raja, Kamran Murtaza, Mustafa Khokhar, Aamir Dogar, Nasir Shirazi and Mohammad Aslam Ghauri,” Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) Vice Chairman Allama Raja Nasir Abbas announced at a press conference at Fazl's residence.

He said a separate subcommittee would work to resolve differences among the parties and explore ways for them to work together in the future. He announced that Sallahuddin Ayubi, Akhunzada Hussain and Khalid Yousaf would serve as its coordinators.

Abbas said the APC would be held within a week to 10 days, with a committee tasked with consulting political parties, finalising the agenda and announcing the date.

Speaking at the presser, TTAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai said the gathering had been convened to condemn the government's attacks on Maulana Fazl and express solidarity with him.

“The way the government is targeting Maulana Fazlur Rehman is condemnable. We have come here to express our solidarity with him,” he said.

“We clearly declare that this approach will not work. If someone speaks the truth and points out your wrongdoings, such behaviour will not only pollute the political arena but could also lead to extremely dangerous consequences,” he warned.

Achakzai said a committee had been formed to arrange the APC, which was expected to be held this month, adding that another committee would work to address differences and reservations between the PTI and the JUI-F and improve relations between the two parties.

He said the opposition would launch a movement across the country against what he termed as an “undemocratic government”.

Criticising the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P, Achakzai said the measures amounted to an insult to the mandate of the province's 40 million people.

“Do not provoke us or launch unjustified attacks against us. God forbid, if an incident takes place as a result, it may become difficult for everyone to handle the consequences,” he warned.

Fazl, addressing the press conference, thanked the opposition leaders for attending the meeting and said the participants had held serious consultations on the country's political situation.

“It has been agreed that this consultation process will continue. A committee has been formed for the All Parties Conference, while a subcommittee has also been established to address any mutual reservations,” he said.

He said the opposition had consistently raised concerns over governor's rule, the imposition of emergency and what he described as attempts to take control of mineral resources.

“We have represented the nation on these issues. We have spoken for the people's trust, and we will play our role in protecting it,” he said.

Fazl alleged that provincial rights and resources were being taken away under various pretexts. Referring to Balochistan, he said attempts were being made to bring profitable coastal areas, including Gwadar, under federal control.

He also referred to discussions about placing islands in Sindh under federal control.

He said the rights granted to provinces and their people under the 18th Amendment were now under threat.

Referring to the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with K-P, he said his party had expressed reservations at the time, arguing that the province was not prepared to absorb the region.

He said the factors behind the earlier move had been political, while the current developments appeared to be driven by control over resources.

“We have reservations about these contradictory policies and strategies. We have presented our concerns with full arguments,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said the opposition was raising national issues through political discourse, but the government was targeting individuals instead of addressing the concerns.

He referred to what he described as attempts to divert public attention towards matters such as the installation of a generator, construction of a cabin and the location of a kitchen at his residence.

“These things are laughable. Through such absurdities, they are diverting the public's attention elsewhere,” he said.

Fazl said his party would not be distracted by such matters and would continue to protect national resources and provincial rights.

“We will neither allow any international institution to plunder our country's assets nor permit Pakistan's own institutions to deprive the people of their rights,” he said.

He alleged that votes were stolen during elections and resources were plundered after governments were formed, saying such practices were contrary to democracy, the Constitution and Shariah.

Responding to a question about the federal government's position on provincial autonomy and the creation of new provinces, Fazl said the centre was particularly concerned about two issues: the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award and mineral resources.

“This has always been our clear stance. You have heard us say that the federal government is currently troubled by two things: the NFC Award and mineral resources,” he said.

He added that his party had raised the issues at public gatherings even before the recent measures, saying the developments had now made its concerns evident.

Questioning the purpose behind calls for creating new provinces, JUI-F chief said granting financial powers to district governments could turn them into rivals of provincial administrations.

“Establishing district governments and granting them financial powers means setting provincial institutions against the provincial government,” he said.

Drawing a comparison with the establishment, he said that an institution which was supposed to be subordinate to the government had become more powerful than it.

“All these measures amount to destroying the country's system. We, however, want a balance within the system in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he said.

Opposition leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also criticised the government's actions, alleging that the country was being run in an unconstitutional manner and that the rule of law had disappeared.

“Lawlessness, oppression and unconstitutional measures are increasing by the day, while the sanctity of homes is being violated,” he said.

He alleged that the government had undermined the electoral process, damaged the Constitution and attacked the independence of the judiciary before moving against people's homes and, subsequently, the mandate of K-P.

“By imposing emergency and governor's rule in the province, the government has sent a message to the people that their mandate has no value,” he said.

Abbas said a country could not function when institutions ceased to exist, and individuals took control of the system. He warned that public confidence in the system was essential for the country's stability.

He also condemned what he described as a campaign of character assassination against Maulana Fazl after the JUI-F chief criticised the government's policies, governor's rule and emergency in K-P.

“Whether this happens to Nawaz Sharif, Shehbaz Sharif or even our enemy, it is wrong and condemnable. This is a bad tradition,” he said.

“Today you are entering our homes; tomorrow people may enter yours. Remember, you reap what you sow,” he added.

Opposition huddle at Fazl's residence

Earlier, opposition parties gathered at Fazl's residence to discuss the prevailing political situation, including the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).

The JUI-F media cell confirmed that it was a meeting of the "united opposition". The Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) also confirmed the development.

Those attending the meeting included Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and National Assembly Chief Whip Aamir Dogar.

Other participants included Senator Noor-ul-Haq Qadri, Senator Kamran Murtaza, former K-P chief minister Akram Khan Durrani, JUI-F leaders Hafiz Hamdullah, Maulana Attaur Rehman and Maulana Attaul Haq Darvesh, and Senator Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi.

The meeting discussed unity among opposition parties, supremacy of the Constitution and the law, protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the prevailing political situation and the opposition's future course of action.

Other participants included Pashtun Tahaffuz Movement (PTM) spokesperson Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai, PTI core committee member and legal counsel to Imran Khan Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, Agha Nasir Shirazi, Akhunzada Hussain, Zahir Durrani and Aslam Ghauri.

On October 11, governor's rule and an emergency were imposed in K-P, transferring executive authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government to the governor. An 11-member advisory council was formed to assist him in overseeing provincial administrative affairs.

The federal government also established a separate administrative structure for 12 districts, including an area representative and a development council to facilitate local representation and development planning.

The latest gathering is the first joint meeting of opposition parties to formulate a response to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, with both Fazl and Achakzai in attendance.

Following the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule, Fazl accused the government of backing out of negotiations with the PTI and the opposition despite initially agreeing to their demands.

He categorically rejected the imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in K-P, saying that if an emergency had to be imposed, it should be imposed on the federal government, which he described as illegitimate.

The criticism subsequently spilled over into the assembly, escalating the war of words between the government and the JUI-F chief. Fazl had accused the government of misusing the Constitution.

Federal ministers hit back, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi criticised Fazl over his opposition to governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

Later, a delegation of the PTI and TTAP expressed full support for the JUI-F chief's speech in the National Assembly and condemned what it described as his character assassination by government ministers following his strong criticism of the government's actions.

headline: KATSEYE apologise to fans after postponing Detroit concert at last minute
description: The announcement came as concertgoers were already inside Little Caesars Arena, with others still making their way
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
KATSEYE have apologised to fans after postponing their Detroit concert shortly before they were due to take the stage, revealing that member Megan Skiendiel had fallen ill and was unable to perform.

The group's November 3 show at Little Caesars Arena was called off around 30 minutes before its scheduled start time, leaving fans who had already arrived at the venue disappointed.

In a statement shared on Instagram Stories, KATSEYE explained that Megan was unwell and needed time to recover.

“We're so sorry to share that tonight's show at Little Caesars Arena has been postponed due to illness,” the group wrote. “Unfortunately, Megan is unwell and unable to perform tonight, and we want to make sure she has the time she needs to rest and recover.”

The members also acknowledged that many fans had travelled to Detroit and made arrangements to attend the concert.

“We know so many of you have travelled, made plans, and been looking forward to tonight,” they continued. “We are incredibly disappointed that we won't get to see you, and we're truly sorry for the inconvenience.”

The group concluded by thanking supporters for their patience and understanding, adding that they loved their fans and looked forward to seeing them soon.

The announcement came as concertgoers were already inside Little Caesars Arena, with others still making their way to the venue. Videos shared on social media showed the postponement announcement displayed on the arena's screens.

The venue also issued an apology, asking ticket holders to keep their existing tickets, which will be valid for the rescheduled date once it is announced. Fans are expected to receive further information by email.

The last-minute decision prompted mixed reactions online. While some fans expressed frustration over the disruption and the money spent on travel and accommodation, others defended the group, pointing out that performers should be given time to recover when they are unwell.

The Detroit concert was part of KATSEYE's Wildworld Tour, which began in September and includes the group's first arena performances. The North American leg is scheduled to continue through November 28, with Mexico City marking the final stop of the run.

KATSEYE are currently performing with four members, as Sophia Laforteza and Manon Bannerman are both on hiatus. Sophia is expected to return in January 2027, while no confirmed return date has been announced for Manon.

“We're so sorry to share that tonight's show at Little Caesars Arena has been postponed due to illness,” the group wrote. “Unfortunately, Megan is unwell and unable to perform tonight, and we want to make sure she has the time she needs to rest and recover.”

The members also acknowledged that many fans had travelled to Detroit and made arrangements to attend the concert.

“We know so many of you have travelled, made plans, and been looking forward to tonight,” they continued. “We are incredibly disappointed that we won't get to see you, and we're truly sorry for the inconvenience.”

headline: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ stars McKenna Grace, Joseph Zada react to fans shipping them IRL
description: Zada described Grace as his younger, younger sister while the Maysillee Donner actress said Joe’s like family
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping stars McKenna Grace and Joseph Zada have shared their reactions to fans hoping their on-screen connection will turn into a real-life romance.

During an interview with Refinery29 Australia, the actors were asked about being shipped by fans because of their characters, Maysilee Donner and Haymitch Abernathy, in the upcoming prequel.

“Yeah, it’s pretty weird,” Zada responded with a smile, pointing out that both actors already have partners.

The 20-year-old actor also described Grace as his “younger, younger sister”, prompting his co-star to jokingly challenge the description. “Younger? Definitely not,” she replied.

View this post on Instagram

Grace, who is dating her Regretting You co-star Mason Thames, said she understands that fan shipping is part of being involved in a major franchise.

“Joe’s like family,” the actress explained. She added that the internet allows people to ship whichever characters or individuals they want, as long as it does not intrude on anyone's personal life.

The pair also had fun suggesting alternative pairings involving their fellow cast members. Zada revealed that he had been shipped with Ben Wang, who plays District 12 tribute Wyatt Callow, adding that he could understand the pairing.

Grace agreed, saying her favourite ship was Ben and Joe. Zada then suggested that Grace could be paired with Laura Marcus, who plays District 1 tribute Silka Sharp.

However, Grace had another pairing in mind. Referring to her character Maysilee and Whitney Peak's Lenore Dove, she said: “I like Maydove. I'm coming for your girl.”

Grace has also previously discussed the intensity of joining the Hunger Games franchise and received advice from original cast member Josh Hutcherson, who played Peeta Mellark in the original films.

The actress revealed that she spoke to Hutcherson while they were working together on Five Nights at Freddy's 2, asking about his experience filming the franchise's arena sequences.

“I spent a lot of time asking him, ‘Was your arena experience as intense as ours was?’ And he was like, ‘Oh yeah, yeah it was,’” she told E! News at the Coach Fall 2026 show in February.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the events of the original film series and follows a young Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games.

Directed by Francis Lawrence, the film also stars Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Jesse Plemons and Maya Hawke. It is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

headline: Revenge vote
description: Revenge vote
author: Imran.Jan
article_text:
When Kamala was running against Trump in 2024, she had more money at her disposal than Trump in order to reach the American voters. Money usually determines the result of an election but sometimes people get fed up and reject all the noise and line up to support anything that fights against the side they hate.

At least that is how I voted back in 2024 when I voted for Trump. It is not that I liked him. But I just wanted to punish the one guy or rather girl who had blindly supported Israel in its genocide against the Palestinians. And I was sickened by Biden's interference in other countries' politics as well. The American people struggled with paying their bills. Living a decent life became a challenge. The credit card debt rose over a trillion dollars. All on Biden's watch. The people had to punish that. Those days are over when people used to vote for the guy they liked. It is the age of revenge voting. I have voted twice in my entire life. And both times, it was a textbook revenge vote.

My second vote was in this Midterm election in the US that just happened and results are coming in as I am writing this piece. But with the results already in, the nation is experiencing what is quickly becoming a social media trend titled Blue Tsunami, meaning the Democrats are winning across many states. Kansas flipped blue after 94 years, which is mind boggling. Texas also flipped blue after more than 3 decades. I voted for the Democrats. Not because I truly admired James Talarico. I didn't even know most people on the ballot but I voted for all Democrats. Every tap on the screen felt like a deliberate act of defiance against Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the rest of the company.

Trump did not learn from how he won from Kamala in 2024. Like I mentioned, she had more money in her campaign than Trump did. This time around, Elon Musk spent close to half a billion dollars to support the Republicans. They faced a shameful loss. It was a slap in the face of Elon Musk by the American people. With money, a lot more noise can be made than those with less money. One can become more famous and more well known. But it doesn't necessarily mean that one would also become more popular. The Indian actor Amresh Puri was as famous as Amitabh Bachchan because they almost always were in the same movie. But Amresh wasn't popular at all. Actually, people hated him and wanted him dead in every movie.

I am personally moved by the outcome of this election because for many months it always felt like even in America, corruption ruled and power always won. As if money always defeated genuineness. Elon Musk and his close alliance of convenience with Trump made many Americans lose faith in the political system because truth, merit and honesty didn't matter.

Tesla reported zero federal income tax. SpaceX gets massive government contracts. Musk's companies wouldn't even be profitable without US government subsidies as many experts point out. All this and many other aspects of massive corruption at the highest echelons of power inside the United States left many of us hopeless and angry. Musk gave $190 million directly to the Super PAC of Ken Paxton because Paxton has regulatory oversight powers over businesses in Texas, including Musk's companies in Texas. While Musk cut funding to education and research through DOGE, he had half a billion to spend for propaganda. The fact that this repulsive liar would have to lawyer up or suck up to Trump for a pardon clearly shows that the American system still has hope. When enough people unite around a cause, they can defeat any amount of money and power. And that is what we saw in America tonight.

Tonight it is the abusers that are feeling abused. I will take that anyday.

headline: Blue Tsunami
description: Blue Tsunami
author: editorial
article_text:
It is blue all over the United States. The Reds have taken a backseat in the House of Representatives and the Senate, pushing the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency into a lame-duck phase. The midterms, indeed, were a Waterloo for Trumpism, as well as a rebuke of the White House incumbent's stewardship. The people voted on issues, squarely reflecting their anger over an escalating cost of living, unprecedented tariffs, and, of course, an undesired war against Iran. In other words, the vote was to curb the President's powers and his impulsive hire-and-fire culture, handing the GOP its worst setback in decades. The backlash was evident from the fact that the Republicans were routed in their strongholds among Black men and Hispanics, and returned the nation's first Muslim senator in Michigan.

In an immediate rejoinder from Iran, Speaker Baqer Qalibaf said, "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said 'No to War', and we endorse this message." With Democrats now controlling the bicameral Congress, Trump will have to wait and watch for reprisals. The landslide grants the Democrats the power to block any legislation and, moreover, initiate investigations into Trump's alleged corruption. Likewise, it will no longer be a piece of cake for Trump to maneuver his favourites into the administration and judiciary, or push for more combat operations in the Middle East for the sake of appeasing the Jewish state.

The election verdict has revealed a fascinating political mosaic. Democrats won in swing states like Georgia, Michigan, New Hampshire and North Carolina, as well as in traditional Republican strongholds such as Iowa, Kansas, Texas, and even South Carolina. Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman anywhere in the country to be elected governor, while in Texas, Gina Hinojosa made history as the state's first Latina governor. Abdul El-Sayed's success confirmed a sweeping wave of anti-incumbency in the decisive state of Michigan. Trump's agenda of penalising allies with tariffs, snubbing NATO protocols and entangling Arab states in a devastating war of survival was rejected with vehement distaste at the polls.

headline: Digital potential
description: Digital potential
author: editorial
article_text:
Pakistan's growing appetite for social media presents an enormous economic opportunity, particularly at a time when unemployment and limited avenues for income generation continue to weigh on the country's youth. Digital platforms have evolved beyond entertainment and communication into important spaces for entrepreneurship and commerce. Content creation and online businesses are opening up new avenues for earning, allowing individuals to reach audiences and markets that were previously beyond their means.

According to PTA, TikTok has around 100 million users in Pakistan, while 96 million people use YouTube, generating approximately 560 million video views daily. With the right policies and investment, Pakistan has the potential to turn its expanding digital audience into a significant contributor to economic growth. However, a large audience alone is insufficient to build a sustainable digital economy. Greater access to monetisation programmes and digital payment facilities is equally necessary to help creators turn their reach into reliable earnings. Despite this promise, Pakistan's inadequate internet infrastructure continues to restrict the growth of its digital economy. Frequent disruptions and sluggish speeds have become persistent obstacles for individuals and businesses dependent on online platforms. The government's emphasis on expanding 5G services is welcome, but technological advancement must not come at the expense of improving existing networks. A country where many rural communities struggle with basic connectivity cannot afford to prioritise headline achievements over dependable service.

The authorities must accelerate fibre-optic expansion and strengthen network capacity. Equally important is ensuring that internet restrictions and disruptions do not undermine investor confidence or jeopardise the livelihoods of those working in the digital economy. Pakistan has the audience, creativity and entrepreneurial talent to develop a thriving digital content industry. What it needs is a policy environment that encourages this.

A country where many rural communities struggle with basic connectivity cannot afford to prioritise headline achievements over dependable service.

The authorities must accelerate fibre-optic expansion and strengthen network capacity. Equally important is ensuring that internet restrictions and disruptions do not undermine investor confidence or jeopardise the livelihoods of those working in the digital economy. Pakistan has the audience, creativity and entrepreneurial talent to develop a thriving digital content industry. What it needs is a policy environment that encourages this.

headline: A warning written in ice
description: A warning written in ice
author: editorial
article_text:
The UN's latest cryosphere reports are concerning for any reader, but especially those of us who worry about Pakistan's water, food and security.

Two UN-backed reports warn that overshooting 1.5°C of warming will bring "large-scale and in many cases irreversible impacts" for glaciers, sea ice, permafrost and polar oceans. Warming has already reached 1.37°C, and the 1.5°C threshold could be crossed around 2030. Scientists now believe a truly safe temperature for the Earth's ice is closer to 1°C - meaning even the Paris target is too weak for the cryosphere.

The stakes could not be higher for Pakistan. We have more than 13,000 glaciers, over 3,000 glacial lakes and 33 lakes officially deemed dangerous. The country has recorded about 131 glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), and 7.1 million people in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa live with the risk. These glaciers feed the Indus, irrigate the fields and generate hydropower; their accelerated retreat is already increasing floods, landslides and water insecurity.

The reports' central warning and key takeaway is that "every extra fraction of a degree and every year spent in overshoot means more devastating impacts." Pakistan can't fix global warming on its own. As is often stated, the country already has a very small pollution footprint relative to its total population. But it can and should take every feasible effort to mitigate the effects of global warming, starting with better water management, including glacier management. Adaptation must be preemptive, rather than reactive.

The loss of glaciers is a national security threat, and Pakistan needs to demand that the parties responsible for endangering its security take remedial measures. At the upcoming COP31 in Antalya, Pakistan must demand serious climate finance and deep global emissions cuts. Meanwhile, the government must put our own house in order by crafting a credible national cryosphere plan and improving collaboration or even integration among SUPARCO, NDMA, the PMD and provincial authorities.

headline: When words speak and silence echoes
description: When words speak and silence echoes
author: Dr Intikhab Ulfat
article_text:
Physics explains that sound originates in vibrations, light travels as electromagnetic radiation, and fragrance spreads through molecular motion. Yet literature transforms these familiar phenomena into something profoundly different. In poetry, silence becomes louder than speech, light illuminates the heart rather than the eye, and fragrance awakens forgotten memories. Reading Naina Adil's poetry reminds me of something our education system frequently overlooks: imagination is not the opposite of scientific understanding. It is often the beginning of it.

Having spent decades teaching physics, I have encountered students who could reproduce complicated equations but struggled to explain the physical phenomena behind them. They knew the mathematical expression for resonance without appreciating why a bridge vibrates or how a musical instrument produces sound. They could calculate wavelengths but found it difficult to imagine the behaviour of light. What was missing was not necessarily intelligence or effort, but the imaginative connection between abstract knowledge and lived experience.

This is precisely where literature can enrich science education.

Scientists and poets begin with curiosity. A scientist asks how something happens; a poet explores what it means. Both depend upon observation, imagination and the ability to discover connections that are not immediately apparent.

Naina Adil's collections, Shabd and Gul Bang, offer fascinating illustrations of this relationship. In Ae Mere Shabd, words become living companions, possessing emotional significance beyond their literal meanings. A physicist understands sound as a mechanical wave requiring a medium, yet a written poem can generate an extraordinary sense of sound in complete silence. This distinction offers an engaging starting point for discussing acoustics, perception and the relationship between physical stimuli and human experience.

Consider Naina's couplet describing two individuals walking together in the rain. One becomes completely drenched while the other remains emotionally untouched. The same rainfall produces contrasting experiences. For a science teacher, such imagery provides an opportunity to distinguish objective measurement from subjective interpretation.

Elsewhere, Naina imagines shaking hands with fragrance. Scientifically, fragrance involves volatile molecules travelling through air and interacting with olfactory receptors. Poetically, it becomes an encounter with memory, intimacy and absence. A teacher introducing diffusion could begin with this imaginative image before moving towards molecular motion and concentration gradients.

Her poem Jwala Mukhi offers another compelling educational possibility. An erupting volcano evokes pressure, heat and the release of accumulated energy. Its metaphorical association with suppressed emotions may help students visualise an otherwise unfamiliar geological phenomenon. The comparison is not a scientific explanation, but an imaginative bridge towards one.

Regrettably, our classrooms have become places where knowledge is memorised rather than imagined, equations are mastered without awakening wonder, and poetry is dissected until its living spirit disappears beneath prescribed interpretations. Students recite Newton's laws without appreciating the elegance of motion, encounter quantum mechanics without experiencing the fascination of uncertainty, and study literature without recognising its intimate conversation with nature and human existence. Somewhere along this educational journey, we have erected an invisible wall between reason and imagination, forgetting that humanity's greatest discoveries often began with curiosity rather than certainty. Difficult scientific phenomena demand mathematical precision, certainly, but also metaphors, visualisation and the courage to imagine what the senses cannot perceive. A metaphor cannot replace scientific evidence, yet it can illuminate the pathway towards understanding. Naina Adil's poetry reminds us that language can make the invisible perceptible, the abstract accessible and the unfamiliar emotionally meaningful. What our universities desperately need is not another exam reform, but a reunion of scientific inquiry and literary imagination, nurturing minds capable of questioning rather than merely remembering.

headline: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa - terrorism and politics
description: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa - terrorism and politics
author: Inam Ul Haque
article_text:
Last week after a cursory look at K-P, sociologically and politically, we surmised that in the province's predominant Pakhtun universe, the force of argument, or overwhelming force, play out effectively in resolving conflict. That in governing the lar (lower i.e. K-P/Balochistan) au (and) bar (upper i.e. Afghanistan) Pakhtunkhwa, the British governance model entailing minimal governance, self-rule and inducements was more successful, as compared to the recent US/NATO's Afghanistan model of central authority, pervasive governance and outlandish ideas, that failed. We discuss terrorism and the political mosaic of K- P.

Terrorism first. Having debated TTP's Afghanistan based framework, it is important to understand that terrorism also has a domestic dimension, besides Afghanistan's inspirational swamp. IEA power grab and six years in Kabul provide a lot of motivation to the would-be jihadists. The 'Jihad Enterprise' per se remains a reliable employer, caring even for the families of suicide bombers. Misguided religious notions dub Pakistani state as an impediment to Sharia implementation, and confederation with Afghanistan. Pakistan's military is painted as a non-religious entity by the ranking cadre of IEA and TTP. Afghan Taliban, TTP, al-Qaeda and IS-K find it easy to fish in Pakhtunkhwa's troubled waters, where sociology is supportive to their cause. And lack of economic opportunities especially in the Upper Pakhtunkhwa/Afghanistan provide an ideal environment for ethno-religious terrorism.

IEA, more precisely, Loya Paktia (Haqqanis) and Qandahar reckon that TTP manipulation can be used as an effective residual leverage with Islamabad, even if it is negative. The murky world of international politics, regional interests and spy games make Afghanistan, and by extension the Lower Pakhtunkhwa, a battleground for influence and resources. Mineral riches define the Western interest, Russian recognition and China's quiet diplomacy. Great Game continues with changed players between the US and China, as explained earlier. Pakistan's nuclear weapons attract awe and attention. India vies for contest, control and domination. And from all this power play, limelight and unwanted attention, Pakistan remains affected because Quetta and Peshawar are joined at the hip with Qandahar and Kabul.

There are stakeholders, irrespective of the conspiracy theories, that would like to see instability the operative norm in Pakhtunkhwa, as instability forces both Pakistan and Afghanistan to remain in a so-called vassal status, susceptible to external manipulation. IEA's avoidable obstinacy helps foster such instability.

Putting it all together, sociology, political economy and religion (as practised) acquiesce to and support terrorism in Pakhtunkhwa, under an enduring construct, that would need focused, concentrated and sustained efforts to defeat. Therefore, in a nutshell, terrorism – sponsored or home-grown – is likely to continue and run its full course. This warrants a whole-of-nation approach, with K-P gearing up administratively, employing police and intelligence effectively, and Federal Government deploying the harder hammer of military power, as needed, where needed. K-P cannot do it alone for reasons well known.

Pakistan had achieved significant successes during the last half of previous decade, when around 2015, it was able to flush terrorism out from Waziristan, Kurram, Swat, Bajaur and Mohmand. And after deploying kinetics, the non-kinetic (hearts, minds and development) prongs were employed with focus on relief, rehabilitation and rebuilding. The botched negotiation by the Bajwa-Faiz Combine (2021-2022) under Haqqani facilitation in Kabul resurrected terrorism, beginning from Swat. And once again Pakistan is in the 'Kinetics' Phase, that although theoretically should be 20% of counterterrorism (CT), is essentially first in the sequence, as it creates the conditions and environment for the deployment of non-kinetics, that constitute around 80% of the 'fight'.

Gleaning from the pervasive and relentless IBOs, the realignment of K-P with Centre, and the consequent change in the politics of K-P, one hopes that 'perhaps', the State is over-the-hill in WOT. Erstwhile FATA, reportedly, is weary of the marauding bands of TTP living off-the-land in extortion, burdening villagers for food and shelter, having unwittingly engineered a huge shift in public opinion. The Afghan Taliban realise the sensitivity and dead seriousness of Pakistan, in obliterating the TTP et al, whatever it takes. And Pakistan's diplomatic ascendance, successful alliances and improving economic conditions (despite the oil shocks) create a space for operational tempo to continue and accrue success. Though domestic political scene needs attention, not that it perils Pakistan, but to drown the political noise and keep the focus. So, with the 20-point National Action Plan (NAP) coordinated under NACTA, it is hoped that terrorism will be contained and eliminated in K-P in the mid- to long-term. It is good to see the glass 'half full'. As far as the Pak-Afghanistan bilateralism goes, it will get worse before it gets better, under B2B and P2P iterations.

With terrorism as an operative but waning norm, the State finally getting its act together to provide political weight and public support to CT operations, and coordinated consistency displayed by all organs of the State, Pakistan will prevail in WOT and against Baloch insurgency, irrespective of the Afghan swamp, external machinations and domestic noise by a political ideology.

Now politics. K-P's politics is likely to remain more of the same. Amongst the 'constants' of ANP, PTI and PML(N)/PPP Combine, JUI-F remains the only 'variable' wild card. The wily Maulana senses the wind direction, the gains to be made and the Miltablishment's mood like no one else and makes a move. Hence the likely scenario remains one of 'Governor's Rule' and 12-district emergency; which must continue under constitutional and legal provisos till the national elections are due in February 2029.

Elections would entail alliances between the 'constants' and the 'variable', too early to predict. JUI-F, however, has a history of political alliance with ANP. JUI-F's religious credentials and ANP's nationalist outlook suit K-P politics. ANP is strong in the northern districts and marginally in former FATA. JUI-F is popular in southern K-P and to a great extent in the former tribal belt. PML(N) remains ensconced in Hazarajat and some urban areas. PPP is urban based and to some extent in Doaba area (Charsadda etc). PTI represents the pervasive youth bulge and will be closely watched by all political forces. Its tug of war with Miltablishment will decide its fate, and hopefully sanity will trump emotions.

There are still slips up to the lips!

(Concluded)

Terrorism first. Having debated TTP's Afghanistan based framework, it is important to understand that terrorism also has a domestic dimension, besides Afghanistan's inspirational swamp. IEA power grab and six years in Kabul provide a lot of motivation to the would-be jihadists. The 'Jihad Enterprise' per se remains a reliable employer, caring even for the families of suicide bombers. Misguided religious notions dub Pakistani state as an impediment to Sharia implementation, and confederation with Afghanistan. Pakistan's military is painted as a non-religious entity by the ranking cadre of IEA and TTP. Afghan Taliban, TTP, al-Qaeda and IS-K find it easy to fish in Pakhtunkhwa's troubled waters, where sociology is supportive to their cause. And lack of economic opportunities especially in the Upper Pakhtunkhwa/Afghanistan provide an ideal environment for ethno-religious terrorism.

IEA, more precisely, Loya Paktia (Haqqanis) and Qandahar reckon that TTP manipulation can be used as an effective residual leverage with Islamabad, even if it is negative. The murky world of international politics, regional interests and spy games make Afghanistan, and by extension the Lower Pakhtunkhwa, a battleground for influence and resources. Mineral riches define the Western interest, Russian recognition and China's quiet diplomacy. Great Game continues with changed players between the US and China, as explained earlier. Pakistan's nuclear weapons attract awe and attention. India vies for contest, control and domination. And from all this power play, limelight and unwanted attention, Pakistan remains affected because Quetta and Peshawar are joined at the hip with Qandahar and Kabul.

There are stakeholders, irrespective of the conspiracy theories, that would like to see instability the operative norm in Pakhtunkhwa, as instability forces both Pakistan and Afghanistan to remain in a so-called vassal status, susceptible to external manipulation. IEA's avoidable obstinacy helps foster such instability.

Putting it all together, sociology, political economy and religion (as practised) acquiesce to and support terrorism in Pakhtunkhwa, under an enduring construct, that would need focused, concentrated and sustained efforts to defeat. Therefore, in a nutshell, terrorism – sponsored or home-grown – is likely to continue and run its full course. This warrants a whole-of-nation approach, with K-P gearing up administratively, employing police and intelligence effectively, and Federal Government deploying the harder hammer of military power, as needed, where needed. K-P cannot do it alone for reasons well known.

Pakistan had achieved significant successes during the last half of previous decade, when around 2015, it was able to flush terrorism out from Waziristan, Kurram, Swat, Bajaur and Mohmand. And after deploying kinetics, the non-kinetic (hearts, minds and development) prongs were employed with focus on relief, rehabilitation and rebuilding. The botched negotiation by the Bajwa-Faiz Combine (2021-2022) under Haqqani facilitation in Kabul resurrected terrorism, beginning from Swat. And once again Pakistan is in the 'Kinetics' Phase, that although theoretically should be 20% of counterterrorism (CT), is essentially first in the sequence, as it creates the conditions and environment for the deployment of non-kinetics, that constitute around 80% of the 'fight'.

Gleaning from the pervasive and relentless IBOs, the realignment of K-P with Centre, and the consequent change in the politics of K-P, one hopes that 'perhaps', the State is over-the-hill in WOT. Erstwhile FATA, reportedly, is weary of the marauding bands of TTP living off-the-land in extortion, burdening villagers for food and shelter, having unwittingly engineered a huge shift in public opinion. The Afghan Taliban realise the sensitivity and dead seriousness of Pakistan, in obliterating the TTP et al, whatever it takes. And Pakistan's diplomatic ascendance, successful alliances and improving economic conditions (despite the oil shocks) create a space for operational tempo to continue and accrue success. Though domestic political scene needs attention, not that it perils Pakistan, but to drown the political noise and keep the focus. So, with the 20-point National Action Plan (NAP) coordinated under NACTA, it is hoped that terrorism will be contained and eliminated in K-P in the mid- to long-term. It is good to see the glass 'half full'. As far as the Pak-Afghanistan bilateralism goes, it will get worse before it gets better, under B2B and P2P iterations.

With terrorism as an operative but waning norm, the State finally getting its act together to provide political weight and public support to CT operations, and coordinated consistency displayed by all organs of the State, Pakistan will prevail in WOT and against Baloch insurgency, irrespective of the Afghan swamp, external machinations and domestic noise by a political ideology.

Now politics. K-P's politics is likely to remain more of the same. Amongst the 'constants' of ANP, PTI and PML(N)/PPP Combine, JUI-F remains the only 'variable' wild card. The wily Maulana senses the wind direction, the gains to be made and the Miltablishment's mood like no one else and makes a move. Hence the likely scenario remains one of 'Governor's Rule' and 12-district emergency; which must continue under constitutional and legal provisos till the national elections are due in February 2029.

Elections would entail alliances between the 'constants' and the 'variable', too early to predict. JUI-F, however, has a history of political alliance with ANP. JUI-F's religious credentials and ANP's nationalist outlook suit K-P politics. ANP is strong in the northern districts and marginally in former FATA. JUI-F is popular in southern K-P and to a great extent in the former tribal belt. PML(N) remains ensconced in Hazarajat and some urban areas. PPP is urban based and to some extent in Doaba area (Charsadda etc). PTI represents the pervasive youth bulge and will be closely watched by all political forces. Its tug of war with Miltablishment will decide its fate, and hopefully sanity will trump emotions.
There are still slips up to the lips!
(Concluded)

headline: India's democracy: the arrogance of power
description: India's democracy: the arrogance of power
author: Durdana Najam
article_text:
There is something almost theatrical about the spectacle unfolding in India. Amit Shah, the country's powerful home minister, marches through Hyderabad holding the national flag, ostensibly to save democracy. Elsewhere, Rahul Gandhi, opposition politicians and thousands of young Indians are taking to the streets carrying the same flag, demanding that democracy be saved from the very government Shah represents. Both the government and the opposition are on the streets to save democracy. How did the world's largest democracy arrive at this extraordinary contradiction?

At the heart of the controversy is an accusation that elections in India have been unfair. Rahul Gandhi has accused the BJP and the Election Commission of manipulating electoral rolls to influence election results.

Gandhi's allegations concern duplicate registrations, fictitious addresses, suspicious additions to electoral lists and the deletion of eligible voters. In Karnataka's Mahadevapura constituency, he identified more than 100,000 allegedly irregular entries. In Maharashtra, he questioned the unusually large increase in registered voters before the 2024 Assembly elections. In Haryana, he alleged that millions of votes had been compromised through electoral irregularities.

The Election Commission of India has rejected these accusations and demanded evidence. Discrepancies in electoral rolls do not, by themselves, establish that fraudulent votes were cast. Nevertheless, the allegations have brought into the open a crisis of confidence that the BJP can no longer dismiss as ordinary opposition rhetoric.

West Bengal has become one of the clearest examples of this controversy. Ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections, approximately 9.08 million voters, nearly 12 per cent of the state's electorate, were removed from electoral rolls through an exercise known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The Election Commission maintained that the exercise was necessary to remove duplicate registrations, deceased persons and ineligible voters. However, serious concerns arose when independent research suggested that approximately 3.11 million of those removed were Muslims, representing 34.3 per cent of the total deletions. The impact was particularly severe during a subsequent stage of scrutiny, when Muslims reportedly accounted for nearly 70 per cent of approximately 2.7 million deletions. Critics argue that such exclusions could serve the BJP's broader political and ideological agenda of promoting Hindutva and transforming India's secular character into one increasingly defined by Hindu majoritarianism.

The BJP subsequently won 207 seats, ending fifteen years of Trinamool rule.

The more troubling development is that these controversies are occurring within a political system that has undergone a profound transformation since Narendra Modi came to power in 2014. What is being questioned today is not merely the conduct of elections but the larger political and economic narrative on which the BJP has built its authority.

The BJP has gradually created a political environment in which power is concentrated around individual leaders, religion plays a growing role in politics, and patriotism is often judged according to the party's own ideology. India, which once took pride in its religious, linguistic and cultural diversity, is now witnessing a situation in which these very differences have been turned into political fault lines.

Meanwhile, a new generation of young Indians is increasingly questioning the political system that has developed under Narendra Modi's leadership over the past decade. Having grown up under BJP rule, many are becoming disillusioned with the government's claims of transparency, fairness and democratic accountability. Their protests initially focused on corruption and irregularities in the education and examination systems, but their concerns have now extended to allegations of electoral fraud. They fear that the democratic values on which modern India was founded are being undermined and that the institutions meant to protect them are losing their independence and credibility.

This growing scepticism is not confined to politics. The BJP's claims of economic success are also being subjected to closer scrutiny. The Modi government reported GDP growth of 7.7 per cent in 202526 and continues to project India as one of the world's fastest-growing major economies. Yet prominent Indian economists have questioned whether the official statistics provide an accurate picture of the country's economic performance. Former Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, along with economists Josh Felman and Abhishek Anand, has argued that between 2012 and 2023, India's annual economic growth was overstated by approximately 1.5 to 2 percentage points. Their research suggests that growth averaged around 4 to 4.5 per cent rather than the officially reported 6 per cent during that period. Former Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan has raised another important question: why has such impressive economic growth not translated into stronger job creation, investment and capital inflows?

The irony is difficult to miss. A government that speaks constantly of India's democratic greatness and economic achievements now finds itself confronting citizens who question both its political practices and its claims of progress.

India's present predicament is therefore larger than the future of Modi or the BJP. It concerns the political character of a country that once derived enormous international prestige from its commitment to democratic pluralism. That reputation, however, depends not merely on the power of its government or the performance of its economy, but on the strength of its democratic institutions and the trust they command among its citizens.

Yet prominent Indian economists have questioned whether the official statistics provide an accurate picture of the country's economic performance. Former Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, along with economists Josh Felman and Abhishek Anand, has argued that between 2012 and 2023, India's annual economic growth was overstated by approximately 1.5 to 2 percentage points. Their research suggests that growth averaged around 4 to 4.5 per cent rather than the officially reported 6 per cent during that period. Former Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan has raised another important question: why has such impressive economic growth not translated into stronger job creation, investment and capital inflows?

The irony is difficult to miss. A government that speaks constantly of India's democratic greatness and economic achievements now finds itself confronting citizens who question both its political practices and its claims of progress.

India's present predicament is therefore larger than the future of Modi or the BJP. It concerns the political character of a country that once derived enormous international prestige from its commitment to democratic pluralism. That reputation, however, depends not merely on the power of its government or the performance of its economy, but on the strength of its democratic institutions and the trust they command among its citizens.

headline: PTI seeks Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital over renewed blood pressure concerns
description: Imran's sister demands independent medical treatment, saying his blood pressure was normal as recently as a year ago.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Wednesday expressed grave concern over the health of its incarcerated founder Imran Khan, saying his blood pressure had reached 192 in recent days, and demanded his immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital for independent medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians.

The statement came two days after a meeting between Imran and his lawyer at Adiala jail on Nov 2, during which the former prime minister reportedly conveyed concerns about his health.

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has allowed Imran to meet his family members, lawyers and other associates twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. However, despite repeated court orders directing the authorities to facilitate these meetings, access to the former prime minister by his family and party leaders has remained largely restricted in recent months.

In the meeting's aftermath, Imran's sister Rubina Khan said her brother had conveyed through his lawyer that his blood pressure had shot up to 192. She alleged that he had accused the authorities of failing to provide him with proper medical treatment.

She said the lawyer had been allowed to meet Imran briefly after seven months, adding that access to a lawyer was a basic right of every prisoner.

“Imran Khan has never had high blood pressure. As recently as a year ago, his blood pressure was normal,” she said, adding that the family’s medical advisers considered it unusual for someone over 70 to suddenly develop high blood pressure.

“As his family, we demand that he be immediately admitted to an independent medical institution in Islamabad for proper treatment, in the presence of his personal doctor and a doctor of my choice,” Rubina said.

She also referred to statements by the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, UN experts, the UN Committee Against Torture and Amnesty International concerning Imran's detention and treatment.

Rubina said the Supreme Court's August 2026 decision requiring immediate medical treatment at Shifa hospital had not been implemented.

She alleged that there had previously been multiple attempts on her brother's life, including an assassination attempt, and said the family feared for his safety in prison.

“If he does not receive medical treatment now, anything that happens to him would amount to cold-blooded murder,” she said.

Sharing his aunt's statement on X, Imran's son Kasim said: “This high blood pressure is not normal. It is the direct result of this isolation.”

“If he is not freed soon, he will die in this cell,” he added.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja called it an "extremely alarming matter”.

He further said: "We now, as a party, need to adopt an effective strategy regarding the health of Khan Sahib and Bushri Bibi. An effective strategy cannot be based merely on excitement and anger ... In this regard, every doubt and apprehension must be eliminated. After consultation with all authorised bodies of the family and the party, including the parliamentary party, a full-force voice will be raised both inside the country and abroad. Protecting Khan Sahib's health is the duty of the entire nation."

In a statement shared by the PTI on X, Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said repeated fluctuations in Imran's blood pressure were a matter of extreme concern, adding that protecting his health was the responsibility of the state and the entire nation.

He accused the government of endangering the life and fundamental rights of the country's most popular political leader by denying him adequate medical facilities, access to his family and treatment of his choice.

Akram demanded immediate implementation of the Supreme Court's August 18 order directing Imran's transfer to Shifa International Hospital, where he should be treated by his personal and family-appointed doctors.

He also called for the release of Imran, Bushra Bibi and all political prisoners detained in Kot Lakhpat jail and elsewhere in the country. He condemned raids on PTI ministers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and what he described as violations of the sanctity of homes in Punjab and K-P.

“Political victimisation and repression must end,” he said, urging the government to release Imran and pursue national reconciliation to put the country back on the path of peace, prosperity and progress.
